Cardiovascular magnetic resonance derived myocardial strain: applications, acquisition techniques, analysis, and reporting. A Scientific Statement of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance, Radiological Society of North America, and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging of the ESC.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract: Myocardial strain imaging enables quantification of cardiac deformation. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) is well suited for strain assessment due to the ability to image in any given plane with high spatial and contrast resolution. CMR strain measures have incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility over conventional clinical imaging parameters across disease states. Routine integration of CMR strain assessment in clinical practice has been hindered by the lack of agreement on imaging protocols and analysis methods, variability due to noise sensitivity, and a paucity of robust normative age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges. In recognition of the expanding applications of strain techniques in clinical and research CMR, this joint SCMR/RSNA/EACVI scientific statement integrates data from original research studies, guidelines, and opinions from experts across the field to guide responsible and evidence-based utilization of CMR strain.

articles.title: Real-World Predictors and Temporal Trends in Intravascular Imaging Use During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in a Publicly Funded Health System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) improves clinical outcomes in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet real-world utilisation remains inconsistent. We evaluated temporal trends and determinants of IVI use within a large publicly funded, non-fee-for-service, healthcare system.

METHODS: All PCI procedures performed across Queensland public hospitals between 2016 and 2023 were analysed using registry data. The primary outcome was IVI use. Independent predictors were assessed using multivariable analysis.

RESULTS: Among 39,136 PCI procedures, IVI was used in 9.0% overall and increased from 5.6% in 2016 to 16.5% in 2023 (ptrend=0.002). Procedural complexity was the primary determinant: left main PCI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.84; 95% confidence interval [CI] 5.26-11.69), intravascular lithotripsy (aOR 8.51; 95% CI 3.78-19.15), and bifurcation lesions (aOR 1.34; 95% CI 1.01-1.78) were independent predictors. Conversely, ST-elevation myocardial infarction predicted lower use (aOR 0.49; 95% CI 0.42-0.59). Higher operator procedural volume was associated with increased IVI use (aOR 1.25; 95% CI 1.00-1.54). While operator training era and institutional factors were significant in unadjusted models, associations were attenuated after accounting for hospital-level clustering, suggesting strong influence of local hospital processes and culture toward IVI.

CONCLUSIONS: IVI use has increased but remains underutilised. Adoption is driven primarily by procedural complexity and operator-level factors, with persistent inter-hospital variability. These findings highlight an ongoing evidence-practice gap and support system-level strategies to standardise IVI use in contemporary PCI.

articles.title: Endovascular management of labyrintho-vascular otic capsule dehiscence (type II): A different therapeutical approach.
articles.journal: European annals of otorhinolaryngology, head and neck diseases
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Otic capsule dehiscence (OCD) encompasses a spectrum of third mobile window disorders, including type II variants characterized by a direct interface between the membranous labyrinth and adjacent vascular structures. These labyrinthine-vascular dehiscences (type IIa: superior semicircular canal-superior petrosal sinus (SPS); type IIb: internal jugular vein-vestibular structures) may induce pulsatile tinnitus, vertigo, and hearing loss. Endovascular treatment has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to conventional surgery, aiming to reduce vascular pulsatility transmission to the inner ear. This study evaluates the interest, clinical outcomes and limitations of such approaches.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series including patients with unilateral type II OCD confirmed by high-resolution imaging and presenting with disabling symptoms as assessed by the DHI and the THI. All patients underwent comprehensive audio-vestibular assessment and multimodal imaging. Endovascular treatment strategies included stenting of the SPS (type IIa) or stent-assisted coiling of the jugular bulb/internal jugular vein (type IIb). Outcomes were assessed clinically, audiometrically, and radiologically at follow-up.

RESULTS: Eight patients were included (4 type IIa, 4 type IIb). Endovascular treatment was feasible in most cases, with one technical failure and one conversion to surgery due to unfavorable venous anatomy. At 6 months, 7/7 evaluable patients showed marked clinical improvement, with significant reductions in THI and DHI scores. Pulsatile tinnitus and vertigo improved in the majority of cases. Audiometric outcomes were variable, with closure of the air-bone gap in 4 patients. Vestibular function remained largely preserved, with only transient postoperative impairment in one case. No major complications or venous thrombosis were observed on follow-up imaging.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular management of type II OCD appears to be a safe and effective minimally invasive alternative in selected patients, particularly for vascular-related symptoms. The outcomes depend heavily on venous anatomy and meticulous preoperative imaging. While clinical outcomes are encouraging, limitations include technical feasibility and variable auditory results. Endovascular approaches may be considered a first-line option when anatomically suitable, with surgery reserved for selected or failed cases.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and management strategies of congenital auricular deformities combined with first branchial cleft anomalies in children: A retrospective study of 25 cases.
articles.journal: European annals of otorhinolaryngology, head and neck diseases
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarise the clinical characteristics and management strategies of congenital auricular malformations with first branchial cleft anomalies (CFBCAs) in children.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 25 children with complete clinical data who were admitted between January 2020 and January 2025.

RESULTS: All patients presented with unilateral auricular malformations. Five had Grade I microtia, two had Grade II conchal adhesion-type deformity, and 14 had Grade II accessory tragus-type deformity; four had hemifacial microsomia. Nineteen had a history of a preoperative infection. CFBCAs are located near the external auditory canal (EAC) and manifest as sinus tracts, fistulas, or small cutaneous pits on the cheek. Based on anatomical location, CFBCAs were classified as type I (located in the postauricular area with roots attached to the cartilage of the inferior wall, n=5), type II (located anterior to the tragus with roots attached to the cartilage of the inferior wall, n=14), and type III (located in the cheek region, which may be accompanied by hemifacial microsomia, with a cartilaginous blind end, n=6). All the lesions were superficial to the facial nerve. Twenty underwent CFBCA excision combined with auricular deformity reconstruction. During the postoperative follow-up (6 months to 5 years), no facial nerve paralysis, recurrence, or auricular infection occurred; five had mild EAC stenosis.

CONCLUSION: Paediatric congenital auricular deformities may coexist with first branchial cleft anomalies, Accurate diagnosis and precise classification are essential for lesion identification and complete excision, which improve treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Costs of two-step MASLD screening using ALT and elastography in children with overweight and obesity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is prevalent among children with obesity. Although screening is widely performed in pediatric obesity-related comorbidity assessment, evidence on effectiveness and costs is lacking. This study quantifies costs of MASLD screening using ALT and vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) in children with overweight and obesity.

METHODS: We prospectively analyzed costs of a two-step MASLD screening strategy in obesity clinics in the Amsterdam region. Children with overweight and obesity underwent ALT testing; those with elevated ALT were referred for further assessment according to MASLD guidelines. Healthcare and societal costs were calculated per child screened and per advanced MASLD case detected (VCTE ≥7.4 kPa). Scenario 1 included limited additional testing for other liver disorders and scenario 2 more elaborate testing.

RESULTS: In a screened population of 2376 children, healthcare costs were €144 per child screened and €5608 per advanced MASLD case detected; healthcare and societal costs combined were €201 per child screened and €7822 per case detected. Scenario 2 increased healthcare costs by 15%.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides novel cost data on pediatric MASLD screening, which may inform policy and implementation strategies for children with overweight and obesity.

Clinical Study of Bullous Pemphigoid With Oral Mucosal Symptoms After Oral Administration of Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors are widely used for diabetes treatment. However, reports of DPP-4 inhibitor-associated bullous pemphigoid (BP) have been increasing. This study examined 12 cases of BP with oral mucosal lesions associated with DPP-4 inhibitor therapy. Six cases presented with only oral mucosal lesions, while the other six patients had non-inflammatory skin lesions. Discontinuation of DPP-4 inhibitors led to symptom improvement in nine cases, whereas three cases did not improve, with lesion progression to the pharynx. Remission was achieved after a mean of 20.8 ± 24.6 months after DPP-4 inhibitor discontinuation, but two cases relapsed. Anti-BP180 NC16a antibodies were positive in six cases, while full-length BP180 ELISA was positive in 8 of 10 tested cases. These findings suggested that DPP-4 inhibitor-associated BP frequently involves oral mucosal lesions, and some cases may present solely with mucosal symptoms. Given the potential for recurrence and severe progression, long-term follow-up is essential.

articles.title: Evaluation of high-dose alerts in computed tomography using an automated dose monitoring system: a retrospective institutional study.
articles.abstract: Radiation dose monitoring software (DMS) tools are increasingly used to support automated monitoring of radiation dose in medical imaging. This study evaluated the frequency and causes of high-dose events detected by a DMS in computed tomography (CT). All CT examinations performed at one hospital across three CT scanners over a one-year period were retrospectively analysed to establish the frequency and causes of high-dose alerts. Descriptive statistics summarized alert frequency and distribution, and multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with high-dose alerts. Of 11,865 CT examinations, 851 (7%) exceeded predefined dose thresholds. High-dose alerts occurred most frequently in spine (17%), musculoskeletal joint (14%), abdomen/pelvis (8%), vascular angiography (8%), chest/lung (5%), and head/face (4%) examinations. Reasons for high-dose alerts included high body mass index (29%), scan repetition (25%), additional scans (15%), patient malpositioning (12%), excess scan range (11%), and orthopaedic hardware (6%). Multivariable analysis showed that overweight status, scanner model, spine and joint examinations, and patients aged 45-74 years were independently associated with high-dose alert occurrence (P < .05). DMS is an effective tool that enables imaging facilities to automatically identify high-dose events, facilitating investigation of their causes, protocol review, and identification of opportunities for dose optimisation.

articles.title: Hemodynamic unmasking of serial cerebral venous sinus stenoses following treatment of the rate-limiting lesion.
articles.abstract: An 18-year-old female presented with headaches, transient visual obscurations, and papilledema secondary to a primary superior sagittal sinus (SSS) stenosis caused by compression from a presumed parasagittal meningioma, with an associated secondary dominant transverse-sigmoid junction (TSJ) stenosis.1 2 3 Initial venous manometry demonstrated a hemodynamically significant pressure gradient across the TSJ stenosis but only a 4 mm Hg gradient across the SSS stenosis. Following TSJ stenting, repeat venous manometry unmasked the hemodynamic significance of the SSS stenosis, prompting subsequent SSS stenting.4 5 Final venous manometry demonstrated elimination of all hemodynamically significant pressure gradients, with improvement in headaches and papilledema at follow-up.6 7This technical video (video 1) demonstrates how serial cerebral venous sinus stenoses can confound interpretation of venous manometry; it highlights the importance of repeat venous manometry following treatment of the rate-limiting lesion, as the hemodynamic significance of adjacent stenoses may only become apparent once the dominant pressure gradient has been eliminated.neurintsurg;jnis-2026-026225v1/V1F1V1Video 1 . Technical video demonstrating the impact of serial cerebral venous sinus stenoses on venous manometry and the role of repeat pressure measurements in guiding endovascular treatment.

Management Strategies for Intracranial Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas with an Isolated Sinus: A 20-Year Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are rare, aggressive subtypes of arteriovenous shunt. Optimal treatment strategies remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To present a 20-year single-center experience evaluating treatment strategies and outcomes for isolated sinus DAVFs.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all adult patients treated for isolated sinus DAVFs at our institution from January 2004 to March 2025. Isolated sinus DAVFs were defined as fistulas draining into venous sinus segments that are functionally isolated, i.e. have no antegrade or retrograde venous sinus outflow. Data included clinical presentation, angiographic features, treatment approach, outcomes, and complications.

RESULTS: Of 425 patients treated for intracranial DAVFs, 35/425 (8%) had an isolated sinus DAVF and underwent 43 treatment sessions. Transarterial embolization (TAE) was the initial treatment in 23/35 (66%) patients, achieving immediate single-session angiographic occlusion in 17/23 (74%) and final single-session occlusion in 18/23 (78%) after spontaneous thrombosis of a residual fistula in one case. Transvenous embolization (TVE) was the initial treatment in 10/35 (29%) patients, achieving immediate single-session angiographic occlusion in 8/10 (80%) and final single-session occlusion in 9/10 (90%) after spontaneous thrombosis in one case. Three open burr-hole-assisted TVE procedures - one primary and two salvage - achieved complete occlusion. Two open surgical disconnections, one primary and one salvage, also achieved complete occlusion. Five patients (5/35; 14%) required more than one treatment session. Three major complications occurred across 43 treatment sessions (3/43; 7%). No residual fistula was identified in any patient at last available imaging follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Isolated sinus DAVFs are challenging to manage and may require multimodal treatment. Our findings support individualized, angioarchitecture-based treatment selection for this complex DAVF subtype.

articles.title: The Added Value of Vessel Wall MRI Over CTA for Differentiating Large-Artery Atherosclerotic and Cardioembolic Stroke in the Anterior and Posterior Circulations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Differentiation between stroke etiologies is essential for secondary prevention; however, etiologic classification remains challenging in many ischemic strokes. We evaluated whether magnetic resonance vessel wall imaging (VWI) plaque markers improve computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based differentiation between cardioembolic (CE) and large-artery atherosclerotic (LAA) stroke in the anterior and posterior circulations, as a step toward improving etiologic classification beyond current criteria.

METHODS: We retrospectively included patients with unilateral anterior or posterior circulation ischemic stroke between June 2022 and April 2024 across an academic health system, classified as LAA or CE according to modified TOAST criteria. Imaging markers included CTA-derived noncalcified plaque extent (>30% stenosis), VWI-derived intracranial plaque enhancement (IPE) extent, and intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) presence, restricted to arterial segments upstream from the infarct. Given potential territory-specific plaque differences, analyses were stratified by circulation. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of CTA and VWI markers with stroke etiology. Associations with LAA were summarized using adjusted odds ratios (aOR; plaque extent variables per 1-SD increase). Overall performance for discriminating between LAA and CE etiologies was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Among 193 patients (median age, 70 years; 60% male), 137 had anterior circulation strokes (65 LAA, 72 CE) and 56 had posterior circulation strokes (38 LAA, 18 CE). In anterior circulation strokes, VWI markers improved discrimination over CTA alone (AUC, 0.57 for CTA alone vs 0.76 for CTA+VWI; p<0.001); CTA-derived noncalcified plaque extent (aOR, 1.7; p=0.02), IPH (aOR, 7.0; p<0.001), and IPE extent (aOR, 1.9; p=0.005) were independently associated with LAA. In posterior circulation strokes, IPE extent improved discrimination over CTA alone (AUC, 0.77 for CTA alone vs 0.84 for CTA+VWI; p=0.02); IPE extent (aOR, 2.2; p=0.02) and CTA-derived noncalcified plaque extent (aOR, 5.9; p=0.002) were independently associated with LAA. IPH was not significantly associated with posterior circulation stroke etiology (p=0.26).

CONCLUSIONS: VWI adds complementary value for differentiating LAA and CE stroke etiologies in both vascular territories, supporting a pragmatic CTA-VWI approach for etiologic characterization beyond stenosis assessment alone.

articles.title: Bevacizumab Infusion into Middle Meningeal Arteries for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: Insights from 35 Hemispheres in 25 Patients.
articles.abstract: Bevacizumab is an anti-vascular endothelial growth factor antibody that may disrupt the pro-inflammatory cascade driving chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) development, expansion, and recurrence. This expanded case series describes clinical and radiographic outcomes of intra-arterial infusion of bevacizumab into the middle meningeal artery for treatment of chronic subdural hematoma in 35 hemispheres of 25 patients. Adult patients with asymptomatic or mild symptoms and either unilateral or bilateral CSDH with mixed-density appearance or presence of membranes infused with intra-arterial bevacizumab in one or both middle meningeal arteries under fluoroscopic guidance were included. The primary outcome was the percent reduction in CSDH size from baseline to 90-day follow-up. Of 25 included patients, median age was 77 years (IQR 68-86). Of 35 treated hemispheres, 80% (28/35) hemispheres demonstrated greater than 50% CSDH resolution, and 25.7% (9/35) hemispheres had 100% resolution by 90 days. There were no rescue interventions for symptomatic recurrence, new stroke or neurological deterioration, or mortality by 90 days. In conclusion, intra-arterial bevacizumab infusion demonstrates potential as a novel endovascular approach to CSDH in select patients.

Magnitude and Moderators of Depressive Symptom Improvement in Digital Placebo Arms: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive disorders are one of the most prevalent psychiatric disorders globally and impose considerable individual and societal burdens. Psychotherapy, including cognitive behavioral therapy, is recommended as a first-line treatment especially for mild to moderate depressive disorders. However, face-to-face psychotherapy is often limited by issues of accessibility and cost. Digital therapeutics (DTx)-defined as health software intended to treat or alleviate a disease, disorder, condition, or injury by generating and delivering a medical intervention that has a demonstrable positive therapeutic impact on a patient by the International Organization for Standardization-have gained increasing attention as alternatives for overcoming these hurdles. With advances in digital technology, digital placebos have begun to be used as comparators in the clinical trials of DTx to assess the effects of active interventions accurately. However, the characteristics of clinical trials, the magnitude of digital placebos effects, and their moderators remain poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize clinical trials using digital placebos in control arms and to assess the magnitude and moderators of Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) improvement in digital placebo arms.

METHODS: The blinded randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating PHQ-9 by setting digital placebos as comparators were identified by searching MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ISRCTN in November 2025. The characteristics of the RCTs and of the digital placebos were reviewed systematically. The meta-analysis including subgroup analyses and meta-regressions were conducted to investigate the magnitude and the moderators of the PHQ-9 improvement in digital placebo arms.

RESULTS: A total of 29 papers and 30 trials with 5680 participants were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. The most common trial design was 2-arm, parallel-group RCTs conducted in a single country, adopting "Replaced" and "Mobile" as the placebo approach and delivery type, respectively. The pooled effect size for all the included trials, representing PHQ-9 changes within control arms, was Hedges g=0.44 (95% CI 0.29-0.59) with high heterogeneity (I2=93.2%, τ²=0.14). Subgroup analyses and univariable regression showed that "Primary psychiatric disorder" group (P=.008) and baseline PHQ-9 score (P<.001) were the independent moderators of the improvement in digital placebo arms. Multivariable regression indicated that these 2 variables are the major contributing factors of the high heterogeneity (I2=82.1%, τ²=0.07, R2=51.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that improvement in digital placebo arms is not negligible and should be incorporated into trial design. The factors identified in this study will be useful when estimating expected improvement in control arms and planning adequately powered future DTx clinical trials, alongside other relevant conceptual and methodological factors that may influence digital placebo effects.

articles.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Appropriateness of an 8-Week Supervised Aerobic Exercise Intervention for Adults With Epilepsy: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy affects multiple dimensions of health. Exercise may serve as a nonpharmacological strategy to improve health outcomes among adults with epilepsy; however, translating this potential into effective and scalable interventions remains challenging. Before advancing to efficacy trials, early-stage research is needed to establish whether exercise interventions are feasible, acceptable, and appropriate for this population.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of an 8-week supervised aerobic exercise intervention for adults with epilepsy, guided by the Obesity-Related Behavioral Intervention Trials (ORBIT) model.

METHODS: Adults with epilepsy aged 18-65 years were recruited between April 2024 and December 2024 and randomized to either a supervised aerobic exercise intervention (n=4) or a control group (n=2). The exercise group completed an 8-week supervised aerobic exercise program consisting of 50-minute sessions performed 3 days per week. The intervention incorporated behavior change techniques, including goal setting, action planning, habit formation, and commitment contracts to support exercise adherence. Process feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, adherence, survey completion, protocol compliance, and safety. Self-reported feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness were assessed using the Feasibility of Intervention Measure, Acceptability of Intervention Measure, and Intervention Appropriateness Measure.

RESULTS: Overall, 34 individuals expressed interest in the study, 25 completed the screening survey, 10 were preliminarily eligible, and 6 were enrolled in the study over 8 months. Recruitment was low, with a recruitment rate of 0.75 participants per month and enrollment achievement of 16.7% of the target sample (target n=36). Retention and adherence were 100%. All exercise participants completed 24/24 sessions, with 100% weekly survey completion. Protocol compliance was high. No seizures occurred during exercise sessions. Mean scores for self-reported feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness were high (>4 out of 5).

CONCLUSIONS: The results of this Phase IIb pilot study suggest that a supervised aerobic exercise intervention for adults with epilepsy is feasible, acceptable, and appropriate to implement among participants who enroll. Recruitment remains the primary challenge to progressing this line of research and may represent a broader field-level barrier. Future trials should focus on improving how adults with epilepsy are reached and engaged in exercise research while preserving intervention strategies that support strong engagement among those who enroll.

articles.title: Amoxicillin shortages in French primary care: a qualitative study of family physicians' behaviors and infectious diseases implications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Amoxicillin is the first-line antibiotic most commonly prescribed by family physicians (FPs) in France, but recurrent national shortages have disrupted its availability since 2013. Data on FPs' adaptations to these shortages, and their infectious disease consequences, remain scarce.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study among 10 FPs practicing in the Hauts-de-Seine and Yvelines departments (France), using semi-structured interviews analyzed with Thomas's general inductive approach.

RESULTS: FPs described a triple uncertainty (drug availability, therapeutic choice, information) which prompted pragmatic prescribing, therapeutic substitution, and reliance on decision-support tools. Shortages reconfigured the physician-pharmacist-patient relation, empowering pharmacists while constraining patients. Substitution toward broader-spectrum antibiotics raised concerns about bacterial resistance, echoed by emerging clinical signals of complicated infections during shortage periods.

CONCLUSION: Structured, real-time information and antimicrobial stewardship-compatible guidance are needed to anticipate future amoxicillin shortages in primary care.

articles.title: Neurocognitive Outcomes in Patients with Pituitary Adenomas.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To perform a systematic review to explore the impact of surgical interventions for pituitary adenomas on cognitive function. We assessed diverse cognitive domains, including memory and learning and complex attention and executive function.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic literature search across six databases. We identified studies published during a 20-year period (2004-2024) that included adult patients diagnosed with NFPA (Non functioning Pituitary adenoma), acromegaly or Cushing's Disease (CD) who had undergone standardised neurocognitive tests pre- and post-surgical interventions. Data synthesis included descriptive statistics and bias assessments using the 'NHLBI' (National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute) and 'GRADE' (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) tools.

RESULTS: We included six eligible studies in our review. Post-operatively, there were significant improvements in memory in patients with diagnosed NFPAs and CD. There was promising recovery of attention, processing speed and working memory following surgical management, particularly for those patients with diagnosed NFPAs. Those patients with diagnosed CD demonstrated post-operative recovery of verbal fluency and general cognition. Conversely, those patients diagnosed with acromegaly had limited improvements in their cognition post-operatively, likely reflecting irreversible neurological changes caused by prolonged exposure to excessive serum levels of growth hormone.

CONCLUSIONS: Surgical interventions for pituitary adenomas offer promising cognitive recovery for those patients diagnosed with NFPAs and CD, although cognitive deficits may persist post-operatively, particularly for those diagnosed with acromegaly. The variability in post-operative cognitive outcomes identified in this review highlights a need for standardised cognitive assessments and longitudinal studies to examine cognitive recovery following surgical management of pituitary adenomas. Clinically, routine cognitive assessment and integration of these measures into multidisciplinary management approaches are important to optimise patient outcomes.

articles.title: Oral or Enteral Levothyroxine for Myxedema Coma When Intravenous Therapy Is Unavailable: A Systematic Review and Descriptive Evidence Synthesis.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Intravenous levothyroxine is generally preferred for myxedema coma but may be unavailable in many healthcare settings. We summarized published treatment regimens and outcomes with oral or enteral levothyroxine when intravenous therapy was unavailable. Intravenous-only and mixed-route reports were included for clinical context.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 2026. Studies reporting myxedema coma treated with oral, enteral, nasogastric, or intravenous levothyroxine and extractable clinical outcomes were included. Pooled proportions were calculated only as descriptive summaries of oral/enteral reports and were not interpreted as treatment-effect estimates. Intravenous-only and mixed-route studies were summarized narratively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence using GRADE.

RESULTS: Nine studies comprising 70 patients were included: six oral/enteral, two intravenous-only, and one mixed-route study. Oral/enteral loading doses ranged from 300 to 1000 μg. Descriptively pooled proportions were 0.20 for mortality, 0.76 for intensive care unit admission, 0.54 for mechanical ventilation, and 0.62 for vasopressor requirement. These estimates are descriptive summaries of selected published reports and should not be interpreted as population-level event rates, treatment-effect estimates, route-specific risks, or expected outcome probabilities in routine clinical practice.

CONCLUSIONS: Published reports document oral or enteral levothyroxine as a rescue approach when intravenous treatment is unavailable. However, evidence is insufficient to establish comparative efficacy, safety, equivalence, or an optimal dosing regimen. Intravenous levothyroxine should remain preferred when available, particularly in patients with shock, ileus, or unreliable gastrointestinal absorption.

articles.title: Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Once-Weekly Lonapegsomatropin in Adults With Growth Hormone Deficiency: Results From a 52-Week Open-Label Extension Trial.
authors: Investigator group for the extension to the foresiGHt trial
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term safety and efficacy of once-weekly lonapegsomatropin in adults with growth hormone (GH) deficiency.

METHODS: This 52-week, multicenter, open-label extension trial enrolled adults with GH deficiency who completed the 38-week phase 3 foresiGHt trial, in which participants received lonapegsomatropin, placebo, or somatropin.1 In the extension, all participants received lonapegsomatropin. Safety assessment included adverse events (AEs), laboratory values, vital signs, immunogenicity, 12-lead electrocardiograms, and fundoscopy. Body composition (trunk percent fat, trunk fat mass, visceral adipose tissue, total body lean mass, trunk lean mass, and appendicular lean mass) was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, and patient-reported outcomes were evaluated.

RESULTS: Following foresiGHt completion, 220 (88.7%) participants enrolled in the extension. Across foresiGHt and the extension, common lonapegsomatropin-associated AEs were nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory infection, and headache. Injection site reactions were infrequent (5.1%) and mild or moderate. After up to 90 weeks of treatment, body composition was maintained in participants continuing lonapegsomatropin, and improved relative to foresiGHt baseline in those initiating or switching to lonapegsomatropin. Clinically meaningful improvements in patient-reported outcomes from foresiGHt baseline were observed; 43.5%, 40.6%, and 35.8% of participants achieving a ≥10-point improvement in Treatment Related Impact Measure-Adult GH Deficiency (TRIM-AGHD) total score among those continuing, initiating, or switching to lonapegsomatropin, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Once-weekly lonapegsomatropin was generally well tolerated and was associated with sustained improvements in body composition and patient-reported outcomes for up to 90 weeks. These findings extend prior evidence and support the long-term benefits of lonapegsomatropin in adults with GH deficiency, including those switching from somatropin.

articles.title: [Let's continue to differentiate VaIN 2 from VaIN 3: a study on the progression of a series of 54 cases of VaIN 2].
articles.abstract: Objective : Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasias (VaIN) are rare pre-cancerous lesions of the female genital tract caused by human papillomaviruses (HPV) (1). Their risk of progression to actual vaginal cancer is estimated between 3% and 12% (2, 5). Since the new 2020 terminology of the World Health Organization (WHO) on high-grade VaIN, gathering VaIN 2 and 3, the recommended management is the same (6). However, the progression of these histopathological entities would be very different, which is why we wanted to study the outcome of VaIN 2 cases followed in our department, depending on whether the management was active through laser destruction, Imiquimod, or surgical excision, or if close monitoring was preferred. Materials and Methods : We conducted a retrospective monocentric study between 1990 and 2024. All patients diagnosed with VaIN 2 and followed for at least 2 years were included. Results : Fifty-four patients were included, one-third of whom were initially monitored, and the average follow-up duration was 54.8 ± 26.8 months. The average age at diagnosis was 52.6 ± 15.9 years, with a history of smoking found in 40% of the patients, immunosuppression in a quarter of them, and 22% of the patients had an HPV 16 or 18 infection. A favorable outcome was found in 66.7% of the monitored cases and in 81.8% of the actively treated cases. There was no significant difference in the progression profiles with p equal to 0.14. There was also no significant difference in event-free survival with p equal to 0.10. Conclusion : Expectant management does not appear to be associated with an increased risk of unfavorable progression compared with ablative treatment. It therefore seems reasonable to propose an appropriate initial surveillance strategy. VaIN 2 lesions appear to have a predominant rate of spontaneous regression, which may call into question the relevance of grouping all high-grade VaIN lesions together.

articles.title: Febrile renal pseudotumors revealing ANCA-associated vasculitis.
Stress-Sensing Over TCR Recognition: γδ T-cell therapy for CMV infection after transplantation.
Switching from mepolizumab to benralizumab in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA).
authors: European EGPA study group (EESG) and the French Vasculitis Study Group (FVSG)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an ANCA-associated vasculitis characterized by eosinophilic asthma and ENT involvement. Both mepolizumab and benralizumab have demonstrated efficacy in EGPA and are now considered front-line options. In patients who do not respond to mepolizumab, benralizumab may be a valuable alternative owing to its enhanced depletion of eosinophils. We assessed the efficacy for and safety of switching from mepolizumab to benralizumab in EGPA.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Is benralizumab effective and safe in EGPA patients after mepolizumab failure, given its enhanced depletion of eosinophil?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective European multicenter study including 68 adult EGPA patients who received benralizumab after mepolizumab failure. Complete (CR) and partial (PR) response were defined as BVAS=0, with prednisone ≤4 mg/day and > 4 mg/day, respectively.

RESULTS: Median benralizumab follow-up period was 28 [20-39] months. CR and PR were achieved in 32% and 25% of patients, and maintained at last follow-up in 19% and 16%. Median time to CR was 6 [4-12] months. Forced expiratory volume in one second improved from 73% to 79%, and 38% of patients discontinued glucocorticoids. Vasculitis flares occurred in six patients. Primary mepolizumab failure was associated with lower CR rates (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.06-0.60). Benralizumab was discontinued in 18% due to persistent respiratory symptoms. Adverse events occurred in five patients, including two severe SARS-CoV-2 infections.

INTERPRETATION: In EGPA patients with persistent respiratory manifestations after mepolizumab failure, switching to benralizumab could represent a valuable option, improving lung function and reducing glucocorticoid use. Further prospective studies are needed to optimize sequencing and patient selection.

articles.title: Occult Infection Risk with Stem Retention in Revision Anatomic to Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In revising failed anatomic shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA) with a convertible humeral component to reverse shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA), surgeons must decide whether to retain or exchange the humeral stem. While retention is less morbid, it may risk missing occult infection in certain cases. The purpose of this study was to describe the risk of occult infection, microbiological findings, and clinical outcomes among patients undergoing conversion of aTSA to rTSA with stem retention using a convertible humeral component.

METHODS: A single institution retrospective case series of patients undergoing conversion from aTSA to rTSA between 12/1/2013 and 7/1/2025 with minimum >1 year follow up was performed. All patients had a convertible humeral stem in which the stem was retained during the procedure. Patients with a clear preoperative diagnosis of infection (pus noted intra-operatively or a sinus tract) were excluded. Variables of interest included 2025 preoperative ICM score, complications, reoperations, postoperative infections, and patient-reported outcomes (VAS, SANE, ASES).

RESULTS: A total of 65 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean preoperative ICM score was 0.43±1.17, with all patients classified in the "Unlikely" PJI risk tier (<10 points). Intraoperative cultures were identified in 14% of the cases, 89% of which were Cutibacterium acnes. Overall, 6 patients (9%) received postoperative oral or IV antibiotics. However, only 2 patients (3.1%) underwent reoperation for infection, neither of which were found to have positive intra-operative cultures at the time of their index revision. Unplanned re-operations occurred in 12 (18.5%) of the cohort. Preoperative ICM scores were not associated with reoperation for infection (p=0.5). At a mean clinical follow up of 34 months, the mean SANE and ASES scores were 60.6± 29.6 and 61.1± 27.4, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with low preoperative concern for infection, retaining a well-fixed humeral stem in revision aTSA to rTSA results in a low rate of PJI. Despite all revisions being characterized as "unlikely" based on the ICM criteria, approximately 1 in 7 patients were found to have unexpected positive intraoperative cultures. While this did not appear to affect postoperative infection rates, high vigilance for infection, even in cases with low preoperative concern, should be considered.

articles.title: Preoperative Pseudoparesis Is Not Associated With Inferior Outcomes After Anterior Latissimus Dorsi and Teres Major Transfer for Irreparable Anterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic relevance of preoperative pseudoparesis after combined anterior latissimus dorsi and teres major transfer (aLDTM) for irreparable anterosuperior rotator cuff tears (IASRCTs) has not been examined in a matched comparison. We hypothesized that, after propensity score matching, final outcomes would not differ significantly between groups.

METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study reviewed patients undergoing aLDTM for IASRCT between April 2015 and January 2024. Pseudoparesis was defined a priori as active forward elevation ≥45° and <90° with preserved passive elevation after local anesthetic injection and without neurologic deficit (n=57); active forward elevation ≥90° defined the comparator group (n=183). True pseudoparalysis (<45°) and advanced arthropathy (Hamada grade >2) were excluded. One-to-one propensity score matching on age, sex, body mass index, diabetes, hypertension, previous cuff repair, acromiohumeral distance (AHD), Hamada grade, intraoperative reparable infraspinatus tear, and fatty infiltration of the four rotator cuff muscles produced 57 pairs (all absolute standardized mean differences <0.10). Outcomes included clinical scores (VAS, ADLIR, Constant, UCLA, ASES), range of motion, strength, subscapularis-specific tests, and tendon integrity on 2-year postoperative MRI. Mean follow-up was 57.0 ± 20.0 months.

RESULTS: Both groups improved in clinical scores, forward elevation, abduction, internal rotation, and most strength measures (all adjusted P < .001); external rotation range of motion did not change significantly. Final clinical scores, range of motion, and strength showed no significant between-group differences (all adjusted P ≥ .569). The pseudoparesis group showed larger gains in forward elevation (69° ± 26° vs 35° ± 28°, adjusted P < .001) and abduction (48° ± 29° vs 29° ± 27°, adjusted P = .007). Subscapularis-specific tests and AHD did not differ between groups. Retear on 2-year postoperative MRI occurred in 3/57 (5.3%) and 4/57 (7.0%) (adjusted P = 1.000).

CONCLUSION: In this propensity score-matched analysis, the pseudoparesis group had lower baseline elevation by definition, whereas final clinical, range-of-motion, strength, and structural outcomes did not differ between groups after aLDTM for IASRCT. These findings should not be extrapolated to true pseudoparalysis or advanced arthropathy.

articles.title: Beyond blood pressure: AI-assisted multi-omics biomarker stratification for stroke risk in hypertension: clinical chemistry, analytical validation, and translational perspectives.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a major contributor to stroke burden; however, conventional blood pressure measurements do not fully capture the heterogeneous biological processes underlying cerebrovascular risk. Residual risk may persist despite apparently controlled blood pressure due to vascular, inflammatory, metabolic, cardiac, renal, and neurovascular abnormalities.

OBJECTIVE: This review summarizes emerging multi-omics biomarker strategies for biological stratification of stroke risk in hypertension, emphasizing mechanistic interpretation, analytical validation, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted integration, and clinical translation.

METHODS: Relevant literature on genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, lipidomic, extracellular vesicle biomarkers, clinical chemistry approaches, and AI-assisted integration was reviewed. Evidence was synthesized according to biological relevance, analytical readiness, validation status, and translational potential.

KEY FINDINGS: Multi-omics approaches provide complementary information regarding vascular remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, oxidative stress, thrombosis, metabolism, and target-organ injury. However, biological associations do not necessarily establish predictive validity, and predictive performance alone does not demonstrate clinical utility. Translation requires analytical validation, standardized workflows, external validation, and evidence of improved clinical decision-making.

LIMITATIONS: Most proposed biomarkers remain in exploratory or early translational stages, with limitations including analytical variability, limited external validation, and insufficient prospective clinical utility studies.

CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omics biomarkers offer a promising framework for understanding biological heterogeneity in hypertensive stroke risk. Future studies should prioritize standardized measurement, prospective validation, and demonstration of clinical utility before routine implementation.

articles.title: Ocular Metastasis: Clinical Course and Survival Analysis of 569 Patients (727 Eyes) Over a 40-Year Interval (1979-2018).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report the clinical course of a large series of patients with intraocular and epibulbar metastases to the eye encountered over a 40-year interval and determine whether recent systemic treatments have improved patient survival following detection compared to earlier cases.

DESIGN: Retrospective case series and trend study.

SUBJECTS: 727 eyes of 569 patients diagnosed with metastasis to the eye(s).

METHODS: Retrospective chart review and statistical analysis with SPSS (including descriptive statistics, cross-tabulations, statistical comparison of distributions, actuarial event rate curves using both Kaplan-Meier and life table methods, and comparison of survival curves using the log rank test).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Sex and age of patients, source cancer and metastatic history, symptoms, laterality and focality of eye metastases, ocular sites of involvement, largest basal diameter and thickness of metastases, ocular biopsies, systemic and ophthalmic treatment, symptomatic and tumor response to treatment, cause of death, and median, 5-year, 10-year, and comparative overall survival among various categorical subgroups.

RESULTS: We identified dates of death for 98.1% of 569 patients. The median overall survival was 8.2 months, the 5-year overall survival was 8.2%, and the 10-year overall survival was 2.8%. Patients encountered in the second half of the study interval did not have significantly better survival compared to those in the first half. Breast cancer was the most common primary cancer. Lung cancer follows as the second most common primary, with affected patients having far worse survival outcomes. Treatment was administered in 435 worse or only affected eyes, and of the 313 of those for which we have follow-up visual acuity data, visual acuity improved or remained stable in 62.6%. Of the 286 of those for which we have a follow-up fundus examination, 85.7% demonstrated initial complete or partial regression. One hundred fifty-seven of 569 total patients (27.6%) ultimately had bilateral ocular involvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Survival for patients with cancer metastatic to the eye, which remains extremely poor, did not improve significantly from 1979 to 2018. Breast and lung cancer remain the predominant primary cancers and are followed by gastrointestinal, hematologic, and genitourinary cancers. Based on available but incomplete data, treatment improves or maintains vision and shrinks metastases in most patients.

articles.title: Impact of Prior Antithrombotic Therapy on Safety and Outcomes of Endovascular Therapy in Large-Core Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Evidence on whether prior antithrombotic drug (ATD) use affects outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT) is limited in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) within 48 hours, symptomatic ICH, 90-day mortality, ordinal mRS shift, and ≥8-point improvement in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score at 48 hours. Logistic regression models were used to assess treatment effects and interactions between ATD and EVT.

RESULTS: A total of 202 patients were included (ATD, n=70; no ATD, n=132). There was no significant interaction between use of ATD and the effect of EVT in terms of the primary outcome (pinteraction=0.944) or secondary outcomes (pinteraction=0.218-0.752). In the EVT cohort, prior ATD use was not associated with the primary outcome (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.41-3.23). Results were consistent for antiplatelet drugs (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.18-2.71) and anticoagulants (adjusted OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.45-5.20).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory subanalysis, prior ATD use did not significantly modify the observed treatment effect of EVT in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that prior ATD use alone should not preclude consideration of EVT.

articles.title: Achieving an Endovascular Therapy Door-to-Device Time Under 90 Minutes in Patients with Ischemic Stroke Associates with 90-day mRS.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The American Heart Association (AHA) has a current goal of performing 50% of endovascular therapy (EVT) procedures with a door-to-device (DTD) time of 90 minutes or less for direct arriving patients. Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke. The likelihood of a favorable patient outcome was quantified for patients with a DTD time ≤90 minutes compared to patients with a DTD time >90 minutes.

RESULTS: DTD ≤90 minutes was associated with an increased odds of having a more favorable (0-2) modified Rankin Score at 90-days (AOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-2.00; P = .004) post stroke compared to DTD >90 minutes. We did not find that DTD under or over 90 minutes had a significant association with discharge home (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.00-1.46; P = .051) or patients' length of stay (β, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.30-0.34; P = .20).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports that EVT completed with DTD time ≤90 minutes was associated with better functional outcomes for patients.

articles.title: Effects of complementary therapies on physiological and psychological outcomes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is the cornerstone intervention for improving respiratory function and symptoms in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, evidence on the effects of complementary therapies (CTs), such as yoga, tai chi/qigong, music therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), relaxation techniques, and water-based exercise, remains limited.

METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving patients with COPD were systematically searched in Embase, Scopus, PubMed, and MEDLINE (Ovid). Study selection followed PRISMA guidelines. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs) using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Thirty-six RCTs involving 3,148 participants were included. Compared with usual care, effects on exercise capacity varied across different CTs, with improvements observed primarily in exercise-based approaches (6-minute walk distance [6MWD]; MD = 58.73 m), pulmonary function (FEV1% predicted; MD = 4.65), dyspnea (modified Borg scale; MD = -0.79; CRQ dyspnea; MD = 1.03), symptom burden (COPD Assessment Test; MD = -3.36), and health-related quality of life (SGRQ total score; MD = -8.40). Anxiety and depression (HADS-A and HADS-D) were also reduced (MD = -1.70 and -1.02, respectively). Compared with PR, CTs showed greater improvements in 6MWD (MD = 8.17) and HADS-D (MD = -0.74).

CONCLUSION: Complementary therapies may improve both physiological and psychological outcomes in patients with COPD and may serve as adjunctive strategies to conventional pulmonary rehabilitation. Further research is needed to identify optimal modalities and patient-specific responses.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Predicts Successful Weaning and ICU discharge alive Following Prone Positioning Ventilation in Moderate-to-Severe Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) Secondary to Pneumonia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We developed and validated interpretable machine learning models predicting successful weaning and survival to ICU discharge in patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia receiving prone position ventilation (PPV).

METHODS: We included 131 patients with moderate-to-severe ARDS secondary to pneumonia undergoing PPV for internal, temporal, and external validation. Models were developed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).

RESULTS: The support vector machine (SVM) model had the highest internal AUC (0.715 weaning; 0.807 ICU discharge). The weaning model was stable in temporal (AUC 0.841) and external (AUC 0.707) validation. The ICU discharge model had limited temporal/external stability (AUCs 0.657, 0.665) and was preliminary. Calibration was good for weaning and acceptable for ICU discharge. DCA suggested potential utility across broad thresholds. SHAP identified key predictors for weaning (septic shock, platelet count, PaO2/FiO2 ratio at PPV, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and peak airway pressure at PPV) and ICU discharge (APACHE II, peak airway pressure at PPV, multidrug-resistant organism infection, and NLR).

CONCLUSIONS: The weaning SVM model showed promising but exploratory performance and may serve as an adjunct for individualized risk stratification during the conventional ventilation/PPV phase, complementing rather than replacing clinical judgement. The ICU discharge model was less stable and should be interpreted cautiously. SHAP improved transparency and generated hypotheses, not causal evidence. Further multi-center prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Barriers to early rehabilitation and mobilization in adult ICUs: A multicenter survey in the Eastern region of Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prolonged Intensive Care Unit (ICU) immobilization leads to complications such as ICU Acquired Weakness (ICU-AW). While Early Rehabilitation and Mobilization (ERM) is proven to improve functional independence and reduce mechanical ventilation (MV) duration, its implementation remains inconsistent. This study aimed to identify barriers to ERM as perceived by adult ICU healthcare practitioners in the Eastern region of Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: A multicenter, cross-sectional survey using a 21-question adapted self-administered questionnaire was conducted between January and April 2023 through QuestionPro platform. The survey was distributed to critical care practitioners including physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists, physiotherapists, and other allied health staff. Respondents represented three hospital categories in the Eastern region: private, Eastern Health Cluster, and other governmental sector hospitals. Barriers were assessed a priori at three levels: patient, provider, and institutional. Internal consistency of the patient-level barrier scale was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Chi-square and Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests compared ERM protocol availability between hospital sectors and knowledge, practice, and resource variables across professional groups.

RESULTS: Of 137 practitioners who accessed the survey, 121of 137 who accessed the link completed the questionnaire (88%completion rate). Although 66 (55%) rated ERM as very important, only 48 (40%) reported always participating in or observing it in practice. The most frequently endorsed ideal initiation time was within 24 hours of admission (38, 31%), whereas the most commonly reported actual initiation point was when patients were conscious and able to cooperate (28, 23%); only 10 (8%) reported initiation within 24 hours. Patient-level barriers were mainly sedation and physiological instability. Provider-level barriers included safety concerns, limited staffing, and inadequate training. At the institutional level, only 57 (47%) respondents reported the presence of a formal ERM protocol, with a significant difference between private hospitals (36/54, 67%) and government hospitals (21/67, 31%) (χ2 = 13.59 df = 1, p < 0.001; OR 4.38, 95% CI 2.04-9.42). Protocol availability, ERM participation, and physiotherapy access also differed significantly across professional groups, with respiratory therapists consistently reporting the lowest access p = 0.013; p < 0.001; p = 0.038; p < 0.001.

CONCLUSION: Despite high awareness of its benefits, ERM implementation across adult ICUs in the Eastern region remains suboptimal relative to the 72-hour initiation window recommended by current consensus guidance and is delivered reactively rather than proactively. Barriers operate at patient, provider, and institutional levels, and both formal ERM protocol availability and profession-based access to ERM structures differ significantly, with respiratory therapists the most excluded despite managing the highest-risk patients. These findings identify protocol availability and interdisciplinary delivery structures as the principal targets for regional implementation efforts.

articles.title: Post thrombotic syndrome after thrombotic venous thoracic outlet syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombotic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (T-vTOS) including Paget-Schrotter syndrom is a rare form of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) that mainly affects young, active individuals. Its optimal management remains debated and medium-term outcomes are poorly documented.

METHODS: Consecutive patients from the vascular medicine department of a university hospital with T-vTOS between 2014 and 2024 were included in a retrospective study. Patients were stratified according to the presence of post-thrombotic syndrome with the modified Villalta score at last follow-up (<5 vs ≥5). Clinical characteristics, therapeutic strategies and outcomes were systematically assessed through a standardized consultation performed by the same physician. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses, using Firth's penalized-likelihood method to account for the limited number of events, were performed to identify factors associated with post-thrombotic syndrome.

RESULTS: Fifty patients were included: 28 with a Villalta score <5 and 22 with a Villalta score ≥5 at last follow-up. Patients with Villalta <5 achieved higher rates of complete subclavian vein recanalization at follow-up (63% vs 32%, p=0.045) and were less likely to have persistent subclavian vein occlusion (26% vs 59%, p=0.023). Villalta ≥ 5 patients more often required prolonged anticoagulation (73% vs 29%, p=0.004) and more frequently underwent acute-phase endovascular treatment (36% vs 4%, p=0.007). In multivariable analysis endovascular treatment alone without thoracic outlet surgery was associated with PTS (OR 10.6, 95% CI 1.15; 98.09) (p=0.037), whereas there was no association between PTS and patients who had undergone both endovascular treatment and TOS surgery: OR 1.3 (95% CI 0.26; 6.87) (p=0.736).

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the central role of venous patency in the clinical course of T-vTOS, with persistent subclavian vein occlusion associated with post-thrombotic syndrome. The association observed between acute-phase endovascular treatment alone and post-thrombotic syndrome does not support a clear benefit of this strategy. However, endovascular therapy in conjunction with surgical decompression of the thoracic outlet may reduce the risk of post-thrombotic syndrome.

articles.title: A Comparison of Aspiration Thrombectomy to Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Management of Paget-Schroetter Syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet (Paget Schroetter Syndrome-PSS) may involve prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein by catheter directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS.

METHODS: Consecutive PSS cases at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded by degree of luminal encroachment, and vessel irregularity: mild (less than 10%), moderate (10-50%) and severe (50-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency at last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. 54 met inclusion criteria: 28 CDT and 26 ASP. 1 week following procedure, re-thrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) CDT and 6 (23.1%) ASP (p<0.5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8%) ASP case. Composite of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Prior to PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) CDT and 8 (30.8%) ASP (p<0.05). PTC mild in 13 (46.4%) CDT and 5 (19.2%) ASP (p<0.05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) CDT and 5 (19.2%) ASP, severe in 9 (32.1%) CDT and 8 (30.8) ASP. At early follow up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) CDT and 4 (23.5) ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) CDT and 1 (5.9%) ASP, severe in 9(39.1%) CDT and 6 (35.3%) ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) CDT and 6 (35%) ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency of 22 (95%) CDT and 15 (88%) ASP.

CONCLUSION: ASP and CDT may both be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS, however, they differ on early efficacy, PTC, and patency. While often more rapid and convenient, our results suggest ASP may be inferior to CAT in management of PSS.

articles.title: Dairy producers' perceptions of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 and their influence on implementation of biosecurity changes.
articles.abstract: The emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 in dairy cattle has presented a major challenge for dairy producers in the USA, who have had to make biosecurity decisions with limited information while balancing evolving guidance, existing beliefs, and farm management constraints. This study aimed to 1) describe dairy producers' perceptions and understanding of HPAI; 2) characterize experiences and perceived impacts among producers affected by HPAI; 3) identify farm characteristics associated with implementation of biosecurity changes in response to HPAI risk; and 4) assess whether perceived biosecurity effectiveness was associated with implementation of biosecurity changes and whether concern about HPAI and perceived farm-level risk helped explain this relationship. A questionnaire mailed to Michigan dairy facilities yielded a 15.6% response rate (n = 120/766). Descriptive statistics, modified Poisson regression, logistic regression, and parallel mediation analysis using parametric g-computation were used to evaluate survey responses and associations with implementation of biosecurity changes. Overall, 18 respondents (15%) reported confirmed or suspected HPAI on their farms. Most respondents reported being moderately to very familiar with HPAI (76%) and receiving sufficient guidance about the disease (83%). The most frequently selected information sources were veterinary professionals (72%), government health agencies (52%), and industry associations (48%). Producers most frequently identified wildlife (74%) as a likely route of HPAI introduction, followed by airborne transmission (34%), cattle movement (23%), and sharing workers with other operations (12%). Among affected farms, the reported clinical phase lasted with a median of 21 d, whereas reduced productivity lasted with a median of 40 d. Median self-estimated economic loss was $152 per lactating cow. Among farms without reported confirmed or suspected HPAI, farms with ≥ 15 employees were more likely to report implementing biosecurity changes than farms with < 5 employees (RR = 2.26; 95% CI: 1.24-4.10), and farms using robotic milking systems were more likely to report changes than farms using parlor or rotary systems (RR = 2.07; 95% CI: 1.21-3.55). From a mediation analysis (n = 93), the estimated probability of implementing biosecurity changes was 45.7% among producers who perceived biosecurity as effective, compared with 21.4% among those who did not, corresponding to a 24.3 percentage-point difference (95% CI: 5.4-42.4). On the odds-ratio scale, perceived biosecurity effectiveness was associated with higher odds of implementing biosecurity changes (OR = 3.17; 95% CI: 1.21-8.26), higher concern about HPAI (OR = 4.26; 95% CI: 1.58-11.51), and greater odds of perceiving the farm as lower risk than other farms in the state (OR = 2.56; 95% CI: 1.05-6.25). The indirect effect through concern about HPAI was 9.4 percentage points, accounting for approximately 39% of the total association, whereas the indirect effect through perceived farm-level risk was small and not clearly different from zero. Overall, these findings suggest that implementation of biosecurity changes may be supported by trusted communication strategies that emphasize the effectiveness of specific biosecurity practices and present the disease as a relevant but still manageable farm-level threat, and better align producers' perceptions with evidence-supported transmission pathways, particularly modifiable routes such as animal movement, personnel movement, and shared equipment.

articles.title: A randomized controlled study evaluating milking performance and udder health on a New York dairy farm using a novel stimulating, cleaning, and drying device for teat preparation.
articles.abstract: Development of automated ways to prepare udders before harvesting milk has allowed for more consistent application of procedures like disinfecting, stimulating, and drying, therefore replacing manual techniques. Holsteins (n = 326) at one NY dairy were enrolled in a randomized, controlled clinical trial to determine the effect of a device that uses a vortex of water, air, and disinfectant to clean and dry teats on milk yield, milk flow rates, teat end cleanliness, odds of bimodal milk flow, and udder health indices. Cows were randomized into one of 2 treatment groups and measurements were collected in a double 24 parallel parlor over 7-wk. Udder preparation for the VORTEX group consisted of using a trigger-activated vortex of water, chemical, and pressurized air to disinfect, clean, and dry teats before attachment of the milking unit. Udder preparation for the control group (TRAD) included application of disinfectant using a foamer cup, manual stripping, and a cloth towel cleaning and drying step before attachment of the milking unit. Compliance to routines, which targeted 12 s of stimulation, 120 s of preparation-lag time, and the same target disinfectant concentration for both groups, was evaluated weekly. Digital milk meters were used to determine session milk yield, duration of milking, and average and maximum milk flow rates, while bi-monthly DHIA testing captured milk yields and linear score (LS) measurements. Vacuum measurement devices were used to determine the incidence of bimodality. Percentage of dirty teat ends was evaluated using gauze impressions. Generalized mixed regression models were used to describe the effect of treatment on the outcome variables. Least squares means (95% CI) were not meaningfully different for cows that were prepared with the vortex device versus the traditional routine, respectively, for: milk yield per session [15.43 (15.10-15.76) and 15.05 (14.71-15.39) kg], test day milk yield [45.8 (45.0-46.6) and 45.3 (44.5-46.2) kg], duration [4.96 (4.80-5.13) and 4.83 (4.66-5.00) min], average flow rate [3.16 (3.14-3.19) and 3.18 (3.16-3.21) kg/min], and maximal flow rate [4.35 (4.26-4.43) and 4.24 (4.16-4.32) kg/min]. The odds of bimodal milk flow were higher for cows that were prepared using the vortex device (odds ratio = 2.4; 95% CI = 1.3 - 4.7). There was an interaction between treatment and test day for LS. Linear scores for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd post enrollment test days [LSM (95% CI)] were 1.95 (1.69-2.21), 1.82 (1.54-2.11), and 2.51 (2.18-2.84) for the VORTEX cows and 1.25 (0.99-1.85), 1.54 (1.23-1.85), and 1.38 (1.00-1.76) for the TRAD cows, respectively. There was a higher odds of dirty teat ends in the VORTEX group (odds ratio = 1.23; 95% CI = 1.00-1.51). The odds of a subclinical infection, defined as a baseline LS graduating from <4 to ≥4, favored the TRAD group (odds ratio = 3.98; 95% CI = 1.64-9.71). Although use of the vortex device did not affect milk production, milking duration, or flow rates, replacing the traditional strip-and-wipe procedures may influence bimodality and udder health, likely due to differences in teat stimulation quality and less precise cleaning, respectively.

articles.title: Structure-activity relationships of BnOCPA derivatives at native pre- and postsynaptic adenosine A1Rs.
articles.abstract: The addition of a benzyloxy group to the adenosine A1R agonist cyclopentyladenosine (CPA) produces a compound (BnOCPA) that selectivity activates A1R signalling via the G protein alpha subunit Gob. In rat hippocampus, BnOCPA inhibits CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission (IC50 65 nM) likely via Gob, with no effect on Goa-mediated postsynaptic membrane electrophysiology at concentrations up to 1 μM. We have investigated how modifications of the benzyloxy group of BnOCPA affects signalling: addition of methoxy group, MBnOCPA, substituting a phenoxy group, PhOCPA; and addition of bromide to the phenoxy group, BPhOCPA. These derivatives, previously shown to be selective A1R agonists, were assessed through inhibition of hippocampal CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission and postsynaptic effects on CA1 pyramidal neurons. All compounds inhibited synaptic transmission and increased paired-pulse facilitation, indicative of presynaptic actions. At a concentration that inhibited synaptic transmission (>75 %), none of the compounds hyperpolarised the resting membrane potential and thus retained the pre- vs postsynaptic selectivity of BnOCPA. Increasing their concentration allowed a measure of the selectivity range. BnOCPA hyperpolarised ∼ 40 % of neurons at 3 μM (∼ 50x the IC50 for synaptic inhibition). For PhOCPA and MBnOCPA, hyperpolarisation, occurred for some neurons, at 1 μM. For BPhOCPA, no hyperpolarisation occurred at concentrations up to 10 μM. Pre-application of the derivatives (at 300 nM) reduced adenosine-mediated hyperpolarisation, showing they bind but do not activate postsynaptic A1Rs. This data shows that modifying the structure of BnOCPA changes the discrimination between different native A1Rs, likely based upon selective activation of G-protein coupling.

articles.title: External validation of a clinical prediction score for melioidosis among patients with community-acquired pneumonia: a substudy of the prospective multicentre MISSION cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary melioidosis may be clinically indistinguishable from other causes of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), delaying appropriate microbiological investigation and antimicrobial therapy. A four-variable clinical prediction score incorporating monsoon-season presentation, diabetes mellitus, shock at presentation, and extrapulmonary focal abscesses was previously developed to identify melioidosis among patients with CAP. We aimed to externally validate this score in a prospective multicentre cohort and explore whether its performance could be improved by adding readily available predictors.

METHODS: This was a nested substudy of the prospective, multicentre, hospital-based MISSION study conducted across 15 tertiary-care centres in India between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025. Hospitalised adults with diabetes mellitus or chronic kidney disease who met predefined CAP criteria were eligible. Participants were excluded if one or more score variables could not be reliably ascertained at presentation, defined as clinical information available before microbiological confirmation. The original score was applied without refitting. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and sensitivity and specificity were calculated at prespecified cut-offs. An exploratory modified score was developed using independent predictors identified through multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 1,418 participants in the parent cohort who met the predefined CAP syndrome definition, 78 were excluded because one or more score variables could not be reliably ascertained at presentation. The final validation cohort included 1,340 participants, of whom 87 (6.5%) had culture-confirmed melioidosis CAP. The original score demonstrated moderate discrimination, with an AUC of 0.718 (95% CI 0.654-0.781). At a cut-off of ≥4, sensitivity was 72.4%, and specificity was 56.4%; at ≥5, sensitivity was 48.3%, and specificity was 86.4%. Extrapulmonary focal abscesses (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 20.56, 95% CI 10.82-39.05), diabetes mellitus (aOR 2.94, 95% CI 1.36-6.37), male sex (aOR 2.39, 95% CI 1.32-4.33), high-risk occupation (aOR 2.37, 95% CI 1.43-3.93), and shock at presentation (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.31-4.05) were independently associated with melioidosis CAP. An exploratory modified score incorporating these variables had an apparent AUC of 0.770 (95% CI 0.711 to 0.828). At a cut-off of ≥3, sensitivity was 63.2% and specificity was 81.4%.

CONCLUSIONS: The original four-variable score demonstrated moderate discrimination when externally validated among high-risk hospitalised adults with CAP. A cut-off of ≥4 may support screening, whereas ≥5 provides greater specificity but misses more than half of melioidosis cases. The exploratory modified score showed modestly higher apparent discrimination, and requires independent external validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Design and Rationale of the CLASP II TR Randomized Trial for Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
articles.abstract: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a progressive disease associated with mortality, heart failure hospitalization (HFH), impaired functional status, and reduced quality of life. Transcatheter tricuspid valve repair and replacement therapies have expanded treatment options for TR patients beyond medical therapy and surgery and improved their functional status and symptoms. The CLASP II TR trial is a prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized trial designed to test superiority of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) with the PASCAL transcatheter valve repair system+optimal medical therapy (device group) versus optimal medical therapy alone (control group) in symptomatic severe TR patients. A total of 450 patients with ≥severe TR as assessed by an independent echocardiographic core laboratory are randomized following central screening committee assessment in a 2:1 ratio (device:control). The primary endpoint is a 6-month hierarchical composite combining key safety and efficacy outcomes (all-cause mortality, durable right ventricular assist device or heart transplant, elective or non-elective tricuspid valve surgery/intervention and number of HFH) with quality-of-life improvement assessed using Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score. Additionally, clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and quality-of-life parameters are also evaluated. Patients are assessed at baseline; 30 days; 3, 6, and 12 months; and annually through 5 years. Crossover of control patients is permitted either after the 2-year visit or when the last randomized patient completes 12-month follow-up. The CLASP II TR trial will inform the safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL system compared to medical therapy alone in the treatment of patients with symptomatic, severe tricuspid regurgitation. The trial has completed enrollment, and the report of primary results is expected. Trial Registration: Edwards PASCAL Transcatheter Valve Repair System Pivotal Clinical Trial (CLASP II TR); NCT04097145; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04097145.

articles.title: Sex-specific association between preoperative foot infection and vein graft stenosis after distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sex differences in lower-extremity bypass outcomes remain controversial, and the mechanism is unclear.
