We examined whether female sex is associated with vein graft stenosis, predominantly due to intimal hyperplasia, after distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and whether preoperative foot infection contributes.

METHODS: We studied 318 limbs with chronic limb-threatening ischemia undergoing para- or inframalleolar autogenous vein bypass at a single center (2000-2014; 74 women, 23%). All analyses were restricted to single-vein grafts; after excluding grafts occluding within 30 days, 232 formed the analytic cohort (182 men, 50 women). Female versus male outcomes were compared by 1:1 optimal matching (Mahalanobis distance within a propensity-score caliper on six covariates) and by inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, which was the primary inference; death was treated as a competing risk. Stenosis was diagnosed by duplex surveillance, with histologic examination of excised segments. Wound, ischemia, and foot infection grades and preoperative C-reactive protein and fibrinogen were analyzed by sex with sex-by-exposure interaction terms; wound cultures were reviewed.

RESULTS: After matching (48 pairs), the 5-year cumulative incidence of vein graft stenosis remained higher in women (44% vs 9%; log-rank P=.004), and primary patency was lower (52% vs 88%; P=.003); secondary patency (85% vs 98%; P=.06) and limb salvage (P=.60) did not differ significantly. Weighting confirmed the excess (adjusted hazard ratio 2.13; 95% confidence interval 1.13-4.02; P=.019). Five-year mortality was 55% in men vs 35% in women; with death as a competing risk, stenosis incidence remained higher in women (34% vs 16%). Preoperative high-grade foot infection was associated with stenosis in women (hazard ratio 4.27; 95% confidence interval 1.56-11.70; P=.005) but not men (hazard ratio 0.87; P=.74), with a significant sex-by-infection interaction (P=.026); wound and ischemia grades showed no sex difference. C-reactive protein and fibrinogen showed the same direction without a significant interaction. All 25 excised stenotic segments showed intimal hyperplasia without active inflammation, and organism type was unrelated to stenosis. In women, foot infection, poor vein quality, and run-off resistance were independent correlates.

CONCLUSIONS: Women undergoing single-vein distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia have a higher incidence of vein graft stenosis despite balanced baseline risk, with the excess concentrated in those with preoperative foot infection. The findings suggest a sex-specific vein-wall response to infection-related inflammation and support intensified, infection-aware graft surveillance in women.

articles.title: Multicenter Outcomes of Peripheral Vascular Interventions in Patients with Active Cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cancer is typically associated with venous thrombosis, but its impact on patients undergoing peripheral vascular interventions (PVI) for concomitant peripheral arterial disease (PAD) remains unclear. This multicenter study examines the characteristics of patients with active cancer and their outcomes after PVI.

METHODS: Institutional vascular quality initiative (VQI) PVI data from 3 tertiary care centers (2019-2023) were combined and expanded through a retrospective chart review to include the presence and types of cancer. All adult patients undergoing endovascular intervention for PAD, including those with claudication, chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and acute limb ischemia (ALI), were included. The primary outcome was the composite of major amputation or mortality at 4 years in patients with cancer compared to those without. Additional long-term outcomes included reintervention, mortality, and major amputation at both 1 and 4 years. Secondary outcomes included perioperative outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 3,072 patients were included. The incidence of active cancer was 2.2% (N=68). Lung cancer was the most common, affecting 30.9% (N=21) of patients. 53% (N=36) presented with advanced stages (3/4) irrespective of cancer type. Patients with cancer were less likely to have diabetes. There was no significant difference in indication, but patients with cancer were more likely to get treated for aortoiliac disease and undergo stenting. Patients with cancer had a higher incidence of distal embolization (4.4% vs 0.6%, P=0.012) and perioperative major amputation (4.4% vs 1.3%, P=0.046). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly higher mortality or amputation in patients with cancer up to 4 years (63% vs 35.1%, P<0.001). Late outcomes in patients with cancer were driven by significantly higher mortality (52.2% vs. 28.3%, p<.001) rather than adverse limb events (amputation: 14.7% vs. 11.4%, p=.50; reintervention:47.8% vs. 48.3%, p=.80). Regression analysis demonstrated independent association of cancer with the composite outcome of mortality or major amputation (aHR=2.24 [1.61-3.10]).

CONCLUSION: Active cancer affects a small proportion of patients undergoing PVI but has a significant impact on perioperative limb outcomes and long-term survival. This multicenter collaboration, combining registry data and EMR review, can shed light on less common risk factors affecting lower extremity revascularization.

articles.title: Outcomes among Patients with Single-Vessel Tibial Runoff Undergoing Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia, and the Role of Peroneal Communicating Branch Quality.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population.

METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, PT). Primary outcomes were wound healing, major amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and amputation/death, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. A subset analysis stratified single-vessel peroneal runoff patients into a three-tiered, Peroneal Communicating Branch (PCB) Grade: Both branches present with at least one robust (PCB Grade 1), a single robust branch (PCB Grade 2), or no robust branch (PCB Grade 3), and compared each to the single-vessel AT/PT reference group.

RESULTS: Overall, 732 patients had single-vessel below-knee runoff: 225 AT, 315 peroneal, and 192 PT. Groups differed significantly in age, sex, and diabetes prevalence. Unadjusted two-year major amputation rates were significantly higher in the peroneal group (19% vs. 9.4% [AT] vs. 8.7% [PT]; P<.001), as were MALE rates (30% vs. 14% vs. 26%; P=.01). After adjustment, peroneal runoff was independently associated with higher risk of major amputation (HR 1.81 [1.04-3.13]) and MALE (HR 1.52 [1.03-2.25]) compared with AT/PT runoff. These associations persisted in the endovascular cohort (major amputation: HR 2.09 [1.06-4.13]; MALE: HR 1.59 [1.08-2.35]) but did not reach significance in the bypass cohort, which was limited by low event rates. When patients with single-vessel peroneal runoff were stratified by PCB Grades, unadjusted one-year major amputation rates followed a clear anatomically-driven pattern (6.9% (AT/PT) vs. 5.4% (PCB Grade 1) vs. 15% (PCB Grade 2) vs. 32% (PCB Grade 3); P<.001). After adjustment, when compared to AT/PT runoff, patients without any robust branch (PCB Grade 3) had significantly higher risk of major amputation (HR 3.21 [1.76-4.84]) and MALE (HR 2.41 [1.53-3.79]), while those with two branches with at least one being robust (PCB Grade 1) demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (HR 1.69 [1.09-2.62]) and no difference in major amputation or MALE.

CONCLUSIONS: Peroneal runoff is independently associated with worse limb outcomes following revascularization for CLTI, but this risk may be primarily driven by patients with absent or diminutive communicating branches. Those with robust branching demonstrate outcomes comparable to AT/PT runoff, underscoring the importance of further evaluation and pre-operative assessment of peroneal communicating branch quality - using the proposed PCB Grading system - in revascularization planning.

articles.title: Bleeding and Hemostasis Optimization in Primary and Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Structured Expert-Opinion Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disruptive bleeding following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) continues to affect postoperative recovery despite advances in perioperative blood management, with wound drainage and dressing-related findings common clinical concerns. Conventional definitions based on estimated blood loss or hemoglobin decline may not capture bleeding events that alter clinical management. This study sought to establish agreement on disruptive bleeding in TKA and identify clinically relevant factors guiding monitoring, escalation, and hemostatic decision-making.

METHODS: A survey-based study was conducted among 14 fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons who had experience in primary and revision TKA. Domains included risk factors, definitions of disruptive bleeding, intraoperative bleeding patterns, postoperative drainage assessment, escalation criteria, and the use of topical hemostatic agents. Responses included Likert-scale ratings, categorical selections, and free-text data. High agreement for items was defined a priori as ≥ 70% agreement.

RESULTS: Respondents supported defining disruptive bleeding as a composite of clinically meaningful outcomes rather than isolated quantitative measures. There was unanimous agreement to include operational indicators (symptomatic hemoglobin decline greater than three g/dL and persistent wound drainage) and downstream events (transfusion, reoperation, embolization, and readmission). Thrombocytopenia and anticoagulant use were important risk factors (n = 14 of 14), followed by coagulopathy and liver disease (n = 12 of 14). Escalation triggers included suspected arterial bleeding (n = 14 of 14), expanding hematoma (n = 13 of 14), hemodynamic instability (n = 13 of 14), neurovascular compromise (n = 13 of 14), and drainage beyond postoperative day five (n = 12 of 14). Routine prophylactic use of topical hemostatic agents was not supported in primary TKA (n = 2 of 14), but was selectively favored in revision cases (n = 7 of 14). Variability remained regarding drainage thresholds and timing of intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Disruptive bleeding in TKA was viewed as a composite construct defined by events that alter care rather than isolated numeric blood-loss measures. These findings represent an exploratory, hypothesis-generating framework requiring multidisciplinary and data-driven validation.

articles.title: Novel phorbol-12-O-octoate derivatives exert a dual effect by inhibiting de novo HIV-1 infection and reactivating latent virus.
articles.abstract: Viral reservoirs represent the primary obstacle to achieving a cure for HIV-1 infection, as viral replication rebounds after interruption of antiretroviral therapy (ART). To identify promising dual-effect phorbol-12-O-octoate derivatives capable of both effectively inhibiting viral replication in acute HIV-1 infection and reactivating latent HIV-1, we designed, synthesized, and evaluated a new series of phorbol esters and explored their underlying mechanisms. HPB-5073 was identified as a promising candidate that inhibits HIV-1 replication at nanomolar concentrations. Further analysis revealed that HPB-5073 reduces the expression of the HIV-1 entry receptor CD4 and co-receptor CXCR4 and impairs the formation of the early reverse transcription intermediate, -ssDNA, indicating that it targets early steps of the HIV-1 life cycle, including viral entry and early post-entry replication. Meanwhile, HPB-5073 effectively reversed HIV-1 latency in both latently infected cell lines and PBMCs from people living with HIV-1 (PLWH) on ART, with minimal cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, HPB-5073 induced the initiation and elongation of HIV-1 LTR transactivation, thereby reactivating latent HIV-1 transcription by modulating the interaction of EGR1 and Tat with the HIV-1 LTR.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes for pre-existing diabetes before and during the pandemic: A population-based study in Ontario, Canada.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC

articles.title: Pulsed administration of inhaled nitric oxide: Development, clinical applications, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) gas continues to be a widely studied and versatile treatment given its broad spectrum of physiological effects such as pulmonary vasodilation, improvement of oxygenation, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects. The idea of administering a pulsed dose of inhaled NO (PiNO) at the beginning of inhalation was developed in the last 20 years as an alternative to continuous inhalation of NO (CiNO) through the respiratory cycle. Across multiple studies, PiNO has repeatedly demonstrated similarly efficacious pulmonary vasodilation and oxygenation improvement as CiNO administration while consistently reducing total NO exposure and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) formation. PiNO has proven to be an effective adjunctive treatment for patients with primary pulmonary hypertension among spontaneously breathing patients. In patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), PiNO reduced pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) in the short term, though further research remains necessary to demonstrate long-term benefits. Similarly, PiNO use in patients with interstitial lung disease has been associated with subjective improvements in exercise tolerance and quality of life. The effect of PiNO on PVR was also confirmed in mechanically ventilated subjects. In this setting, PiNO reduced anesthesia-associated hypoxemia and improved shunt fraction and oxygenation. Overall, the scientific body of evidence surrounding PiNO supports it as a safe, effective, and efficient alternative to CiNO delivery that can be utilized in a wide range of clinical settings. Future research may continue to expand the application of PiNO to different clinical settings.

articles.title: AgomiR-31-5p ameliorates diabetes-associated cognitive impairment by suppressing hippocampal neuroinflammation via RAGE-associated signaling.
articles.abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment is closely linked to hippocampal neuroinflammation, but effective treatments remain limited. This study investigated the protective effects of agomiR-31-5p against cognitive dysfunction and neuroinflammatory injury in db/db mice. Male db/db mice received agomiR-31-5p via tail-vein injection, followed by assessments of cognition, hippocampal microglial activation, synaptic integrity, apoptosis, and inflammatory signaling. AgomiR negative controls were included in the corresponding molecular and cellular experiments. AgomiR-31-5p improved cognitive performance compared with vehicle treatment and attenuated microglial activation, as evidenced by reduced IBA1 and CD68 immunoreactivity, partial normalization of microglial morphology, decreased iNOS expression, and increased IL-10 expression. It also restored PSD95 and SYN expression, reduced the spatial association between microglial and PSD95 signals, and ameliorated apoptosis-related alterations. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between agomiR-31-5p and RAGE. In vivo, agomiR-31-5p reduced RAGE expression, p38/ERK/NF-κB signaling activation, and hippocampal TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β levels. In high glucose-exposed primary microglia, agomiR-31-5p suppressed inflammatory activation and RAGE/NF-κB signaling. RAGE overexpression partially reversed these effects, supporting the functional involvement of RAGE-associated signaling without establishing RAGE as a direct agomiR-31-5p target. Collectively, agomiR-31-5p may alleviate diabetes-associated cognitive impairment by attenuating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation, preserving synaptic integrity, reducing apoptosis-related injury, and modulating RAGE-associated signaling.

articles.title: DLL1 promotes diabetic cataract progression by driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) via activation of the Notch signaling pathway.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
articles.abstract: Diabetic cataracts (DCs) are a major vision-threatening complication of diabetes mellitus; however, their molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The present study aimed to investigate the role of the Notch ligand δ-like ligand 1 (DLL1) in the pathogenesis of DCs. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed elevated DLL1 expression in anterior lens capsule tissues from patients with DCs compared with patients with age-related cataracts. In vitro, high-glucose treatment combined with TGF-β2 treatment induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in human lens epithelial cells (HLEB3), and this was accompanied by increased DLL1 expression. Knockdown of DLL1 significantly suppressed TGF-β2-induced cell proliferation, migration and EMT, as evidenced by restored E-cadherin levels and reduced fibronectin and vimentin levels. Furthermore, the effects of DLL1 knockdown were enhanced by pharmacological inhibition of Notch signaling using N-[N-(3,5-difluorophenacetyl)-L-alanyl]-S-phenylglycine t-butyl ester (DAPT), confirming that DLL1 exerted its effects via the Notch pathway. In a streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model, intravitreal administration of DLL1 small interfering RNA markedly attenuated lens opacity progression, improved lens histo-architecture, and downregulated the expression levels of EMT markers and Notch downstream targets (hes family bHLH transcription factor 1 and hes related family bHLH transcription factor with YRPW motif 1). Collectively, these findings demonstrated that DLL1 promoted DC progression by driving EMT via activation of the Notch signaling pathway. Therefore, targeting DLL1-mediated Notch signaling may potentially play a role in delaying or preventing DCs, although further studies are needed.

articles.title: Dysphagia, Oral Health Burden, and Stool-Detected Oral-Associated Taxa in Older Inpatients After Stroke: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Swallowing and oral intake limitations and poor oral health may accompany altered stool microbial profiles after stroke. We examined their associations with a stool-detected oral-associated taxa profile in older inpatients.

METHODS: This registry-based cross-sectional analysis included 156 inpatients aged ≥65 years. Swallowing/oral intake status and oral health were assessed using the Food Intake Level Scale (FILS) and Revised Oral Assessment Guide (ROAG). The outcome was a study-defined, standardized six-genera stool-detected oral-associated taxa score. Linear regression used HC3 robust standard errors and clinical covariates. FILS < 7 was the primary exposure; continuous FILS and ROAG were secondary exposures. Additional sensitivity analyses addressed score construction, ordinal FILS, nutritional exposure, missingness, and model diagnostics.

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 78.4 years; 55.8% were men, and 25 (16.0%) had FILS < 7. In separately adjusted models, the score was lower with FILS < 7 (β -0.99; 95% CI -1.34 to -0.63), higher per FILS point (β 0.15; 95% CI 0.10-0.20), and lower with each 1-SD increase in ROAG (β -0.32; 95% CI -0.45 to -0.18; all p < 0.001). In the joint model, ROAG was attenuated (β -0.13; 95% CI -0.30 to 0.03; p = 0.111), whereas FILS remained associated. The primary association persisted after energy/protein adjustment and diagnostic checks.

CONCLUSIONS: Poorer swallowing/oral intake status and greater oral health burden were each associated with a lower stool-detected oral-associated taxa profile in separately adjusted models. The exploratory findings do not establish independent oral-health effects, oral origin, causality, or clinical utility.

articles.title: Clinical dietitian presence is associated with a two-fold higher rate of nutritional intervention in hospitalized cancer patients: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Malnutrition is common in hospitalized patients with cancer, yet guideline-recommended nutritional care is implemented inconsistently. We compared nutritional care processes in hospitalized patients with solid tumors on wards with and without a ward-based clinical dietitian. The primary objective was to assess receipt of nutritional intervention among patients meeting a predefined clinical indication. Secondary objectives were discharge nutritional recommendations, NRS-2002 documentation quality, and GLIM-defined malnutrition identification.

METHODS: Single-center cross-sectional census study at a tertiary oncology hospital (October 2024). Of 1,382 hospitalized patients, 986 with solid tumors across 19 wards were included; hematological malignancies and sarcomas, treated almost exclusively on non-dietitian wards were excluded. The primary outcome was receipt of nutritional intervention (dietetic consultation, oral nutritional supplements, enteral or parenteral nutrition) among patients meeting an ESPEN-aligned clinical indication (NRS-2002 ≥3, GLIM-defined malnutrition, weight loss >10%, or age-adjusted low BMI). Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, tumor site and disseminated disease with cluster-robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Overall, 369 patients met the clinical indication. Patients on dietitian wards were twice as likely to receive nutritional intervention (adjusted rates 91.4% vs 45.2%; adjusted OR 17.32, 95% CI 6.42-46.72), consistently across sensitivity analyses. Discharge nutritional recommendations were also more frequent (78.7% vs 27.8%; adjusted OR 13.48, 95% CI 6.18-29.40). NRS-2002 documentation quality and GLIM-defined malnutrition identification were not independently associated with dietitian presence.

CONCLUSION: Ward-based dietitian presence was associated with a two-fold higher rate of nutritional intervention and more frequent discharge recommendations, but not with screening or diagnostic quality. The single-center, non-randomized design precludes causal inference and limits transportability; multicenter confirmation is needed.

articles.title: Comment on "Phase angle as a marker of frailty and prognosis in heart failure: Evidence from a prospective cohort study".
Tirzepatide persistence, adherence, and dose escalation in a real-world setting with high out-of-pocket costs: a Polish cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Tirzepatide is effective in clinical trials, but its real-world use where obesity pharmacotherapy is self-funded remains poorly characterized. We aimed to characterize tirzepatide persistence, adherence, and dose escalation in a high out-of-pocket-cost setting.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed nationwide electronic health records from a large Polish private healthcare provider. We included 3,030 adults with a first recorded tirzepatide prescription between November 2023 and February 2025. The primary endpoint was time to observed treatment discontinuation. Multivariable Cox regression identified persistence predictors, while adherence was assessed using proportion of days covered (PDC). Successful titration was escalation from 2.5 or 5 mg to ≥10 mg.

RESULTS: The cohort included 69.0% women; 83.3% had obesity and 20.0% had type 2 diabetes. Higher first recorded dose was associated with earlier loss of observed treatment. Compared with 2.5 mg initiators, the hazard ratio for discontinuation was 1.44 (95%CI 1.26-1.64, p<0.001) for 15 mg and 1.24 (95%CI 1.12-1.39, p<0.001) for 10 mg doses. Traditional comorbidities did not independently predict persistence (all p>0.10). Among385 patients persistent for ≥180 days, median PDC was 0.86 (IQR 0.73-0.95), with 68% classified as adherent (PDC ≥80%). Of 2,194 eligible low-dose patients, 565 (25.8%) escalated to ≥10 mg, corresponding to 18.6% of the full cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Real-world tirzepatide persistence was suboptimal and associated with recorded starting dose. Traditional clinical comorbidities had limited impact on discontinuation timing. Nonclinical factors, including affordability, tolerability, and patient expectations, may contribute to early loss of observed treatment; although these were not directly measured.

articles.title: Charge Comparison of Standalone Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization to Non-surgical Medical Management for Chronic Subdural Hematoma - A Propensity Score Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent randomized clinical trials have shown middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) reduces the need for subsequent burr hole drainage of chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), both as an adjunct to initial drainage or as a standalone procedure. We compared the 6-month total hospital charges for standalone MMAE (sMMAE) versus nonsurgical medical management in patients with cSDH.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who presented with unilateral, >1cm in size, cSDH initially managed without drainage from January 1, 2020, through July 30, 2024. Seventy-two patients were identified: 46 managed conservatively and 26 with sMMAE. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on patient age, cSDH size, and length of index hospitalization. The primary endpoint was the mean difference in total hospital charges at 6 months.

RESULTS: After PSM, 23 patients who underwent sMMAE alone were compared to 23 patients receiving nonsurgical medical management. Groups were not significantly different regarding age, Charlson comorbidity index, cSDH size, midline shift size, antiplatelet/anticoagulation, symptoms, and length of index hospitalization, though standardized mean differences remained elevated. Medically treated patients had higher mean total number of hospital days (8.0 vs. 3.0, p=0.03). sMMAE patients had higher mean total 6-month hospital charges ($125K ±34Kvs. $101K ±94K, p=0.02), primarily driven by the procedure itself. Five medically managed patients required rescue drainage, compared with none in the sMMAE group (p=0.05).

CONCLUSION: Initial treatment of cSDH with sMMAE had higher average 6-month hospital charges compared to medically managed controls. Patients treated with sMMAE had shorter hospital stays and did not require rescue drainage within 6 months.

articles.title: Endoscopic Endonasal Ligation of the Internal Carotid Artery: A Cadaveric Study and Case Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice is occasionally required in complex skull-base pathology. Endovascular techniques remain the primary strategy, but intravascular metallic devices may complicate subsequent surgery and imaging surveillance in selected patients. We evaluated the anatomical feasibility and clinical application of endoscopic endonasal ICA ligation.

METHODS: Three fresh cadaveric heads (six sides) were dissected to identify accessible distal ligation sites and define the requirements for circumferential ICA dissection and direct ligation. The technique was subsequently applied in five selected patients, whose records were retrospectively reviewed.

RESULTS: Circumferential ICA exposure and mobilization were achieved on all six sides. The lower paraclival ICA, caudal to its entry into the cavernous sinus, provided reproducible working space for ligature passage. A fibrous band extending from the middle cranial fossa dura toward the foramen lacerum was consistently identified and provisionally termed the meningo-lingual band; its division facilitated circumferential ICA mobilization. Endoscopic endonasal ICA ligation was completed in all five patients without new neurological deficit, stroke, embolic complication, or other major procedure-related adverse event.

CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic endonasal ICA ligation may provide direct vascular control in highly selected patients who already require an endonasal approach and direct management of the diseased ICA. The paraclival ICA below the cavernous sinus is a practical distal ligation target when safe circumferential dissection and secure ligation are possible. This technique should be considered complementary to contemporary endovascular strategies.

articles.title: SGLT2 inhibitor use is associated with reduced myocardial glucose uptake during oncologic FDG PET/CT.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology

articles.title: An overview of current technologies in the development of drugs and vaccines against dengue virus.
articles.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
articles.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus with four distinct serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and is endemic in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. It can cause a range of illnesses, from self-resolving dengue fever to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever or dengue shock syndrome. Dengue fever is a major public health hazard in tropical and subtropical areas. Advances in treatment and prevention have mainly focused on developing vaccines and antiviral medications. Currently, no treatment for dengue fever works for everyone. While some antiviral candidates are in clinical trials, most remain in preclinical or early research stages. Regarding vaccinations, the WHO has approved or prequalified two live-attenuated options: TAK-003 (Qdenga®) and Dengvaxia® (CYD-TDV). However, both vaccines have drawbacks, including limited effectiveness across serotypes and safety issues in seronegative individuals. Current research aims to elucidate the complex host immune responses that underlie dengue pathogenesis and vaccine-induced protection, to develop more effective treatments and preventive measures. Critically, most approaches remain at the experimental or preclinical stage and require further clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Lateralized amyloid PET uptake and beta-band connectivity in relation to cognition in temporal lobe epilepsy.
articles.abstract: We examined focus-relative amyloid PET asymmetry and its associations with resting-state EEG connectivity and processing speed in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE). Thirty adults with clinically assigned MTLE (19 right-focus, 11 left-focus) underwent 18F-florapronol PET and resting-state EEG. Regional standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and sensor-level weighted phase lag index (wPLI) were evaluated using paired comparisons, rank correlations and exploratory bootstrap indirect-association models. Cognitive data were available for 26 participants, including Digit Symbol Coding (DSC) for 25. Under the original analytical convention, mean medial temporal SUVR was 1.066 ipsilaterally and 1.013 contralaterally (difference 0.053, 95% CI [0.013, 0.093]; p = 0.011; Cohen's dz = 0.500). The contrast differed by focus side (interaction p = 0.002) and was 0.038 under source-table reconstruction (p = 0.075). Ipsilateral SUVR correlated with inter-hemispheric beta wPLI (ρ = 0.617, q = 0.034 across 240 tests). The intra-contralateral association (ρ = 0.536) did not survive this broader correction. Indirect estimates for Trail Making Test A (0.279, 95% bootstrap CI [0.043, 0.761]) and DSC (0.151, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.114, 0.476]) did not survive correction across 136 models. Regional medial temporal PET uptake was associated with beta-band scalp connectivity in this small cohort, while focus-side heterogeneity and labeling sensitivity limit a uniform ipsilateral interpretation. Processing-speed indirect associations were exploratory and did not establish compensation or causality. Replication with structural correction, longer EEG sampling and longitudinal cognitive follow-up is required.

articles.title: Evaluation of antitrichomonal activity of coffeewaste compounds against different Trichomonas vaginalis strains: An in vitro and in silico study.
articles.abstract: Trichomoniasis is a Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) caused by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, closely related to secondary viral infections that have a high impact in the public health costs. Nitroimidazole drugs are the only available treatment options. Thus, refractory cases have emerged in recent years, leading to the necessity of therapeutic alternatives. The use of coffee by-products such as pulp, husks and leaves may represent a sustainable alternative for treatment. The aim of the study was to evaluate the trichomonacidal activity in vitro and in silico of compounds commonly isolated from coffee waste. For this, caffeine, chlorogenic acid, quinic acid, caffeic acid, and mangiferin were tested in vitro for their anti-T. vaginalis activities against strains CDC085 and JT. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and molecular docking were performed to unravel a possible mechanism of action. Cytotoxicity in vitro was performed against HeLa cells and vaginal microbiome bacterial isolate, Lactobacillus jensenii. Caffeine, chlorogenic acid, and quinic acid presented potent activity against CDC085 strain of T. vaginalis, with IC50 of 4.83 μM, 10.01 μM, and 12.73 μM, respectively. TEM showed alterations in trophozoites hydrogenosomes for both organic acids treatments and autophagy process when treated with caffeine. The compounds had no inhibitory effect against the JT strain. Quinic acid revealed promising interactions with parasite's lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) through in silico molecular docking. The three promising compounds did not show cytotoxicity against HeLa cells (selectivity index > 10) nor against bacteria from the vaginal microbiota (MIC>400 μM). Our findings have pointed caffeine and quinic acid as potent anti-T. vaginalis agents, with impactful IC50 values and primarily safe against HeLa and L. jensenii cells. Their exact mechanism of action still remains unclear, although TEM and molecular docking results may orientate next steps regarding autophagy alterations and LDH interaction, respectively. We highlight that coffee-derived compounds should be considered as drug candidates for trichomoniasis, presenting promising agents with potential for further preclinical evaluation.

articles.title: Interaction and Internalisation of Gram-Positive Orthopaedic Pathogens in MG-63 Osteoblast-Like Cells and Antibacterial Activity of Vancomycin-Eluting Polymethylmethacrylate.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Orthopaedic implant-associated infections (OIAIs) are frequently caused by Gram-positive bacteria capable of invading osteoblasts, promoting persistence and treatment failure. Local antibiotic delivery using polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) with vancomycin may improve extracellular bacterial eradication but may not directly address intracellular bacterial reservoirs. This study evaluated the interaction and internalization of Gram-positive bacteria in MG-63 osteoblast-like cells and the antibacterial activity of vancomycin-eluted PMMA.

METHODS: Adhesion, interaction, and internalization assays were performed using six previously sequenced clinical isolates of coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) (Staphylococcus epidermidis, S. haemolyticus, S. capitis, S. warneri, and S. caprae) and Cutibacterium acnes. Intracellular localization was confirmed by transmission electron microscopy. Vancomycin-impregnated PMMA beads were added to infected cell cultures to assess antibiotic elution and antibacterial activity. Statistical analyses included ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests, with paired t-test and Wilcoxon sensitivity analysis for biomaterial assays.

RESULTS: All isolates adhered to, interacted with, and internalized into MG-63 cells. Staphylococcus warneri exhibited the greatest cellular interaction, whereas S. caprae showed the highest internalization index despite lower interaction. C. acnes also demonstrated efficient intracellular localization, confirmed by transmission electron microscopy. Vancomycin-eluted PMMA significantly reduced the bacterial inoculum of all CoNS isolates and C. acnes.

CONCLUSIONS: CoNS and C. acnes can invade osteoblast-like cells, supporting their role in the persistence of orthopaedic implant-associated infections. Vancomycin-eluted PMMA demonstrated significant antibacterial activity, supporting local antibiotic delivery as a complementary strategy for managing osteoarticular infections.

articles.title: ATF3 inhibits retinal pigment epithelial cell injury by activating HSPA5:A mechanistic insight for diabetic retinopathy.
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of vision loss in working-age adults. Heat shock protein family A (Hsp70) member 5 (HSPA5) has been reported to be a core ferroptosis-related gene in DR, while its regulatory mechanism remains unclear. DEGs were screened from the GSE233164 dataset with strict thresholds (P < 0.01, |log2FC| > 3). Bioinformatics enrichment and PPI network analyses were performed to screen genes. Clinical samples from 49 DR patients and 49 healthy controls were used for external validation. HG-induced ARPE-19 cell models were established to evaluate cell viability, proliferation, apoptosis, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammation. The ATF3-HSPA5 transcriptional regulatory relationship was predicted by JASPAR and verified via ChIP and dual-luciferase assays. 171 DEGs were screened, and 39 core genes were retained for network analysis. HSPA5 was consistently downregulated in HG-stimulated ARPE-19 cells and DR clinical samples, with a high diagnostic AUC of 0.93. HG exposure triggered RPE cell dysfunction, oxidative damage, ferroptosis, and inflammation, all of which were significantly rescued by HSPA5 overexpression. ATF3 was also downregulated in DR models and clinical samples and positively correlated with HSPA5. Mechanistically, ATF3 directly bound and transcriptionally activated the HSPA5 promoter. Rescue experiments confirmed that HSPA5 knockdown completely abolished the protective effects of ATF3 against HG-induced cell injury and ferroptosis. ATF3 alleviates HG-induced retinal pigment epithelial cell injury and ferroptosis by transcriptionally activating HSPA5. The ATF3-HSPA axis represents a potential therapeutic target for DR.

articles.title: Utilization of serum cystatin C for early detection of chronic kidney disease in Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease is a global health challenge and its early diagnosis is still a challenge, particularly when relying on conventional biomarkers like serum creatinine. In this systematic review, PRISMA guidelines were followed with a comprehensive search on various databases focusing on studies assessing estimated cystatin C levels, and creatinine levels among patients with chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. The Joanna Briggs Institute's critical assessment tool was used to estimate quality and risk bias of included studies. This systematic review included 21 studies with maximum studies demonstrating cystatin C based eGFR may provide more reliable and accurate estimate of kidney function than creatinine based eGFR, specifically for early identification of kidney dysfunction. The findings suggest that serum cystatin C is an early diagnostic and prognostic marker and its incorporation into routine testing will increase the clinical utility by improving risk stratification. In general, this systematic review highlights the diagnostic and prognostic utility of serum cystatin C for early detection of kidney dysfunction.

articles.title: Combining imaging strategies with physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling to improve precision dosing & drug delivery in brain tumors.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Small molecule targeted therapies frequently fail to control brain metastases and primary brain tumors even when systemic exposure reaches toxicity-limiting levels. Systemic exposure-response relationships are often absent, which is well documented for tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Target-site information is therefore needed, since the concentration reached in the tumor is determined not by plasma exposure, but by passive and active transport across the blood-brain barrier and by intratumoral heterogeneity. Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling provides the mechanistic framework to describe this. Models built solely on in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation of permeability and transport have repeatedly required correction factors derived from rodent data, and their evaluation in humans still depends on invasive sampling or microdialysis. Microdialysis performs poorly for lipophilic, highly protein-bound drugs. We argue that quantitative imaging can supply the missing in vivo input. In a hybrid strategy, in vitro-derived transport parameters serve as the starting point, while blood-brain barrier influx and efflux are recalibrated on positron emission tomography (PET) microdose measurements in patients. This could lead to improved prediction of brain concentrations at therapeutic doses and allows simulated target-site exposure to be weighed against in vitro potency for compound and dose selection. Beyond whole-brain averages, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can provide permeability and perfusion parameters longitudinally and in larger cohorts, whereas mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) techniques can map intratumoral heterogeneity in drug distribution in the tumor microenvironment and identify potential sanctuary sites. We map each modality onto the specific PBPK parameters it can inform, and argue that imaging-informed, spatially resolved PBPK is a realistic route toward model-informed precision dosing in neuro-oncology.

articles.title: Hepatocyte Serine Palmitoyltransferase 3 is essential for mitochondrial ceramide homeostasis and electron transport chain function.
articles.abstract: Sphingolipids constitute essential membrane lipids that also function as signaling molecules mediating fundamental cellular processes. Disruption of constitutive sphingolipid metabolism contributes to a range of metabolic diseases. Sphingolipid biosynthesis is initiated by serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT), a heteromeric enzyme composed of Sptlc1 and either Sptlc2 or the less-characterized subunit Sptlc3. While the canonical Sptlc1/Sptlc2 complex generates most sphingolipids, Sptlc1/Sptlc3 produces non-canonical sphingolipids that remain poorly understood. Sptlc3 expression increases in liver disease in both mouse models and humans, yet its biological role remains unclear. To address this, we generated a liver-specific SPTLC3 knockout (SPT3-hKO) mouse model. Loss of SPTLC3 resulted in severe mitochondrial dysfunction in hepatocytes, characterized by reduced oxygen consumption, decreased ATP production, and elevated NADH/NAD+ ratios with a concomitant increase in glycolytic activity. Mechanistically, we found a defect in the electron transport chain (ETC) which stemmed not from intrinsic impairment of the ETC complexes but rather from hindered electron flow between complex I and complex III likely due to reduced availability of Coenzyme Q. While atypical ceramides constituted (∼4% of total ceramides) when measured in liver homogenates, there measurements in mitochondria-enriched fractions revealed enrichment in this cell compartment. Together, our findings identify SPTLC3 as a critical modulator of mitochondrial ceramide composition and ETC function, revealing a specialized role for non-canonical sphingolipids in hepatocyte energy metabolism.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiac Electrophysiology Ethics, Explainability, Equity, and the Road Ahead.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming cardiac electrophysiology (EP) by enabling automated interpretation of electrocardiograms, intracardiac electrograms, wearable sensor data, and imaging modalities. These technologies promise improved diagnostic accuracy, procedural efficiency, and personalized risk stratification across a wide spectrum of arrhythmia care. However, the integration of AI into clinical EP raises important ethical, practical, and regulatory concerns. Many current models function as opaque systems with limited explainability, while training datasets often lack adequate representation across sex, race, geography, and socioeconomic status. These limitations raise the risk of biased performance, reduced generalizability, and erosion of clinician trust. Furthermore, cost, infrastructure requirements, and regulatory complexity threaten equitable global adoption. This review examines the ethical foundations of AI in electrophysiology, focusing on dataset bias, fairness, explainability, and accountability. We discuss the clinical consequences of black box models, outline strategies to improve transparency, and explore emerging regulatory and legal frameworks. Finally, we highlight future horizons including digital twins, multimodal risk engines, and real time procedural guidance systems. Responsible deployment of AI in EP will require rigorous validation, continuous monitoring, clinician oversight, and intentional efforts to ensure equitable access across diverse populations.

articles.title: TERT is a therapeutic target for tertiary stroke prevention.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tertiary stroke prevention aims to mitigate long-term disability and improve life quality for stroke survivors. While primary and secondary stroke prevention strategies have been extensively investigated, tertiary prevention remains a critically understudied area, and there is currently no clinically approved drug for tertiary stroke prevention.

OBJECTIVES: We previously discovered a transcription-regulatory function of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) in cultured primary neurons. Here, we further explored the in vivo functional role of TERT in neural repair and functional recovery after ischemic stroke.

METHODS: We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis in a photothrombosis (PT)-induced permanent ischemic stroke mouse model to characterize TERT expression in the cerebral peri-infarct tissue, which was verified by PT and middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mouse model with immunofluorescence analysis. CUT&Tag-sequencing was used to profile the whole-genome TERT binding loci and transcriptional activity in the isolated neurons from the peri-infarct tissue. We further used phospho-proteomic analysis to identify the signaling mechanism of TERT regulation in neurons.

RESULTS: snRNA-seq revealed TERT expression was increased in neurons in the peri-infarct tissue during the critical post-stroke recovery period in PT mice. This result was confirmed by immunofluorescent imaging in the PT and MCAO stroke models. Intravenous delivery of brain-targeted AAV-mediated neuron-specific overexpression of TERT significantly bolstered neural repair and functional recovery in the PT stroke model. Additionally, pharmacological upregulation of TERT expression in post-stroke recovery period by oral gavage of cycloastragenol (CAG) conferred prominent neural repair, improved sensorimotor functional recovery and alleviated post-stroke depression-like behaviors. Knockdown of neuronal TERT abolished the spontaneous and CAG-induced neural repair-promoting effect in PT mice. Mechanistically, we discovered that neuronal TERT is a transcriptional co-regulator of CREB-target genes including GAP43, EVL, NR4A3, and NRP2 which are associated with enhanced axon sprouting, dendritic branching and synaptogenesis in recovery phase of PT stroke. We further demonstrated that CAG upregulates TERT expression by promoting STAT3 phosphorylation at serine 727 in a DAPK1-dependent manner.

CONCLUSION: Overall, these results demonstrate that TERT is a promising therapeutic target for tertiary stroke prevention.

articles.title: OPTIMIZATION OF THE RELATIONSHIP WITH PRIMARY CARE TO MAXIMIZE THE DIAGNOSIS OF HEPATITIS B VIRUS INFECTION IN MIGRANT POPULATIONS FROM HIGH-PREVALENCE AREAS: VHBilbao PROJECT.
Biological Response Stability of Refrigerated Cosacthen after Opening and Non-Hormonal Effects of ACTH Stimulation Testing in Healthy Dogs.
articles.abstract: The adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test (ACTHST) is widely used to evaluate adrenal reserve in dogs. This study assessed the effects of refrigerated storage of tetracosactide (Cosacthen) after opening for up to three weeks and investigated hematological, biochemical, and electrolyte changes following ACTH stimulation. Ten healthy beagle dogs (five males and five females) were enrolled. Each dog received tetracosactide (5 μg/kg, IV) at vial opening (T0) and at 7-day intervals over 3 weeks (T1 to T3), using aliquots from the same vial stored at 2-8°C. Blood samples were collected before and 1 hour after ACTH administration to measure cortisol, hematology, biochemistry, and electrolytes. Clinical monitoring was performed after each test. Cortisol concentrations increased significantly after ACTH administration at all time points (T0-T3). Delta-cortisol was higher at T1 than at T0 (P = 0.0104) and lower at T2 than at T1 (P = 0.0059), with no differences among T0, T2, and T3. After ACTH administration, red blood cell count, hematocrit, hemoglobin, albumin, alkaline phosphatase, triglycerides, cholesterol, potassium, and total calcium decreased significantly, whereas glucose increased. All values remained within reference intervals, and no adverse effects were observed. Refrigerated storage of Cosacthen after opening did not alter cortisol responses. Post-ACTH changes in laboratory variables should be considered when interpreting results.

articles.title: Long-Term Patient-Reported Outcomes After Pancreatic Surgery During Childhood, Adolescence, and Young Adulthood.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term functional and patient-reported outcomes after pancreatic surgery performed during childhood, adolescence, or young adulthood remain poorly characterized. This study assessed perioperative, long-term functional and patient-reported outcomes after pancreatic surgery in patients aged ≤21 years at the time of surgery.

METHODS: Patients aged ≤21 years undergoing elective pancreatic surgery between 2000 and 2023 were retrospectively identified from a prospectively maintained database. Perioperative outcomes were assessed in all patients. Long-term pancreatic function and health-related quality of life were evaluated among surviving questionnaire respondents using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-PAN26. Exploratory subgroup analyses used Mann-Whitney U tests with rank-biserial correlations (rrb).

RESULTS: Eighty-eight patients were included. Major postoperative morbidity (Clavien-Dindo ≥III) occurred in 15 patients (17.0%), with no in-hospital or 90-day mortality. Among 83 surviving patients eligible for long-term assessment, 36 (43.4%) responded at a mean of 10.6±6.3 years after surgery. New-onset diabetes occurred in two patients (5.6%), and eleven patients (30.6%) required regular pancreatic enzyme replacement. Mean global quality-of-life score was 75.5±19.9. Compared with respondents operated on for neoplastic disease, those operated on for chronic pancreatitis reported higher physical functioning (rrb = 0.428, nominal p = 0.017) and lower pancreas-specific pain (rrb = -0.487, nominal p = 0.012).

CONCLUSIONS: No perioperative mortality was observed. Among long-term respondents, patient-reported quality of life was generally favorable, while pancreatic enzyme dependence and gastrointestinal symptoms remained clinically relevant in a subset. These findings highlight the importance of long-term functional and patient-reported assessment after pancreatic surgery at a young age.

articles.title: Effect of Integrated Respiratory and Functional Training on Weaning from Mechanical Ventilation, Respiratory and Peripheral Muscle Strength, Functional Ability, and Pain After Emergency Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of integrated respiratory and functional (multidimensional functional) training versus high-intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) plus conventional chest physiotherapy (CPT) on ventilator weaning after emergency abdominal surgery.

DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial.

SETTING: Two intensive care units.

PARTICIPANTS: Ninety mechanically ventilated patients with difficult weaning following emergency abdominal surgery (N=90).

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to the study group and control groups. The study group received multidimensional functional training, high-intensity IMT and conventional chest physiotherapy. The control group received high-intensity IMT and conventional chest physiotherapy.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were weaning success and maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP). Secondary outcomes included rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI), peripheral muscle strength, Functional Independence Measure (FIM), pain, weaning duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay.

RESULTS: Weaning success was significantly higher in the study group (95.6% vs 82.2%; P = .044). Both groups significantly improved MIP, with no between-group difference after treatment (mean difference [MD]=0.30 cmH₂O; 95% confidence interval [CI], -4.11 to 4.72; P=0.89). Compared with control group, the study group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in all peripheral muscle strength measures and FIM domains (all P<0.001), greater reductions in RSBI (MD=-3.92 breaths/min/L; 95% CI, -6.85 to -1.00; P=0.01) and pain (MD=3.22; 95% CI, 3 to 3.44; P<0.001), and shorter weaning duration (MD=-5.82 days; 95% CI, -7.98 to -3.67; P<0.001) and ICU length of stay (MD=-7.74 days; 95% CI, -11.37 to -4.11; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Both training approaches improved MIP, whereas multidimensional functional training resulted in higher weaning success and greater improvements in peripheral muscle strength, functional independence, pain, weaning duration, and ICU length of stay than high-intensity IMT+CPT in patients following emergency abdominal surgery.

articles.title: Amine-PEG functionalized graphene oxide enhances the mechanical performance and biocompatibility of bovine pericardium for cardiovascular applications.
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease remains a global health challenge, with increasing demand for aortic valve replacement procedures worldwide. Tissue engineering has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome limitations of conventional bioprosthetic valves, particularly long-term degeneration and limited durability. In this study, graphene oxide (GO) functionalized with amine-polyethylene glycol (GO-PEG-NH2) was incorporated into bovine pericardium by adsorption and chemical reaction to improve mechanical performance for cardiovascular applications. Structural, chemical, and morphological characterizations supported successful GO synthesis and functionalization with PEG-NH2. Atomic force microscopy demonstrated surface modifications and reduced roughness, particularly through chemical reaction. Mechanical assays revealed improvements in stiffness, 0.2% offset yield strength, tensile strength, and maximum load, with chemically incorporated membranes showing superior performance. GO reduced cell viability at concentrations ≥50 μg/mL, whereas GO-PEG-NH2 did not significantly reduce CHO cell viability at 10-200 μg/mL. Isolated atrial reactivity showed a more favorable biological response to GO-PEG-NH2 than to unmodified GO under the evaluated conditions.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Transplacental Treatment of Fetal Ventricular Tachycardia: A Nationwide Survey in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal ventricular tachycardia (VT) is an ultra-rare form of tachyarrhythmia, and no established management strategy currently exists.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the current diagnostic and management approaches for fetal VT.

METHODS: A nationwide survey of suspected fetal VT was conducted across 77 tertiary referral facilities in Japan between 2014 and 2023.

RESULTS: In total, 24 fetal VT cases from 18 facilities were analyzed. Twenty cases were diagnosed based on atrioventricular dissociation. Four were initially diagnosed as supraventricular tachycardia. VT occurred by 32 6/7 weeks of gestation in all nine long QT syndrome (LQTS) cases (LQT 2 in six, LQT 3 in two, and other in one), whereas 8/15 non-LQTS cases occurred at term. Eight of 20 cases managed as fetal VT, and three of four cases managed as fetal supraventricular tachycardia received fetal treatment. Fetal treatments were effective in 9/11 cases overall and in 8/9 LQTS cases. Side effects were observed in 6/11 cases; however, no serious adverse events occurred, except one case of lidocaine toxicity. After birth, LQTS cases were more likely to be refractory to treatment than non-LQT cases (8/9 vs. 6/14), requiring multidisciplinary management. Neurodevelopmental delay was more frequent in LQTS cases than in non-LQTS cases (6/9 vs. 2/14).

CONCLUSIONS: Transplacental treatment is highly recommended for preterm fetal VT. In particular, in cases of fetal VT diagnosed before 33 weeks of gestation, aggressive fetal treatment including magnesium sulfate and β-blockers should be considered with the possibility of LQT 2 or 3.

articles.title: Substrate Comprising Fibrosis and Epicardial Adipose Tissue-Associated Electrophysiological Remodeling Can Sustain Atrial Fibrillation Drivers: Insights from Image-Personalized Computational Simulations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computational models of atrial fibrillation (AF) help clarify arrhythmia mechanisms, but the contribution of left atrial (LA) epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is rarely included.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether incorporating EAT-associated effects into fibrosis-based atrial models alters reentrant arrhythmia inducibility, and to characterize the pro-arrhythmic properties of EAT-affected tissue.

METHODS: LA fibrosis and EAT were quantified by LGE and Dixon MRI in 19 patients with persistent AF. For each patient, three anatomically identical image-personalized models were built (fibrosis only; fibrosis plus half-epicardial EAT effects, 0.5 mm; fibrosis plus full-epicardial EAT effects, 1.0 mm), yielding 855 simulations. In EAT regions, inward rectifier K+ current was reduced by 35%, intracellular K+ by 50%, and conduction velocity by 25%.

RESULTS: Sustained reentry occurred in 370 simulations (43.3%), of which 306 had a functional (rotor-driven) component. Functional reentry inducibility rose from 22.8% (fibrosis only) to 41.4% (half-EAT) and 43.2% (full-EAT). At least one functional reentry was inducible in 12/19 fibrosis-only models, 18/19 half-EAT models, and 19/19 full-EAT models. Median inducible simulations per patient increased from 4 to 6 (p=0.004) and 7 (p=0.003), without significant difference between half- and full-EAT (p=0.895). Fibrosis/EAT overlap regions comprised only 2.1% of the LA wall but were the most arrhythmogenic, with a median 65.5% of their volume harboring reentry versus 8.8% (non-substrate), 37.3% (fibrosis), and 42.8% (EAT) (all p<0.001). In an exploratory analysis of PVI-only ablation patients (n=13), fibrosis-EAT overlap outside the PVI region was associated with 1-year recurrence (log-rank p=0.007).

CONCLUSION: Adding EAT effects to fibrosis-based models increased sustained functional reentry, with transmural depth contributing only modestly. Reentry anchored preferentially where fibrosis and EAT effects coexisted.

articles.title: Differences in Tricuspid Valve Insufficiency, Mechanical Synchrony, and Cardiac Remodeling Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Right Ventricular Pacing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac implantable electronic device-induced tricuspid regurgitation (CIED-induced TR) involves primary (lead-induced) and functional etiologies. The impact of left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) versus right ventricular pacing (RVP) on these mechanisms remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and mechanisms of TR among pacing modalities, and evaluate the prognostic significance of these mechanisms.

METHODS: We analyzed 225 patients with first-time RV apical pacing (RVAP, n=97) or RV septal pacing (RVSP, n=78) using stylet-driven leads, and LBBAP (n=50) using lumenless leads. Echocardiography and electrocardiography were performed at baseline and 2 years post-implantation. Three-dimensional echocardiography assessed lead interference. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared event-free survival between lead-induced (LITR) and functional TR (FTR) groups. Cox regression identified predictors for adverse outcomes.

RESULTS: Despite a higher baseline heart failure burden than RVP (P< .001), LBBAP showed the lowest TR progression rate (20.0% vs RVAP 43.3% vs RVSP 35.9%, P=.020) over 25.8 months. Mechanistically, LBBAP shortened QRS duration (vs RVP widening, P< .001) and demonstrated less lead interference than RVAP (28.0% vs 50.5%, P= .009). Furthermore, LBBAP showed greater left-heart reverse remodeling and improvement in mitral regurgitation, while preserving right-heart structure and function better than RVP. Over 37.4 months, LITR showed worse outcomes than FTR (P= .03). LITR, pulmonary hypertension, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and elevated creatinine were independent predictors for adverse outcomes.

CONCLUSION: LBBAP was associated with less CIED-induced TR than RVP, likely through reduced mechanical interference, superior electrical synchrony, and favorable cardiac remodeling. Furthermore, LITR was associated with a worse prognosis than FTR.

articles.title: A Rounding Error Dressed as Reform: The Implications of a Large Private Health Insurance Company's Prior Authorization Concession for the Electrophysiology Patient.
Nuclear magnetic resonance-derived lipoprotein profile and risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation: a case-cohort design within the PREDIMAR trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoproteins could be potential biomarkers of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence (TAR) after catheter ablation; however, their association remains inconclusive and based exclusively on routine lipid measurements. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) enables detailed lipoprotein characterization beyond conventional assays.

OBJECTIVE: To identify a baseline NMR-derived lipoprotein profile associated with the risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

METHODS: We conducted a case-cohort study (212 cases and 238 participants in a random sub-cohort, with 93 overlapping cases) nested in the PREDIMAR (PRevención con DIeta Mediterránea de Arritmias Recurrentes) trial. Conventional lipoprotein profiles were measured using the Pentra C-200 and advanced lipoprotein profiles were assessed by NMR. Lipoprotein values were normalized and scaled to one standard deviation using Blom's inverse normal transformation. Cox models were used to assess the associations between baseline lipoproteins and TAR. Additionally, a cholesteryl ester transfer (CETP)-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was constructed and evaluated.

RESULTS: After 18-month follow-up, higher baseline remnant cholesterol (hazard ratio = 1.26, 95% confidence interval= 1.06-1.51, per SD), higher cholesterol and triglyceride content in very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.22, 95% confidence interval= 1.03-1.46) or in intermediate-density lipoproteins (IDL) (hazard ratioperSD = 1.29, 95% confidence interval= 1.09-1.52), showed increased risks of TAR. Higher triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio was directly associated, and higher triglyceride-to-VLDL cholesterol and triglyceride-to-IDL cholesterol ratios were inversely associated with recurrence. A CETP-mediated lipoprotein exchange score was directly associated with recurrence.

CONCLUSION: An atherogenic lipoprotein profile characterized by elevated remnant cholesterol is associated with a higher risk of TAR after catheter ablation.

articles.title: Altered cardiac progenitor transcriptional program accompanies NOS-associated DNA damage in a human Duchenne muscular dystrophy organoid model.
articles.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a rare X-linked disorder caused by dystrophin mutations, leads to progressive muscle degeneration and cardiomyopathy. We previously showed elevated DNA damage and mutagenesis in DMD pluripotent stem cells, due to nitric oxide synthase (NOS) dysregulation and reactive species. Here we examined how these disruptions influence cardiac tissue development. In developing cardiac organoids, the DMD cardiovascular progenitor (CP) population shows a premature, elevated activation of CP markers, followed by early maturation gene expression and reduced proliferation. DMD organoids exhibit elevated DNA damage in CPs, persistent pro-inflammatory signaling, and increased expression of inducible NOS. These early molecular disruptions lead to an impaired cardiac differentiation with a lower fraction of spontaneously contracting organoids. DMD organoids show higher cardiac troponin release and accelerated collagen accumulation, mirroring heart failure pathology in mdx mice and DMD patients. Inducing DNA damage in early-stage wild-type organoids reproduced part of the altered gene expression seen in DMD. NOS inhibition in DMD organoids reduced DNA damage and improved organoid contraction, though it did not prevent CM death or collagen accumulation or restore normal gene expression. Together, these findings position NO/NOS modulation as relevant to early cardiac differentiation defects, with isoform balance likely shifting across developmental stages.

articles.title: A stewardship framework for incretin-based therapies in weight management.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of incretin-based therapies, including GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonists, for weight management and related cardio-kidney-liver-metabolic comorbidities has expanded rapidly, yet real-world practice is challenged by inconsistent prescribing, access barriers, limited long-term safety data, low treatment persistence, and concerns regarding equity and financial sustainability. These gaps highlight the need for a structured, coordinated stewardship model to guide safe and evidence-based use of incretin-based therapies.

OBJECTIVES: To develop a scalable, multidisciplinary stewardship framework for incretin-based therapies that supports consistent and efficient prescribing practices, optimizes patient outcomes, strengthens medication access and safety monitoring, and defines the role of pharmacists in chronic weight management.

METHODS: Two sequential expert workgroups were convened, composed of clinicians and pharmacy leaders from 21 health systems. Workgroup 1 identified foundational stewardship elements drawing from established antimicrobial and opioid stewardship models. Workgroup 2 applied these core principles to incretin-based therapies, informed by real-world challenges, emerging evidence, and clinical experience in weight and diabetes management. Consensus was established using a Delphi process, with ≥60% agreement required for inclusion.

RESULTS: Workgroups reached consensus on a stewardship framework comprising multidisciplinary leadership, stakeholder engagement, pharmacy expertise, defined priorities, evidence-based interventions, education, data and reporting strategies, communication pathways, and mechanisms for feedback and continuous assessment. In addition, consensus-based pharmacist-led initiatives and metric categories were developed to support implementation and program evaluation across varied ambulatory environments, with pharmacists identified as central to therapy initiation and titration, adverse effect management, access navigation, patient education, and care coordination.

CONCLUSION: A structured stewardship model offers a feasible and scalable approach to optimize incretin-based therapies in weight management. By integrating multidisciplinary collaboration with pharmacy expertise and clinical and operational strategies, health systems can promote safe, equitable, and sustainable use of these therapies, improve population-level outcomes, and safeguard long-term value amid rapidly expanding utilization.

articles.title: Allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis associated with Talaromyces boninensis: A case report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is a chronic inflammatory pulmonary disorder characterized by type I and III hypersensitivity reactions to Aspergillus fumigatus in the airways of patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis. However, other filamentous fungi can cause similar pathophysiological changes, a condition referred to as allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis (ABPM). Data on ABPM involving non-Aspergillus fungi remain limited. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first case of ABPM associated with Talaromyces boninensis. The patient met the diagnostic criteria proposed by the Japan ABPM Research Program, and T. boninensis was isolated from bronchial lavage fluid and identified by molecular analysis.

articles.title: Affective prosody and facial expression cues differentially augment spoken sentence and discourse comprehension for acute left and right hemisphere stroke survivors.
articles.abstract: Comprehension for spoken sentences and discourse is differentially impacted by left- (LH) and right-hemisphere (RH) brain damage, such as that caused by stroke. Comprehension deficits can have disabling effects on one's ability to process information, participate in everyday life, and create and maintain relationships. This cross-sectional, observational study evaluated differences in sentence- and discourse-level comprehension between LH and RH stroke survivors across different prosodic conditions and examined relationships between comprehension and damage to key LH and RH regions. Participants included 43 LH and 46 RH acute stroke survivors and 39 controls. All participants completed an in-house clinical assessment that included short passages presented in three conditions: neutral prosody, affective prosody, and affective prosody plus facial expression cues. Stroke survivors also completed magnetic resonance imaging. Consistent with expectations, stroke participants achieved lower comprehension accuracy than controls across conditions. LH participants' accuracy in the 'affective prosody plus facial expressions' condition was greater than in the neutral prosody condition, and total LH lesion volume was associated with performance. RH participants' accuracy in the 'affective prosody' and 'affective prosody plus facial expressions' conditions was greater than in the neutral prosody condition. Overall, both groups' scores increased linearly from Condition 1 to 3. None of the prespecified LH or RH brain regions were significantly associated with performance. Findings suggest that some acute LH and RH stroke survivors with comprehension deficits can benefit from affective prosody and facial expression cues, but different or additional cues may be needed for greatest benefit.

articles.title: Prevalence of Diabetic Retinopathy and Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Diverse Hispanic/Latino Adults: HCHS/SOL and SOL Ojos Results.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence among Hispanic/Latino adults with diabetes, assess heterogeneity by background group, and evaluate cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis of SOL Ojos, a multicenter ancillary study embedded within the population-based Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL).

PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥40 years completing HCHS/SOL Visit 3 (V3; 2020-2024) from Chicago and Miami were examined (3,294/3,864; 85.2%). The analytic sample included 1,224 participants with diabetes and gradable retinal imaging (mean age, 62.7 years [95% CI, 61.4-64.0]; 48.6% female).

METHODS: Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic examinations with centrally graded ultra-widefield fundus imaging. Major CVD risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, obesity, smoking) were assessed at V3 and analyzed individually and cumulatively. DR, macular edema (ME), and vision-threatening DR (VTDR) were graded using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) protocols. Survey-weighted analyses estimated age-standardized prevalence, and sequentially adjusted logistic regression evaluated associations.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Age-standardized prevalence of DR outcomes and associations with CVD risk factors.

RESULTS: Age-standardized any DR prevalence was 34.7% (95% CI, 29.2-40.2). Among men, any DR and VTDR prevalence was 41.8% (95% CI, 33.5-50.0) and 13.4% (95% CI, 7.4-19.5), versus 27.2% (95% CI, 19.5-34.9) and 9.4% (95% CI, 1.4-17.4) among women. Any DR ranged across Hispanic/Latino backgrounds from 13.9% (95% CI, 1.8-26.0) to 55.4% (95% CI, 49.2-61.6) in men and 15.3% (95% CI, 4.4-26.2) to 39.2% (95% CI, 22.3-56.1) in women, with the highest estimates among Cuban individuals. CVD risk factors were common and clustered (≥4: men 42.7% [95% CI, 34.5-50.9]; women 35.6% [95% CI, 29.3-41.9]). In adjusted models, hypertension was associated with any DR (OR, 3.16 [95% CI, 1.76-5.65]) and VTDR (OR, 2.86 [95% CI, 1.05-7.79]). Overall cumulative CVD risk burden was not significantly associated with VTDR (Type III F test, P=0.1193), despite adjustment for diabetes duration; the 3-risk-factor category had higher estimated odds than the 1-risk-factor category (OR, 5.10 [95% CI, 1.22-21.39]).

CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional study of Hispanic/Latino adults with diabetes, more than one-third had DR, with substantial heterogeneity across background groups. Hypertension was associated with DR outcomes, particularly VTDR. Findings provide contemporary prevalence estimates and support longitudinal evaluation of cardiometabolic risk and DR outcomes.

articles.title: Assessment of the Necessity for High-Level Disinfection (HLD) of Reusable Ophthalmic Devices: A Multisociety Position Paper.
articles.abstract: Regulatory agencies in the United States and abroad are increasingly citing clinics and surgical facilities for what they deem to be inadequate disinfection of Goldmann applanation tonometry (GAT) tips, gonioscopy lenses, laser lenses, and other reusable clinic devices that contact the ocular surface. These regulators require routine high-level disinfection (HLD) of these reusable devices to prevent infection transmission. A multisociety task force formed to assess the necessity of HLD found no published evidence that these devices transmit sight-threatening infections or that HLD reduces infection transmission compared with lower-level disinfection methods. Meanwhile, routine use of chemical HLD reduces clinic efficiency, increases healthcare costs and waste, and may damage device surfaces potentially affecting patient care. Underlying these mandates for HLD is the nearly century-old Spaulding classification system, which inappropriately groups the ocular surface with heavily contaminated mucous membranes. A task force survey with more than 1000 ophthalmologist respondents found that the most common reprocessing methods were alcohol wiping for GAT tips and either alcohol wiping or soap and water for diagnostic or laser lenses. Many respondents using chemical HLD reported adverse effects, including ocular surface chemical toxicity and device damage. Despite infrequent use of HLD, reported infection transmission was exceedingly rare and generally limited to self-limited adenoviral conjunctivitis. The task force agreed with the majority (88%) of ophthalmologists surveyed that HLD should not be required for these reusable devices in routine clinical care. Instead, HLD should be a discretionary consideration in higher-risk circumstances, such as following use of these devices in patients with suspected infection. This paper presents the summary recommendations of a policy statement approved by the American Academy of Ophthalmology Board of Trustees and endorsed by four subspecialty societies.

articles.title: Pre-participation cardiovascular evaluation in Italian elite athletes (2023-2026): diagnostic yield, accuracy, and cost analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Elite athletes represent a unique population within competitive sports. Despite repeated cardiovascular screening during their careers, they may harbour clinically silent but potentially serious cardiovascular diseases. Therefore, cardiovascular evaluation in elite athletes may require a sensitive and comprehensive diagnostic approach.

METHODS: We analyzed 1505 elite athletes, undergoing comprehensive PPS including resting ECG, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Major cardiovascular abnormalities (MCA) and cardiomyopathies were established according to the final clinical diagnosis, served as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (NPV), and ROC analyses were assessed for ECG alone and for ECG combined with CPET or TTE.

RESULTS: MCA were identified in 17 athletes (1.13%), including 7 cardiomyopathies (0.46%) and 6 channelopathies (0.40%). CPET identified additional cardiomyopathies through exercise-induced arrhythmias, including cases not detected by resting ECG, whereas TTE identified structural and coronary abnormalities not evident on ECG. Resting ECG showed a sensitivity of 58.8% and specificity of 94.0% for MCA, with a NPV 99.5%. The addition of CPET increased sensitivity to 82.4%, although specificity decreased to 82.2%. ECG + TTE achieved a sensitivity of 76.5% and specificity of 91.5%. ROC analysis showed AUCs of 0.76 for ECG, 0.82 for ECG + CPET, and 0.84 for ECG + TTE for MCA.

CONCLUSION: In this highly selected cohort of elite athletes, integrating ECG, CPET, and TTE provided complementary diagnostic information and increased the detection of MCA compared with resting ECG alone. These findings support the feasibility of a comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation model in highly selected athletes evaluated within specialized sports cardiology settings.

articles.title: Evaluation of Active Surveillance Testing for Candidozyma (Candida) auris and Impact on Infection Control Behaviors in an Acute Healthcare System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of active surveillance testing (AST) for Candidozyma auris on healthcare system epidemiologic trends and infection prevention and control (IPC) behaviors.

DESIGN: Explanatory sequential mixed methods study using retrospective electronic medical record review, hand hygiene observations, and healthcare personnel focus groups.
