articles.title: Real-World, Device-Based Peak Cadence Metrics in Black and White Adults With Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Walking performance is worse in Black than White adults with multiple sclerosis (MS), and that difference might extend into real-world, device-based measurements.

OBJECTIVE: The current study examined peak 30-minute cadence (Peak-30CAD) and peak 1-minute cadence (Peak-1CAD) in Black and White adults with MS.

METHODS: Participants with MS who self-identified as Black (n = 43) or White (n = 96) completed the Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25FW) and 6-Minute Walk (6MW), and wore an accelerometer on a belt around the waist during the waking hours of the day for a 7-day period.

RESULTS: Peak-30CAD and Peak-1CAD along with T25FW and 6MW were significantly lower in Black than White participants when controlling for imbalances in age, sex, education, and disease duration, with the differences approaching a moderate magnitude. The differences in Peak-30CAD and Peak-1CAD were smaller and non-significant in additional sensitivity analyses further controlling for number of days of valid accelerometer data. Peak-30CAD and Peak-1CAD had strong correlations with T25FW and 6MW in Black and White participants.

CONCLUSION: Peak-30CAD and Peak-1CAD were associated with laboratory-based walking performance in both Black and White adults with MS and may provide complementary real-world mobility metrics.

articles.title: Rapid Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae in Infants With Severe Infection Disease by Instant Nanofluorescent Microspheres-Immunochromatography Combined With Recombinase Polymerase Isothermal Amplification Technology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is an important and virulent pathogen causing acute respiratory infections in infants. Currently, traditional methods for detecting Klebsiella pneumoniae in babies are labour-intensive and time-consuming, and their accuracy and sensitivity require improvement. Recombinant enzyme polymerase amplification technology (RPA) has the advantages of good specificity, high sensitivity, and isothermal amplification. It can be combined with fluorescence immunochromatography test strip (FICTS) based on nanofluorescent microspheres (nFM) to achieve rapid, low-cost, high sensitivity, and specific detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae in infants.

METHODS: mdh was selected as a genus-specific gene from Klebsiella pneumoniae, and recombinant polymerase isothermal amplification-nanofluorescence microsphere immunochromatography (RPA-FICTS) was established by using standard strains. The sensitivity and specificity of this detection technology can be improved by the magnetic bead purification step of RPA nucleic acid amplification products. Subsequently, rapid quantitative detection of K. pneumoniae in infant samples was performed using fluorescent immunochromatographic test strips. A total of 19 clinical samples of Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) and 7 clinical samples of non-Klebsiella pneumoniae (nKP) were detected by the new detection technology platform established in this paper, and the specificity and sensitivity of RPA-FICTS were verified by agarose gel electrophoresis.

RESULTS: Under the optimal detection conditions, the maximum detection limits of RPA-GE (agarose gel electrophoresis) and RPA-FICTS are 9.03 × 10-3 and 9.03 × 10-8 ng/μL. RPA-FICTS can quickly detect Klebsiella pneumoniae and specifically distinguish between Klebsiella pneumoniae and non-Klebsiella pneumoniae. Compared with traditional detection methods, this method has a shorter detection time (55 min), strong specificity, high sensitivity, and simple operation, providing a new method for rapid detection of human Klebsiella pneumoniae.

articles.title: Hierarchical Triboelectric-Plasmonic-Coupled All-Fabric Dual-Mode Platform for Self-Powered Respiratory Monitoring and Electrostatic-Driven In Situ Pseudovirus Detection.
articles.abstract: Respiratory infectious diseases represented by COVID-19 necessitate proactive wearable diagnostic platforms with high integration and sensitivity. In this study, we present a hierarchical, all-fabric dual-mode sensor seamlessly integrating a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for self-powered physiological pre-alert and a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate for biochemical verification. The core innovation is a rationally engineered bilayer silver (Ag) fabric via secondary Ag plating (Ag nanoparticles: ∼16 nm bottom, ∼92 nm top), forming abundant plasmonic "hot spots" and enabling SERS detection with an LOD down to 10-16 M. Meanwhile, the same fabric serves as a robust TENG electrode paired with high-β-phase PVDF nanofibers (∼70% β-phase), enabling a power density of 461.28 mW m-2 and real-time respiratory monitoring within < 0.02 s, with the results visualized on a self-developed mobile APP for on-site use. Moreover, TENG-driven field-assisted enrichment promotes the accumulation of negatively charged viral particles near the sensing surface, while the hierarchical Ag architecture provides abundant SERS-active interfaces for virus-substrate interactions, jointly facilitating in situ SERS detection down to 5 × 103 TU mL-1 for SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus. The smart mask prototype also demonstrates > 99.4% antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. This "monitor-enrich-detect" triboelectric-plasmonic-coupled platform holds promise for early warning and risk mitigation of respiratory infectious disease transmission.

articles.title: Parvovirus B19 and inflammatory arthritis: from viral mimicry to infection-associated autoimmunity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Parvovirus B19 is a clinically important viral mimic of systemic inflammatory rheumatic diseases, frequently presenting as an abrupt-onset inflammatory polyarthritis in adults. While typically self-limiting, B19V infection can induce transient autoantibodies, cytopenias, and phenotypes resembling rheumatoid arthritis or systemic lupus erythematosus. In specific contexts, it may also lead to persistent or atypical musculoskeletal manifestations.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review summarizes the epidemiology, immunopathogenesis, clinical spectrum, diagnostic approach, and management of B19V-associated arthritis. Literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and relevant reference lists from inception to 23 September 2026, using terms related to parvovirus B19, arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmunity, synovitis, cytokines, PCR, serology, and intravenous immunoglobulin.

EXPERT OPINION: B19V-associated arthritis should be recognized as a time-sensitive clinicovirological diagnosis, not merely a diagnosis of exclusion. Advancing the field requires prospective outbreak-based cohort studies, standardized diagnostic criteria, and the integration of virological and immunological biomarkers to distinguish self-limiting infection from evolving autoimmune disease.

articles.title: Zika virus-like particles' production lab protocol in chemically defined medium using quality by design.
articles.abstract: Zika virus remains a global health emergency without approved vaccines or drugs. Virus-like particles (VLP) provide a safe vaccine-development platform, but optimizing the baculovirus/insect-cell expression system to obtain these nanostructures is difficult because multiple critical parameters interact. This study used statistical experimental designs with low control requirements and operating costs to optimize multiplicity of infection (MOI), time of infection (TOI), and time of harvest (TOH) for Zika VLP production. VLP were immunochemically characterized. Dot-blot chemiluminescence provided volumetric total signal intensity as a measure of relative protein expression, while negative-stain transmission electron microscopy and immunolabeling determined morphology, mean particle size, and heterogeneity through the unbiased standard error of mean particle size. Mathematical models related MOI, TOI, TOH, and their interactions to recombinant-protein quality and relative quantity. A desirability-function optimization identified MOI 0.2 pfu cell-1, TOI 46 h, and TOH 48 h as optimal. These conditions predicted VLP with a mean diameter of 58.52 nm, a standard error of 3.52 nm, and signal intensity equal to 64.57% of the study maximum. Thus, subsequent process-development stages involving equipment-dependent parameters relevant to commercial scale can be completed faster and at lower cost, supporting efficient scale-up of a promising Zika vaccine candidate platform.

articles.title: The professional knowledge, skills and specialist functions of certified clinical coding auditors.
articles.journal: Health information management : journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The quality of Australia's coded clinical data is essential for its reliability in myriad applications throughout the healthcare system, signalling the need for clinical coding auditing. Internal clinical coding auditors audit hospitals' coded data, 'in-house'. Independent, external auditors undertake audits on behalf of purchasers and providers: state/territory governments; health insurance funds; private hospital proprietors.

OBJECTIVE: To identify the professional knowledge, skills and specialist functions of certified clinical coding auditors in Australia.

METHOD: A cross-sectional study design was utilised. A purposively designed, self-administered online survey was distributed to the study population (N = 241), who achieved a 'Certificate of External and Internal Clinical Coding Auditing' or 'Certificate of Internal Clinical Coding Auditing' from La Trobe University, Australia, from 2005 to 2021.

RESULTS: Of the 93/241 (38.6%) respondents, these results concern those who had engaged, predominantly, in either external or internal auditing within their previous 5 years of employment. The responses of 42 practising auditors were analysed: 83.3% (n = 35) had predominantly undertaken internal auditing within the past 5 years; 59.5% (n = 25/42) had a Certificate of External and Internal Clinical Coding Auditing, 28% (n = 7/25) of whom had predominately undertaken external auditing. The respondent-auditors reported on 52 core knowledges/skills/functions, which we aggregated into 4 discrete clusters: (a) health classification; (b) health informatics and technology; (c) health data analysis; (d) health information and business management. Of these knowledges/skills/functions, six applied to 100% of internal and external auditors; most applied fairly equally to external and internal auditors; four were utilised by <25% of external auditors; eight were used by <25% of internal auditors; 57.1% of external, and 68.6% of internal, auditors reported statistically analysing audit results.

CONCLUSION: The findings provide the first evidence-base for clinical coding auditors' knowledges/skills/functions, and prompt recommendations for their more extensive engagement in: (a) data analysis (including underpinning research methodology); and (b) preparation for artificial intelligence-related developments.Implications for health information management practice:This pioneering research on the work of clinical coding auditors provides a platform to inform (a) educational curricula updates, (b) development of professional competency standards for clinical coding auditors, (c) enhanced governance in audit practice and (d) development of national standards for clinical coding auditing.

articles.title: Multidimensional Determinants of Quality of Life in Men With Klinefelter Syndrome: A Narrative Review of Workshop Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Klinefelter syndrome (KS), typically characterized by a 47, XXY karyotype, is the most common sex chromosomal aneuploidy in males, with a prevalence of approximately one in 600-660 individuals. Despite its frequency, the syndrome remains significantly underdiagnosed, with 50%-75% of affected individuals never receiving a clinical diagnosis. While the classic phenotype includes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and infertility, recent evidence highlights a lifelong burden of neurocognitive, psychological, and socioeconomic challenges.

OBJECTIVES: This study synthesizes current evidence regarding the determinants of quality of life (QoL) in men with KS, specifically contextualizing the registry data and clinical trajectories discussed during the fourth International Workshop on Klinefelter Syndrome.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: To perform a narrative review, a literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. The search focused on peer-reviewed articles published up to March 2026, utilizing primary keywords such as "Klinefelter Syndrome," "47, XXY, " "Quality of Life, " "Socioeconomic Status, " and "Testosterone Replacement Therapy."

RESULTS: Affected individuals consistently report lower QoL across physical, psychological, and social domains compared to healthy controls, with social relationship scores often reaching levels observed in psychiatric reference populations. Key drivers of reduced well-being include lower educational achievement, precarious employment, chronic health comorbidities, and experienced discrimination.

DISCUSSION: While testosterone replacement therapy is essential for physical virilization, it is frequently insufficient to normalize QoL or alleviate deep-seated psychological distress, highlighting the impact of unmitigated developmental hurdles, metabolic burdens, and infertility-related psychological trauma.

CONCLUSION: A multidisciplinary approach-integrating endocrinology with specialized psychological, fertility, and educational support-is strictly required to address the complex, multidimensional needs of this population across the lifespan.

articles.title: Survey of the health and welfare of imported dogs presenting to UK veterinary surgeons.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since changes to legislation in 2012, numbers of dogs imported into the UK, especially rescues, have increased substantially. We aimed to explore the health and behaviour issues among imported dogs presented to UK veterinary surgeons.

METHODS: An online survey was completed by 413 veterinary surgeons practising in the UK in 2023. The findings were analysed with descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Thirteen percent had encountered imported dogs who had died during or shortly after transportation and two-thirds reported observing dogs they considered were unfit to travel, including dogs with unhealed wounds and fractures. Common behavioural concerns included fear of people, noises or objects, and unwanted behaviours when confined or alone. The most common infectious diseases reported as being diagnosed were leishmaniasis, dirofilariasis and brucellosis. Suspected falsified health documentation or passports had been observed by almost two-thirds of respondents. Less than half of respondents reported specific practice policies or testing protocols for exotic diseases.

LIMITATIONS: This convenience sample is limited by what is presented to veterinary surgeons and recall over the previous 24 months.

CONCLUSION: Participants reported significant welfare concerns in current dog importation practices and highlighted a need for clearer guidance on management and treatment of imported dogs in veterinary practice.

articles.title: Management of postoperative hypothermia in the cardiovascular surgery intensive care unit: A qualitative study based on insights from nurses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monitoring and managing postoperative hypothermia in patients undergoing cardiac surgery is essential. Nevertheless, little is known about nurses' experiences in assessing and managing postoperative hypothermia after cardiac surgery, highlighting the need for studies to explore their clinical experiences and perspectives.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the experiences of cardiovascular surgery intensive care unit nurses in managing postoperative hypothermia after cardiovascular surgery.

METHODS: This interpretative/constructivist phenomenological study was conducted with 12 nurses working in a cardiovascular surgery intensive care unit. Data were collected through in-depth online interviews using a semi-structured questionnaire and analysed using content analysis. Participants were selected purposively to obtain diverse perspectives on postoperative hypothermia management.

RESULTS: Data analysis identified five themes and 35 sub-themes: clinical challenges associated with postoperative hypothermia, strategies for managing postoperative hypothermia, barriers to effective postoperative hypothermia management, strategies for achieving standardised practices and suggestions for improving postoperative hypothermia management. Nurses emphasised early recognition, continuous temperature monitoring and timely interventions to prevent postoperative hypothermia-related complications.

CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first qualitative study focusing on postoperative hypothermia management in a cardiovascular surgery intensive care unit. Findings highlight the need for advanced warming technologies, ongoing staff education and standardised protocols. Enhancing healthcare professionals' knowledge and developing evidence-based protocols and care bundles are essential for optimising perioperative hypothermia management.Reporting:COREQ (the consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research).

articles.title: Disease of South American camelids in England and Wales: Analysis of diagnoses from Animal and Plant Health Agency laboratory submissions between 2012 and 2021.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: South American camelids (SACs) have become increasingly popular in the UK. Consequently, knowledge among veterinary practitioners about diseases in these non-native species has improved, although gaps remain. The remit of this study was to identify common diseases of SACs based on Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) surveillance data from testing of carcass and sample submissions.

METHODS: A total of 3541 data sets of SAC submissions to APHA between 2012 and 2021 were analysed.

RESULTS: The overall diagnostic success rate was 39.5% but was significantly higher in carcass submissions (74%) compared to non-carcass submissions (23%). It was also significantly higher in post-weaned crias (53.4%) than in adults (40.5%), whereas fetuses (18.2%) had the lowest rate. The most common diagnoses were similar to those in an earlier study, with an even higher percentage of diagnoses of gastrointestinal parasitism among other frequent diagnoses of parasitic disease. Among non-infectious disease causes, nutritional diseases were most frequently diagnosed.

LIMITATIONS: Passive disease surveillance data rely on submissions by veterinarians to the APHA surveillance network and will therefore not mirror disease prevalence.

CONCLUSION: A detailed summary of laboratory-based diagnoses provides veterinarians and owners with guidance on frequent significant diseases of SACs in England and Wales and encourages submission of carcasses rather than samples for diagnostics where appropriate.

articles.title: Notation System for Liver Transplant Recipients: Key Information in Transplant Procedure.
articles.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is a standard therapy for patients with end-stage liver disease and certain hepatic malignancies. The LT procedure has diversified due to donor shortages and advances in immunosuppressive treatments and surgical techniques. Donor organ shortages have promoted the use of living donor liver transplantation and "marginal" livers, including donation after circulatory death. ABO-incompatible liver transplants now show outcomes comparable with ABO-compatible transplants when a desensitization protocol is used. Hepaticojejunostomy, rather than duct-to-duct anastomosis, is performed in select cases with an unsuitable common bile duct or in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis. These procedural differences affect follow-up management in LT recipients. Given the increasing diversity of transplant surgeries and the long-term prognosis after LT, it is essential for healthcare professionals and transplant societies to be informed about the specific procedures performed in LT recipients. We aimed to propose a notation system for LT recipients that documents key procedural information, including the number of transplantations, donor type with donor/recipient blood types in ABO-incompatible transplantation, graft type, the number of reconstructed vessels, and the number and type of biliary reconstruction. The use of a common notation system for transplant procedures can facilitate patient management, communication, and accurate understanding of transplant procedures.

articles.title: Hydrochlorothiazide Exposure and Skin Cancer Hazards Versus ACE Inhibitors Among Adults Aged 65 Years or Older: A TriNetX-Based Cohort Study.
A Survey and Analysis of the Current Status of MRI Safety Management in Medical Institutions in Korea.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MRI safety management is essential for patient safety and for standardizing institutional practices. However, nationwide data on MRI safety readiness in Korean tertiary hospitals remain limited.

PURPOSE: To evaluate MRI safety management across all 47 Korean tertiary hospitals and identify major gaps in safety infrastructure, staffing, and education.

STUDY TYPE: Cross-sectional census survey.

POPULATION: MRI safety managers from all 47 Korean tertiary hospitals in 2025.

ASSESSMENT: A structured 50-item questionnaire was developed based on the American College of Radiology (ACR) MRI safety guidelines. A composite safety maturity index (0-100) was calculated as the unweighted arithmetic mean of four domain scores derived from 32 binary safety-practice items, with mandatory items weighted 2 and recommended items weighted 1 in accordance with the 2024 ACR Manual on MR Safety.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Descriptive statistics were used to summarize institutional characteristics and safety compliance. Comparisons of staffing patterns by time period were evaluated using inferential tests, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: The response rate was 100% (47/47). The mean number of MRI units per hospital was 5.32 ± 3.50, and 3.0 T systems were predominant. Compliance was universal for closed-circuit television (CCTV) monitoring and MR Conditional monitoring devices but was low for ferromagnetic detection systems (17.0%), Magnetic Resonance Safety Officer (MRSO) appointment (17.0%), and Level 1 safety education (23.4%). MRI-related safety incidents were reported by 44.7% of hospitals. Two-person staffing decreased significantly from 97.9% on weekday daytime hours to 55.3% on Saturdays, 44.7% at night, and 38.3% on holidays. The overall composite safety maturity score was 63.08 ± 15.04.

DATA CONCLUSION: Considerable variability remains in MRI safety management across Korean tertiary hospitals. These findings highlight the need for national MRI safety standards in the Republic of Korea.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 4.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 4.

articles.title: Mitochondrial dynamics and repair differences in two mouse models of Friedreich's ataxia.
articles.abstract: Friedreich's ataxia (FA) is an inherited disorder caused by reduced expression of the mitochondrial protein frataxin (FXN). Although defined as a neurodegenerative disease, cardiomyopathy is the leading cause of mortality. Cardiac manifestations of FA span from concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with preserved systolic function and impaired diastolic relaxation, resembling heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), to systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The molecular mechanisms driving progression towards these cardiac phenotypes remain poorly understood. We examined mitochondrial content, dynamics and mitophagy in two FA mouse models: cardiac/skeletal muscle-specific MCK-Cre FXN knockout (FXN-cKO) mice, which develop HFrEF, and inducible FXN knockdown (FXNKD) mice, which develop HFpEF-like cardiomyopathy. FXN-cKO hearts exhibited increased mitochondrial transcription factor A expression, an elevated mitochondrial-to-nuclear DNA ratio and greater mitochondrial density by electron microscopy, consistent with enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis. In contrast, FXNKD hearts showed no changes in mitochondrial content or biogenesis markers. Mitochondrial dynamics were markedly altered in FXN-cKO hearts, with reduced mitofusin-2 and increased FIS1 expression, accompanied by smaller, fragmented mitochondria. FXNKD hearts exhibited preserved fission, modestly increased fusion and mild mitochondrial enlargement. Markers of mitophagy were increased in FXN-cKO hearts, but a reduced LC3-II/I ratio suggested impaired autophagosome maturation and defective mitochondrial clearance. No changes in mitophagy were observed in FXNKD hearts. These findings demonstrate that FA-associated HFrEF is characterized by increased mitochondrial biogenesis coupled with impaired mitochondrial quality control and fragmentation, whereas FA-associated HFpEF-like phenotype shows preserved mitochondrial architecture and turnover. Mitochondrial remodelling programmes may underlie divergent cardiac phenotypes in FA and represent therapeutic targets for disease modification. KEY POINTS: Friedreich's ataxia (FA) cardiomyopathy develops as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)-like disease, but mechanisms leading to different cardiac phenotypes are unclear. We compared mitochondrial remodelling in FA mouse models with divergent cardiac phenotypes. Frataxin knockout (FXN-cKO) mice with HFrEF phenotype showed increased mitochondrial biogenesis, fragmentation and impaired mitochondrial quality control. FXN knockdown (FXNKD) mice with HFpEF-like phenotype showed largely preserved mitochondrial structure and turnover. Distinct mitochondrial adaptations may drive phenotype-specific cardiac outcomes in FA.

articles.title: First Report of Natural Co-Infection by Gyrodactylus lenoki and Lactococcus garvieae in Farmed Rainbow Trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss): Field and Experimental Evidence for Parasite-Enhanced Mortality, With a COI-Morphology Species Discordance.
articles.abstract: It is well established that ectoparasite infection can increase the pathogenicity of, and host susceptibility to, bacterial infections in fish, including rainbow trout; however, no interaction between the ectoparasite Gyrodactylus and the bacterium Lactococcus garvieae has previously been documented. This study presents the first report of a severe natural co-infection of Gyrodactylus lenoki and Lactococcus garvieae in farmed rainbow trout in Vietnam, with mortality rates ranging from 25% to 43% within 4 to 5 days of the first recognised pathogen-associated fish mortality. The identity of both pathogens was established using morphological characterisation, sequencing, and PCR assays, providing clear evidence of dual infection under natural conditions. Molecular (COI) data initially suggested homology with Gyrodactylus salaris, a notifiable pathogen of major regulatory concern that has not previously been recorded outside Europe, but size-invariant morphological analysis of the marginal hook sickles confirmed the parasite as G. lenoki, demonstrating that COI barcode data alone can be misleading for regulatory-critical species identification within this genus. Experimental challenge trials demonstrated that while G. lenoki exhibits low virulence toward rainbow trout on its own, it significantly exacerbates the severity of L. garvieae infection, leading to higher mortality (approximately 25% mortality in fish infected with L. garvieae alone, rising to up to 45% in co-infected fish, with mortality occurring earlier in co-infected groups). Notably, the population dynamics of the ectoparasite varied across experimental groups, with a strong correlation (r = 0.97) observed between host mortality and G. lenoki infection levels. These findings underscore the critical role of ectoparasitic infections in increasing rainbow trout susceptibility to bacterial invasion and highlight the diagnostic risks of relying on molecular barcoding alone when regulatory-notifiable pathogens are suspected.

articles.title: Association of extracorporeal therapy with persistent neurologic sequelae after lithium poisoning: A multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lithium poisoning may result in persistent neurologic sequelae, including irreversible neurotoxicity. Although extracorporeal therapy enhances lithium elimination, its effect on clinically meaningful outcomes remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between extracorporeal therapy and persistent neurologic sequelae in patients with lithium poisoning.

METHODS: We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study including 268 patients with lithium poisoning from four tertiary hospitals in Spain. The primary outcome was persistent neurologic sequelae for ≥2 months. Secondary outcomes included mortality, hospital length of stay and treatment-related complications. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score weighting were used to adjust for differences in baseline severity and treatment indication.

RESULTS: Among 268 patients, 108 (40.3%) received extracorporeal therapy. Patients receiving extracorporeal therapy had more severe poisoning, with higher peak lithium concentrations and more frequent acute kidney injury and neurologic manifestations. Persistent neurologic sequelae occurred in 55 patients (20.5%) and were less frequent among patients treated with extracorporeal therapy (11.1% vs. 26.9%; p = 0.002). In multivariable analysis, extracorporeal therapy was independently associated with lower odds of persistent neurologic sequelae (adjusted odds ratio 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.45). Higher peak lithium concentration and pre-existing neurologic disease were independently associated with persistent neurologic sequelae. Findings remained consistent after propensity score weighting. The association was strongest among patients meeting EXtracorporeal TReatments In Poisoning (EXTRIP)-recommended criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: Extracorporeal therapy was associated with a lower frequency of persistent neurologic sequelae in lithium poisoning, particularly among patients meeting EXTRIP Workgroup 'recommended' criteria. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings, particularly in intermediate-risk poisoning.

articles.title: Letter: Interpreting Rule-Out and Rule-In Enhanced Liver Fibrosis Thresholds in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
Patient Perspectives on a Nurse-Led Personalised Cardiovascular Risk Intervention in Type 2 Diabetes: A Qualitative Study Within the VOLTAIRE Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To explore patient perspectives on the acceptability of a nurse-led personalised cardiovascular risk intervention in Type 2 diabetes.

DESIGN: A qualitative study nested within a randomised controlled trial.

METHODS: Two online focus groups (n = 5 per group) were conducted with adults who received personalised cardiovascular risk information through computed tomography coronary angiography or polygenic risk scores within a nurse-led intervention. A co-designed discussion guide explored risk understanding, views of the nurse-led consultation, emotional responses, behaviour change and feasibility. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability.

RESULTS: Five interrelated themes were identified: (1) making personalised risk tangible; (2) interpretation requires relationship; (3) channelling concern into action; (4) from insight to incremental agency; and (5) feasibility and system conditions for scale.

CONCLUSION: Among focus group participants who completed the intervention, the model was highly acceptable, with nurse-led translation of complex risk information supporting engagement and behaviour change.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND PATIENT CARE: Cardiovascular nurse coaching may strengthen the clinical value of personalised risk tools by supporting understanding, emotional response and translation into achievable prevention goals.

IMPACT: This study addressed the limited understanding of how adults with Type 2 diabetes perceive personalised cardiovascular risk communication. It found that acceptability was dynamic and improved when nurse-led explanation and goal setting supported behavioural engagement, with implications for cardiovascular nurses and services implementing personalised prevention.

REPORTING METHOD: This study adhered to the consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Participants contributed to study design through co-development of the focus group guide and informed interpretation of findings.

TRIAL AND PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07091162).

articles.title: Inhibition of xanthine oxidase protects against heatstroke-related acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heatstroke-induced acute kidney injury (HS-AKI) is a critical type of visceral injury. This study aimed to explore whether xanthine oxidase (XOD) promotes the progression of HS-AKI and whether febuxostat (Feb) attenuates HS-AKI through the inhibition of oxidative stress.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Both in vitro (HK-2 cells) and in vivo (a mouse model) approaches were used to evaluate the role of XOD in HS-AKI. In vitro, genetic gain-/loss-of-function (mediated by an XDH overexpression plasmid/siRNA) and pharmacologic intervention (febuxostat) were performed in HK-2 cells exposed to hyperthermia. In vivo, C57BL/6 mice were pretreated with febuxostat (or saline) before heat exposure, and the Control, Feb, HS, and Feb + HS groups were established. Quantitative proteomics was used to screen for proteins that were differentially expressed under thermal stress. Renal function, histopathology, oxidative stress (ROS, MDA, and SOD levels), expression levels f the cytoprotective protein HO-1, inflammatory cytokine (TNF-α and IL-1β), and apoptosis were thoroughly analyzed.

RESULTS: Proteomic analysis revealed upregulated expression of XOD in the HS group compared with the control group. The activity and expression of the XOD enzyme were considerably higher in a high heat environment. XOD overexpression significantly increased HS-induced oxidative stress, the inflammatory response, and apoptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells. The inhibition of XOD with febuxostat markedly reduced oxidative stress, thereby preventing inflammation and apoptosis and alleviating HS-AKI.

CONCLUSION: XOD-driven oxidative stress is a key pathogenic mechanism in HS-AKI. Febuxostat, a XOD inhibitor, showed protective efficacy in an animal model, highlighting this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Association of enteral nutrition reduction or discontinuation with diarrhea volume and caloric delivery in critically ill adults with diarrhea: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: When critically ill patients receiving enteral nutrition (EN) develop diarrhea, clinicians often reduce or discontinue EN, although evidence supporting this practice is limited. We examined the association between EN management after diarrhea and diarrhea volume in critical care patients.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult intensive care unit patients who developed new-onset diarrhea (Bristol Stool Form Scale ≥6 on 2 consecutive days) during EN. Based on Day 1 EN management, patients were classified as continuation (infusion rate decrease <10 mL/h) or reduction/discontinuation (decrease ≥10 mL/h or complete discontinuation). The primary outcome was cumulative diarrhea volume (grams) on Days 1-2. Cumulative EN calories (kcal) on Days 1-2 was a key secondary outcome. Inverse probability of treatment weighting with regression adjustment accounted for 8 pre-specified confounders. Sensitivity analyses included alternative exposure thresholds and propensity score models.

RESULTS: Of 135 patients analyzed (median age, 74 years; 32% female), 96 (71.1%) continued EN and 39 (28.9%) underwent EN reduction/discontinuation. After adjustment, the reduction/discontinuation group had lower cumulative diarrhea volume on Days 1-2 (adjusted mean difference, -183.4 g; 95% confidence interval [CI], -350.1 to -16.7; p = 0.033) but received substantially fewer calories (-1260.1 kcal; 95% CI, -1464.4 to -1055.9; p < 0.001). The direction of the reduction in diarrhea volume was consistent across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Reducing or discontinuing EN after diarrhea was associated with a modest reduction in diarrhea volume but a substantial caloric deficit. This trade-off should be considered when reducing EN for diarrhea.

articles.title: ALBI-6-A Novel Prognostic Score Combining ALBI and Interleukin-6 in Patients With HCC Treated With Atezolizumab and Bevacizumab.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Despite widespread use of combination immunotherapy in advanced liver cancer, reliable biomarkers for baseline risk stratification remain lacking. The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 has established prognostic relevance in this cancer. We investigated the prognostic value of interleukin-6 and developed a combined score (ALBI-6) integrating interleukin-6 with albumin-bilirubin grade, a marker of liver function.

METHODS: In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, 216 patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab were analysed. Interleukin-6 was measured at baseline, first response, best response, and progression. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n = 98) and a validation set (n = 90). ALBI-6 was derived using Cox regression and evaluated against several established prognostic scores.

RESULTS: Elevated baseline interleukin-6 was consistently associated with worse overall survival and remained independently prognostic after adjustment for tumour and clinical factors (extrahepatic spread, vascular invasion, alpha-fetoprotein, performance status, liver function class). In the validation cohort, ALBI-6 achieved a concordance index of 0.716 and separated patients into three risk groups with significantly different survival (log-rank p = 0.002); ALBI-6 was significantly more discriminative than one comparator score (modified albumin-bilirubin grade, p = 0.040), with numerically higher performance than the remaining comparators. In a separate analysis of the full cohort, ALBI-6 significantly outperformed the CRAFITY score at all assessed time points. Bootstrap validation confirmed model stability.

CONCLUSIONS: ALBI-6 integrates systemic inflammation and liver function into a simple composite index enabling meaningful risk stratification in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with immunotherapy. Prospective external validation is warranted.

articles.title: Psychometric properties of the REACh developmental screening tool for preschool children in Sri Lanka.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To design a culturally appropriate and cost-effective developmental screening tool with better psychometric properties to assess preschool children aged 3 to 5 years.

METHOD: A cross-sectional study was conducted using the second iteration of the Ragama Early Assessment of Children (REACh) tool. Item analysis and revisions were confirmed with consensus agreement. It was piloted and later administered by 28 teachers. The accuracy of findings by teachers and the tool's internal consistency were evaluated. Concurrent validity was confirmed with criterion-standard assessments by a developmental paediatrician. Psychometric properties were assessed using the Kuder-Richardson 20 (KR-20) and kappa statistics. Cut-offs for fine motor, gross motor, receptive language, expressive language, social-emotional, and pre-academic were derived using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.

RESULTS: The tool was administered on 597 children. The accuracy of findings by teachers was 100% for all domains. All KR-20 values for 3- to 4-year-olds were greater than 0.7 except for fine motor (0.629). All KR-20 values for 4- to 5-year-olds were greater than 0.7 except fine motor (0.683) and social-emotional (0.694). The sensitivities for all domains were greater than 0.7 except for receptive language and social-emotional in the 3- to 4-year-olds and for expressive language and pre-academic in the 4- to 5-year-olds.

INTERPRETATION: Acceptable sensitivity for most items in this iteration of the REACh will enable screening and referral to services. The findings suggest that the REACh can be adapted for use in South Asian settings and is suitable for implementation in other low-resource settings.

articles.title: Tumor-Intrinsic HEXB Drives Endothelial-To-Mesenchymal Transition and Confers Resistance to Anti-Angiogenic Therapy in Glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: Although anti-angiogenic (anti-VEGF) therapy is widely used for glioblastoma (GBM), its efficacy is severely limited by acquired resistance. Here, we identify endothelial-mesenchymal transition (Endo-MT) in brain endothelial cells as the primary driver of this resistance, fundamentally modulated by hexosaminidase B (HEXB). Mechanistically, HEXB directly binds and stabilizes heat shock protein 60 (HSP60) by inhibiting its ubiquitination and degradation. This stabilization upregulates insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 (IGFBP1), thereby promoting the Endo-MT process. Addressing its clinical relevance, the combination of a HEXB inhibitor and anti-VEGF therapy exerts potent synergistic therapeutic effects in GBM murine models. Overall, our study establishes HEXB as a key driver of Endo-MT and provides a promising dual-targeting strategy to overcome anti-VEGF resistance in GBM.

articles.title: Trustworthy AI in intensive care: From model performance to clinical decisions.
SfHsp20.2 is required for male fertility by controlling eupyrene sperm bundle morphogenesis and sperm migration in the fall armyworm.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda, is a destructive pest threatening global food security. The sterile insect technique (SIT) is a promising eco-friendly control strategy, which relies on exploring genes regulating male fertility. Small heat shock proteins (sHSPs) act as molecular chaperones and participate in insect reproduction, yet their roles in lepidopteran dimorphic spermatogenesis remain poorly understood.

RESULTS: Here, we functionally characterized a testis-enriched sHSP gene, SfHsp20.2, in S. frugiperda. Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout, we found that loss of SfHsp20.2 caused severe morphological defects in eupyrene sperm bundles and reduced the abundance of apyrene sperm bundles. Mutant sperm could be transferred normally to the female bursa copulatrix but failed to migrate to the spermatheca, eventually leading to male-specific near-sterility. Transcriptome analysis revealed that SfHsp20.2 mutation disturbed energy metabolism and stress response pathways in testes.

CONCLUSION: Our results demonstrate that SfHsp20.2 is essential for dimorphic sperm development and sperm migration. This gene represents a potential candidate target for SIT-based management of S. frugiperda. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: A qualitative evidence synthesis on perinatal screening for sickle cell disease in high-burden countries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sickle cell disease (SCD) screening can improve lives and reduce mortality through prevention and targeted treatment, but screening programmes are not universally available in the settings which could most benefit from them. We aimed to understand the implementation considerations for prenatal and newborn SCD screening programmes in countries with a high livebirth prevalence of SCD using the socioecological model of health.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of qualitative evidence relating to prenatal and newborn screening programmes for SCD in the thirty countries with the highest SCD case to livebirth ratio. We included 18 papers published between 2004 and 2024 that covered nine countries and performed the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme Qualitative Studies Checklist on each. Through recursive interaction with our data, we interpretively developed four themes using reflexive thematic analysis and used the GRADE-CERqual method to appraise our key findings.

RESULTS: We framed our results using the socioecological model of health which organizes influences on health into individual, community, and systems levels. From macro to micro levels, our themes are (1) sustainable SCD screening programmes require financial and political support from government and integration into existing healthcare infrastructure, (2) experiences of and knowledge-sharing about SCD fosters further acceptance and opportunity for newborn screening, (3), the decision to conduct a SCD test has extensive ramifications for both child and family, and (4) prenatal and newborn screening modalities offer parents of affected children different options for action. Our policy suggestions focus on planning for programme sustainability at the outset, leveraging existing community knowledge, alleviating stigma, and providing different testing options for families.

CONCLUSIONS: We identified the need for more qualitative inquiry on systems-level implementation of SCD screening programmes and impact of external funding. We call for decreased stigmatization by supporting knowledge-sharing programmes grounded in local modes of understanding and recognize SCD screening decisions as both consequential to families and shaped by parents' experiences over time.

articles.title: Immune Biomarkers of Islet Transplant Rejection Revealed by Synthetic Immunological Niche.
articles.abstract: Islet transplantation can restore glycemic control in type 1 diabetes, yet heterogeneity of immune responses and transplant outcomes necessitates improved graft monitoring. Since transplanted islets are diffusely engrafted within the liver and inaccessible to biopsy, clinical monitoring relies on blood glucose and C-peptide, which change only after substantial graft injury. Here, we developed a synthetic immunological niche (IN) that captures graft-associated immune responses through serial subcutaneous biopsy. We evaluated the IN across murine syngeneic, allogeneic, and autoimmune islet transplant models, including CD40/CD154 blockade with anti-CD40L. The IN identified immune populations and transcriptomic signatures reflective of the graft and distinguished syngeneic from rejecting allografts. In anti-CD40L-treated allografts, the IN revealed innate immune programs characterized by macrophage- and dendritic cell-associated signatures linked to acceptance versus rejection, whereas untreated allografts showed stronger adaptive immune signatures. Longitudinal IN profiling detected inflammatory activation in accepted allografts, indicating persistent subclinical risk. Finally, in autoimmune allografts treated with anti-CD40L plus rapamycin, IN identified a 13-gene signature that separated early from late rejection and distinguished autoimmune- from alloimmune-associated rejection programs. These findings establish the IN as a platform for identification of early biomarkers of islet graft rejection before overt dysfunction, addressing an unmet need in islet transplant monitoring.

articles.title: The relationship between fear of negative evaluation and social anxiety: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fear of negative evaluation (FNE) is widely regarded as a central cognitive component of social anxiety (SA). However, the strength and stability of the association between FNE and SA, as well as potential moderating factors, remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically synthesize existing evidence on the relationship between FNE and SA and to examine potential moderators.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024619488). A systematic search of major databases was conducted for studies published between January 2010 and April 2025. Eligible studies examined the association between FNE and SA. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled effect sizes, with heterogeneity assessed using Q and I² statistics. Moderator analyses were conducted to explore sources of variability.

RESULTS: A total of 143 studies comprising 146 independent samples (N = 80,285) were included. The pooled correlation between FNE and SA was r = 0.53 (95% CI: 0.50-0.55; I² = 88.62%), indicating a moderate positive association. Significant heterogeneity was observed across studies. Moderator analyses suggested that social anxiety measurement tools and cultural background were associated with variability in effect sizes, with stronger correlations observed in Western samples (r = 0.59) compared to Eastern samples (r = 0.52). In contrast, gender, age, publication year, and FNE measurement tools were not significant moderators. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings, and no evidence of substantial publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis provides robust evidence for a moderate positive association between FNE and SA, suggesting that FNE is an important cognitive component of social anxiety. The strength of this association varies across cultural contexts and measurement approaches, highlighting the importance of contextual and methodological factors in shaping observed effects. However, the substantial heterogeneity and predominance of cross-sectional designs limit causal interpretation. Future longitudinal and cross-cultural studies are needed to clarify the developmental and contextual dynamics of this relationship.

articles.title: Scalp acupuncture coupled with speech-language therapy modulates the ventral-dorsal structural brain network in patients with post-stroke anomia: a randomized clinical and DTI neuroimaging trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scalp acupuncture (SA) is used as adjunctive rehabilitation for post-stroke aphasia, but its effect on naming recovery and structural language-network changes remains unclear. We evaluated SA coupled with speech-language therapy (SLT) in patients with post-stroke anomia and explored diffusion tensor imaging markers of ventral-dorsal structural language networks.

METHODS: This randomized controlled trial recruited 85 patients with post-stroke anomia and randomly assigned them to SA or control. Both groups received conventional stroke treatment and SLT; the SA group additionally received scalp acupuncture synchronously with SLT during needle retention. Treatment was delivered once daily, 5 days/week for 4 weeks. The primary outcome was WAB naming total score. Diffusion tensor imaging assessed white matter integrity and topological properties before and after treatment.

RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the SA group showed greater improvements in the WAB naming total score (P = 0.009), object naming, sentence completion, responsive speech, BNT spontaneous naming, and SAQOL-39 communication. In the ventral-dorsal structural network, the SA group showed smaller changes in the area under the curve (AUC) of small-worldness properties (P = 0.008) and normalized clustering coefficient (P = 0.017), and greater changes in clustering coefficient and local efficiency. In the SA group, the change in small-worldness was negatively correlated with the change in the WAB naming total score (r = -0.451, P = 0.027). The SA group also showed smaller axial diffusivity (AD) changes in the left uncinate fasciculus (P = 0.003, Bonferroni corrected), which correlated negatively with the WAB naming total score change (r = -0.440, P = 0.031). Exploratory adjusted regression showed that SA-group assignment was associated with greater naming improvement after adjustment for baseline naming and clinical covariates.

CONCLUSIONS: SA coupled with SLT was associated with greater naming recovery in patients with post-stroke anomia. The benefit was accompanied by changes in structural language-network topology and white matter integrity, particularly involving the left UF. These findings support further evaluation of scalp acupuncture as an adjunct to language rehabilitation and suggest structural network plasticity as a relevant imaging correlate.

articles.title: Bayesian probabilistic statements for communicating clinical trial results.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical trials are often analyzed using frequentist methods and results are interpreted according to their statistical significance. However, p-values and effect measures such as odds or hazard ratios are poorly understood by researchers and policymakers, and even less by patients and clinicians. Moreover, communicating uncertainty around treatment effects is challenging. Probabilistic statements from Bayesian analyses (e.g., the probability that a drug is more effective than placebo) offer an intuitive way to convey results and uncertainty, may provide insight, and support clinical decision-making. We aimed to (i) empirically evaluate the utility of probabilistic statements by re-analyzing data from previously published trials using Bayesian methods, and (ii) provide instructional examples of how probabilistic statements can be used to communicate and interpret results from clinical trials.

METHODS: We analyzed data on primary outcomes obtained from trials previously published in leading medical journals, using Bayesian methods. We included 169 primary outcomes from 130 negative trials (p-values > 0.05) across various medical fields, and 234 outcomes from 225 positive trials (p-value < 0.05) in oncology. We used uninformative priors for illustration, supplementing them with skeptical priors in sensitivity analyses. We estimated the probabilities that active treatments were more effective or safe than controls, for each outcome. We also estimated probabilities that the treatment effects were above specific thresholds for clinical significance. We described three of the included trials in more detail and additionally analyzed one trial in neurology as didactical case studies, to illustrate the use of probabilistic statements.

RESULTS: So-called negative studies may sometimes yield clinically relevant evidence of an effect: in 26/169 (15%) cases we found > 90% probability that the experimental treatment is better than control; for 12/169 (7%) of them, this probability was > 95%. Conversely, positive trials may not always show evidence of clinically meaningful effects: in 25/234 (11%) of the positive oncology trials, there was less than 50% probability that treatment reduces hazards by 20% or more. Our case studies illustrate how to use probabilistic statements in medical decision making in practice.

CONCLUSIONS: Relying on statistical significance without considering clinical importance can mislead decision-making and potentially harm patients. Probabilistic statements from Bayesian analyses can complement traditional approaches to communicating clinical trial results.

articles.title: "It gives me confidence and value": evaluating All_Ears@UoS patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) group three years on.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: All_Ears@UoS is a thriving patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) group that was established in March 2022. The ethos of All_Ears is to create an enduring partnership between researchers and people with lived experience of hearing loss to shape and inform research. This paper describes the findings from an evaluation to measure the perceived impact, value and engagement of the group. The UK Standards for Public Involvement were used as a framework. These include; Communications, Governance, Impact, Working together, Support and learning and Inclusive opportunities.

METHODS: Two surveys were co-designed with members of All_Ears and shared via an online platform to evaluate what was working well and what could be improved from the group members' and researchers' perspectives. Each survey combined demographic questions, rating scale questions to measure satisfaction and open-text questions to gather feedback. Descriptive statistics were used to describe the satisfaction and demographic data. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to analyse the free-text responses.

RESULTS: Strengths aligning to several of the UK Standards for Public Involvement were identified. Thematic analysis of group member responses developed six themes, encompassing the perceived value of the group for research, opportunities for learning and raising awareness, the benefits of the group, aspects that were working well or less well, and considerations around diversity and inclusivity. Four themes were developed from the analysis of researcher responses. Three themes reflected strong support for PPIE within research, while one focused on strengths and challenges in how the group was organised and run. Suggested areas for improvement were to enhance training opportunities to develop skills to support involvement and greater flexibility around meeting scheduling. Group members suggested that a faster reimbursement process is necessary while researchers highlighted a need for increased visibility of public involvement within the University.

CONCLUSIONS: This evaluation has highlighted the perceived value, impact and benefits of embedding enduring PPIE on research and at an individual and societal level from the group members' and researchers' perspectives. We hope the findings enable biomedical and clinical researchers to see the value of building partnerships with patients and the public.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: ACCEPT 3.0: Recalibrating ACute COPD Exacerbation Prediction Tool (ACCEPT) for global use.
authors: NOVELTY Scientific Community and NOVELTY study investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ACute COPD Exacerbation Prediction Tool (ACCEPT) is an algorithm for predicting 12-month risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations. To make it suitable for international use, we externally validated and recalibrated ACCEPT 2.0 to incorporate country-specific background exacerbation risk, using multi-country data from NOVELTY (a NOVEL observational longiTudinal studY).

METHODS: Our study cohort included patients aged [Formula: see text]40 years with physician-diagnosed COPD and [Formula: see text]30 days of follow-up. We predicted the occurrence of any moderate-to-severe (primary endpoint) and severe (secondary) exacerbations at 12 months, using country-level random effects to account for between-country differences in background exacerbation risks unexplained by predictor effects. We assessed model performance via discrimination, calibration, and net benefit.

RESULTS: The analysis sample comprised 5,181 patients (59.4% male, mean age at baseline 66.5 years) from 18 countries, with a mean follow-up of 357 days. 12-month risks ranged between 0.11 and 0.46 (mean = 0.26) for moderate-to-severe and 0.03-0.21 (mean = 0.08) for severe exacerbations. Without country-level adjustment, ACCEPT 2.0's area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.73 (95% CI 0.72-0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI 0.73-0.78) for moderate-to-severe and severe exacerbations, respectively. However, ACCEPT 2.0 consistently overpredicted risks (observed-to-expected [O/E] risk ratio = 0.57 [95% CI 0.54-0.60] and 0.51 [95% CI 0.46-0.56]). After country-level recalibration, ACCEPT 3.0 showed similar AUROCs (0.75 and 0.76) but substantially improved calibration (O/E ratios: 0.99 [95% CI 0.94-1.05] and 0.99 [95% CI 0.90-1.09]). The net benefit of ACCEPT 3.0 exceeded ACCEPT 2.0 across treatment thresholds of 5%-20%.

CONCLUSION: Recalibrating ACCEPT 2.0 with country-level effects significantly improved calibration of COPD exacerbation risks. The resulting ACCEPT 3.0 is expected to provide higher clinical utility across a range of treatment thresholds.

articles.title: Less regurgitation without reverse remodeling: what the PROVE trial teaches us about functional tricuspid regurgitation.
High diversity and novel host associations of bat haemosporidian parasites in Cambodia: insights from a nationwide bat survey and multilocus analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemosporidian ("malaria") parasites are a diverse group of vector-borne apicomplexan parasites that infect a wide range of vertebrate hosts, including humans. Bats harbour a remarkable diversity of haemosporidians and are considered important hosts in the evolution of mammalian haemosporidian lineages, yet parasite diversity, host associations, and evolutionary relationships remain poorly understood, particularly in biodiversity-rich Southeast Asia.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide molecular survey of 1180 bats representing 34 species across Cambodia and combined extensive sampling with multilocus phylogenetic and ecological analyses to investigate haemosporidian diversity, host associations, evolutionary relationships, and ecological correlates of infection.

RESULTS: Haemosporidian infections were detected in 12.9% of the sampled bats and comprised diverse Polychromophilus and Hepatocystis taxa, including several novel host associations. Notably, Hepatocystis was detected in Emballonuridae for the first time and occurred across multiple bat families. We substantially expand sampling of a previously described Scotophilus-associated Polychromophilus lineage and demonstrate its remarkable genetic conservation across geographic regions. In contrast, Hepatocystis parasites exhibited substantial genetic diversity across multiple host taxa. Multi-gene analyses expanded phylogenetic representation of bat-associated Hepatocystis and revealed close relationships between some bat- and squirrel-associated lineages. These data further suggest considerable diversity among Asian Hepatocystis parasites and phylogenetic patterns consistent with diversification across Asian host groups. Ecological analyses indicated that the infection varied more among host species and sampling sites than with measured host traits or landscape attributes and revealed pronounced seasonal differences in infection probability together with lower infection rate in more densely populated landscapes.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings expand current knowledge of bat haemosporidian diversity, host associations, and evolutionary relationships in Southeast Asia. Novel host associations, including the first record of Hepatocystis in Emballonuridae, highlight previously undocumented parasite diversity in regional bat communities. Infection was structured principally by host species and by conditions at individual roosting sites rather than by broader landscape composition, indicating that fine-scale roost ecology and vector biology are the more promising targets for understanding transmission in bats. Together, these findings contribute to a broader understanding of diversification and host associations in mammalian malaria parasites.

articles.title: Trigeminal sensory neuropathy developing as a late complication after the treatment of surgically induced necrotizing scleritis following pterygium surgery: a case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgically induced necrotizing scleritis (SINS) is an immune-mediated disease that occurs infrequently after ocular procedures, with latency ranging from days to years. There are various early and late complications that can negatively affect quality of life after SINS. This case report aims to present late trigeminal sensory neuropathy (TSN), corresponding in this patient to painful post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy (ICHD-3 13.1.2.3), as a complication in a patient who developed SINS after pterygium surgery (PS).

CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old woman was admitted to our clinic for cosmetic surgical removal of bilateral pterygium. She had an unremarkable medical history. Following the 10th postoperative day in the right eye, the patient complained of eye irritation, visual impairment, and hypersensitivity to light. On biomicroscopic examination, the conjunctival autograft on the sclera had melted, and a choroidal reflex was visible. A multi-layered amniotic membrane graft was applied to the erosion during our initial repair; however, the graft deteriorated within one week. Conjunctival covering surgery with a pericardial patch was performed on the patient's area of scleral melting. Rheumatological evaluation was unremarkable, with no evidence of an underlying systemic disease. The patient, who had been undergoing systemic pulse steroid treatment and topical cyclosporine/steroid treatment for scleritis, was diagnosed with painful post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy in the neurology department 3 months after her third surgery. This diagnosis was based on persistent symptoms (photophobia, dental pain, and headache) that did not respond to systemic and topical treatments for SINS. The patient who was treated for TSN responded to oral gabapentin treatment.

CONCLUSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of painful post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy as a late complication of SINS following pterygium surgery. Physicians should consider this diagnosis in patients with persistent neuropathic pain after SINS.

articles.title: Prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a widespread condition affecting individuals globally in the aftermath of disasters. For this review, the disaster-affected population refers to individuals or populations who have experienced a potentially traumatic event with psychosocial consequences. The current review aims to assess the prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in the present study. Relevant keywords were identified and used to search databases, including Scopus, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane, as well as websites and reference lists, to identify eligible studies. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow chart was used for the final included studies to reveal the results. The current review conducted a critical appraisal of the included studies by using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) quality evaluation. Meta-analysis using Jeffreys's Amazing Statistics Program (JASP) software and manual analysis was done to assess the psychosocial factors and conceptual framework.

RESULTS: A total of 1370 documents were identified from the databases, and 151 documents were duplicates. Following title/abstract screening, 1178 studies were excluded, 21 full text not retrieved, and 20 studies were included for the final results. The critical appraisal results found that more than half of the studies demonstrated good methodological quality. The results revealed that the pooled prevalence of PTSD was 38%, with young populations disproportionately affected, although no significant associations were found with age group, disaster type, or region. Nineteen psychosocial risk factors were identified, prominently including loss of family members or pets and property damage. The conceptual framework highlights the interplay between traumatic events and psychosocial factors in PTSD outcomes.

CONCLUSION: The findings underscore the need for multidisciplinary collaboration among mental health professionals, long-term intervention strategies, and evidence-based practices to address India's mental health challenges.

articles.title: Cell wall integrity and elicitor peptide signaling modulate jasmonic acid-mediated camalexin production in Arabidopsis.
articles.abstract: Plant cell walls constitute dynamic barriers that are essential for defense against pathogens. Beyond a structural role in blocking pathogen infection, innate mechanisms monitor cell wall integrity (CWI) in Arabidopsis thaliana and trigger local responses where integrity is impaired. Here, we show that THESEUS1 (THE1)-dependent CWI signaling induces accumulation of the antimicrobial metabolite camalexin upon cell wall damage (CWD) caused by isoxaben (ISX)-induced cellulose biosynthesis inhibition or infection with the phytopathogenic fungus Colletotrichum higginsianum. CWD caused by ISX alters THE1 plasma membrane nanodomain organization and involves calcium signaling components that modulate camalexin production. Induction of camalexin requires jasmonic acid (JA) signaling and JA-dependent expression of the transcription factor MYB47. In line with its antagonistic function on CWI signaling, the plant elicitor peptide Pep3 suppresses camalexin biosynthesis downstream of THE1 by inhibiting JA-dependent pathways. Our findings reveal a regulatory network where CWI and Pep3 signaling modulate antimicrobial defense via JA-mediated camalexin production. This network requires input from independent CWD-induced pathways, providing insights into how plants balance distinct defense processes in response to cell wall stress.

articles.title: The risk of not imaging: a three-scenario framework for justification.
articles.abstract: A recurring argument in radiological protection holds that the radiation risk of an imaging examination must be weighed against the clinical risk of not performing it. The argument is applied inconsistently, and evidence on that clinical risk remains sparse compared with the extensive literature on radiation risk. This asymmetry masks an important distinction: the clinical risk of not imaging is not uniformly high. We propose a three-scenario framework for medical imaging, illustrated using computed tomography. In Scenario 1, the harm of withholding or delaying imaging is well documented and substantially exceeds the radiation risk, as in appendicitis, stroke, pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, and polytrauma. In Scenario 2, imaging is repeated at low incremental yield, exposure accumulates, and guidance on intervals is limited, so radiation risk may outweigh marginal diagnostic gain. In Scenario 3, evidence on both sides is insufficient, and decisions are best supported by clinical decision rules and shared decision making. The framework addresses procedure-level and individual justification, and is confined to the balance between clinical and radiation risk. We suggest that clinical specialty organizations develop guidance on imaging frequency that incorporates review of cumulative exposure, and that ICRP address the place of such exposure within the justification framework.

articles.title: Alkylating Agent-Induced FANCL Impairment Damages Pulmonary Arterial, Venous, and Microvascular Endothelial Cells and Predisposes to PAH/PVOD.
articles.abstract: Alkylating chemotherapies such as mitomycin C (MMC) and cisplatin (CDDP) are associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD) features, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using established MMC and newly developed CDDP rat models, we found that both agents induced PAH/PVOD, as evidenced by elevated right ventricular systolic pressure, pulmonary arterial, venous and microvascular remodeling, and right ventricular dysfunction, with MMC causing more severe pathology. In cultured pulmonary arterial, venous, and microvascular endothelial cells, MMC and CDDP induced elevated DNA damage, apoptosis, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, together with impaired angiogenic capacity, proliferation, and barrier junction. These phenotypical changes were accompanied by conserved Fanconi anemia complementation group L (FANCL) downregulation. FANCL deficiency in mice drove spontaneous and exacerbated CDDP‑induced PAH/PVOD, whereas AAV‑mediated FANCL rescue or treatment with a DNA protector, amifostine, significantly attenuated the disease pathogenesis in mouse and rat models. Collectively, this study establishes a novel CDDP‑induced rat model, identifies a conserved FANCL-DNA damage-endothelial dysfunction mechanistic axis underlying PAH/PVOD induced by MMC or CDDP, and highlights FANCL rescue and DNA damage inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies for this severe form of pulmonary vascular disease.

articles.title: The contribution of circadian, sleep and hormonal rhythms to pregnancy outcomes: an opportunity for improved management of women during pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms are fundamental regulators of physiology and play a critical role in reproductive success. During pregnancy, precise temporal coordination of endocrine, metabolic, and immune processes is required to support maternal adaptation, placental function, and foetal development. Disruption of circadian rhythms through environmental factors such as light at night, shift work, or sleep disorders has emerged as a significant risk factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, gestational diabetes, and preeclampsia. In this review, we synthesize current evidence linking circadian and sleep disruption to pregnancy complications, with a particular focus on the temporal regulation of key hormones, including progesterone, oestrogen, cortisol, oxytocin, and melatonin. We discuss how altered rhythmicity of hormone production and tissue responsiveness may impair target tissue function, maternal cardiovascular adaptation, and the development of gestational diabetes. We highlight emerging mechanistic insights into molecular clock regulation across reproductive tissues and its interaction with environmental cues. Finally, we outline opportunities for clinical translation, including chronobiology-informed diagnostics and chronotherapeutic strategies, to improve pregnancy management and reduce the burden of adverse outcomes.
