articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: The recent International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation consensus statement on frailty provides a crucial framework for operationalizing objective frailty metrics and prehabilitation in adult lung transplant candidates. However, translating adult frailty constructs to pediatric candidates with end-stage lung disease presents unique physiological and developmental challenges, as measures of physical performance must account for ongoing linear growth, somatic maturation, and neurodevelopmental trajectories. These complexities are heightened in critically ill pediatric patients, particularly those bridged to transplantation via mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), where distinguishing acute illness-attributable neuromuscular deconditioning from systemic, irreversible frailty remains an obstacle. The creation and incorporation of developmentally appropriate frailty measures into pediatric transplant evaluation will be essential to refine candidate selection, optimize pre-transplant functional capacity, and improve post-transplant outcomes. Accomplishing this task will require multidisciplinary collaboration involving critical care, lung transplant, nutritional support, rehabilitation, and behavioral health team members. Key priorities include validating pediatric-specific functional tools, establishing longitudinal tracking of sarcopenia and growth, implementing age-appropriate, play-based prehabilitation paired with nutritional support, and standardizing assessment across the transplant trajectory, including for patients bridged to transplant with inpatient mechanical support such as ECMO or lung assist devices, as well as those managed in the outpatient setting with chronic mechanical respiratory support.

articles.title: Persistent Sex Gaps and the Screening-Treatment Paradox in Hypertension Management: 25 Years of Self-Reported Swiss Health Survey Data.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess how sex differences in hypertension management have evolved over a 25-year period in Switzerland, focusing on screening, diagnosis, treatment, and control, and to determine whether age modifies these differences.

METHODS: We analyzed self-reported data from six consecutive Swiss Health Surveys (1997-2022) from samples representative of the Swiss population. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic and lifestyle covariates. Age-stratified analyses were conducted using age >50 years as a proxy for menopausal status.

RESULTS: Among 94,785 participants (55.3% female), females consistently had a higher likelihood than males of reporting blood pressure screening (e.g., adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.62, 95% CI 1.50-1.75 in 2022), with no narrowing of the trend over time. In contrast, from 2012 onward, females had a lower likelihood of reporting a diagnosis of hypertension (e.g., aOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.68-0.79 in 2022) or antihypertensive medication use among those diagnosed (e.g., aOR 0.84, 95% CI 0.74-0.95 in 2022), with gaps widening over time. No sex differences in self-reported blood pressure control were found among those reporting treatment. Age-stratified analyses showed consistent sex differences across both age groups, though the onset and magnitude varied.

CONCLUSION: Despite comparable treatment outcomes, our findings show a paradoxical sex difference in earlier stages of hypertension management, higher screening yet lower treatment in females.

articles.title: Diaphragm ultrasound beyond numbers: A call for Bayesian reasoning in critical care.
articles.abstract: Diaphragm ultrasound (DUS) has become a widely available tool in critical care for assessing respiratory muscle function, monitoring ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction (VIDD), and supporting weaning prediction. However, its expanding use as a routine or screening examination, including in clinical scenarios where the pre-test probability of clinically relevant diaphragm dysfunction is low, raises concerns about diagnostic overuse. This narrative opinion article argues that DUS should be understood through the lens of Bayesian reasoning applied to clinical decision-making. The framework is intended to strengthen clinical reasoning rather than to assert superiority over alternative diagnostic strategies. Without explicit estimation of pre-test probability and prior definition of decision thresholds, the positive predictive value of DUS decreases, favoring false-positive findings, physiological overinterpretation, and potentially inappropriate clinical decisions. The available evidence indicates substantial heterogeneity in protocols, populations, and cut-off values, limiting the generalizability of findings and reinforcing the need for clinical contextualization. We propose a conceptual repositioning of DUS as a confirmatory and integrative tool, grounded in genuine clinical uncertainty, explicit Bayesian reasoning, and value-based care.

articles.title: Long-Term Psychological, Cognitive and Quality of Life Outcomes in Covid-19 Severe Acute Respiratory Failure patients managed with Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ICU admission with severe acute respiratory failure (SARF) can result in extended recovery and rehabilitation. We sought to evaluate the long-term psychological, cognitive and quality of life outcomes of Covid-19 SARF patients to inform our understanding of the longer-term health burden to survivors.

DESIGN: Retrospective single centre cohort study.

SETTING AND PATIENTS: All surviving SARF Covid-19 patients admitted to a regional ECMO centre in London between March 2020 - February 2022 attending ICU follow-up clinic.

INTERVENTIONS: None MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: CORE ICU validated outcome measures alongside clinical interview. Of the surviving (n = 116) patients, 97 (83.6%) attended at least one ICU follow-up clinic. For those attending multiple reviews, despite an improvement in quality of life, depression, anxiety and PTSD were no different between 0 - 2 years and 2 - 4 years after discharge. Comprehensive long-term reviews held between 18 months and 4 years [ IQR 17.5 m - 44.8 m ] following discharge, n = 87) found prevalence of depression (44%), anxiety (25%) and PTSD (33%). Half were still receiving care from specialist healthcare teams. Cognitive impairment was seen in 63% and functional impairment in 31%. Over a quarter (26%) remained not working. Depression and PTSD scores were lower in those who had returned to work. Thematic analysis of long-term reviews revealed six key themes: a plateaued recovery, the traumatising experience, forgetfulness, family strain, appreciation and gratitude, and awareness of the fragility of life.

CONCLUSION: Despite improvements to quality of life, impairments in psychological, cognitive and aspects of health-related quality of life can persist as long as four years after discharge in SARF ECMO survivors. Qualitative findings illustrated the enduring impact of critical illness alongside themes of gratitude an altered life perspective.

articles.title: Association between complement de-escalation and prognosis in sepsis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Substantial evidence indicates that sepsis is accompanied by intense complement activation. This study aims to systematically evaluate the association between reduced complement activation levels and the prognosis in septic patients after treatment.

METHODS: A meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. The search databases included Web of Science, PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, SinoMed, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, and VIP Database. The search timeframe spanned from the inception of each database to June 2025. Included studies were required to report cases with further reductions in complement activation levels following predefined treatments, while concurrently recording mortality and other biochemical indicators. Subsequently, a meta-analysis assessed mortality, inflammatory biomarkers (WBC, CRP, and IL-6), APACHE II scores, and indicators reflecting renal function (SCr and BUN) levels.

RESULTS: A total of 7,694 articles were retrieved, and 11 studies were ultimately included after screening. Although IL-6 (MD: -196.83; 95% CI: -329.16, -64.49; P < 0.001), CRP (MD: -9.09; 95% CI: -14.44 -3.74; P < 0.001) and APACHE II scores (MD: -4.55; 95% CI: -6.98 -2.12; P < 0.001) decreased significantly, reduced complement levels following multiple treatments in septic patients were not associated with lower mortality rates (RR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.63, 1.71; P > 0.05). Additionally, there were no significant differences in WBC, SCr, and BUN levels.

CONCLUSION: The reduction in complement activation levels following treatment in septic patients is associated with disease severity scores and certain inflammatory biomarkers, but is not correlated with mortality.

articles.title: Psoriasiform Plaques as a Cutaneous Clue to Persistent Inflammation in Infantile Kawasaki Disease.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease is typically associated with a polymorphous exanthem, but persistent psoriasiform or pustular plaques during the acute illness may be mistaken for infection, drug eruption, or a separate inflammatory dermatosis. We report a 4-month-old boy with Kawasaki disease who developed erythematous scaly plaques with pustules during the acute phase, in temporal association with recurrent mucosal inflammation and evolving coronary artery dilation requiring repeat intravenous immunoglobulin. Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with parakeratosis, loss of the granular layer, neutrophilic exocytosis, papillary dermal edema, and dilated capillaries, supporting psoriasiform dermatitis in the setting of Kawasaki disease. This case highlights the value of clinicopathologic correlation when atypical plaques arise in Kawasaki disease and suggests that such eruptions should prompt careful assessment for ongoing systemic inflammation and coronary involvement.

articles.title: Opioid use and naloxone-identified suspected opioid-related adverse events in a tertiary pediatric hospital: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Opioids are essential for analgesia and sedation in pediatric inpatient care, particularly in perioperative and intensive care settings. However, their use requires careful monitoring because children, especially infants and critically ill patients, may be vulnerable to respiratory, cardiovascular, and neurological adverse effects.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study evaluated opioid administration records and naloxone-identified suspected opioid-related adverse-event episodes at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Brazil from January 2019 to September 2024. Opioid administration records were identified from hospital pharmacy dispensing data. Medical records of patients with naloxone administration records were reviewed to classify naloxone indication, opioid involvement, clinical manifestations, hospital setting, underlying conditions, and short-term outcomes.

RESULTS: During the study period, 154,867 opioid administration records were identified. A total of 284 naloxone administration records were screened. After medical record review, 171 naloxone administrations did not meet criteria for suspected opioid-related adverse-event episodes and were excluded from the main adverse-event analysis. The final naloxone-identified sample included 112 episodes. Events occurred predominantly in intensive care settings, especially the cardiac intensive care unit. The most frequently documented manifestations were bradycardia, oxygen desaturation, apnea, chest wall rigidity, drowsiness/somnolence, and worsened respiratory pattern. Most episodes improved after naloxone administration.

CONCLUSION: Naloxone-identified suspected opioid-related adverse-event episodes were uncommon relative to the total volume of opioid administration records and were concentrated in clinically complex pediatric inpatients. These findings support risk-stratified monitoring, standardized documentation of naloxone indications, and continued opioid stewardship in tertiary pediatric care.

articles.title: Estimates, temporal evolution, and contributors of the stroke burden due to air pollution and non-optimal temperature across G20 nations, 1990-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Air pollution and non-optimal temperature are major modifiable environmental risk factors for stroke. This study assessed their attributable stroke burden across G20 countries from 1990 to 2023 and projected trends to 2040.

METHODS: Using data from the GBD 2023, we analyzed age-standardized mortality (ASMR) and disability-adjusted life year rates (ASDR) for stroke attributable to air pollution (ambient particulate matter and household air pollution from solid fuels) and non-optimal temperature (high and low), and stratified according to the Socio-demographic Index (SDI). Joinpoint regression, decomposition analysis, and ARIMA modeling were employed.

RESULTS: The ASMR for stroke attributable to these environmental risks in G20 countries declined from 52.81 (95% UI: 32.05-71.82) to 17.46 (95% UI: 10.58-24.53) per 100,000 from 1990 to 2023, with an estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) of -3.44% (95% CI: -3.57 to -3.30). The ASDR declined from 1,148.95 (95% UI: 693.62-1,576.02) to 394.91 (95% UI: 229.91-550.54) per 100,000 (EAPC: -3.29%, 95% CI: -3.41 to -3.17). This was driven by a sharp decrease in household air pollution burden. However, burdens attributable to ambient particulate matter and high temperature increased or remained stable, exhibiting marked geographical disparities, with low- and middle-SDI G20 nations bearing a disproportionately high burden. Projections to 2040 indicate a continued overall decline, but burdens attributable to ambient particulate matter and high temperature are expected to persist.

CONCLUSIONS: While progress has been made, ambient particulate matter pollution and high temperature remained important contributors to the estimated GBD-attributable stroke burden in the G20, underscoring the need for targeted intervention.

articles.title: Multi-criteria proton treatment planning incorporating spot boosting for prompt gamma in-vivo range verification.
articles.abstract: Objective.Prompt gamma (PG) detection enables beam range verification and margin reduction in proton therapy, but its effectiveness is limited by counting statistics. Spot boosting has been proposed to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio by increasing the number of protons in selected spots of a pencil beam scanning treatment plan. This work integrates PG monitoring into an multi-criteria optimization (MCO) framework to investigate trade-offs between proton counts in boosted spots and dosimetric metrics.Approach.Intensity modulated proton therapy (IMPT) plans for a prostate-tumor and a brain-tumor patient were optimized in OpenTPS. Dose, LET weighted dose (LETxdose) and PG distributions were simulated for each pencil beam using the fast Monte Carlo (MC) engine MCSquare. For each field, ten candidate spots were selected based on three metrics quantifying the quality of PG monitoring and an even spatial distribution across the clinical target volume. Initial pencil beam weights and corresponding dose and LETxdose distributions were imported into an MCO framework for re-optimization, simultaneously considering both dosimetric goals and boosting objectives.Main results.Boosting up to 5 • 108protons/spot maintained the plan quality without violating constraints in the prostate case. In the brain case, spot boosting required moderate deviations from the initial target dose constraints. For both cases, only minor boosting gains were obtained by relaxing dose metrics for organs at risk.Significance.This study is the first to visualize spot boosting trade-offs via Pareto fronts to support an informed decision, integrating verification quality aspects into the treatment planning stage. The approach enables selection of plans that preserve dose and LETxdose objectives while enhancing PG signal in targeted spots for reliable in-vivo range verification. The framework is broadly applicable and can provide a strategy for embedding verification-driven objectives into treatment optimization beyond PG monitoring.

articles.title: Influence of a long air gap and a ratio 15:1 antiscatter grid on pediatric fluoroscopy and angiography image quality.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveX-ray angiography and fluoroscopy systems are used to diagnose and treat congenital heart disease in pediatric patients. Among the substantial variabilities in this clinical patient population is that patient weight ranges from <1 kg premature infants to large adolescents. The primary aim of this work was to assess whether an air gap or antiscatter grid is more efficient to mitigate the detrimental influence of scatter radiation on pediatric image quality.ApproachThe experimental approach was guided by a 2 year review of pediatric patient imaging conditions. Uniform density water-equivalent phantoms with thickness in the range 6-24 cm were used. For each phantom thickness, the X-ray technique was manually set to mimic the technique selected by automatic dose rate control. The influence of four combinations of air gap and ratio 15:1 antiscatter grid on test object SNR was measured. The air gap was varied by changing the X-ray source to detector distance from 107 to 120 cm. The analytical methods estimated pixel-specific snr2 contributions to object SNR2, thus providing for the use of iodine disks and pediatric implantable devices as test objects.Main resultsPatient weight ranged from 0.5 to 134 kg. The relationship between patient water equivalent thickness and weight was demonstrated. For all phantom thicknesses, object SNR was highest using a long air gap, non-grid technique. Decreasing the air gap between the phantom and detector and use of the anti-scatter grid both degraded SNR. These major findings were consistent between iodine disks and clinical devices as test objects.SignificanceThe findings of this phantom study suggest that a long air gap, non-grid imaging technique may improve radiation dose efficiency of fluoroscopy and angiography imaging across a broad range of pediatric patient sizes.&#xD.

articles.title: Silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates for ultrasound-activated immunomodulatory therapy of MRSA pneumonia.
articles.abstract: The clinical management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pneumonia is hindered by biofilm infections and cytokine storms. A key challenge is the lack of real-time monitoring tools for the inflammatory microenvironment during treatment. In this study, we developed a theranostic platform (CS@EAgNP) using TPP-modified chitosan to load silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates (AgNP) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). This system combines ultrasound imaging with ultrasound-activated therapy. The CS@EAgNP nanoparticles can act as an excellent ultrasound contrast enhancer. In vivo ultrasound imaging indicated that AgNP generated significantly enhanced echo signals at the infection site, providing real-time and highcontrast visualization of the inflammatory foci that was unattainable with normal lung tissue.Moreover, these nanoparticles release NO, silver and EGCG under ultrasound. The NO and silver penetrate biofilms to kill MRSA, while EGCG scavenges ROS and modulates inflammation. This reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and TNF-α, mitigating the cytokine storm. In vivo results further confirm that this image-guided strategy achieves significant bacterial clearance and promotes lung tissue regeneration without detectable toxicity to major organs. This integrated approach bridges diagnosis and treatment, offering a promising solution for managing MRSA pneumonia.

articles.title: When the fungus is susceptible, but the patient is not: reading antifungal susceptibility from bench to bedside.
articles.abstract: Antifungal susceptibility testing is increasingly available and is central to the management of invasive, refractory, recurrent, and breakthrough fungal infections. However, minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) are not self-interpreting results. They measure in vitro antifungal activity under defined laboratory conditions, but clinical outcome is shaped by species identification, method, breakpoint or epidemiological cutoff values, availability, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic exposure, infection site, fungal burden, source control, biofilm formation, and host immunity. Non-classic fungal drug-response phenotypes, including tolerance, heteroresistance, persistence, adaptive resistance, trailing growth, paradoxical growth, and biofilm-associated survival, can further weaken the link between a susceptible MIC and therapeutic success. In this Personal View, we argue that antifungal susceptibility testing should be understood as a shared clinical-laboratory interface rather than as a standalone laboratory result. The microbiologist makes the MIC interpretable by defining organism, method, interpretive threshold, confidence, and need for confirmation; the clinician makes it clinically useful by integrating exposure, site, source control, toxicity, interactions, and clinical trajectory. Future reports should therefore move from isolated MICs towards structured interpretation, uncertainty flags, and interpretive guidance, while avoiding forced susceptible-resistant categorisation when evidence is incomplete. Such reporting can strengthen stewardship, surveillance, and patient-level decisions across tertiary, routine, and resource-constrained settings, without overstating what MICs can predict alone at the bedside.

articles.title: Current Practices in Antenatal CMV Testing and Management in Belgium.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe current practices regarding antenatal cytomegalovirus (CMV) testing, valaciclovir treatment and termination of pregnancy (TOP) in Belgium, where universal antenatal CMV screening is not recommended and testing during pregnancy is not reimbursed.

METHOD: We conducted an online survey of practitioners involved in antenatal care or specialist management of CMV (obstetricians, midwives, general practitioners, fetal medicine specialists) between September and November 2024. Quantitative data from complete questionnaires were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and responses to open questions underwent thematic analysis.

RESULTS: We analyzed 298 complete responses. Most respondents (89.4%) reported requesting antenatal CMV testing despite antenatal CMV screening not being recommended in Belgium and the absence of routine reimbursement for CMV testing during pregnancy. Antenatal testing may have included both determination of maternal serostatus and testing intended to detect primary maternal infection or seroconversion. Testing objectives included fetal imaging follow-up, hygiene counseling, and prevention of vertical transmission with valaciclovir, while considering TOP was less frequently cited. TOP was perceived as occurring at all stages after maternal infection, but predominantly in cases of severe fetal involvement. Among fetal medicine specialists, 51.7% prescribed valaciclovir routinely, while others prescribed it non-routinely. Treatment acceptance and adherence were perceived as good, with cost identified as the main barrier for treatment acceptance and high pill burden identified as the main barrier for treatment adherence.

CONCLUSION: Antenatal CMV testing was commonly reported among respondents, despite heterogeneous use due to cost barriers. TOP may occur even in cases without severe fetal involvement, underscoring the need for high-quality counseling and updated national guidance.

articles.title: Clinicopathological Profile of Disordered Proliferative Endometrium in Anovulatory Abnormal Uterine Bleeding and Determinants of Response to Levonorgestrel-Releasing Intrauterine System Therapy.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.abstract: Disordered proliferative endometrium is an under-recognized endometrial lesion, with limited evidence regarding its clinicopathological characteristics and predictors of treatment response. The present study aimed to characterize the clinical and histomorphological features of disordered proliferative endometrium, evaluate the response to treatment with a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, and identify the clinicopathological determinants of progesterone responsiveness. A 3-year cross-sectional study was conducted involving 124 women with histopathologically confirmed disordered proliferative endometrium. Clinical, demographic, radiological, and histopathological parameters were analysed, and the treatment response to the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system was assessed after 3 months using pictorial blood assessment chart scores and symptom improvement. The median age at presentation was 42 years, with 59.7% of patients belonging to the perimenopausal age group (40-49 y). Heavy menstrual bleeding was the predominant presenting complaint (68.5%). Most patients were overweight or obese (64.5%), and 85.5% had anaemia. Hypertension (22.6%), hypothyroidism (13.7%), and diabetes mellitus (12.1%) were the most common associated comorbidities, while coexisting gynaecological pathologies were identified in 23.4% of cases. Histopathological examination consistently demonstrated focal glandular crowding and cystic glandular dilatation, with gland-to-stroma ratios ranging from 30:70 to 60:40; an irregular glandular architecture was observed in 93.5% of cases. Following levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system insertion, 69.4% of patients experienced significant clinical improvement. A higher body mass index was the only independent predictor of reduced treatment response. Disordered proliferative endometrium predominantly affects perimenopausal women with heavy menstrual bleeding and metabolic risk factors, exhibits characteristic histomorphological features, and responds well to progesterone therapy in most cases. Recognition of factors influencing the treatment response may facilitate individualized management and improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Immunoregulatory gene GIMAP6 suppresses lethal atherosclerotic vasculopathy and ischemic heart failure.
articles.abstract: Controlling hyperlipidemia has reduced but not eliminated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) as a major cause of human mortality. Here, we report that loss of the immunoregulatory gene GTPase of immunity-associated protein 6 (Gimap6) in mice causes an inflammatory vasculopathy and accelerated atherosclerosis in the absence of hyperlipidemia. These vascular abnormalities cause progressive cardiac ischemia, myocardial infarction, and heart failure, culminating in early death. GIMAP6 loss precipitates early endothelial barrier failure and a mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS)-PPARγ-CD36 lipid-influx cascade that lowers the threshold for foam-cell formation and induces IL-6/MCP-1/TNF-mediated inflammation. Human hypomorphic GIMAP6 variants, including the African-ancestry-enriched V65I allele, are associated with altered monocyte redox balance, increased CD36-mediated lipid uptake, and early ASCVD. Thus, GIMAP6 is a crucial safeguard for vascular integrity that restrains endothelial dysfunction, macrophage foam cell generation, and inflammation that can cause lethal ASCVD independently of systemic hyperlipidemia.

articles.title: Native pathogen-phage networks reveal multilayered defense and gut-active anti-phage immunity.
articles.abstract: Bacteriophages drive pathogen evolution, yet the mechanisms governing phage susceptibility in native bacterial backgrounds, and their consequences within mammalian hosts, remain poorly understood. Here, we mapped >1,000 interactions between 20 diverse Salmonella isolates and 52 wild phages from global disease reservoirs, integrating genome-scale fitness profiling with comparative genomics. Receptor identity and surface phase variation, including Hin-mediated flagellar switching, explained ∼67% of phage susceptibility patterns, identifying cell-surface architecture as the major determinant of phage host range in Salmonella. Among resistance phenotypes not explained by surface features, we discovered anti-phage-packaging agent (AppA), a prophage-encoded defense factor that abrogates phage replication within its native host. AppA inhibits phage DNA packaging through functional mimicry of a terminase assembly interface, revealing a previously unrecognized mechanism of phage defense. AppA is expressed under conditions encountered during mammalian infection and suppresses phage expansion in the murine gut, demonstrating that prophage-encoded single-gene defenses can shape disease outcomes in vivo.

articles.title: Immunological Discordance in People with HIV Receiving Contemporary Integrase Inhibitor-Based Antiretroviral Therapy: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study from Türkiye.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Immunological discordance, the persistence of CD4+ T-cell depletion despite sustained virological suppression on antiretroviral therapy (ART) in people with HIV, remains incompletely characterized in the contemporary integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) era. A multicenter, retrospective cohort study was conducted through chart review at four Turkish tertiary infectious diseases units across three regions. Adults with HIV-1 who had received ART for at least 12 consecutive months were eligible. The primary outcome was immunological discordance, defined as a current CD4+ count <350 cells/µL despite plasma HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL. Associations were examined using Firth-penalized logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation and E-value sensitivity analysis. Among 207 participants (median age 38 years, 85.5% male, 99.0% on INSTI-based regimens), 23 (11.1%; 95% CI: 7.5-16.2) had immunological discordance, 180 (87.0%) had concordant responses, three (1.4%) had virological discordance (HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL despite CD4+ ≥350 cells/µL), and one (0.5%) had dual nonresponse. In the multivariable Firth-penalized analysis, advanced disease at diagnosis (adjusted odds ratio: 5.74; 95% CI: 2.08-16.34), age greater than 50 years (3.71; 1.25-11.07), and previous AIDS-defining opportunistic infection (3.42; 1.09-10.85) were independent predictors of immunological discordance (area under the curve: 0.81; optimism-corrected: 0.78). In this contemporary INSTI-treated cohort, approximately one in nine virologically suppressed patients failed to achieve adequate CD4+ recovery. Late HIV diagnosis emerged as the principal modifiable upstream driver of incomplete immune recovery, reinforcing the need for earlier diagnosis and rapid linkage to care in Türkiye.

articles.title: Risk of febrile seizure associated with β-lactam antibiotic use: a case-crossover study with an active comparator.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: β-Lactam antibiotics are generally considered safe, but neurotoxicity has been reported. These reports mainly involve adults; however, evidence in children remains limited. Although febrile seizure (FS) is the most common type of seizure in early childhood, multiple factors contribute to FS onset, and a potential association with β-lactam exposure has not been fully examined. We therefore investigated the association between oral β-lactam antibiotics and FS using a case-crossover design with an active comparator.

METHODS: Children younger than 6 years who experienced an incident FS were identified from a Japanese health insurance claims database. Exposure to oral β-lactam antibiotics was assessed on the hazard date (day -1) and the control date (day -22), while oral macrolides served as the active comparator. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs), and comparator-adjusted ORs were derived by dividing β-lactam ORs by macrolide ORs. The attributable fraction among the exposed (AFe) was calculated from the comparator-adjusted OR.

RESULTS: We identified 43,936 children. The comparator-adjusted OR for FS with oral β-lactam exposure was 1.21 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.40). These results were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses in which the control date was shifted from day -22 to day -15 or day -29.

CONCLUSION: Oral β-lactam antibiotics were associated with a modestly increased risk of FS. This finding should be interpreted cautiously because residual time-varying confounding by infection severity and fever may remain. Clinically indicated β-lactam antibiotics should not be withheld on the basis of these findings alone.

articles.title: The scientific consensus on the beauty of snowflakes: A case study for the aesthetics of science.
articles.journal: Studies in history and philosophy of science
articles.abstract: Philosophers of science interested in aesthetics have tended to privilege the epistemic and cognitive dimensions of science. Historians of science interested in aesthetics have largely focused on the aesthetics of scientific images and artefacts. Productive exchanges between these traditions of scholarship have been few and far between. Drawing inspiration from recent studies on the aesthetics of paleontology and geology, I aim to stimulate such exchanges by offering a historically rooted case study for the aesthetics of science, centred not on a theory or discipline but on an object: the snowflake. The history of snowflake science is replete with remarks about the aesthetic qualities of these objects and their study, offering various ways for scholars interested in aesthetics to approach this history. I propose three. First, I address the objects themselves, and how their aesthetic appreciation is related to the goal of understanding their formation. Focusing in particular on the question of the snowflake's symmetry, I show how aesthetic and epistemic values were often "blurred". Second, I look at the embodied practice of observing the objects, and the way aesthetic pleasure influences it. I propose to view this influence in terms of physical costs and aesthetic benefits. Third, I draw attention to the environmental context of observation, and its relevance for the way aesthetic and epistemic understandings blurred.

articles.title: A feasibility study investigating quantitative and qualitative effects of exercise in the workplace during work time for menopausal women.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the feasibility of exercise classes undertaken in the workplace during work time in healthy menopausal women, and to study the potential benefits of this intervention.

STUDY DESIGN: Of the 28 women (54.3 ± 6.5 years old; 162.6 ± 7.6 cm; 65.6 ± 12.5 kg) enrolled in the study, 22 completed it. It consisted in two testing sessions before and immediately after a 12-week exercise intervention that comprised two exercise classes (a choice from body conditioning, Zumba Gold, Pilates and high-intensity interval training) and two independent exercise sessions (exercise and timing of their choice) weekly.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Feasibility outcomes, including drop-out, retention and compliance, were measured during the intervention, and semi-structured interviews were conducted post-intervention. Psychological outcomes, menopause symptoms, physical activity levels and anthropometric and fitness variables were measured before and immediately after the intervention.

RESULTS: Participants' drop-out, retention and compliance were 14.3%, 78.6% and 79%, respectively. The exercise programme had a positive effect in four main areas: positive organisational work culture, impact on menopausal physiological outcomes, impact on menopausal psychological outcomes, and improvements and growth for the programme. Finally, participation in the intervention was associated with favourable changes in body fat in the trunk, physical performance, menopause symptoms, mental health, and integrated and intrinsic motivation; however, the absence of a control group precludes causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: A workplace physical activity intervention during work time for menopausal women is feasible and was associated with favourable changes in several psychological and physical outcomes after 12 weeks, although the lack of a control group limits our ability to attribute these changes solely to the intervention.

articles.title: Co-development of an intervention to support families of chronic critically ill children in paediatric critical care-The OCTO-Plus intervention.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Families of chronic critically ill (CCI) children hospitalised in paediatric critical care (PCC) experience high stress, impaired family functioning, and multiple unmet needs. Structured, evidence-based support remains inconsistent and fragmented. Addressing all concerns requires a multicomponent, family-centred approach that integrates emotional, cognitive, and behavioural support into routine PCC practice.

OBJECTIVE: To report the design of a co-developed multicomponent intervention to support families of CCI children hospitalised in PCC.

METHODS: Development followed the updated Medical Research Council framework, focusing on five core elements: identifying uncertainties, engaging stakeholders, tailoring to context, defining program theory, and refining components and processes. The intervention is grounded in family-centred care and Calgary's family systems model, targeting affective, cognitive, and behavioural domains of family functioning through actionable tools. Stakeholder engagement included three focus groups with 11 parent partners and two focus groups with 27 healthcare professionals, to iteratively shape contextual adaptations, component selection, and delivery mechanisms. Context analysis was used to identify constraints, existing communication pathways, and opportunities to embed training and documentation within routine PCC practice and the clinical information system. Components (therapeutic family consultations, patient and family diaries, and interprofessional handovers) were modelled using the Implementation Research Logic Model and described with the Template for Intervention Description and Replication.

RESULTS/FINDINGS: For the OCTO-Plus intervention, stakeholders prioritised feasibility and sustainability, leading to simplification of the intervention, integration into routine PCC workflows, and creation of a practical toolbox for trained interventionists (nurses and physicians). Anticipated barriers (multicomponent complexity, scheduling) and facilitators (stable staffing, low turnover, robust clinical information systems) informed design decisions. The final delivery plan provides structured family consultations with pre and posthandovers beginning on day 8 (±48 h), repeated on day 12, weekly until discharge, at discharge, and 1 month after PCC discharge. Diaries are introduced at the first consultation to support narrative sense-making, emotional processing, and transparent communication among families and healthcare professionals.

CONCLUSIONS: OCTO-Plus emerged from a rigorous, iterative process that emphasised contextual relevance, stakeholder partnership, and implementation readiness. The intervention is poised to enhance family functioning, communication, and continuity. Validation of its feasibility and acceptability will determine real-world uptake and sustainability in PCC.

articles.title: Cognitive impairment after critical illness: A scoping review of recovery trajectories, assessment practices, and risk factors.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent cognitive impairment is an important long-term sequela of critical illness, yet evidence regarding its post-intensive care unit (ICU) trajectories, determinants, and assessment practices remains fragmented.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to map the literature on persistent post-ICU cognitive impairment among adult survivors of critical illness, with particular attention to recovery trajectories, cognitive assessment practices, associated risk factors, and evidence gaps.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Cochrane, CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to 20 November 2025. Studies involving adult ICU survivors (aged ≥18 years) reporting postdischarge cognitive outcomes, including persistent post-ICU cognitive impairment, were included. In contrast, studies assessing cognitive dysfunction exclusively during hospitalisation or delirium without postdischarge cognitive assessment were excluded. Data were synthesised using descriptive and evidence-mapping approaches.

RESULTS: Forty-one studies were included, predominantly prospective cohort studies from Europe and North America. Cognitive impairment was most prevalent within the first month after ICU discharge, with substantial heterogeneity in recovery trajectories over time. While partial recovery occurred in some individuals, a considerable proportion experienced persistent impairment at mid- and long-term follow-up. Memory and executive functions were most frequently affected. Associated factors were clustered into six domains: patient vulnerability, ICU-related factors, sedation and treatment exposure, psychological factors, biomarkers/neurobiology, and protective or modifiable factors. Considerable variability existed in cognitive assessment tools and timing, with limited alignment across domains and follow-up phases. Evidence mapping revealed gaps in studies of older adults, low- and middle-income settings, and intervention-based research beyond early recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent post-ICU cognitive impairment is common and heterogeneous among adult survivors of critical illness, with cognitive deficits often emerging early after ICU discharge and persisting in some survivors. These findings support the conceptualisation of cognitive recovery as a dynamic and multifactorial process influenced by patient vulnerability, critical illness, treatment exposures, and postdischarge factors. Evidence remains limited regarding predictors of prolonged or persistent impairment. Greater standardisation of cognitive assessment and longitudinal and interventional research is needed to characterise recovery trajectories, identify individuals at risk of persistent impairment, and evaluate potentially modifiable targets.

articles.title: Effect of virtual reality during cycle ergometer session in the intensive care unit: A pilot randomised cross-over trial.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early mobilisation, including a cycle ergometer, is a cornerstone of best practices in the intensive care unit (ICU). Virtual reality (VR) has increasingly been integrated into healthcare, showing benefits in reducing depressive symptoms, improving mobility, and managing pain. However, the combined use of VR and cycle ergometry to enhance physical performance in the ICU has not been investigated.

OBJECTIVES: The primary objective of this study was to assess whether a single session of VR-based cycle ergometry increases active cycling distance (ACD) compared with a conventional session. Secondary objectives were to examine its effects on motivation, immersion, and perceived exertion and to monitor the occurrence of adverse events.

METHODS: This single-centre, randomised, open-label, two-period crossover trial compared two 30-min cycle ergometer sessions, one with VR and one without, delivered in a randomised order. Eligible participants were adults (aged ≥18 years) admitted to a surgical ICU for more than 48 h, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15 and the ability to sit in a chair. The primary outcome was ACD (km) per session. Secondary outcomes included adverse events and self-reported perceived effort, sense of immersion, and motivation, assessed using 11-point visual analogue scale (0-10).

RESULTS: Estimated mean difference in ACD between VR and no-VR sessions was 0.25 km (95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.50 to 1.00; p = 0.50). No period effect was observed (p = 0.15). No serious adverse events occurred. VR did not significantly affect perceived effort (mean difference: 0.53; 95% CI: -1.29 to 0.23; p = 0.163). VR significantly increased sense of immersion (mean difference: 4.08; 95% CI: 2.80 to 5.36; p < 0.0001) and motivational state (mean difference: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.16 to 2.14; p = 0.024).

CONCLUSIONS: VR did not significantly increase ACD, it substantially enhanced subjective immersion and motivation. These findings support further investigation of immersive technologies as adjuncts to early rehabilitation strategies in the ICU.

articles.title: To report or not? A qualitative study of critical care nurses' experiences of incident reporting.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critical care nurses have a key role in identifying and reporting incidents. These reports are used to improve patient safety and to deliver high-quality care, particularly within intensive care settings where patients are highly vulnerable. However, critical care nurses reporting behaviours are influenced by various organisational and individual factors.

AIM/OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to explore the experiences of critical care nurses in Australia with incident reporting and the perceived barriers and facilitators that influence reporting behaviours in critical care settings.

METHODS: Using a qualitative descriptive method, semistructured interviews with eight nurses from intensive care units across Australia were conducted. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Three overarching themes were found: Facilitators of effective incident reporting, Barriers to incident reporting, and To report or not. Findings showed that organisational culture played a substantial role in shaping intensive care nurses' willingness to report incidents. Intensive care nurses were more likely to engage in reporting when a supportive, nonpunitive culture was present and when incident reports led to constructive feedback and educational opportunities. A lack of support from management, complicated reporting systems, insufficient education, and using reporting as a weapon were identified as barriers preventing incident reporting. Due to heavy workloads and the perception that some incidents seemed minor, nurses occasionally preferred to report problems informally, which could limit efforts to improve safety.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the impact organisational and supportive culture play a major role in critical care nurses' willingness to report incidents. These findings explore the experiences of incident reporting among critical care nurses in Australia, which organisations may use to address the barriers and emphasise the facilitators to encourage effective reporting.

articles.title: Early-Life Nutritional and Environmental Factors in the Pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A DOHaD Perspective.
articles.abstract: The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) hypothesis posits that nutritional and environmental exposures during critical developmental periods, including fetal life, the suckling-weaning period, and early adulthood, strongly influence later disease risks. Research on DOHaD has expanded rapidly in recent years. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major risk factor for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases, and its prevalence is increasing in adults, children, and adolescents. Exposures during "the first 1000 d" of life, spanning fetal development to weaning, determine later risk of lifestyle-related diseases. This review summarizes recent epidemiological findings and mechanistic insights from animal DOHaD studies, particularly regarding MASLD. Specifically, drawing on the Barker hypothesis, the modern DOHaD framework, and the mismatch hypothesis, it discusses how maternal obesity, diet quality, early antibiotic exposure, and the timing of breastfeeding and complementary feeding may influence MASLD risk. In animal models, developmental exposure to undernutrition, hypoxia, early weaning, and high-fat/high-sugar diets promotes hepatic lipid accumulation, endoplasmic reticulum stress, inflammation, and fibrosis. The proposed mechanisms include i) leptin resistance and impaired insulin signaling; ii) intestinal barrier breakdown with gut-liver axis inflammation; iii) reduced very-low-density lipoprotein secretion, increased de novo lipogenesis, and impaired β-oxidation; iv) dysregulation of lipid droplet regulators, including cell death inducing DFFA-like effector, perilipins, and phosphatidylcholine/ phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase; and v) epigenetic memory via DNA methylation and histone modifications. By integrating evidence that prenatal and early-life environments shape susceptibility to MASLD, this review provides deeper insight into MASLD pathogenesis.

articles.title: Potential association between Epstein-Barr virus infection and myasthenia gravis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) has been implicated in multiple autoimmune disorders; however, its role in myasthenia gravis (MG) remains incompletely defined. We investigated EBV nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA-1)-specific humoral immunity in MG and examined whether human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genotypes modulate this association.

METHODS: Serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels were measured in 106 treatment-naïve MG patients and 230 healthy controls (HCs). An independent MG cohort (n = 244) underwent whole-genome sequencing for HLA genotyping, with 44 treatment-naïve patients also tested for anti-EBNA-1 IgG.

RESULTS: MG patients showed higher proportions of anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels above the upper detection limit (>600 U/mL) compared with age- and sex-matched HCs (67% vs. 50%, p = 0.082). Among individuals with detectable antibody levels (3-600 U/mL), MG patients exhibited significantly higher titers than matched HCs (306.0 [181.5-391.0] vs. 157.0 [92.4-250.0] U/mL, p = 0.0065). No significant associations were found between anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels and MG clinical phenotypes. HLA association analyses identified the HLA-DRB4*01:03-/DRB3*02:02+ genotype as a significant genetic risk factor for generalized MG versus ocular MG (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.29-5.21, p = 0.01). Among patients who were tested for both HLA and anti-EBNA-1 IgG and had anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels >600 U/mL, ocular MG patients carried HLA DRB4*01:03 more frequently than generalized MG patients (81.8% vs. 23.5%, p = 0.006).

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest a potential association between EBV-specific immune responses and MG. Furthermore, the HLA-DRB4*01:03-/DRB3*02:02+ genotype may confer susceptibility to generalized MG, supporting an interaction between EBV infection and host genetics in MG pathogenesis.

articles.title: Long-term injectable non-insulin antidiabetic drug use and in-hospital mortality in sepsis: A nationwide analysis of the 2023 National Inpatient Sample.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Injectable non-insulin antidiabetic agents have hypothesized antiinflammatory effects in sepsis, but no nationally representative US inpatient analysis has examined their association with in-hospital outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 National Inpatient Sample. Adults with any-listed sepsis and diabetes were included; exposure was documented long-term injectable non-insulin antidiabetic use (ICD-10-CM Z79.85). Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality across three pre-specified comparators.

RESULTS: Among 241,808 hospitalizations, 5238 (2.2%) carried Z79.85. Adjusted odds of death were 0.53 (95% CI, 0.45-0.63) versus the full cohort, 0.73 (0.61-0.87) therapy-matched, and 0.77 (0.64-0.93) versus oral therapy alone. The E-value was 1.61.

CONCLUSIONS: Exposure was associated with lower in-hospital mortality, attenuating under stricter comparators. Findings are hypothesis-generating and subject to residual confounding.

articles.title: Neurologic complications in venoarterial versus venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurologic complications are among the most devastating events associated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), yet propensity-balanced comparisons of mode-specific neurologic risk between venoarterial (VA) and venovenous (VV) configurations remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the 30-day incidence of five discrete neurologic outcomes: ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, seizures, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), and brain death, between adult VA and VV ECMO patients.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX federated network, adults undergoing VA or VV ECMO (2015-2024) were identified by ICD-10-PCS codes and 1:1 propensity score matched on demographics, comorbidities, and antithrombotic exposures. Odds ratios (OR), risk ratios, and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated within 30 days; multivariable Cox regression was performed for each outcome.

RESULTS: After matching (6944 per cohort), VA ECMO was associated with higher 30-day rates of cerebral infarction (7.04%vs 5.13%; OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.22-1.61), seizures (OR 1.15, 1.002-1.324), HIE (OR 2.17, 1.82-2.58), and brain death (OR 2.63, 1.67-4.14). Hemorrhagic stroke did not differ (OR 0.83, 0.66-1.04). Cox models concordantly showed higher hazard for all outcomes except hemorrhagic stroke (brain death adjusted HR 2.37, 1.58-3.57); heparin exposure was associated with lower hazard of cerebral infarction and HIE.

CONCLUSION: VA ECMO was associated with higher 30-day ischemic and hypoxic-ischemic neurologic risk than VV ECMO, while hemorrhagic risk did not differ. The hypoxic-ischemic endpoints are not separable from the indication for VA support and reflect burden rather than modality effect. These findings motivate prospective evaluation of mode-specific neurologic surveillance.

articles.title: Determinants of unwitnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review (HL-D-26-00618).
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately half of all out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) cases are unwitnessed, with survival rates below 5%. Although early recognition is critical for improving outcomes, factors associated with unwitnessed OHCA have not been systematically reviewed.

OBJECTIVES: To systematically review and synthesize the available evidence on determinants of unwitnessed OHCA.

METHODS: We included peer-reviewed observational studies investigating associations between demographic, socioeconomic, clinical, or situational factors and witnessed status of OHCA in adults. No restrictions were placed on setting, language, or publication year. A systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science Core Collection was performed from inception to July 17, 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the QUIPS tool. Findings were synthesized narratively by determinant domain, summarizing study counts, effect directions, statistical significance, and consistency.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies including 210,028 individuals were analyzed. Female sex and arrest occurring at home were most consistently associated with unwitnessed OHCA. Limited evidence, predominantly from unadjusted analyses, suggested higher rates of unwitnessed OHCA among Black individuals, those with low socioeconomic status or living in more deprived areas, individuals with type I diabetes, psychiatric illness, and arrests occurring at night, during sleep, or in residential or rural settings.

CONCLUSION: This systematic review identified several factors associated with unwitnessed OHCA, with the most consistent evidence for female sex and arrests occurring at home. These findings may help guide targeted prevention and public health strategies.

articles.title: A multi-dimensional attention-based framework for personalized driver fatigue assessment for proactive commercial-vehicle crash prevention.
articles.abstract: Driver fatigue is a major safety concern in commercial vehicle operations, yet conventional detection approaches often rely on fixed driving-time thresholds that overlook inter-driver variability, cumulative effects across trips, and contextual differences. This study proposes a multi-dimensional, context-aware fatigue assessment framework that combines a driver-specific Bayesian baseline and cross-trip cumulative fatigue debt with six behavioral, spectral, contextual, and event-based indicators through a time-varying attention mechanism. The framework was evaluated using 43.8 million Digital Tachograph (DTG) records from 1,813 commercial drivers in Korea. The estimated fatigue score exhibits a clear diurnal pattern, increases consistently with cumulative fatigue debt, and reveals heterogeneous driver-level profiles. Spatial aggregation identified heterogeneous fatigue-prone road sections, while correspondence with independently identified accident-prone locations was sensitive to the spatial unit of analysis. Because direct physiological measurements and crash-event labels are unavailable, the framework is positioned as an operational fatigue-management tool rather than a clinically validated fatigue detector or crash-prediction model. The proposed approach provides a scalable basis for individualized driver monitoring, fleet scheduling, recovery management, and identification of fatigue-prone road sections, supporting proactive fatigue-risk management in commercial transport operations.

articles.title: Autoimmune gastritides: A critical review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune gastritis (AIG) has long been considered a host-related autoimmune disease that results in oxyntic atrophy, leading to Pernicious Anemia and increasing neoplastic risk. Current evidence discloses that gastric autoimmunity includes a spectrum of inflammatory diseases (i.e., Autoimmune Gastritides) with distinct etiologies, comorbidities, clinical presentations, histological phenotypes, and outcomes.

AIM: To distinguish the clinical-pathological subtypes of immunomediated gastric disorders.

RESULTS: Gastric autoimmune diseases comprise Type-1 and Type-2 variants. Type-1 atrophic AIG may lead to vitamin B12 malabsorption, resulting in pernicious anemia, and carries a high risk of Type-1 neuroendocrine gastric neoplasia. Type-1a AIG includes two subtypes. Type-1a is the canonical oxyntic-restricted AIG subtype with no history of exposure to H. pylori infection. In this subtype, a T-cell-rich, cytolytic infiltrate targets the corpus/fundus mucosa, resulting in oxyntic-restricted atrophic changes. Type-1b combines autoimmune etiology with prior or current exposure to H. pylori infection. The dual etiology of Type-1b AIG combines autoimmune oxyntic damage with H. pylori-related antral lesions. This condition may lead to extensive (antral and oxyntic) atrophy, necessitating cancer prevention strategies tailored to the histological stage of gastritis. Type-2 AIG is far less frequent than Type-1, presents with mucus-secreting (antral-pyloric) and oxyntic (corpus/fundus) erosive mucosal high-grade pangastritis, and involves symptomatic multiorgan immune-mediated comorbidities, irrespective of H. pylori status. Type-2 combines Type-1-like serology with a wide, variable spectrum of circulating organ-specific and non-organ-specific autoantibodies and requires targeted treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: The nosology of autoimmune gastritides should reflect their diverse etio-pathogenesis, clinicopathological presentations, and outcomes.

articles.title: Longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine immunogenicity in inflammatory bowel disease in relation to anti-TNF therapy and age: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. We followed humoral and cellular responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination over 12 months.

METHODS: In this single-centre, prospective cohort study, adults with IBD received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. Two doses were administered 28 days apart and a third dose 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed with rank-based longitudinal models and with mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex.

RESULTS: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. Geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 3 months, GM NT50 values were lower against BA.1 (9.0) than against wild-type (24.2) or Delta (26.9), and 13 patients (24.5%) never reached a wild-type NT50 of 1:16. Anti-TNF therapy (32/53, 60.4%) was significantly associated with faster waning. At 6 months, adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990). In 33 thrice-vaccinated patients, intercurrent infection (15/33) raised S1-RBD IgG 4.6-fold more than the third dose alone, without a measurable gain in neutralisation. In the adjusted model, IFN-γ ELISpot responses did not differ between treatment groups.

DISCUSSION: Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.

articles.title: The IL-27/IL-27R axis attenuates hypoxia-induced cardiac remodeling and is associated with altered p38 MAPK signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hypoxia is a major driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) and adverse cardiac remodeling. Although IL-27/interleukin-27 receptor (IL-27R) signaling has been implicated in tissue-protective responses, its role in hypoxia-induced cardiac remodeling remains unclear.

METHODS: We used a combination of in vivo and in vitro approaches to investigate the role of IL-27/IL-27R in hypoxia-induced cardiac remodeling. Wild-type (WT) and interleukin-27 receptor α knockout (IL-27Rα KO) mice were exposed to chronic hypoxia. Interventions included recombinant mouse IL-27 (rmIL-27), lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated IL-27 mRNA (LNP-IL-27 mRNA), and sildenafil. Echocardiographic, histological, and molecular analyses were performed to assess cardiac remodeling.

RESULTS: IL-27Rα deficiency was associated with worsened hypoxia-induced remodeling, including more marked cardiac structural abnormalities, impaired functional indices, and increased myocardial fibrosis. rmIL-27 attenuated these changes and showed more consistent protective effects than LNP-IL-27 mRNA and sildenafil across the measured endpoints. In hypoxic cardiomyocytes, IL-27 was associated with altered downstream signaling, with p38 MAPK showing a pattern more closely associated with the protective phenotype than STAT1 or STAT3.

CONCLUSION: The IL-27/IL-27R axis attenuates chronic hypoxia-induced cardiac remodeling, with associated changes in p38 MAPK signaling, although the underlying mechanisms require further investigation.

articles.title: The CLEC7A Y238∗ variant and susceptibility to pneumonia: a prospective population-based cohort study and mechanistic investigation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: DECTIN-1, a C-type lectin receptor encoded by CLEC7A, mediates antifungal immunity, but its antibacterial role remains unclear. We investigated, using human genetic and animal studies, whether the common loss-of-function CLEC7A Y238∗ variant (rs16910526) influences susceptibility to bacterial respiratory infection, and sought to identify the bacterial ligand mediating DECTIN-1 recognition.

METHODS: We analysed Y238∗ and pneumonia risk in the Malmö Diet and Cancer Study, a prospective Swedish cohort, using Cox models with age as timescale (28,126 participants, 5493 events; 26,601 and 5190 fully adjusted) over a mean 17·3 years of follow-up. We challenged wild-type, Clec7a+/-, and Clec7a-/- mice with Streptococcus pneumoniae and non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi). Affinity proteomics, ELISA, flow cytometry, and NF-κB reporter assays identified and validated the ligand.

FINDINGS: Y238∗ carriers had elevated pneumonia risk in adjusted Cox models (HR 1·12, 95% CI 1·04-1·20; p = 0·002; concordant competing-risk sHR 1·12, 1·04-1·20). Clec7a-deficient mice showed gene-dose-dependent impairment of S. pneumoniae clearance, impaired NTHi clearance, and blunted cytokine responses. Affinity pull-down identified elongation factor Tu (EF-Tu) as a DECTIN-1 ligand that bound the carbohydrate-recognition domain and activated NF-κB signalling when clustered; orthologues from four bacterial species also bound.

INTERPRETATION: These findings support a role for DECTIN-1 in pulmonary antibacterial defence and suggest that inherited deficiency increases pneumonia susceptibility in humans. EF-Tu is a candidate ligand that provides mechanistic support for the association.

FUNDING: Swedish Research Council, Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, Swedish Heart Lung Foundation, Swedish Government Funds for Clinical Research (ALF), Skåne County Council's Research and Development Foundation.

articles.title: Will they stay? A survey of nursing bridging students' intentions for retention in long-term and home and community care sectors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retention of nurses in long-term care (LTC) and home and community care (HCC) remains critical; however, less is known about factors that influence nurses' intentions to remain in these sectors. Nursing bridging students represent an important emerging workforce as they transition into new nursing roles within these sectors.

PURPOSE: This study explored differentiating characteristics of nursing bridging students' retention intentions in LTC and HCC.

METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional pilot study employed a survey co-designed with nursing knowledge users was distributed by a provincial nursing association to nurse bridging education students with a return-of-service commitment in LTC or HCC. Respondents rated their likelihood of remaining in the sector over 3, 5, and 10 years. Validated measures assessed psychological empowerment, work engagement, career commitment, resilience, burnout, and prosocial motivation. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted separately for Practical Nurse (PN) and Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BScN) bridging students.

DISCUSSION: In total, 174 respondents were included. Among PN students, higher age (p = .01) and personal accomplishment (p < .05) predicted greater intention to stay. Income predicted short-term retention intentions at 3 years (p = .01) only. Among BScN bridging students, work engagement predicted retention intentions at 3, 5, and 10 years (p < .05). Previous sector experience predicted short-term intentions at 3 years (p = .03), while older age predicted longer-term intentions at 5 and 10 years (p < .05).

CONCLUSION: Predictors of retention intentions differed by bridging pathway and timeline. Retention strategies should be tailored to educational pathway and work experiences, fostering personal accomplishment and work engagement.

articles.title: Measurement properties of instruments for post-extubation dysphagia in critically ill patients: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Post-extubation dysphagia (PED) is a common but often under-recognised complication in critically ill patients following invasive mechanical ventilation. Systematic assessment of PED in routine ICU practice is not common. This systematic review aimed to identify clinical instruments used to assess PED in critically ill adult patients and to evaluate their measurement properties.

METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the COSMIN methodology for systematic reviews of measurement instruments. A comprehensive evidence search was performed in multiple databases and other sources. Studies were included if they developed or applied standardised assessment instruments for the identification of PED in critically ill adults (≥18 years).

RESULTS: Of 2769 abstracts reviewed, 22 studies met criteria for inclusion. Sixteen different instruments for the assessment of PED were identified. These were categorised into water swallow tests, multi-consistency tests, and assessments without a swallowing evaluation. For nine instruments, measurement properties were reported, focusing on content validity, criterion validity and reliability, and demonstrated mostly good measurement properties. The Post-Extubation Dysphagia Screening Tool was the only evaluated across all three properties and showed sufficient measurement properties. The overall quality of evidence was mostly low to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: There are various clinical assessment instruments for PED in critically ill adults. Most instruments showed good criterion validity, indicating their potential for clinical use. However, other measurement properties are largely unknown, and the quality of evidence is generally low. Thus, it is currently unclear which tool is best suited for assessing PED. Further research investigating validity and reliability is needed to identify instruments suitable for routine ICU use.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Systematic detection of PED is important. Assessment instruments with good diagnostic performance should be used to improve ICU care.

articles.title: Appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms: A retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV place considerable pressure on healthcare systems. Inconsistent respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms may delay recognition of respiratory viral infections and implementation of appropriate infection prevention and control measures.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the appropriateness of respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms and to identify factors associated with inappropriate screening.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study in a 2500-bed tertiary hospital in Belgium during three periods of the 2022-2023 influenza epidemic. Medical records were reviewed for demographic and clinical characteristics, respiratory symptoms, and respiratory virus screening practices. Screening was classified as appropriate or inappropriate (delayed or absent despite indication) based on prevailing guidelines. Determinants of inappropriate screening were explored using univariable analyses.

RESULTS: Of 743 hospital admissions assessed for eligibility, 345 (46%) involved patients with respiratory symptoms and constituted the primary analysis population. Respiratory virus screening was appropriate in 75% (258/345) and inappropriate in 25% (87/345) of cases. Appropriate screening was more frequent among patients admitted for respiratory conditions and among those meeting criteria for severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). Screening appropriateness was significantly lower among patients who developed respiratory symptoms during hospitalization than among those with symptoms documented at admission (37% vs. 77%, p < 0.001). Isolation status could not be reliably determined for 44% of patients and was therefore considered descriptive only.

CONCLUSION: Gaps remain in appropriate respiratory virus screening among hospitalized patients with respiratory symptoms, particularly among patients who develop symptoms during hospitalization. Systematic symptom-based screening and standardized decision-support tools may help improve adherence to respiratory virus screening recommendations.

articles.title: Tracking SARS-CoV-2: Molecular epidemiology and surveillance in Health Region VIII, Buenos Aires, Argentina (2020-2021).
articles.abstract: To describe the classical and molecular epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in Health Region VIII (HRVIII, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina), we analyzed 120421 respiratory samples from patients with acute respiratory infection during the first two pandemic years. Complete genome or partial spike gene sequences were obtained for phylogenetic analyses to investigate viral introductions, transmission dynamics, and genetic diversity. Substitution rates were estimated for predominant lineages. SARS-CoV-2 positivity was significantly higher in 2020 (37.4%) than in 2021 (31.9%, p<0.001). In 2020, positivity was higher among travelers (41.7%) than residents (36.4%), a trend that reversed in 2021 (33.4% vs. 28.0%), reflecting the region's socioeconomic and touristic characteristics. The first wave peaked at epidemiological week (EW) 37 of 2020 and was dominated by lineages B.1.1.33, N.3, and B.1.499. A resurgence in early 2021 involved lineage N.5 and emerging Alpha and Lambda variants. The second wave peaked at EW 20 and featured cocirculation of Gamma and Lambda, which were later displaced by Delta after EW 31. Estimated substitution rates ranged from 2.4×10-4 to 6.8×10-4substitutions/site/year across different clades. This study provides a detailed overview of SARS-CoV-2 circulation in HRVIII and underscores the importance of integrating genomic surveillance into public health systems to monitor emerging variants and support timely response strategies.

articles.title: Agent-based simulation and digital twins in heart failure care: Current evidence, validation and implementation barriers.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) requires coordinated care across home, ambulatory, emergency, inpatient and hospital-at-home settings. Agent-based models (ABM), discrete-event simulation (DES) and digital twins (DT) have been proposed to support service design and individualized decisions, but their clinical maturity is uncertain. We performed a narrative review, updated through 31 July 2026, separating established clinical evidence for HF care models from HF-specific computational evidence and extrapolated cardiovascular DT literature. The evidence map includes nine representative HF-specific computational studies: four agent-based or hybrid systems, one DES model and four DT-oriented studies. Most were conceptual, simulation-based, retrospective or proof-of-concept; only a small number included external or invasive-reference validation, and none established routine DT-guided clinical care. Current evidence supports ABM/DES mainly for hypothesis generation and service design. HF digital twins remain investigational. Prospective validation, interoperability, recalibration, cybersecurity, workflow integration, cost-effectiveness and digital equity are prerequisites before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Histone Demethylase KDM5A Is Activated and Pathogenic in a Mouse Model of LMNA-Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Heart failure is associated with widespread epigenetic remodeling in cardiomyocytes, but the chromatin regulators driving this process remain poorly defined. We identify the histone H3K4 demethylase KDM5A as a key epigenetic mediator of heart failure in a cardiomyocyte-specific lamin A-deficient mouse model. Disease-associated activation of KDM5A leads to redistribution of promoter histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation and repression of genes regulating sarcomere structure and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Genetic deletion of Kdm5a restores histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation enrichment, reactivates cardiac and metabolic transcriptional programs, improves cardiac function, and prolongs survival. These findings identify KDM5A-mediated chromatin remodeling as a previously unrecognized mechanism of heart failure and highlight KDM5A as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Blockade of gastrin-releasing peptide receptor in the PVN alleviates maternal vascular and placental dysfunction in preeclamptic rat.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by placental ischemia-induced systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and maternal vascular dysfunction. We previously reported that upregulated gastrin-releasing peptide (GRP) and its receptor (GRPR) within the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of PE rats contribute to the progression of PE. However, whether such central upregulation contributes to the peripheral organs damage in PE remains unknown. This study investigated the protective effects of the GRPR antagonist ICI-216140, administered via PVN microinjection, on mesenteric arteries and placenta in the reduced uterine perfusion pressure (RUPP) rat model initiated on gestational day (GD) 14. GRPR was antagonized with ICI-216140 (1 mM/side/day, PVN microinjection) from GD14 to GD19. On GD19, the mean arterial pressure (MAP) was recorded via carotid artery catheterization, the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and plasmatic norepinephrine were determined. Mesenteric arteries function and structure were characterized via isometric myography and H&E staining, while mitochondrial dynamics and biogenesis were evaluated through immunofluorescence and Western blotting. Additionally, inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in placentae and mesenteric arteries were assessed. Microinjection of ICI-216140 in the PVN prevented RUPP-increased MAP, proteinuria and circulating norepinephrine. In addition to suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress in both placentae and mesenteric arteries, ICI-216140 alleviated structural remodeling and contractile dysfunction, and ameliorated the imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics and biogenesis within mesenteric arteries. Our findings suggest that central antagonism of GRPR in the PVN reduced the hallmark features of PE, including hypertension, proteinuria, vascular dysfunction, and placental damage, underscoring the therapeutic potential of central interventions in preventing multi-organ damage.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction in chronic critical illness: mechanisms, clinical consequences and therapeutic perspectives.
