articles.title: Association of altered body composition with cardiac wasting in cancer with and without cardiotoxic therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In advanced cancer, associations among changes in body composition, cardiac wasting and prior cardiotoxic anticancer therapy have not been investigated.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Using bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), body composition was measured in 206 patients with mostly advanced cancer without known cardiovascular disease or infection (stage III/IV: 84%, prior cardiotoxic anticancer therapy: 55%). Left ventricular (LV) mass was assessed by transthoracic echocardiography and grouped by presence of cardiac wasting according to previously established sex-specific thresholds for LV mass adjusted for height2 (<61 g/m2 for women, <57 g/m2 for men). BIA measurements (indexed to height2) included fat mass index (FMI), fat-free mass index (FFMI), skeletal muscle mass index (SMMI), visceral fat index (VFI), total body water index (TBWI) and extracellular water index (ECWI).

KEY RESULTS: Patients with cancer and cardiac wasting (n = 88) were younger (57±15 vs 62±13 years) and more often women (68% vs 29%) compared to those without cardiac wasting (n = 118). Patients with cardiac wasting had significantly lower FMI (-12%), FFMI (-14%), SMMI (-16%), VFI (-46%), TBWI (-13%) and ECWI (-14%). For women, FFMI was significantly associated with LV mass/height2 (r = 0.41) and VFI for men (r = 0.40). In the multivariable linear regression analysis, FFMI was the strongest significant predictor of cardiac wasting, with no significant interaction by sex or previous cardiotoxic therapy.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Cardiac wasting in advanced cancer is associated with lower FFMI and VFI independent of prior cardiotoxic therapy.

articles.title: Mild, Fast, and General Biocatalytic Deprotection Strategies for Automated Fluorine-18 Positron Emission Tomography Radiotracer Synthesis.
articles.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) has become an essential tool in nuclear medicine, driving the continuous development of new radiotracers. Owing to the short half-life of fluorine-18 (110 min), radiotracer production requires fast, robust, and fully automated synthetic protocols. Reactive functional groups present on precursor molecules must be protected to prevent competition during radiofluorination, with deprotection typically achieved under harsh chemical conditions that may compromise automation and lead to partial molecular degradation. Herein, we report a general biocatalytic deprotection strategy based on porcine liver esterase (PLE) as a mild and efficient alternative to conventional chemical methods. Three protecting groups (valerate, pivaloyloxymethyl and pivaloyl ethylidene carbamate) were selected to enable the PLE-deprotection of a broad range of functional groups found in radiotracers and drugs (alcohols, phenols, carboxylic acids, amines, anilines, sulfonamides). The PivEC protective group of amines, anilines and sulfonamides was specifically developed for allowing an esterase deprotection. This approach was validated across a broad substrate scope and was successfully automated on ORA-Neptis modules for clinically relevant PET tracers, including [18F]FMISO, [18F]CABS13, and [18F]Nifene. This work establishes enzymatic deprotection as a versatile and practical strategy for PET scan application.

articles.title: Hemostatic Considerations of New Treatment Options for Hemophilia During Surgery, Infection, and Bleeding in Children and Adolescents.
articles.abstract: In recent years, the therapeutic landscape for hemophilia has changed significantly, with the approval of several innovative agents, some featuring entirely novel mechanisms of action. These advances have substantially improved outcomes and reduced the treatment burden. However, clinical experience with these novel therapies in special situations-such as bleeding, surgery, trauma, and infection-remains limited. Factor replacement therapy has been the standard of care for a long time, with extensive clinical experience. The introduction of non-factor therapies has raised important questions: Is additional treatment required after injury or during surgery? What are the considerations in cases of sepsis or disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)? This summary focuses on emicizumab, efanesoctocog alfa, newly approved TFPI inhibitors, nonacog beta pegol, and the extension of indications for PEGylated FVIII preparations to younger age groups. We will therefore also briefly address these developments. The largest part of this manuscript will focus on emicizumab due to its longer approval history and the most extensive data available. Most other medications were licensed in 2024 or later.

articles.title: [Comparison of counselling statistics of the Single Points of Contact for Employers (EAA) across the German federal states].
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In 2022, lawmakers established the Single Points of Contact for Employers (§185a SGB IX) across Germany with the aim of improving opportunities for people with disabilities to particpate in the labor market. The EAA are intended to inform, advise, and support employers on issues related to disability and work. The EAA's funding and employment structures differ considerably between the federal states. The aim of this article was to compare the EAA's counseling figures across the various federal states and to identify opportunities for further developing the EAA's case data documentation.

METHODS: Methodologically, the study followed a multi-method design combining descriptive analyses of state-level EAA case data for the 2024 reporting period with guided expert interviews. In addition, the findings were discussed with EAA experts in a participatory dialogues.

RESULTS: The results showed substantial differences between the federal states in terms of documented contact occasions. These differences can be attributed to variyng interpretation of key terms and documentation practices, different employment situations and prior structures as well as heterogeneous provider structures.

CONLUSION: The EAA case documentation offers opportunities for a targeted management of this new labor market policy instrument. Documentation should be further standardized across federal states in order to enhance comparability. Nevertheless, each federal state should formulate individual (sub)goals, taking into account its own conditions and specificities.

articles.title: Effect of glycemic control on periodontal parameters in people with type 2 diabetes -a single-arm interventional pilot trial.
articles.journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
articles.abstract:
AIM: Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes show a bidirectional relationship. This pilot study investigated the possible association between glycemic control and periodontal status in people with type 2 diabetes without periodontal treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: People with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c-value ≥ 8.0 %) received intensified antihyperglycemic therapy. Periodontal and metabolic parameters were assessed at baseline (T1) and after three months (T2). No dental prophylaxis or subgingival instrumentation was performed. Clinical assessment included pocket probing depths (PPD), bleeding on probing (BOP), clinical attachment level (CAL), periodontal inflamed surface area (PISA), plaque index (PI), and gingival index (GI). Primary outcome parameter was PISA. Patients' oral health-related quality of life was assessed with the OHIP-G 14 questionnaire.

RESULTS: A significant reduction of HbA1c from average 9.3 % to 8.2 % after 3.8 ± 1.1 months resulted in significant reductions of PISA and BOP (p=0.001; p=0.001). Higher HbA1c values were significantly associated with higher PISA (p=0.006) and BOP values (p=0.026). No significant change was observed in OHIP-G14 scores.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that improved glycemic control may be associated with reduced periodontal inflammation (BOP, PISA), even without periodontal therapy. These findings support the importance of good glycemic control for periodontal health in people with type 2 diabetes. Given the exploratory nature of this study, these findings require cautious interpretation and confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Trends and Characteristics of Maternal Mortality in Guilan Province, Northern Iran.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-related mortality significantly impacts families and societies, reflecting healthcare access and effectiveness. Maternal mortality rates vary globally, with higher rates in developing countries. This study investigates maternal mortality in Guilan Province, Northern Iran, focusing on the incidence, causes, and implications for healthcare policy and societal development.

METHODS: This study used registry-based census data to analyze all maternal mortality cases recorded in Guilan Province between 2014 to 2024. Data were collected via a checklist from the vice-chancellor of health, Guilan University of Medical Sciences. The study included deaths during pregnancy, childbirth, or postpartum.

RESULTS: Among 62 maternal deaths, the overall MMR was 22.83 per 100,000 live births. The highest proportion in the 31-35 age group (33.9%). Pre-existing conditions were present in 41.9% of decedents, and 53.2% had undergraduate education. MMR increased 3.2-fold during the pandemic period (40.38 vs. 12.75 pre-pandemic), peaking at 49.83 in 2022. Substantial geographic variation was observed, with Rudsar district showing the highest mortality (8.43 per 100,000). COVID-19 was the leading cause of death (19.35%), followed by hemorrhagic shock (16.13%), pulmonary embolism (9.68%), infection (8.06%), and cardiac ischemia (6.45%). A sensitivity analysis excluding 12 COVID-19-related maternal deaths showed that non-COVID MMR remained elevated during 2020-2021 and increased again in 2023-2024.

CONCLUSION: The persistence of elevated non-COVID maternal mortality suggests that factors beyond direct COVID-19 mortality may have contributed to the observed temporal pattern, although causal relationships cannot be established from this descriptive study.

articles.title: Patient acceptability of and satisfaction with enhanced patient care services within a clinically integrated network of community pharmacies.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CPESN USA is a clinically integrated network (CIN) through which pharmacies provide enhanced services. While it is known that these services benefit patients, no studies have quantified patient acceptability of these services, or general patient satisfaction with pharmacies in a CIN.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study are to assess patient: 1) acceptability of enhanced services received at pharmacies participating in payer programs within a CIN; and 2) satisfaction with their overall care experience at these pharmacies.

METHODS: The study design was a cross-sectional survey. Subjects were Medicaid beneficiaries who received enhanced pharmacy services from a random sample of CIN pharmacies in one state. Survey items were informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. The survey covered acceptability of nine enhanced services and general satisfaction through multiple-choice, Likert scale, and open-ended questions. The survey was deployed electronically from August-December 2024. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize all data. Median composite acceptability scores (1 lowest, 5 highest) were calculated for each service. Content analysis of responses to open-ended survey items was performed.

RESULTS: Fifteen pharmacies obtained 163 survey responses. The mean age of respondents was 46.9 years and the majority (80%) were White. Median acceptability scores for each of the nine services were 4.4 or greater. A total of 88% of respondents were very satisfied with their pharmacy. Open-ended item responses focused on the pharmacies' person-centered care, reliability, accessibility, and strong communication.

CONCLUSION: Patients reported high acceptability with enhanced patient care services and the majority were very satisfied with their overall care at CIN pharmacies.

articles.title: Development of a clinically integrated pharmacy network: Pennsylvania pharmacists care network.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community pharmacy practice is readily modernizing to a patient-centered model of care where implementation of patient care services, evolving business models, and a consistent approach to the way payment for services occurs is essential to long-term sustainability.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the development, implementation, and growth of a community pharmacy clinically integrated network (CIN) for pharmacist-provided patient care services throughout Pennsylvania.

PRACTICE DESCRIPTION: The Pennsylvania Pharmacists Care Network (PPCN) is an affiliated chapter of CPESN USA, a CIN providing nationwide support, infrastructure, and best practice alignment. PPCN's collaboration with colleges/schools of pharmacy, the state pharmacy association, CPESN USA and other key partners have been essential to network formation. Network pharmacies must meet a minimum set of patient care requirements including documentation of patient care services through an electronic care plan, using the Pharmacists eCare Plan (PeCP) standard.

PRACTICE INNOVATION: PPCN partners with health payors in contracting patient care services on behalf of participating pharmacies. Payor contracts include fee-for-service and value-based care reimbursement structures. Regular communication with payor partners and network pharmacies help ensure quality and achievement of programmatic goals.

EVALUATION METHODS: Descriptive statistics were used to characterize patient care service PeCP data between September 2017 and December 2025.

RESULTS: Between September 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, pharmacists provided 198,626 patient encounters through seven payor programs. January 1, 2021, marked the launch of additional payor programs and the inclusion of data collection through a more comprehensive PeCP report. During this time, over 200 pharmacies and pharmacy teams engaged 25,371 unique patients through a payor program.

CONCLUSION: The development and growth of PPCN has led to a steady volume of payor contracts for a wide variety of pharmacist-provided patient care services. Collaboration among different stakeholders is vital to network development, and payment mechanisms are essential to sustain and grow network services.

Adverse events and associated factors during intra-hospital transport of mechanically ventilated intensive care patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-hospital transport (IHT) of critically ill patients remains a high-risk procedure, particularly in intubated and mechanically ventilated intensive care unit (ICU) patients requiring multiple invasive devices. Data from prospective multicentre studies using standardized definitions of adverse events (AEs) remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of AEs during IHT and to identify factors associated with their occurrence.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicentre observational study in nine French ICUs. All consecutive IHTs involving intubated and mechanically ventilated adult patients were included. AEs were defined according to the 2011 SFAR recommendations and recorded across five predefined transport phases, from preparation to patient reinstallation. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with AE occurrence.

RESULTS: Among 160 analysed transports, at least one AE occurred in 56.4% of IHTs (95% CI 48.6-64.2). Most events were clinical (47.5%); serious AEs were rare (0.6%). The procedural phase accounted for the highest proportion of events (66.7%). In multivariable analysis, AE occurrence was independently associated with neuromuscular blocking agent use (OR 4.0 [1.2-13.5]), ≥4 invasive devices (OR 2.6 [1.1-6.1]), and ≥3 accompanying staff members (OR 2.7 [1.4-5.5]). Emergency status and transport indication were not significantly associated with AE occurrence.

CONCLUSION: IHT of mechanically ventilated ICU patients is associated with a high rate of AEs, driven primarily by patient severity and procedural complexity. These findings support the need for structured transport protocols and larger multicentre studies to evaluate targeted safety strategies.

articles.title: How vascular territories change in intracranial atherosclerosis - a CT perfusion flow territory mapping study.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial atherosclerosis is common and has a high recurrence rate. It has been theorized that vascular territory volumes change in ICAD due to collateral activation, but this has not been demonstrated. CT perfusion territory flow mapping is a recently developed technique that uses the collision of wavefronts from perfusion data of different territories to calculate territory volumes. We aimed to investigate how territory volumes change in ICAD.

METHODS: This was a multi-centre international case-control study where we measured arterial territory volumes in 72 patients with ICAD, as well as 49 controls using CT perfusion-based flow territory mapping. ICAD-affected and ICAD-adjacent territory volumes were compared to their homologous pairs and to control patient territories. Correlation between territory volumes and percentage vessel stenosis was tested.

RESULTS: The territory volumes in the ICAD-affected regions were significantly smaller (p<0.001) and adjacent territories significantly larger (p<0.001) than homologous contralateral territories. ICAD-affected territory volume ratios were also significantly smaller than control territory ratios, median 0.84 (IQR 0.63-0.99) vs 0.97 (IQR 0.87-1.09), p<0.001. For the largest group (MCA affected territories), the median of the ICAD affected sides was 232.3mls (IQR 162.4-275.9mls) and the median of the unaffected sides was 270.1mls (IQR 241.0-303.7mls). Adjacent territory ratios were significantly larger than control territory ratios 1.19 (IQR 0.95-1.55) vs 0.97 (IQR 0.87-1.09), p<0.001.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that the presence of ICAD is associated with reduction in volume of the affected arterial territory with increases in the adjacent territory volumes.

articles.title: The effects of exercise on pulmonary function and respiratory muscle strength in patients with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) have impaired respiratory function. Although exercise provides several benefits in this population, its effects on respiratory outcomes remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities on pulmonary function and respiratory muscle strength in patients with CKD across different stages.

METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies. Searches were conducted from database inception to May 2026 in MEDLINE/PubMed, CENTRAL, EMBASE, PEDro, Web of Science, LILACS and supplementary searches of grey literature sources, without language or publication-year restrictions. Outcomes included forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), FEV1/FVC ratio, peak expiratory flow (PEF), maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), and maximal expiratory pressure (MEP). Random-effects models were used for meta-analyses.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included in the meta-nalyses. Exercise significantly improved FVC (MD=0.25 L; 95% CI: 0.01-0.50; I2=51%), MIP (MD=11.47 cmH2O; 95% CI: 7.73-15.22; I2=52%), and MEP (MD=10.42 cmH2O; 95% CI: 5.53-15.31; I2=58%), whereas no significant effects were observed for FEV1, FEV1/FVC, or PEF. In exploratory subgroup analyses, both respiratory interventions and peripheral exercise significantly improved MIP and MEP. However, no significant subgroup differences between exercise modalities were observed for MIP (p=0.67), MEP (p=0.20), or FVC (p=0.70).

CONCLUSIONS: Exercise may improve FVC and respiratory muscle strength in patients undergoing haemodialysis. Exploratory analyses did not provide evidence effects between respiratory interventions and peripheral exercise. These findings suggest that exercise may be considered a complementary strategy to improve respiratory function in rehabilitation programmes for these patients.

articles.title: Glycaemic remission in type 2 diabetes and subsequent microvascular and macrovascular outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes remission may reduce the long-term burden of vascular complications, but the magnitude and consistency of this association remain uncertain. We systematically evaluated whether remission was associated with lower subsequent microvascular and macrovascular or cardiovascular risk compared with non-remission. PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched through 31 August 2026 for longitudinal cohorts comparing adults with and without biochemical remission. Eight reports from seven independent cohorts were included, with five cohorts contributing to quantitative vascular synthesis. Remission was associated with lower microvascular risk (pooled HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.59-0.77; I2 = 4.1%) and lower macrovascular or cardiovascular risk (pooled HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.61-0.87; I2 = 8.7%). Findings were consistent across lifestyle, routine-care, and metabolic-surgery settings. Additional cohorts associated remission with lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. However, risk of bias was moderate or serious because remission was not randomized and may reflect favorable post-baseline risk-factor changes. Type 2 diabetes remission is associated with substantially fewer subsequent vascular events, but causal attribution remains uncertain. Remission should complement, rather than replace, continued complication surveillance and multifactorial risk management.

Anterior cingulate cortex glutamatergic projection neurons modulate motion sickness susceptibility via a cortico-vestibular circuit.
articles.abstract: Motion sickness (MS) is a prevalent and debilitating vestibular disorder with limited therapeutic options, yet the cortical mechanisms governing individual susceptibility remain elusive. Using a biaxial rotation mouse model, we investigated the role of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in MS by integrating morphology, calcium imaging, electrophysiology, cell ablation, chemogenetics, and optogenetics. Biaxial rotation induced hypothermia, anorexia, taste avoidance, locomotor hypoactivity, and gait incoordination. ACC pyramidal neurons exhibited enhanced activation and increased intrinsic excitability following vestibular stimulation. Ablation of ACC CaMKII+ neurons alleviated MS symptoms, and bidirectional chemogenetic manipulation demonstrated that ACC glutamatergic projection neurons are both necessary and sufficient for MS behaviors. Furthermore, the ACC to medial vestibular nuclei parvicellular part (MVePC) projection was identified as a previously uncharacterized cortico-vestibular circuit that bidirectionally mediates MS susceptibility. Whole-brain projectome analysis further revealed anatomically heterogeneous projection subtypes of ACC-medial vestibular neurons. These findings advance our understanding of the cortical mechanisms underlying MS and establish the ACC-MVePC pathway as a mechanistic entry point for future neuromodulatory strategies.

articles.title: Impact of Early Bloodstream Infections on Clinical Outcomes Following Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation with Post-Transplant Cyclophosphamide-Based GVHD Prophylaxis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) remain a significant cause of morbidity and mortality following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT), particularly during the post-transplant neutropenia and immune reconstitution phase. Notably, studies have identified high rates of BSI in the early post-transplant period with PTCy regimens, including single-center cohorts that have highlighted Candida, Enterococcus, and gram-negative rods (GNRs) as predominant pathogens. However, the broader clinical impact of pathogen-specific BSI on post-HCT outcomes in PTCy recipients remains incompletely defined. We aimed to study allo-HCT outcomes in patients who developed BSI in the first 100 days.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective, registry-based cohort analysis using dataset P-5242 from the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR). Adult patients who underwent allo-HCT with PTCy-based GVHD prophylaxis between 2009 and 2016 were included. Microbiologically confirmed BSIs within the first 100 days post-HCT were categorized by pathogen. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations between specific pathogens and acute GVHD (grade II-IV), chronic GVHD, time to neutrophil engraftment (ANC ≥ 500), overall survival (OS), and Non-relapse mortality (NRM). Adjusted covariates included patient age, gender, disease type, conditioning intensity, graft source, donor type, Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-Comorbidity Index, and Karnofsky performance score.

RESULTS: A total of 385 patients who developed BSI within the first 100 days post-transplant were included. The mean age was 50.0 years (SD 18.6), and 60.5% were male. 49.1% had acute myeloid leukemia (AML), 15.8% had acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), 26.5% had myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), and 8.6% had non-malignant diseases. Total body irradiation (TBI) was used in 56.4% patients, and only 5.7% received anti-thymocyte globulin. Graft sources were peripheral blood stem cells (PBSC) in 54.8%, bone marrow in 45.2%, and cord blood in 0.3%. 51.2% had a Karnofsky Performance Score of <90, and 53.8% had an HCT-comorbidity index score>3. In multivariable analysis, Candida infections and Enterococcus were associated with inferior survival (HR 3.369, 95% CI, p < 0.001, and HR 1.497, 95% CI, p = 0.049, respectively). Non-Enterobacteriaceae gram-negative rod BSI was also independently associated with inferior non-relapse mortality (HR 2.198; 95% CI, p = 0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: This analysis demonstrates that early bloodstream infections significantly alter clinical outcomes in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients receiving PTCy-based GVHD prophylaxis. Infections caused by Candida, Enterococcus species, and non-Enterobacteriaceae GNRs were associated with poorer survival. These findings highlight the importance of enhanced antimicrobial surveillance and interventions to protect patients against high-risk pathogens.

articles.title: Adoption and Utilization Trends of a New Diagnosis Code for Pediatric Intestinal Failure: A multicenter retrospective cross-sectional database analysis.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In October 2023, a new ICD-10-CM diagnosis code (K90.83) for intestinal failure (IF) was introduced in the United States. Previous studies have relied on complex algorithms to find intestinal failure patients in large databases.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize the use of the new diagnosis code for intestinal failure and its association with healthcare resource utilization.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cross-sectional study using the Pediatric Health Information System database from October 2023 through December 2025. Pediatric inpatient encounters coded with K90.83 were identified. Temporal trends in code utilization were assessed using hospital fixed-effects Poisson regression with robust standard errors clustered at the hospital level. Secondary analyses examined clinical characteristics and cumulative inpatient utilization among children who ever received an IF diagnosis code.

RESULTS: We identified 3,362 IF-coded encounters from 1,869 children across 48 hospitals. Median age at first IF-coded encounter was 2.1 years. IF-coded encounters increased linearly by 2.6% per month (incidence rate ratio 1.026, 95% CI 1.012-1.040; p<0.001), corresponding to an approximate 36% annual increase, without a significant change in slope over time. Among IF-coded encounters, 86.9% included parenteral nutrition and 21.9% included CLABSI. Children who ever received an IF diagnosis code accounted for 25,144 inpatient encounters totaling 241,748 hospital days and more than $1.21 billion in standardized inpatient costs.

CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of the IF diagnosis code has increased gradually. Although clinically coherent, incomplete adoption likely underestimates true disease burden. Even when identified solely by diagnosis code, pediatric IF is associated with substantial inpatient morbidity and cost.

articles.title: Lifestyle determinants of glycemic responses to snacking in free-living adults without diabetes: an intensive longitudinal observational study.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Snacking is common and can contribute to blood glucose fluctuations. However, large studies investigating lifestyle determinants of glucose responses to snacking under real-world conditions are scarce.

METHODS: In this intensive longitudinal observational study, we analyzed data from 3,325 snacking episodes captured by ecological momentary assessment surveys (six daily), continuous glucose monitoring, and accelerometry over nine free-living days among 785 male and female adults aged 21-69 years without diabetes in Singapore. Postprandial glucose responses were assessed using 2-hour postprandial glucose incremental area under the curve (iAUC) following snacking episodes. Lifestyle exposures included consumption of snack foods and beverages, snack timing, postprandial physical activity, and daily physical activity and sleep prior to snacking episodes. Linear mixed-effects models were used to estimate within-person and between-person associations between these exposures and 2-hour postprandial glucose iAUC.

RESULTS: The average 2-hour postprandial glucose iAUC was 63.8 (SD: 61.8) mmol/l*minute after snacking episodes. Consumption of bread or buns (within-person β: 30.7; 95% CI: 20.4, 41.1), deep-fried foods (β: 19.8; CI: 9.2, 30.4), sweets (β: 14.6; CI: 6.6, 22.6), and sugary beverages (β: 12.2; CI: 4.3, 20.0) was associated with higher glucose iAUC. In contrast, greater postprandial moderate-to-vigorous physical activity was associated with a lower glucose iAUC (β: -28.4 per hour; CI: -49.2, -7.5). In addition, glucose iAUC was higher following afternoon snacking (β: 9.3; CI: 2.0, 16.6) and early evening (β: 10.7; CI: 2.5, 18.9) than morning snacking.

CONCLUSIONS: Snack composition, snack timing, and postprandial physical activity were associated with postprandial glucose responses to snacking in adults without diabetes. Recommendations on snacking-related lifestyle behaviors may improve glycemic control in daily life.

articles.title: Hippo-YAP signaling: A novel pathway regulating platelet activation and thrombogenesis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the functional significance of Hippo-YAP signaling in platelet activation and thrombosis.

METHODS: Expression and phosphorylation of YAP were examined in platelets exposed to physiological agonists as well as mechanical cues (adhesion to matrices having varying stiffness and activation of mechanosensitive channel Piezo1). Involvements of LATS kinase and RhoA-ROCK-actomyosin axis in YAP signaling were evaluated. Effect of pharmacological inhibition of YAP on platelet activation parameters (αIIbβ3 activation, adhesion, α-granule secretion, extracellular vesicle release, and fibrin clot retraction) were studied ex vivo. Contribution of YAP to pathological thrombosis was further investigated in a murine model in vivo. YAP activity was also assessed in platelets obtained from patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome.

KEY FINDINGS: Platelets expressed mRNA transcript as well as peptide of YAP, whose phosphorylation (at Ser-127) was modulated in response to physiological agonists and mechanical stimuli. Adhesion to immobilized matrix, Piezo1 stimulation, and exposure to agonists markedly enhanced YAP expression. Concomitantly, these factors prompted dephosphorylation of YAP, suggestive of YAP functional impairment, driven by the upstream LATS kinase and RhoA-ROCK-actomyosin signaling axis. Inhibition of YAP impaired key platelet functions ex vivo, that included integrin αIIbβ3 activation, adhesion, α-granule secretion, extracellular vesicle release, and fibrin clot retraction, and exerted marked protection against pathological thrombosis in a murine model in vivo. Consistent with above, platelets obtained from patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome were found to harbour enhanced YAP activity.

CONCLUSION: These findings underscore a contributing role of YAP in thrombogenesis, highlighting its potential as an antiplatelet therapeutic target.

articles.title: Beyond the glomerular filtration barrier: How endothelial glycocalyx damage drives kidney disease in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Current therapies for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) slow progression but fail to halt irreversible renal fibrosis, largely because early pathogenic drivers are overlooked. While endothelial glycocalyx disruption is recognized as an initiator of albuminuria, existing literature lacks a unified model connecting this initial barrier loss to the full fibrotic cascade. This review systematically integrates the molecular networks driving glycocalyx degradation, specifically detailing the synergistic interplay among oxidative stress, sheddase activation, and the AGEs/RAGE/NF-κB axis. Unlike previous reviews, we explicitly map how the shedding of core components-such as Syndecans and Glypicans-triggers downstream leukocyte adhesion via the intracellular MyD88/NF-κB pathway, actively propagating renal inflammation and exacerbating the progression of renal fibrosis. By redefining glycocalyx damage as a critical pathological amplifier that actively drives glomerular filtration barrier disruption and subsequent inflammatory and fibrotic cascades, rather than a passive structural consequence of hyperglycemia, we expose critical gaps in standard DKD management. We further critically evaluate the clinical viability of emerging glycocalyx-targeted strategies, highlighting specific applications for early diagnostic biomarkers and addressing current challenges in targeted drug delivery, ultimately providing a precise roadmap for preventing DKD progression.

articles.title: CONGENITAL HEPATOPULMONARY FUSION IN RIGHT CONGENITAL DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA: SURGICAL STRATEGY AND OUTCOMES IN A MULTICENTER COHORT.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Congenital hepatopulmonary fusion (CHPF) is a rare anomaly associated with right congenital diaphragmatic hernia (RCDH), for which optimal diagnosis and surgical management remain undefined. This study aimed to explore the impact of surgical separation on outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective multicenter study reviewed neonates with intraoperatively or radiologically confirmed CHPF associated with RCDH. Demographic data, imaging, surgical strategy, and outcomes were analyzed. Patients were stratified according to whether surgical separation of the fusion was performed (CHPF-S) or not (CHPF-NS).

RESULTS: Forty-three patients were included (26 CHPF-S and 17 CHPF-NS). Prenatal diagnosis of RCDH occurred in 20.9% of cases, while most diagnoses were made postnatally. Imaging findings suggestive of CHPF were identified preoperatively in a minority of patients, with computed tomography angiography providing additional information regarding vascular anatomy in selected cases. Baseline demographic characteristics, gestational age, birth weight, and CDH defect distribution were comparable between groups. The age at surgical repair differed, however not significantly, with earlier intervention in the CHPF-S group (9.0 ± 15.8 vs 17.9 ± 24.2 days, p=0.099). Complete parenchymal fusion was more frequently observed in the CHPF-NS group, whereas partial fusion was more common in the CHPF-S group. Pulmonary hypertension occurred in 55.8% of patients and extracorporeal life support was required in 7.0%. Overall mortality was 27.9%, including 7 deaths in the CHPF-NS group and 5 in the CHPF-S group (41.2% vs 19.2%, p=0.117), predominantly related to severe pulmonary hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: Surgical separation of the fusion may be selectively advisable in hemodynamically stable patients with a thin membrane or partial fusion, although non-separation often remains prudent. In critically ill neonates, patch repair or closure around the fused organs without separation represents a safer alternative. Early suspicion of CHPF in RCDH and thorough preoperative planning are essential to optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Incident and Recurrent Sexually Transmitted Infections by Gender Identity Among Sex Workers on HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex workers on HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) experience high bacterial sexually transmitted infection (STI) rates. We assessed associations between gender identity and first/recurrent STI incidence to inform risk-stratified screening.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study (Madrid, 2022-2026) evaluated sex workers initiating PrEP. Participants underwent quarterly screening for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and Treponema pallidum. We used Cox and Prentice-Williams-Peterson models to evaluate first and recurrent STIs, adjusting for confounders.

RESULTS: We included 147 sex workers (71 transgender women, 48 cisgender men, 28 cisgender women) with ≥3 months follow-up and ≥1 STI screening. First STI incidence was 5.14/100 person-months (cisgender men: 6.90; cisgender women: 2.13). Recurrent STI incidence was 3.26/100 person-months. Most incident STIs (93.1%) were asymptomatic. In multivariable analyses (reference: cisgender women), cisgender men had higher hazards for first (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.20; 95% CI, 1.47-6.99) and recurrent STIs (aHR, 4.04; 95% CI, 1.83-8.95). Transgender women also had higher hazards for first (aHR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.02-4.22) and recurrent STIs (aHR, 2.25; 95% CI, 1.10-4.61).

CONCLUSIONS: STI incidence during PrEP differs by gender identity, being highest in cisgender men and lowest in cisgender women. These findings support evaluating risk-stratified screening approaches over uniform quarterly guidelines.

articles.title: Telmisartan: distinct pharmacological features, partial PPAR-γ modulation, and pleiotropic therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Telmisartan, a selective angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor antagonist, is widely used in the management of hypertension by selectively blocking AT1 receptor mediated signaling, thereby attenuating the deleterious effects of excessive renin angiotensin aldosterone system (RAAS) activation without directly inhibiting ACE2, AT2 receptors, or other components of the renin angiotensin system. This results in reduced vascular resistance, decreased aldosterone secretion, and improved cardiovascular and renal protection. This review outlines the broadened therapeutic scope of telmisartan, highlighting its established pleiotropic mechanisms and emerging therapeutic applications beyond its primary antihypertensive indication. Accumulating data indicate that it influences metabolic homeostasis by enhancing insulin responsiveness and regulating lipid dynamics, suggesting potential utility in conditions associated with metabolic imbalance. In addition, telmisartan demonstrates the capacity to modulate inflammatory pathways and counteract oxidative stress, contributing to improved vascular integrity and functional stability. Compared with other ARBs, telmisartan is distinguished by its partial PPARγ agonistic activity, prolonged elimination half-life, high lipophilicity, and sustained AT1 receptor blockade, which may provide additional metabolic and vascular effects. However, these pharmacological distinctions do not consistently translate into superior clinical outcomes across all therapeutic settings, and direct comparative evidence remains limited. Emerging evidence also points toward its involvement in interconnected cellular signaling networks, extending its relevance in complex disease mechanisms. Collectively, these findings support the concept that telmisartan exerts diverse biological effects, positioning it as a versatile therapeutic agent in modern clinical practice with implications that extend beyond traditional RAAS inhibition.

articles.title: The Immunomodulatory Landscape of Anesthetic Agents: Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and Therapeutic Potential.
articles.abstract: The pharmacological actions of anesthetic agents extend far beyond neurodepression, encompassing complex immunomodulatory effects with implications for perioperative immune function, surgical outcomes, infection risk, and cancer biology. This review critically evaluates current evidence on how different anesthetic classes influence innate and adaptive immunity, examining cellular targets and signaling mechanisms. Rather than viewing anesthesia as monolithically immunosuppressive, current evidence supports a nuanced understanding in which immunological effects vary according to anesthetic agent, dose, timing, and clinical context. Volatile anesthetics (isoflurane, sevoflurane) attenuate natural killer cell cytotoxicity and neutrophil function, promote lymphocyte apoptosis with T helper 2 cell skewing, and exhibit context-dependent anti-inflammatory properties. Propofol preserves immune function by attenuating ROS-mediated cellular damage and maintaining Th1/Th2 balance. Ketamine exerts concentration-dependent immunomodulatory effects including anti-inflammatory actions on macrophages and biphasic lymphocyte modulation. We discuss clinical implications in oncological surgery, sepsis, and autoimmune disorders, emphasizing strengths and limitations of current evidence. Emerging frontiers include personalized anesthesia guided by immune phenotyping, novel targeted agents, and the gut microbiome as a modulator of anesthetic-immune interactions, though these remain promising directions rather than established practice. This review integrates mechanistic insights with clinical evidence and identifies priorities for translational research.

articles.title: Divergent Cardiac and Renal Outcomes by Systolic Blood Pressure in HFrEF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated systolic blood pressure (SBP) is associated with paradoxically lower mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but whether this reflects underlying pathophysiology or residual confounding remains uncertain. Because higher SBP is also a risk factor for kidney failure, we tested the hypothesis that a higher risk of kidney failure despite lower mortality would support a pathophysiological explanation for this mortality paradox.

METHODS: We assembled a propensity score-matched cohort of 59,834 patients with HFrEF, hypertension, and no baseline kidney failure. The 29,917 pairs with SBP ≥130 versus <130 mmHg were balanced on 77 baseline characteristics. Outcomes were two-year all-cause mortality and incident kidney failure. Cox regression estimated associations of SBP ≥130 mmHg with outcomes, and restricted cubic splines assessed nonlinearity across the SBP continuum.

RESULTS: All-cause mortality occurred in 24.9% of patients with SBP <130 mmHg and 23.0% of patients with SBP ≥130 mmHg (HR associated with SBP ≥130 mmHg, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.88-0.94). Corresponding rates for kidney failure were 1.0% and 1.5% (HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.24-1.66). SBP had a nonlinear association with mortality (P<0.001 for nonlinearity), with progressively higher risk at SBP below 130 mmHg but no higher risk above 130 mmHg. The association with kidney failure was linear (P=0.68 for nonlinearity) with progressively higher risk above 130 mmHg.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HFrEF, elevated SBP is associated with lower mortality but a higher risk of kidney failure. These opposing cardiac and renal associations support a pathophysiological explanation for the inverse relationship between SBP and mortality in HFrEF.

articles.title: The Indispensable Role of Sham Controls in Evaluating Interventional Therapies: The Need for Objective Rigor in Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
Early Readmission and Mortality Across Periprosthetic Joint Infection Trajectories After Revision Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Revision for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) carries greater morbidity than aseptic revision, but infection history alone does not distinguish patients who remain infection-free from those who develop recurrent PJI. We examined readmission and mortality across an exploratory revision-infection trajectory framework.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,228 patients who underwent revision hip or knee arthroplasty between September 30, 2008, and September 1, 2024. Patients were categorized into four trajectory groups according to the indication for index revision and subsequent post-revision PJI status. Outcomes were 90-day unplanned readmission after index revision and all-cause mortality. Because post-revision PJI status was determined during follow-up, 90-day readmission was interpreted descriptively as an early feature of the observed trajectory; mortality was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Post-revision PJI occurred in 43 patients (3.5%). The median follow-up was 73.7 months (range, 0.7 to 202.2). Among patients who developed post-revision PJI during follow-up, six of 43 (14.0%) had a 90-day readmission, compared with 54 of 1,185 (4.6%) without post-revision PJI (adjusted odds ratio (OR), 4.39; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.69 to 11.42; P = 0.002). The highest observed readmission rate was in the trajectory defined by index revision for PJI followed by recurrent PJI (five of 30 [16.7%]). In Cox proportional hazards analyses, post-revision PJI was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio (HR), 3.51; 95% CI, 1.34 to 9.22; P = 0.011); this trajectory also had the highest mortality point estimate (adjusted HR, 5.31; 95% CI, 1.88 to 15.00; P = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Early readmission was more common among patients whose trajectories included post-revision PJI, whereas the trajectory defined by index revision for PJI followed by recurrent PJI had the highest observed mortality. The sequence of revision and infection events may provide more context than infection history alone, but these exploratory associations require external validation.

articles.title: Cemented Femoral Fixation for Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty in the United States: How Surgeon-Cemented Volume Impacts Failure Risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although cementless femoral fixation remains the United States (U.S.) standard, recent data shows a decline in exclusive cementless usage from 34 to 14% between 2018 and 2024. Whether surgeon-cemented total hip arthroplasty (THA) volume affects implant survivorship remains unclear in this traditionally low-volume environment. As such, we evaluated the association between surgeon cemented stem volume and risk of all-cause revision.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used a national database to identify primary THAs with cemented femoral fixation from 2016 to 2020. Surgeons were classified by their five-year cemented stem volume: Group 1 (less than 60 stems) or Group 2 (≥ 60 stems). Patients had a minimum two-year follow-up and were propensity score-matched 1:1 based on demographics and comorbidities. A total of 7,174 matched patients were analyzed (3,587 per cohort). Outcomes were all-cause revision, periprosthetic fracture (PPF), mechanical loosening, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and dislocation within five years.

RESULTS: Patients treated by Group 1 surgeons had higher rates of all study outcomes. At two years, Group 1 patients had higher odds of all-cause revision (odds ratio (OR) = 2.10; 95% confidence interval: 1.44 to 3.11; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed revision risk diverged sharply within the first postoperative year and persisted through five years. At two-year follow-up, Group 1 patients had increased risk of PPF (OR = 1.58; P = 0.038), loosening (OR = 2.21; P < 0.001), PJI (OR = 2.19; P < 0.001), and dislocation (OR = 2.51; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Low surgeon cemented stem volume is strongly associated with increased risk of revision following cemented THA. While cemented femoral fixation remains a useful alternative for high-risk patients undergoing elective THA, the benefits may be compromised if the surgery is performed by surgeons whose specific volume for this type of fixation is low.

articles.title: Systemic Exposure and Renal Safety After Intrawound Vancomycin Powder in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Intrawound vancomycin powder has been proposed as a local prophylactic measure, but concerns remain regarding systemic absorption and nephrotoxicity. This study evaluated systemic absorption, renal safety, and postoperative infection outcomes after intrawound vancomycin use in primary TKA.

METHODS: This prospective comparative cohort study included 260 patients who underwent primary TKA at a single tertiary care center: 130 in the vancomycin cohort and 130 in the control cohort. The vancomycin cohort received one gram of intrawound vancomycin powder before closure. Serum vancomycin levels were measured 12 hours postoperatively. Serial renal function and kidney disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO)-defined acute kidney injury (AKI) was analyzed in all patients. Infection and wound-complication outcomes were assessed in patients who completed at least six months of follow-up.

RESULTS: The 12-hour serum vancomycin levels were below the laboratory reporting threshold (less than 1.00 mg/L) in 104 of 130 patients (80.0%). Among the remaining 26 patients who had numerical values, the median concentration was 0.28 mg/L (interquartile range [IQR], 0.21 to 1.26; range, 0.01 to 2.76 mg/L), which was well below systemic therapeutic levels. Serum vancomycin concentration was not correlated with early changes in serum creatinine or estimated glomerular filtration rate (Spearman ρ range, -0.08 to -0.03; all P ≥ 0.720). AKI occurred in nine patients (6.9%) in the vancomycin group and eight patients (6.2%) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.13; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 3.04; P = 1.000). All AKI events in the vancomycin group were stage 1. Surgery-related complication rates were similar between groups, with no statistically significant differences in PJI, superficial infection, or wound dehiscence.

CONCLUSION: Intrawound administration of one gram of vancomycin powder in primary TKA resulted in minimal systemic exposure and showed no clinically meaningful nephrotoxicity signal. However, it was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in infection or wound-complication outcomes; therefore, these data do not support its routine prophylactic use in primary TKA.

articles.title: Beyond the Surgical Factors: Preoperative Habits, Cutaneous Sensation, and Adaptive Strategies as Predictors of Kneeling Ability Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kneeling is consistently the poorest patient-reported outcome after TKA. While previous studies have examined surgical variables as predictors of kneeling ability following TKA, a discrepancy between patients' perceived and observed ability to kneel suggests that kneeling behavior is influenced heavily by psychological or contextual factors. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate several non-surgical factors as predictors of kneeling ability following TKA.

METHODS: Patients who underwent primary TKA between May 1, 2021, and April 30, 2024, were included. There were 165 patients who were successfully contacted for administration by telephone of a novel patient-reported questionnaire that assessed pre- and post-surgical kneeling frequency and exercise regularity, activity-based need for kneeling, adaptations to kneeling strategy, and cutaneous patellar sensation. Statistical analyses were conducted to identify relationships between variables.

RESULTS: Greater exercise activity before surgery was associated with higher frequency of kneeling both pre- (P < 0.001) and post-surgery (P < 0.001). Higher perceived importance of kneeling was associated with higher frequency of kneeling both pre-surgery (P < 0.001) and post-surgery (P < 0.001). Those who indicated kneeling for leisure activities were more likely to employ adaptations to their kneeling strategy and to report a higher frequency of kneeling post-surgery (P < 0.001). Greater reported severity of abnormal sensation on the patellar region was associated with greater reported impact on kneeling (P < 0.001). Hypersensitivity and burning or shock-like sensations were associated with lower frequency of kneeling post-surgery (P = 0.046 and P = 0.035, respectively), while numbness and hypersensitivity were associated with an established habit of avoiding kneeling (P = 0.017).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that kneeling outcomes following TKA may be influenced by patients' pre-surgical exercise and kneeling behavior. Activity-specific motivation and greater perceived importance of kneeling were associated with behavioral self-management and improved functional outcome. Also, we found that varying superficial sensory changes on the patellar region demonstrated distinct associations with kneeling-related behaviors.

articles.title: Impact of Revised Cardiac Risk Index, Individual Risk Factors, and Their Duration on Major Adverse Cardiac Events After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Nationwide Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) is widely used to assess major adverse cardiac events (MACE) preoperatively, the impact of risk-factor duration and age stratification on its predictive performance after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains unclear. This study evaluated post-TKA MACE incidence and risk according to RCRI score, individual risk factors, their preoperative duration, and age strata.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used a nationwide claims database, including primary TKA patients (2017 to 2021). The RCRI was modified for claims data by defining renal impairment as chronic kidney disease stage ≥ 3. Following propensity-score matching by RCRI scores (0, 1, ≥ 2), risk factors were categorized by preoperative duration: absent, ≤ one year, or greater than one year. The primary outcomes were 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year MACE. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using stratified Cox models.

RESULTS: Among 72,672 matched patients, MACE incidence was 0.18, 0.40, and 1.43% at 30 days, 90 days, and one year, respectively. The MACE risk increased with the RCRI category; versus RCRI 0, RCRI 1 raised the postoperative 1-year risk (aHR 1.34, P < 0.001), whereas RCRI ≥ 2 roughly doubled the risk across all periods (aHR 1.86 to 2.15, all P-values ≤ 0.003). Moderate-to-severe renal impairment was the most consistent predictor (all P-values ≤ 0.001), especially when diagnosed ≤ one year preoperatively. Among RCRI ≥ 2 patients, age ≥ 75 years increased 30-day MACE risk (aHR 2.27, P = 0.004), whereas risk in those aged less than 75 years became significant at 90 days (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The RCRI provides predictive validity for post-TKA MACE. Beyond static scores, risk-factor duration and age stratification offer incremental prognostic value. Patients who had recent moderate-to-severe renal impairment and older age (≥ 75 years) combined with RCRI ≥ 2 warrant closer perioperative monitoring.

articles.title: Mitochondria-associated ferroptosis in ischemic stroke: Pathophysiological evolution, interorganelle crosstalk, and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) results from an acute interruption of cerebral blood flow and the ensuing collapse of energy metabolism. Although vascular recanalization can salvage the ischemic penumbra, its overall benefit remains constrained by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, contributes to neuronal injury after IS and can amplify ischemia/reperfusion injury. By integrating energy metabolism, iron homeostasis, and redox balance, mitochondria can shape ferroptosis susceptibility within the energy-depleted, iron-dysregulated, and oxidatively stressed ischemic brain. However, most studies have examined iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation at the whole-cell level, leaving the temporal and interorganelle dimensions of mitochondrial regulation of ferroptosis insufficiently integrated. Here, we organize mitochondria-associated ferroptosis across the pathological course of IS, from metabolic reprogramming and substrate accumulation during ischemia to the reverse electron transport-associated reactive oxygen species burst during early reperfusion and subsequent disruption of mitochondrial quality control. We further examine mitochondrial crosstalk with the endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, lipid droplets, and nucleus, compare ferroptosis susceptibility across neurovascular unit cell populations, and map these mechanisms onto pharmacological interventions and mechanistically plausible therapeutic windows. Finally, we assess barriers to the clinical translation of mitochondria-targeted therapies and provide a stage-resolved framework for developing neuroprotective strategies in IS.

articles.title: Tongmai Yizhi Decoction Improves Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment by Inhibiting Monoamine Oxidase to Reduce Dopamine Metabolism.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Tongmai Yizhi Decoction (TMYZD), a classic Chinese ethnomedical formula derived from Danggui Shaoyao San and Shenghui Decoction, has long been used for post-stroke amnesia and dementia as it activates blood circulation, tonifies kidney essence, resolves phlegm, and opens cerebral orifices. Its clinical efficacy against post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is verified, but the underlying pharmacological mechanisms remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effect of TMYZD against PSCI and verify whether it acts via modulating the dopamine metabolic pathway to elucidate its molecular targets and pharmacological basis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology was applied to predict therapeutic targets, and metabolomics combined with mass spectrometry was used to identify regulated pathways. In vivo, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion rats were assessed for cognitive function, synaptic ultrastructure, and key target proteins. In vitro, HT22 cells under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation with monoamine oxidase-B (MAOB) overexpression were used for target validation.

RESULTS: PSCI rats exhibited severe cognitive decline and synaptic structural damage. Monoamine oxidase-A (MAOA) and MAOB were identified as core therapeutic targets. TMYZD significantly regulated the dopamine pathway, upregulated tyrosine hydroxylase and dopamine receptor D2, downregulated MAOA/MAOB, and ameliorated synaptic injury. MAOB overexpression partially abolished the neuroprotective effect of TMYZD, confirming MAOB as a key target.

CONCLUSIONS: TMYZD improves cognitive function in PSCI by regulating dopamine metabolism, elevating dopamine levels, and enhancing synaptic plasticity, with MAOB as a critical target. These findings provide scientific evidence for the ethnomedical application of TMYZD in PSCI.

articles.title: Bioactivity-guided identification of antithrombotic peptides from an ethanol-soluble fraction of Hirudo nipponia with anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Medicinal leeches have long been administered orally in traditional Chinese medicine for blood stasis-related disorders. The thermal instability and poor oral bioavailability of hirudin suggest that other heat- and digestion-resistant constituents may contribute to the pharmacological activity of orally administered leech preparations.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To characterize the antithrombotic activity of an ethanol-soluble fraction derived from processed Hirudo nipponia decoction pieces (Hn70) and identify peptide candidates with anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Hn70 was prepared by aqueous extraction followed by 70% ethanol fractionation. Its anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities, in vivo antithrombotic effects, and retention of anticoagulant activity under thermal and simulated gastrointestinal conditions were evaluated. Antithrombin activity was quantified using recombinant hirudin as an activity reference. The major active fraction was isolated by bioactivity-guided gel filtration, followed by coagulation factor and platelet aggregation assays, nLC-MS/MS-based de novo sequencing, bioinformatics screening, molecular docking, and functional validation of selected peptides.

RESULTS: Hn70 showed concentration-dependent anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities and significantly reduced carrageenan-induced thrombosis in vivo. Six batches showed a specific antithrombin activity of 1.156 ± 0.020 ATU·mg-1 dry Hn70 (CV, 1.70%). Hn70 retained substantial anticoagulant activity after thermal and simulated gastrointestinal treatment. Hn70-D was identified as a major active fraction that reduced multiple coagulation-factor activities and inhibited platelet aggregation. Twenty-eight peptides were identified, and seven selected synthetic peptides exhibited both activities in single-concentration assays.

CONCLUSION: Hn70 is an antithrombotic fraction of Hirudo nipponia that retains substantial anticoagulant activity after thermal treatment and simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Bioactivity-guided analysis identified Hn70-D and candidate peptides for further investigation of its antithrombotic pharmacology.

articles.title: Aqueous Hellenia speciosa rhizome extract attenuates hepatic injury in high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhizomes of Hellenia speciosa (J.Koenig) S.R.Dutta (Costaceae), used in Ayurvedic and folk medicine as Costus speciosus for diabetes and jaundice, remain underexplored. No chemically characterised aqueous preparation has been evaluated against a clinical comparator in diabetes-associated hepatic injury.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To test whether an aqueous H. speciosa rhizome extract (CS-AE) is associated with attenuated hepatic injury in high-fat diet (HFD)/streptozotocin (STZ) diabetic male rats, and to benchmark it against metformin (MET).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Wistar rats were randomised into six groups (n = 10): normal control (NC), NC + CS-AE, diabetic control (DC), and DC receiving MET (200 mg/kg/day), CS-AE (500 mg/kg/day) or both, orally for six weeks. This single CS-AE dose is 4.5-9 times the pharmacopoeial dose. Endpoints included metabolic and hepatic biochemistry, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, protein/gene expression and histopathology. CS-AE was characterised in-house by an ICH Q2 (R2)-validated HPLC-DAD method against four markers at Schymanski Level 3.

RESULTS: Versus DC, CS-AE was associated with reduced fasting glucose (218 vs. 310 mg/dL), HOMA-IR (24.0 vs. 58.3), ALT (48 vs. 91 U/L) and malondialdehyde (3.1 vs. 4.4 nmol/mg protein; all p < 0.001). CS-AE showed larger Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 changes than MET, whereas MET showed lower glucose and higher p-AMPKα. The combination gave the most favourable profile.

CONCLUSIONS: At this supra-traditional dose, CS-AE was associated with attenuated diabetic hepatic injury; its profile complemented metformin's. Findings are association-level. Dose-response studies that include the traditional dose, and causal, pharmacokinetic, sex-inclusive and clinical studies, are required before any therapeutic recommendation.

articles.title: Finger Citron Fruit Ameliorates Ovariectomy-Induced Postmenopausal Metabolic Syndrome Through Regulation of Lipogenesis and Ferroptosis-Related Alterations.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: In Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), "Jianpi Liqi Huatan" (strengthening the spleen, regulating qi, and resolving phlegm) represents a traditional therapeutic strategy for managing obesity-associated metabolic disorders. According to TCM theory, postmenopausal MS is primarily associated with spleen deficiency, qi stagnation, and phlegm-dampness accumulation. Finger Citron Fruit (FCF), a representative Lingnan medicinal and edible herb and a core herb for Jianpi Liqi Huatan, The correspondence between the traditional properties of FCF and this TCM pathological framework provides an ethnopharmacological rationale for investigating its effects on postmenopausal metabolic dysfunction.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the metabolic effects and mechanisms of FCF in postmenopausal MS.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An ovariectomy (OVX)-induced mouse model, OA&PA-induced primary hepatocytes, and untargeted serum metabolomics were employed to evaluate the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of FCF against postmenopausal MS.

RESULTS: FCF significantly improved metabolic homeostasis by reducing body weight gain, dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, adipose tissue accumulation, and systemic inflammation, while increasing whole-body energy expenditure. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that FCF restored a candidate metabolite putatively annotated as indole-3-acetylglutamic acid. FCF improved hepatic steatosis in association with downregulation of SREBP-1c/ChREBP-related lipogenic signaling and restoration of GPX4 and SLC40A1 expression, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation.

CONCLUSIONS: FCF ameliorated postmenopausal MS by suppressing hepatic lipogenesis and attenuating ferroptosis-related alterations. These findings provide metabolomic and molecular evidence supporting its traditional "Jianpi Liqi Huatan" functions and highlight its therapeutic potential for postmenopausal MS.

articles.title: Respiratory viruses and pulmonary diseases: Mechanisms, therapies, and metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Respiratory viral infections constitute a substantial global health challenge, extending their impact beyond acute inflammation to encompass long-term pulmonary sequelae. Recent evidence highlights that respiratory viruses such as influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 reprogram host metabolism to facilitate their replication, with significant alterations in glucose metabolism playing a critical role. This metabolic reprogramming augments glucose metabolism via activation of core signaling pathways including PI3K/Akt/mTOR, HIF-1α, and c-Myc. Beyond facilitating viral proliferation, these metabolic changes crosstalk with oncogenic signaling. By triggering chronic inflammation, oxidative stress and genomic damage, they disrupt the pulmonary immune microenvironment and ultimately promote the pathogenesis of lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The pathogenesis of these symptoms is multifactorial and is influenced by genetic susceptibility, environmental exposure, and key interactions between persistent viral infection and the host's immune system. In this review, we synthesize recent advancements on the molecular mechanisms linking virus-induced metabolic alterations to the progression of pulmonary diseases. Furthermore, we discuss novel therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting these metabolic vulnerabilities to mitigate the long-term risks associated with respiratory infections.

articles.title: Fetal Cardiac Structure and Function in Diabetic Pregnancies Within Recommended Glycemic Targets: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate fetal echocardiographic parameters in diabetic pregnancies meeting guideline-recommended HbA1c targets (< 6.5%) and explore variations across glycemic strata.

DATA SOURCES: Seven databases were searched from inception through November 2025.

STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Observational studies comparing fetal echocardiograms between diabetic pregnancies (mean maternal HbA1c < 6.5%) and healthy controls.

STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: Quality was assessed using Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and JBI checklists; evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Random-effects models pooled mean differences (MD) and standardized mean differences (SMD).

RESULTS: Twenty studies (2,690 participants; 70% East Asian) were included. In the third trimester, fetuses of diabetic mothers with HbA1c < 6.5% exhibited subtle cardiac alterations: increased interventricular septal thickness (MD, 0.67 mm [95% CI, 0.31 to 1.03 mm], P < .001; 95% PI, -0.58 to 1.92 mm), decreased mitral valve E/A ratio (MD, -0.07 [95% CI, -0.12 to -0.02], P = .01; 95% PI, -0.25 to 0.11), and elevated left ventricular myocardial performance index (MD, 0.08 [95% CI, 0.05 to 0.12], P < .001; 95% PI, -0.04 to 0.20). In exploratory subgroup analyses, differences were attenuated in cohorts reporting mean HbA1c ≤ 5.5%. Univariate meta-regression identified maternal age as an exploratory moderator for mitral valve E/A ratio (P = .0016).

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetic pregnancies meeting target HbA1c (< 6.5%) exhibit subtle fetal cardiac differences, which attenuate at ≤ 5.5%. However, very low-certainty evidence, wide prediction intervals crossing null, and residual confounding limit generalizability to higher-BMI or diverse populations, warranting rigorously adjusted prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Changes in Weight and Metabolic Indices after Switching to Aripiprazole Once-Monthly in Patients with Schizophrenia According to Prior Oral Antipsychotics.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Antipsychotic-induced weight gain and metabolic disturbance are common in schizophrenia, but liability varies across agents. Aripiprazole has a relatively favorable metabolic profile, yet evidence on aripiprazole once-monthly, its long-acting injectable formulation, remains limited. We hypothesized that switching from a higher liability antipsychotic would yield a greater weight reduction than switching from a lower liability agent.

METHODS: This 16-week, prospective, open-label, multicenter study enrolled patients with stable schizophrenia. Participants were stratified by the metabolic liability of their prior oral antipsychotic (high vs. low). Participants received aripiprazole once-monthly 400 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks, with cross-titration of the prior agent. Anthropometric and metabolic parameters were assessed every 4 weeks from baseline. Weight changes at week 16 were the principal outcome, and all analyses were exploratory. Mixed models for repeated measures evaluated changes over time, adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Among the 151 participants (100 low-risk and 51 high-risk participants), weight, body mass index, and waist circumference decreased significantly in the high-risk group only, and more high-risk patients reached clinically meaningful improvement. Most lipid and glycemic indices changed little, although low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and total cholesterol decreased in both groups. Psychiatric symptoms remained stable. In a subgroup switched from oral aripiprazole (n=73), anthropometric and metabolic parameters were all unchanged.

DISCUSSION: In patients previously exposed to high-metabolic-risk antipsychotics, switching to aripiprazole once-monthly was associated with short-term reductions in weight and central adiposity-consistent with the reversal of the prior agents' metabolic burden-while psychiatric stability was maintained. Longer-term studies are needed to confirm their durability and clinical significance.

articles.title: High rate of neoplasia diagnosis at endoscopic reassessment and incidence of progression in patients with ultra-long Barrett esophagus referred to expert centers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surveillance recommendations for Barrett esophagus (BE) are based on BE length, since the risk of progression to dysplasia or esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) has been shown to increase with greater BE length. The 2023 European Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Guideline on BE advises referral to Barrett expert centers (BECs) for surveillance of ultra-long ( ≥ 10 cm) BE. This study evaluated the outcomes of expert care for patients with ultra-long BE in the Netherlands.

METHODS: This retrospective, nationwide cohort study including patients referred with ultra-long nondysplastic BE (NDBE) to Dutch BECs. Outcome parameters were number of cases upgraded to dysplasia/esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) at expert endoscopic reassessment, and number of cases with progression to high-grade dysplasia (HGD)/EAC during surveillance after a confirmed diagnosis of NDBE at expert endoscopic reassessment.

RESULTS: 168 patients were referred with ultra-long NDBE, namely with Barrett length (median and interquartile range [IQR]), circumference (C) 11 cm (9-12), maximum (M) 12 cm (10-14). Upon expert endoscopic reassessment, 28 /168 (17 %) patients were diagnosed with dysplasia/EAC, among whom 5 /168 (3 %) had HGD/EAC in a visible lesion. In 11 patients no Seattle protocol biopsies were obtained, thus 129 patients had an NDBE diagnosis based on Seattle protocol biopsies. Of these, 95 /129 (74 %) had > 1 surveillance endoscopy at the BEC. During surveillance 20 patients progressed to LGD (n = 11, 12 %), HGD (n = 4, 4 %) or EAC (n = 5, 5 %); all progressors underwent endoscopic therapy.

CONCLUSION: Expert care with dedicated BE endoscopy programs and experienced endoscopists may be beneficial for patients with ultra-long BE.

articles.title: Impact of dementia and its progression on mortality in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction -insight from the KUNIUMI registry chronic cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is highly prevalent among older adults, while dementia is also an age-related condition characterized by cognitive decline, behavioral changes, and functional impairment. Although cognitive dysfunction is associated with worse outcomes in general HF populations, the specific prognostic implications of dementia and its progression in HFpEF remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate these associations in a real-world elderly HFpEF cohort.

METHODS: This prospective study included 965 patients with HFpEF without a history of stroke, drawn from 1646 consecutive HF patients in the KUNIUMI Registry Chronic Cohort, a population-based registry in Japan. Dementia was defined as an ABC Dementia Scale (ABC-DS) score < 100, and dementia progression as a ≥ 14-point decline in ABC-DS over 1 year. The primary endpoint was all-cause death, and the secondary endpoint was cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization over a mean follow-up of 2.0 ± 0.1 years.

RESULTS: Patients with dementia had significantly higher rates of all-cause death and cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization than those without dementia. These findings remained consistent after adjustment for baseline characteristics using propensity score matching. Furthermore, patients with dementia progression at 1 year had significantly higher all-cause death and cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization than those without progression. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, dementia progression was associated with all-cause death.

CONCLUSIONS: Dementia, especially its progression, was associated with worse prognosis in HFpEF. These findings highlight the importance of longitudinal cognitive assessment to improve risk stratification and guide management strategies.

articles.title: Nationwide Survey of Prehospital 12‑lead Electrocardiogram Recording and Transmission in Japan: Equipment Availability Is No Longer the Major Barrier.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prehospital 12‑lead electrocardiogram (ECG) improves survival in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, the current status of prehospital 12‑lead ECG recording and transmission by emergency medical services (EMS) in Japan has not been investigated.

METHODS: A questionnaire survey on 12‑lead ECG recording and transmission was conducted in collaboration with the Fire and Disaster Management Agency of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, targeting all 723 fire departments in Japan in 2023. Official data released by each fire department were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Of 588 responding fire departments (81.3%), 545 (92.7%) had at least partial access to 12‑lead ECG recording equipment, whereas only 57 (9.7%) routinely utilized both recording and transmission. Multivariable logistic regression analysis indicated that routine 12‑lead ECG recording [odds ratio (OR) 2.88, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.70-4.87; p < 0.001], the presence of acute coronary syndrome or chest pain protocols (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.86-4.48; p < 0.001), the presence of 12‑lead ECG recording equipment in all ambulances (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.36-0.81, p = 0.003), and time from emergency call to arrival at the scene (OR 1.15, 95% CI 1.01-1.31, p = 0.028) were significant factors for the introduction of 12‑lead ECG transmission systems. When comparing responding facilities in regions with a single percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)-capable hospital within the medical control council (46 facilities) and those with ≥2 PCI-capable hospitals (405 facilities), the 12‑lead ECG transmission system introduction rate was significantly higher in single PCI-capable hospitals than in ≥2 PCI-capable hospitals (46% vs. 30%, respectively; p = 0.027).

CONCLUSIONS: Prehospital 12‑lead ECG recording equipment is widely available in Japan, but 12‑lead ECG transmission systems remain insufficiently implemented. The principal challenge is no longer equipment availability but establishing effective EMS-hospital communication pathways within regional STEMI networks.

articles.title: Simplified Cardiac Auscultation for the Detection of Valvular Heart Disease.
Barriers to and Facilitators of the Adoption of Peritoneal Dialysis: A Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
