BACKGROUND: Freiberg's disease is an osteochondrosis of the lesser metatarsal heads, most commonly the 2nd, that predominantly affects adolescent females and causes pain and limited motion; early cases are treated conservatively, while advanced or refractory ones may need dorsal closing wedge osteotomy. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical and radiological outcomes of dorsal closing wedge osteotomy fixed with a single mini-screw in patients aged 13 to 30 years.

METHODS: This prospective observational case series included 48 consecutive patients with Freiberg's disease, Smillie stage II, III, or IV, who underwent dorsal closing wedge osteotomy with mini-screw fixation after failed conservative treatment. Pain was assessed with a 0-10 visual analogue scale (VAS) preoperatively and at the final 6-month follow-up, radiographs were reviewed for osteotomy union, and complications were recorded.

RESULTS: There was a substantial reduction in pain, with the mean VAS score improving from 8.67 ± 0.88 to 1.33 ± 2.01 (P<0.001). Radiographic union was achieved in all patients at a mean of 7.31 ± 1.22 weeks. Intraoperative fragmentation of the metatarsal head occurred in 3 patients (6.25%) and superficial wound infection in 3 (6.25%), and all patients had some loss of metatarsophalangeal joint plantarflexion (mean 11°).

CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, dorsal closing wedge osteotomy with mini-screw fixation for Freiberg's disease was associated with a substantial reduction in pain and a low complication rate, although some loss of metatarsophalangeal joint motion occurred in all patients.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, prospective observational case series study.

articles.title: Prehospital Prognostication after Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Tertiary Care Centers: The R-EDByUS Score in the JAAM-OHCA Registry.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The R-EDByUS score predicts unfavorable neurological outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) using prehospital variables alone, with separate models based on return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) status at hospital arrival. However, whether the score remains valid in patients transported to tertiary care centers is uncertain. We therefore aimed to validate it externally in this setting.

METHODS: Using the JAAM-OHCA Registry, we analyzed adult patients with presumed cardiogenic OHCA transported to tertiary care centers. The regression-based R-EDByUS score was applied to predict unfavorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 3-5) at 1 month in the prehospital ROSC and ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) cohorts. Discrimination and calibration were assessed, and score performance was examined across in-hospital intervention subgroups (percutaneous coronary intervention, targeted temperature management, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation). We also assessed the proportion of patients with unfavorable outcomes among those with a predicted probability ≥99%.

RESULTS: Of 29,345 patients, 3,305 were classified into the prehospital ROSC cohort and 26,040 into the ongoing CPR cohort. The score showed good discrimination, with areas under the curve of 0.906 and 0.913, and good calibration in the prehospital ROSC cohort. Discrimination was lower among patients who received PCI, TTM, or ECMO in the ongoing CPR cohort. Among patients with a predicted probability ≥99%, 100% (112/112; prehospital ROSC) and 99.9% (20,560/20,588; ongoing CPR) had unfavorable outcomes.

CONCLUSION: The R-EDByUS score showed good discrimination in the JAAM-OHCA Registry, supporting its use for early risk stratification in cardiogenic OHCA even in tertiary care centers.

articles.title: One-year Outcomes of Mechanical Thrombectomy and Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism, mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed for up to one year or until death.

RESULTS: A total of 724 patients were included: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of cases. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index (sPESI) > 0 (73% vs. 60%, p < 0.001). Age, rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between groups. Median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, IQR 46-89) than CDT (58 minutes, IQR 40-77; p = 0.003). Median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs. 0%, p = 0.048), while CDT was associated with higher ICU admission rates (83% vs. 36%, p < 0.001). However, thirty-day mortality was similar between groups (CDT: 2.6% vs. MT: 4.6%; p = 0.27). Additionally, the one-year incidences of CTEPH (MT: 4.5% vs. CDT: 3.4%, p=0.69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%, p=0.31) and all-cause mortality (MT:7.8% vs. CDT: 5.8%, p=0.41) were not statistically significant between MT and CDT respectfully.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable mortality, CTEPH, and PE recurrence rates at one-year. MT was associated with higher intraoperative cardiac complications, whereas CDT required more frequent ICU admission.

articles.title: Burden of fall-related injury and its predictors among stroke survivors attending comprehensive specialized hospitals in the Amhara Regional State, Ethiopia, 2024: A multicenter prospective study.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study was conducted to identify the burden of fall-related injury and associated factors among stroke survivors attending comprehensive specialized hospitals in Amhara Regional State, Ethiopia, in 2024.

DESIGN: A multi-center cross-sectional study design was deployed among 269 stroke survivors from June 1 to August 1, 2024.

SETTING: This study was conducted in five comprehensive specialized hospitals in the Amhara region: the University of Gondar, Bahir Dar (Feleghiwot and Tebebe Ghion), Debreberhan, and Dessie.

PARTICIPANTS: The study comprised stroke survivors who had experienced at least one fall, were able to walk independently with or without mobility aid, and were attending the outpatient physiotherapy departments in the five comprehensive specialized hospitals. A systematic random sampling techniques was employed with a sampling interval K =2 and participants were proportionally allocated for each comprehensive specialized hospital.

INTERVENTION: Not Applicable MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S): Fall-related injury: any injury caused by a fall, as reported by staff/patient/caregiver or documented in the medical record during the data collection period.

RESULT: The prevalence of fall-related injury among stroke survivors in Amhara Regional State was 79.9% (95 CI: 75.1-84.4). Variables including age > 65 (AOR=2.670, 95% CI: 1.083-6.585), rural residence (AOR=2.352, 95% CI: 1.037-5.332), and injury occurring during walking and turning (AOR=2.960, 95% CI: 1.081-8.103) were significantly associated with fall-related injury.

CONCLUSION: The burden of fall-related injury was relatively high among stroke survivors in Amhara Regional State, Ethiopia. Being older, living in a rural areas, and engaging in the activity of walking and turning were predictors associated with fall-related injury.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of the Si-AAA Prognostic Score for Five-Year Overall Survival after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in Patients with Asymptomatic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although endovascular aneurysm repair is widely used for the treatment of asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm, long-term survival is influenced by patient comorbidities and aneurysm-related characteristics. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair. Candidate predictors included demographic, clinical, aneurysm-related, and laboratory variables. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of 5-year mortality. Continuous predictors were categorized using clinically interpretable thresholds derived from time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and a simplified point-based score was constructed from regression coefficients. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's concordance index, and internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples to obtain an optimism-corrected concordance index. Calibration was evaluated using bootstrap-based calibration plots.

RESULTS: A total of 445 patients were screened, and 443 complete cases were included in the final analysis. During follow-up, 133 deaths (30.0%) occurred. The estimated 5-year overall survival rate was 62.8% (95% CI, 57.8%-68.0%). Independent predictors of 5-year mortality included age >70 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.66, 95% CI 1.06-2.62; P = .029), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.08-2.69; P = .023), unfit status (aHR 2.32, 95% CI 1.58-3.39; P < .001), serum albumin ≤3.5 g/dL (aHR 2.80, 95% CI 1.97-3.98; P < .001), and abdominal aortic aneurysm diameter ≥7 cm (aHR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.38; P = .023). The final score ranged from 0 to 7. The apparent concordance index was 0.721, with an optimism-corrected concordance index of 0.713 after bootstrap validation. Risk stratification showed clear separation between low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (5-year overall survival: 82.5%, 53.4%, and 23.8%, respectively; log-rank P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: A simple prognostic scoring system incorporating age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unfit status, serum albumin, and aneurysm diameter demonstrated acceptable discrimination and good calibration for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. This tool may assist in risk stratification and long-term clinical decision-making. As this score was derived and internally validated in a single-center cohort, external validation in independent cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Sex-based differences in mortality and prognostic factors for infective endocarditis: insights from a retrospective cohort of 519 patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infective endocarditis (IE) remains a severe disease with high mortality despite advances in management. Although it predominantly affects male patients, female patients account for about one-quarter of cases. Sex-specific differences in outcomes and prognostic factors remain insufficiently explored.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study including 519 patients ≥16 years hospitalized for definite or possible IE (ESC 2023 criteria) at La Timone Hospital, Marseille, between March 2019 and October 2023. The primary endpoint was one-year mortality; secondary endpoints included surgical management, valve involvement, and prognostic factors.

RESULTS: Of the 519 patients, 26% were female patients. One-year mortality was comparable between sexes (27% in female patients vs. 23% in male patients, p = 0.415). Post-discharge mortality was not significantly different between sexes (p = 0.096). Mitral valve involvement was more frequent in female patients, and aortic involvement predominated in male patients. Independent predictors of mortality included annular complications and lack of surgery. Importantly, sex-specific differences in prognostic factors were observed in this exploratory analysis: in female patients, TAVI and ischemic heart disease were associated with higher mortality; in male patients, right-sided IE and pacemaker presence were predictive. Furthermore, fatal cases in male patients were marked by more in-hospital complications (heart failure, cardiogenic or septic shock, acute renal failure), suggesting distinct mortality pathways.

CONCLUSION: Although overall mortality was similar between sexes, male patients and female patients with IE appeared to show different prognostic profiles in this single-center cohort. These preliminary, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that some established risk factors may largely reflect male data, emphasizing the need for larger, multicenter studies to confirm sex-specific determinants and improve individualized management.

articles.title: Design and rationale of the Urine Sodium-directed Diuretic Adjustment Strategy in Heart Failure (US-DASH) trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Recent studies have shown natriuresis-guided diuretic adjustment strategies result in greater natriuresis and diuresis than the standard of practice in acute heart failure. There is no consensus for which natriuretic goal optimally balances decongestion with adverse clinical outcomes.

PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS: This study will test the hypothesis that (i.) a high-threshold natriuresis target improves natriuresis compared with both a low-threshold natriuretic strategy and traditional methods, and (ii.) natriuresis in absence of urine output monitoring can safely guide management. The primary endpoint is 24-hour natriuresis.

DESIGN: Pragmatic, single-center, randomized, controlled, open-label with stratification by eGFR (greater than versus less than 60 mL/min/1.73 m²) and number of home diuretics (0-1 versus 2+).

articles.title: Design and baseline characteristics of the CagriSema cardiovascular outcomes trial (REDEFINE 3).
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) is a fixed-dose combination of the amylin receptor agonist cagrilintide and the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide administered subcutaneously once weekly. CagriSema has demonstrated significant weight reduction and improved glycemic control in participants with excess adiposity and type 2 diabetes (T2D).

METHODS: REDEFINE 3 is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving participants with established cardiovascular disease (CVD) and body mass index (BMI) ≥25.0 kg/m2 with/without T2D randomized to CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg or placebo, plus standard of care. The safety objective is to confirm noninferiority of CagriSema compared with placebo on cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (MACE-3). The efficacy objective is to confirm the superiority of CagriSema compared with placebo on cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or revascularization (MACE-4).

RESULTS: Between 1/2023-12/2024, 7076 adults at 575 sites in 24 countries were randomized. Mean age at baseline was 66 years. BMI ≥30 kg/m2 was present in 76% of participants (n=5370). In participants with T2D (n=4348, 61%), the mean duration of T2D was 12 years and mean glycated hemoglobin was 7.7%. Most participants had a prior myocardial infarction (n=4369, 62%). Prior stroke (n=1311, 19%) and peripheral arterial disease (n=769, 11%) were less common, and 617 participants (9%) had more than one qualifying CVD criteria.

CONCLUSION: The REDEFINE 3 trial will provide evidence regarding the cardiovascular safety and efficacy of CagriSema, a novel fixed-dose combination therapy that could improve cardiovascular outcomes in a broad population of people with established CVD and excess adiposity.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The REDEFINE 3 trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05669755).

articles.title: Rational design and molecular docking-guided screening of high-affinity β-glucosidase affibodies for application in a lateral flow immunoassay platform.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis drives progressive bone destruction through dysregulated osteoblast-osteoclast crosstalk, yet the role of exosome-mediated circular RNA (circRNA) communication in this process remains poorly understood. This study aimed to determine whether exosomal circRNAs derived from S. aureus-infected osteoblasts orchestrate osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Exosomes were isolated from hFOB1.19 osteoblasts with or without S. aureus infection, characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and Western blotting, and their circRNA profiles were screened by RNA sequencing. A murine femoral osteomyelitis model was established via intramedullary S. aureus inoculation followed by tail-vein exosome injection, with bone microarchitecture and osteoclastogenesis assessed by micro-CT, histology, TRAP/ALP staining, qPCR, and Western blotting. The circ_0001843/miR-369-5p/TAFA5 axis was validated by dual-luciferase reporter assays. S. aureus infection markedly upregulated exosomal circ_0001843. In vivo, exosomes from infected osteoblasts aggravated bone destruction, evidenced by decreased BV/TV, increased trabecular separation, enhanced osteoclast activity, and suppressed osteogenic markers. In vitro, circ_0001843 knockdown attenuated RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation while promoting osteoblast proliferation and mineralization; these protective effects were reversed by exosomes from infected osteoblasts or miR-369-5p inhibition. Mechanistically, circ_0001843 sponged miR-369-5p to derepress TAFA5, thereby disrupting bone remodeling homeostasis. These findings identify exosomal circ_0001843 as a novel mediator of infection-induced bone loss via the miR-369-5p/TAFA5 axis, highlighting a potential therapeutic target for osteomyelitis-associated bone destruction.

articles.title: Dynamically crosslinked hydrogel dressings with pH-responsive drug release and antibacterial properties for infected wound healing.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infection perturbs the wound microenvironment, thereby profoundly impeding the healing process. Functional hydrogels exhibit unique advantages for treating infected wounds because they possess high drug-loading capacity and well-controlled release performance. Herein, we constructed a dynamic covalent network using carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS), luteolin (Lut), and 2-formylphenylboronic acid (2-FPBA), fabricating a CFL hydrogel for infected wound healing. Notably, the fabrication of this hydrogel is straightforward, requiring only a simple mixing step without the need for complex chemical modification or purification. This network incorporates Schiff base and boronate ester bonds, endowing it with responsiveness to the acidic microenvironment in infected wounds. Upon exposure to acidic conditions, these bonds dissociate, releasing CMCS and Lut. The released agents work synergistically to combat bacteria and promote wound closure. In addition, the CFL hydrogel exhibits tissue-adhesive properties, antioxidant activity, and good biosafety. In infected full‑thickness skin wounds of rats, the CFL hydrogel led to 99% wound closure by day 11, while also promoting collagen deposition and hair follicle regeneration in the treated wounds. In summary, the developed multifunctional CFL hydrogel represents a viable approach to treating infected skin wounds.

articles.title: Harnessing reactive oxygen species for advanced drug delivery and therapeutics.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) have a unique position at the intersection of biology, chemistry, materials science, and medicine. They are indispensable mediators of physiological signalling, host defence, tissue remodelling, and cellular adaptation, yet their dysregulation is intimately associated with cancer, chronic inflammation, infection, metabolic disease, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, tissue injury, and ageing. This duality has made ROS both a therapeutic target and an attractive biological trigger for drug delivery. The Journal of Controlled Release Special Issue on "Harnessing Reactive Oxygen Species for Advanced Drug Delivery and Therapeutics" brings together a diverse collection of contributions that together present an important transition in the field. ROS-based delivery is moving beyond the conventional concept of a material that simply responds to an elevated oxidative environment. The contributions assembled here demonstrate that ROS can be scavenged, generated, amplified, buffered, spatially confined, chemically translated into drug release, coupled to immune modulation, integrated with metabolic sensing, and incorporated into theranostic and adaptive therapeutic systems.

articles.title: PI3K is the dominant signalling pathway recruited by IRS proteins to mediate their effects on metabolism and growth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Insulin and Igf1 have pleiotropic effects on development, growth and metabolism. The activated insulin and IGF1 receptors engage insulin receptor substrate (IRS) proteins, intracellular adaptor molecules that recruit multiple downstream signalling pathways, including PI3K and GRB2-RAS-MAPK. Global deletion of IRS1 or IRS2 in mice results in divergent effects on growth, metabolism, and ageing. However, the precise signalling pathways recruited by IRS1 or IRS2 to mediate their physiological effects in vivo have not been defined.

METHODS: We generated knock-in mice in which either IRS1 or IRS2 was mutated to prevent downstream recruitment of PI3K or GRB2 and undertook phenotypic analysis of these animals.

RESULTS: Knock-in mice unable to recruit PI3K to IRS1 (Irs1YnF) or to IRS2 (Irs2YnF) had limited or no compensation in IRS2 and IRS1 signalling respectively. Irs1YnF mice were growth restricted, with reduced adiposity and insulin resistance, but did not develop diabetes due to compensatory increase in β-cell mass. Irs2YnF mice were obese and insulin resistant and developed diabetes due to β-cell failure. In contrast knock-in mice unable to recruit GRB2 to IRS1 (Irs1Y891F) or to IRS2 (Irs2Y911F) displayed normal growth and metabolism.

CONCLUSIONS: PI3K recruitment by either IRS1 or IRS2 is the primary signalling mediator of the effects of these adaptor molecules on growth and metabolism in mice, and suggest that the other signalling pathways recruited by IRS1 and IRS2, including GRB2, have minimal or redundant roles.

articles.title: Self-Reported Health, Stress, and Lifestyle Behaviors Among U.S. Chief Executive Officers: A Comparison of Two Cohorts.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate self-reported health and lifestyle behaviors among U.S. Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) and to identify patterns relevant to executive healthcare delivery.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: An anonymous health and lifestyle survey was distributed to two populations: patients enrolled in the Mayo Clinic Executive Health Program (MC-EHP; n=14,240) and members of the Chief Executive Group (CEG; n=146,641). Data were collected between August 8 and October 2, 2025. Descriptive statistics were summarized for CEO survey responders (MC-EHP, n=792; CEG, n=613). Group comparisons were performed using Kruskal-Wallis and chi-square tests. No adjustment was made for multiple comparisons; therefore, inferential findings should be interpreted as exploratory.

RESULTS: Compared with CEG CEOs, MC-EHP CEOs were older (P<.001), more likely to be male (83.5% vs 76.1%; P<.001) and White (97.0% vs 93.0%; P=.001). MC-EHP CEOs self-reported less sedentary time (6.1 vs. 6.8 hours/day; P<.001), fewer work hours (40.3 hours vs 53.8 hours/week; P<.001), and lower stress levels (4.6 vs. 6.3, P<.001). They also reported fewer sleep disturbances (P=.003), fewer chronic medical conditions and higher quality-of-life (P<.001). Use of prescription medications was higher among the MC-EHP CEOs (78.6% vs 72.0%, P=.004), whereas use of over-the-counter medications/supplements was lower (P=.022). Several statistically significant differences were modest in absolute magnitude.

CONCLUSION: Among surveyed U.S. CEOs, participation in a comprehensive executive health program was associated with lower self-reported stress, healthier lifestyle behaviors, and higher quality-of-life. The findings underscore lifestyle factors relevant to overall health and highlight areas for clinicians to prioritize when treating CEO patients. Prior research suggests that CEO well-being may have broader implications for employee well-being, further supporting the need for regular patient feedback to help executive health programs adapt healthcare services to the evolving needs of their patients.

articles.title: Identification of Plasma Immune markers Associated with Latent Tuberculosis Conversion in HIV-Infected Individuals who received isoniazid preventive therapy.
articles.journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis remains a major risk for people living with HIV, even those on antiretroviral therapy, due to increased susceptibility to latent TB infection. Identifying immune signatures that distinguish progression from resistance is critical for developing predictive biomarkers and targeted prevention strategies. In this study, 80 HIV-infected adults on antiretroviral therapy who received isoniazid preventive therapy (IPT) were followed for six months and categorized as Progressors, Sustainers, Converters, or Resisters based on serial QuantiFERON-TB results. Plasma levels of cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors were analyzed using a Luminex assay, alongside machine learning and pathway analyses. Progressors and Sustainers exhibited elevated proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors, while Resisters showed dynamic immune modulation following preventive therapy. Key predictors of progression included PD-L1, TNF-α, IL-17A, and FGF2. Network and pathway analyses highlighted persistent inflammatory signaling in Progressors and adaptive immune regulation in Resisters. Findings suggest distinct immune profiles associated with TB risk, offering potential for improved prediction and targeted interventions.

articles.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Alcohol Septal Ablation Versus Surgical Myectomy in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) complicates 20-25% of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) cases and independently predicts heart failure progression, thromboembolism, and mortality. Both surgical myectomy (SM) and alcohol septal ablation (ASA) are associated with new-onset AF through opposing mechanisms; myectomy promoting left atrial reverse remodeling, ASA generating a chronic arrhythmogenic septal scar. Yet no propensity-matched study has directly compared AF incidence between these procedures.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the incidence and temporal trajectory of new-onset AF following ASA versus SM at prespecified landmarks of Day 1, Day 7, and Day 30 in a propensity score-matched cohort with 3 years of follow-up.

METHODS: Patients with obstructive HOCM who underwent ASA or SM without prior AF were identified in the TriNetX database between Jan. 2010 and Apr. 2023 and were followed for up to 3 years. After 1:1 propensity score matching on demographics, comorbidities, and atrial substrate risk factors, 223 patients remained in each cohort; new-onset AF was ascertained using clinical diagnosis codes applied symmetrically across both groups.

RESULTS: Of 1,188 patients (539 ASA, 649 SM), 223 were matched per cohort (mean age 59.5 ± 15.5 years, 37.4% male, 80.3% White); all standardized mean differences were <0.20 after matching. At Day 1, AF occurred in 16.1% vs. 12.1% (ARD 4.0%; HR 1.22, 95% CI 0.74-2.01; p = 0.437). At Day 7, a significant divergence emerged (15.8% vs. 8.4%; ARD 7.4%; RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.10-3.21; p = 0.019). By Day 30, ASA carried a nearly three-fold higher AF risk (15.4% vs. 5.3%; ARD 10.1%; HR 2.75, 95% CI 1.39-5.42; p = 0.039), with AF-free survival of 82.59% vs. 93.83% (log-rank p = 0.002), with progressive Kaplan-Meier separation sustained through 3 years.

CONCLUSIONS: In a propensity-matched cohort, ASA was associated with a progressively higher risk of new-onset AF compared with SM, with divergence emerging by Day 7 and widening through Day 30, consistent with substrate reversal after myectomy versus substrate maturation after ASA. These findings support incorporating differential AF risk into procedural selection discussions, extending postprocedural monitoring after ASA, and reassessing early anticoagulation thresholds in ASA patients.

articles.title: Outcomes of Mitral Valve Intervention for Patients with Bileaflet Mitral Valve Prolapse and Preoperative Ventricular Arrhythmias.
articles.abstract: Bileaflet mitral valve (MV) prolapse may be associated with ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Given the paucity of data analyzing the role of MV interventions, we analyzed outcomes of MV surgery in patients with bileaflet MV prolapse and preoperative ventricular arrhythmias. Between 1994 and 2018, 30 adult patients with bileaflet MV prolapse, severe MV regurgitation, and documented preoperative ventricular arrhythmias underwent MV operation at our institution. Ventricular arrhythmia was defined as ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, cardiac arrest, or bigeminy. Pre- and postoperative ventricular arrhythmias and mortality were identified from medical record review. Median age was 51 years (IQR: 41.2, 59.5), and 20 (66.7%) patients were female. The most common preoperative arrhythmia was ventricular tachycardia (73%), followed by ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest. Most patients (N=28, 93.3%) underwent bileaflet MV repair, and 2 (6.7%) underwent MV replacement. There was no 30-day mortality. Ventricular arrhythmias did not recur postoperatively in 19 patients, and three patients with preoperative cardiac arrest improved without further cardiac arrest episodes but had ventricular tachycardia. The 1-year estimate of freedom from ventricular arrhythmia recurrence was 70%. Patients with recurrence were older and had longer delays between arrhythmia diagnosis and surgical referral. Higher body mass index and lower preoperative ejection fraction were associated with increased recurrence risk. In conclusion, surgical correction of bileaflet MV prolapse for severe MV regurgitation with preoperative ventricular arrhythmias can be performed safely. Although the majority of patients experienced a sustained reduction in arrhythmia burden postoperatively, recurrence was observed in a subset. Therefore, patients should be counseled regarding ongoing medical management and the possibility of recurrence despite correction of MV regurgitation.

articles.title: Title: Maternal circulating cytokine and chemokine levels during pregnancy and risk of autism spectrum disorder in offspring: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy has been implicated in offspring neurodevelopment, but evidence linking maternal gestational immune mediators with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains heterogeneous. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether maternal circulating cytokine and chemokine levels during pregnancy are associated with autism in offspring.

METHODS: Five databases were searched for human observational studies measuring maternal blood cytokines or chemokines during pregnancy and reporting autism outcomes in offspring. Eligible studies included autism versus control comparisons using maternal serum or plasma samples. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted using odds ratios (ORs) as the primary effect measure. Standardised mean differences (SMDs) were also analysed where group-level concentration data were available. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics, and small-study effects were explored using Egger's test where estimable.

RESULTS: Seven studies met the eligibility criteria. In OR-based analyses, nominal associations with autism were observed for IL-10 (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.06-1.69), CXCL10 (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.24-2.11), IL-1α (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.23-1.65), IL-5 (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.18-1.89), and IL-17A (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.94). CCL4 showed a borderline association. Supportive SMD analyses indicated higher IL-6 and lower IL-1β concentrations in autism-associated pregnancies. Heterogeneity varied across analytes and was substantial for IL-10 and CCL4.

CONCLUSION: Maternal gestational immune profiles may differ in pregnancies later associated with autism, but current evidence does not support a single robust cytokine biomarker. Progress requires larger prospective cohorts with repeated sampling, harmonised assays, pathway-level analyses, and integrated placental-fetal neurodevelopmental phenotyping.

articles.title: Neuro-oncological emergencies requiring critical care intervention.
articles.abstract: Patients with primary or metastatic brain tumours can deteriorate abruptly, and the acute physician is often the first to respond. This review covers the recognition and initial management of the neurological emergencies most likely to need critical care: raised intracranial pressure from peritumoural oedema and herniation; seizures and status epilepticus, including non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE); intracranial haemorrhage; acute hydrocephalus; and venous thromboembolism. It also covers two treatment-related emergencies that the general physician must now recognise: immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome after chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitor encephalitis. Throughout, the text indicates wither recommendations rest on guidelines and where on observational data. The focus is on recognising time-critical treatment, timely escalation to neurosurgical and neurocritical care services, and the early, values-based discussion of goals of care.

articles.title: Rodent Models of Glaucoma: Pathogenic Mechanisms, Phenotyping Strategies, and Translational Relevance.
articles.abstract: Glaucoma comprises a heterogeneous group of optic neuropathies characterized by progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons. Rodent models have been widely used to investigate disease mechanisms, identify neuroprotective targets and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies because they are cost-effective, genetically tractable and experimentally controllable. However, mice and rats differ substantially from humans in anterior-segment anatomy, trabecular meshwork architecture, Schlemm's canal development, lamina cribrosa structure, retinal ganglion cell composition and optic nerve head vascular supply. These interspecies differences influence model construction, phenotypic interpretation and the translational value of preclinical findings. This narrative review summarizes key anatomical differences between rodent and human eyes and discusses major categories of rodent glaucoma models, including intraocular pressure (IOP)-dependent models, IOP-independent models, immune-mediated and multifactorial models, and spontaneous or genetically engineered models. We emphasize that no single rodent model can fully reproduce the chronic, multifactorial, and regionally selective nature of human glaucoma. Instead, model selection should be driven by the specific scientific question, disease subtype, observation window, and translational goal. IOP-dependent models are particularly useful for investigating pressure-induced RGC degeneration and optic nerve injury, while selected models also reproduce aspects of aqueous outflow dysfunction, linking anterior-segment abnormalities with posterior-segment neurodegeneration. IOP-independent and genetic models, by contrast, are ideal for studying normal-tension glaucoma, neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation, metabolic stress, and gene-specific mechanisms. Future efforts should prioritize standardized phenotypic evaluation, multimodal imaging and multi-omics integration to improve the reliability and translational relevance of findings from rigorously validated rodent models.

articles.title: Adult-administered chronic nicotine remodels nigral dopaminergic and pedunculopontine cholinergic physiology.
articles.abstract: Nicotine is linked to neuroprotection and has been proposed as a potential preventative treatment for Parkinson's disease (PD). Because PD is an aging disorder, such a treatment would necessarily be administered to adults. However, previous studies examining the effects of chronic nicotine in neurons vulnerable to PD have primarily been conducted in juvenile animals. Here we administer chronic nicotine to adult mice of both sexes. We examine nicotine-induced functional adaptations in two brain structures vulnerable to PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) and the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN). Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we observed changes in cellular properties that potentially contribute to reduced risk of PD associated with nicotine exposure. Chronic nicotine decreased pacemaking frequency, burst propensity, and rebound firing in SNc dopaminergic neurons, while decoupling tonic firing rate from dendritic calcium levels. These changes in the SNc occurred without altering L-type channel contributions, dendritic arborization, or excitatory synaptic drive. Although the PPN degenerates in PD and is the primary cholinergic input to the SNc, no previous studies have evaluated the effects of chronic nicotine on this structure. We find that chronic nicotine induced subregion-specific plasticity in the PPN. Rostral PPN neurons showed depolarized membrane potentials, broadened action potentials, and dendritic pruning, whereas caudal PPN neurons showed reduced spike frequency adaptation and accelerated excitatory postsynaptic current kinetics. While these PPN alterations do not have a previously established link with cellular vulnerability, synaptic and physiological changes in this region may have unexpected contributions to PD progression. In addition, these findings reveal novel mechanisms that could underlie nicotine's modulation of brainstem circuitry controlling arousal, sensory gating, and drug dependence.

articles.title: Impact of Air Pollutants and Meteorological Factors on the Transmission Rate of Scarlet Fever in China.
articles.abstract: Scarlet fever, a resurgent childhood infection, lacks a comprehensive understanding of how environmental factors influence its intrinsic transmission. Most existing studies directly link environmental exposures with incidence rates, the results of which may be confounded by intervention measures. In this work, we aim to investigate the lagged and nonlinear effects of air pollutants and meteorological factors on the transmission rate (β(t)) of scarlet fever across 31 provinces in China from 2013 to 2020. We first reconstruct the time-varying transmission rate from surveillance data based on an SEIRA model using a discrete inverse method. Subsequently, Distributed Lag Non-linear Models (DLNM) are applied to analyze associations between β(t) and four pollutants and four meteorological variables.Our results reveal substantial spatiotemporal heterogeneity in the inferred transmission rate. DLNM analysis identifies complex exposure-lag-response relationships. Key findings include: O3 showed positive exposure-lag at longer lag periods; CO showed a weak and nonlinear association with the transmission rate; higher relative humidity showed positive associations over medium to longer lag periods; and sunlight showed a nonlinear and exposure-dependent association with the transmission rate. Our study confirms that environmental pollutants and climatic factors are associated with the transmissibility of scarlet fever through lagged effects spanning several months. Shifting the analytical focus from incidence rates to model-inferred transmission rates can more clearly reveal the association patterns between environmental factors and transmission rates, and provide a potential scientific reference for building climate-sensitive early warning systems.

articles.title: Characterizing Pediatric Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Symptom Burden, Functional Impairment, and Comparison With Adults in the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS (MCAM) Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical, functional, and educational characteristics of adolescents with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and compare selected illness domains with adults in the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS (MCAM) study.

STUDY DESIGN: Baseline cross-sectional data from adolescents aged 10-17 years enrolled in MCAM were analyzed. Standardized measures included the Short Form-36 (SF-36v2), CDC Symptom Inventory (CDC-SI), Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-20), and selected domains of the DePaul Questionnaire. Descriptive statistics characterized the pediatric cohort and bivariate analyses compared adolescents with adults enrolled in MCAM.

RESULTS: Forty adolescents (mean age 15.3 years; 52.5% female) were included. Mean illness duration was 4.0 years. Educational disruption was substantial: 64% received homebound or homeschool instruction, 89% missed school because of illness, and participants missed a mean of 10.8 school days during the preceding month. Physical health-related quality of life was substantially impaired. Persistent post-exertional malaise (PEM), unrefreshing sleep, fatigue, and neurocognitive symptoms were common. Compared with adults (n = 595), adolescents had shorter illness duration and better physical functioning, vitality, and social functioning, whereas mental health scores were similar. Adults reported greater burden across several physical symptom domains although many between-group differences were small.

CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents with ME/CFS experience substantial multisystem symptom burden, impaired physical functioning and educational disruption. Many core clinical features were similar to those in adults, supporting the need for early recognition and appropriate clinical and educational support.

articles.title: Reply.
Association of Early Low Superior Vena Cava Flow among Neonates Born Very Preterm and Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review systematically and meta-analyze the association of low superior vena cava flow (SVCF), diagnosed on echocardiography within the first 48 hours after birth, with morbidity, such as intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and mortality among preterm neonates (<32 weeks gestational age [GA]).

STUDY DESIGN: PROSPERO, Medline, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure Database were searched for cohort studies and randomized controlled trials including neonates < 32 weeks' GA evaluating the associations of low vs normal SVCF in the first 48 hours after birth with clinical outcomes. Data were combined using random effects meta-analyses. Main outcome measures included any and severe IVH, all-cause mortality, periventricular leukomalacia, necrotizing enterocolitis and neurodevelopmental impairment in early childhood.

RESULTS: Fourteen original studies enrolling 1,366 patients were included. Low SVCF was associated with increased adjusted odds of any IVH (3 studies; n= 381; OR 4.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.3, 9.5; 95% prediction interval [PI] 0.99, 22.1; low certainty) as well as increased unadjusted odds of severe IVH (10 studies; n=996; OR 4.8 95% CI 2.5, 9.2; PI 1.6, 15.1; low certainty) and all-cause mortality (6 studies; n=724; OR 4.2, 95% CI 1.8, 9.7; PI 0.7, 23.7; very low certainty). Low SVCF was not associated with other outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Low SVCF within the first 48 hours after birth for very preterm neonates may be associated with increased IVH and mortality.

articles.title: The Parasite Paradox: Therapeutic Insights from Parasite-Host Interactions - A Focus on Beneficial Physiological Modulations.
articles.abstract: A compelling and paradoxical body of evidence challenges the traditional view of parasites solely as pathogens. This narrative review synthesizes a growing literature suggesting that specific, chronic parasitic infections-particularly by helminths, but also certain protozoa-can, under precise ecological conditions, confer a spectrum of protective and ameliorative effects on the host. We comprehensively detail these effects across two interconnected domains. First, we examine organ-specific immunomodulation, focusing on the attenuation of inflammatory and autoimmune pathologies within the cardiovascular, neuroinflammatory, renal, hepatic, and pulmonary systems. Second, we explore systemic physiological modulations that extend beyond classic immunology, including enhanced tissue repair, improved metabolic homeostasis, neuroprotection, anti-tumor activity, and the engineering of a health-promoting gut microbiome. Underpinning these benefits are shared mechanistic pillars: the induction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-10, TGF-β), polarization of macrophages toward an M2 reparative phenotype, and profound remodeling of the gut microbiota. Crucially, we emphasize that these "benefits" are incidental by-products of host-parasite co-evolution, observed only in contexts of low-burden, chronic infection with particular species, and are vastly outweighed by the direct morbidity of active parasitosis. The true translational promise lies in parasite-inspired pharmacology: the identification, synthesis, and therapeutic application of discrete parasite-derived molecules to treat inflammatory, metabolic, degenerative, and neoplastic diseases, offering a novel paradigm for drug discovery inspired by nature's most adept manipulators of host biology.

articles.title: A pH-Sensitive and ROS-Responsive Hydrogel Enhanced by Arginine-Derived Carbon Dots for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Infected Wounds.
articles.abstract: Effective repair of infected wounds requires both precise elimination of bacteria in the host and accelerated healing, yet strategies that integrate real-time diagnosis with targeted therapy remain scarce. Here, we synthesize L-arginine-derived carbon quantum dots (Arg‑CQDs) and incorporate them into a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate/carboxymethyl chitosan (PEGDA/CMCS) double-network hydrogel via free-radical polymerization. The resulting Arg‑CQDs-enhanced hydrogel functions as a sensitive pH-responsive optical sensor. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that under acidic conditions, Arg‑CQDs possess a smaller HOMO-LUMO gap and a larger oscillator intensity, favoring intense radiative electronic transitions. Under alkaline conditions, a larger gap and a smaller oscillator intensity promote dominant non‑radiative transitions. Consequently, the ultraviolet (UV)-excited luminescence intensity of the composite hydrogel decreases as pH increases, enabling visual assessment of infection via smartphone-based RGB color channel analysis. Moreover, the hydrogel exhibits microenvironment-selective pro-oxidant and antioxidant behavior. In bacterial environments, the positively charged Arg‑CQDs disrupt the electron transport chain and elevate reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, achieving potent bactericidal activity. In cellular environments, they scavenge excess ROS through the up-regulation of GGT5 and Aldo-Keto reductase, thereby activating JAK2-STAT3/IL‑10 signaling to promote macrophage anti-inflammatory responses. In a rat model of infected wounds, this hydrogel achieves re‑epithelialization and vascularized wound closure within 14 days, outperforming commercial Ag+ dressings. This "sense‑and‑act" smart hydrogel represents a promising platform for the simultaneous diagnosis and treatment of infected wounds. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This work reports an Arg-CQDs-enhanced PEGDA/CMCS composite hydrogel that functions as a pH-responsive optical sensor, enabling smartphone‑based visual assessment of infection. DFT calculations reveal that acidic conditions promote intense radiative electronic transitions, whereas alkaline conditions favor weak non-radiative transitions, accounting for the pH‑dependent luminescence. Furthermore, the hydrogel exhibits microenvironment‑selective behavior. In bacterial niches, it elevates ROS levels to achieve potent sterilization. In cellular environments, it scavenges excess ROS and up-regulates GGT5 and Aldo‑Keto reductase, thereby activating JAK2-STAT3/IL-10 signaling to orchestrate anti-inflammatory responses. In a rat model of infected wounds, this "sense‑and‑act" hydrogel accomplishes complete re-epithelialization and vascularized closure within 14 days, outperforming commercial Ag+ dressings. Collectively, these findings establish a promising platform for the simultaneous diagnosis and treatment of infected wounds.

articles.title: Multiomics reveals alterations in the gut microbiome, host proteins, and host metabolites correlating with SADS-CoV pathogenicity and the immune response in piglets.
articles.abstract: Swine acute diarrhea syndrome coronavirus (SADS-CoV) infection causes severe acute diarrhea, vomiting, and lethality in piglets. To explore the molecular mechanisms by which intestinal flora regulate viral infection, we conducted multi-omics analysis [proteomics, metabolomics, short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) quantification] and 16S rRNA sequencing on intestinal mucosal and fecal samples from piglets infected with highly pathogenic SADS-CoV P7 stain or low-pathogenic SADS-CoV P83 strain. In both ileal mucosa and fecal samples, the abundance of Enterobacteriaceae was markedly higher in the highly pathogenic strain infection group than in either the control group or the low-pathogenic strain infection group. The concentration of SCFAs was significantly lower in the highly pathogenic SADS-CoV infected pigs than the low-pathogenic strain infected pigs, and SCFA levels were negatively correlated with the abundance of Enterobacteriaceae and Escherichia coli in the ileal mucosa. Compared with the low-pathogenic group, differentially expressed proteins in the highly pathogenic group were mainly associated with extracellular matrix-receptor interaction and focal adhesion pathways. SADS-CoV P7 infection increased both the adhesion capacity and the number of adherent Escherichia coli O157 on IPEC-J2 cells. This study demonstrates that the highly pathogenic SADS-CoV P7 strain remodels gut microbiota to exacerbate intestinal inflammation and tissue damage via activating integrin alpha5-mediated extracellular matrix-pathogen interactions. In contrast, the low-pathogenic SADS-CoV P83 strain exhibits attenuated virulence due to a lack of these regulatory pathways. This study elucidates the distinct pathogenic mechanisms of highly pathogenic and low-pathogenic SADS-CoV strains and provides critical insights for the development of broad-spectrum anti-coronavirus therapeutics and rational vaccine design.

articles.title: Infused CD34+ cell dose predicts response to stem cell boost in children with poor graft function following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a multicenter study from the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (GETH-TC).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor graft function (PGF) is a severe and potentially life-threatening complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), characterized by persistent cytopenias despite adequate donor chimerism. Although CD34+ selected stem cell boost (CD34+SCB) has emerged as a promising treatment, evidence in pediatric patients remains limited, and the optimal CD34+ cell dose required to achieve complete hematologic recovery has not been established.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate outcomes of CD34+SCB in children with PGF, identify factors associated with hematologic recovery and survival, and determine the CD34+ cell dose required to achieve complete hematologic recovery with external validation.

METHODS: We conducted a national multicenter retrospective study. Pediatric patients (≤18 years) with severe PGF involving at least two hematopoietic lineages who received CD34+SCB from the original donor were included in the training cohort (n=42). Primary endpoint was complete response (CR). Secondary endpoints included overall response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS) and factors associated with CR and OS. The optimal CD34+ cell dose threshold predicting CR was identified using maximally selected rank statistics and externally validated with an independent cohort.

RESULTS: Median time from HSCT to PGF diagnosis was 89 days, and 88% of patients presented with trilineage cytopenia. The median infused CD34+ cell dose was 7.3 × 106/kg. ORR and CR were 83.3% and 61.9%, respectively, with median time to CR of 43 days. With a median follow-up of 19.9 months, 2-year OS was 59.5%. Most deaths were due to infections and occurred in non-responders. In multivariable analysis, infused CD34+ cell dose was the only independent factor predictor of CR (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.02-1.26; p=0.019). A threshold of 4.65 × 10⁶ CD34+ cells/kg significantly discriminated the probability of achieving CR in the training cohort (p=0.016) and was independently validated in the external cohort (p=0.013). Previous chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and haploidentical transplantation were independently associated with inferior OS. CD34+SCB demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with low incidences of de novo acute and chronic GVHD CONCLUSION: CD34+SCB is an effective and safe therapeutic strategy for pediatric PGF following HSCT, achieving high hematologic recovery rates with acceptable long-term survival. Infused CD34+ cell dose is the main determinant of complete hematologic recovery, and a minimum threshold may help optimize treatment outcomes. Further studies are warranted to refine risk-adapted approaches in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Pathogenic traits of coagulase-negative Staphylococci and Mammalicoccus isolated from neonatal sepsis blood cultures in low- and middle-income countries.
articles.abstract: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) are increasingly recognised as neonatal pathogens in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet are often dismissed as contaminants. We characterised the genomic landscape, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and virulence of 48 CoNS isolates recovered as the sole pathogen from neonates with clinical sepsis across seven hospitals in five LMICs. Whole-genome sequencing determined sequence types, resistomes, and virulomes, whilst virulence was assessed using a Galleria mellonella in vivo model. Species identified included Mammaliicoccus sciuri (n=19; 40%), S. haemolyticus (n=15; 31%), S. epidermidis (n=11; 23%), S. saprophyticus (n=2), and S. xylosus (n=1). M. sciuri predominated in early-onset sepsis (63%); S. haemolyticus (87%) and S. epidermidis (64%) dominated late-onset cases. Multidrug resistance (≥3 classes) was pervasive in S. haemolyticus (93%) and S. epidermidis (91%), with 41.7% of all isolates harbouring mecA-positive SCCmec elements. In Galleria, S. haemolyticus induced significantly higher mortality than S. epidermidis and M. sciuri (p<0.01). Genomically, expanded cap8 capsular gene cassette carriage in S. haemolyticus negatively correlated with pathogenicity (p=0.011), suggesting extensive encapsulation masks acute toxicity. Conversely, S. epidermidis exhibited a broader pathogenic arsenal (adherence, exoenzymes, Type VII secretion), wherein adherence-gene burden positively correlated with mortality (p=0.035), whilst biofilm (icaA-D) carriage showed no significant association (p=0.412). The recovery of these isolates challenges their perception as mere contaminants. Whilst M. sciuri is associated with early-onset disease, the pronounced virulence of S. haemolyticus and the pervasive MDR profiles of both S. haemolyticus and S. epidermidis highlight them as critical, overlooked pathogens in the neonatal unit.

articles.title: Co-infection dynamics of Aeromonas jandaei and Edwardsiella tarda in Oscar fish (Astronotus ocellatus): Effects on pathogenicity, oxidative stress and immune responses.
articles.abstract: Co-infections involving multiple bacterial pathogens represent an emerging challenge in aquaculture, yet their effects on host physiology and immune responses remain poorly understood. The present study investigated the pathogenicity and host responses associated with experimental co-infection of Aeromonas jandaei and Edwardsiella tarda in Oscar fish (Astronotus ocellatus). Following determination of the median lethal dose (LD50) for each pathogen, fish were challenged with single infections or a co-infection and evaluated for mortality, clinical signs, biochemical responses, and immune-related gene expression in the spleen and kidney. Co-infection resulted in the highest cumulative mortality (87.9%), compared with fish infected with A. jandaei (68.5%) or E. tarda (56.5%) alone, and produced more severe clinical manifestations, including lethargy, anorexia, abnormal swimming behaviour, and internal haemorrhaging. Biochemical analyses revealed significant elevations in glutamate pyruvate transaminase (GPT) and glutamate oxaloacetate transaminase (GOT) activities, with GPT reaching 43.52 ± 5.51 U/mg tissue in the co-infected group on 7th day post infection. In contrast, superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity declined markedly in infected fish, indicating increased oxidative stress, while catalase (CAT) activity increased significantly during the later stages of infection. Immune gene expression analysis demonstrated significant modulation of immunoglobulin M heavy chain (IgM-H), interleukin-8 (IL-8), major histocompatibility complex-IIα (MHC-IIα), and chemokine-1 (CC-1). In the spleen, MHC-IIα expression was strongly induced, reaching 15.7 ± 0.25 fold in the E. tarda infected group and 12.0 ± 0.52 fold in the A. jandaei infected group on 7th day post infection, whereas IgM-H expression peaked at 4.6 ± 0.61 fold in A. jandaei infected fish. In the kidney, co-infection elicited a pronounced inflammatory response, characterized by elevated IL-8 (3.7 ± 0.29 fold) and CC-1 (2.5 ± 0.37 fold) expression on 7th day post infection, indicating enhanced immune cell recruitment and activation. Co-infection altered the magnitude and pattern of immune gene expression, suggesting complex pathogen-host interactions and immune modulation. The findings demonstrate that simultaneous infection exacerbates disease severity, enhances oxidative stress, and significantly influences host immune responses, highlighting the importance of considering polymicrobial infections in disease management strategies for ornamental aquaculture.

articles.title: Serial In Vivo Passage of Acanthamoeba lugdunensis Is Associated with Altered Transcription and Increased Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability in Mice.
articles.abstract: We examined passage-associated phenotypic and transcriptional changes in the clinical Acanthamoeba lugdunensis keratitis isolate KA/E2 using preplanned serial in vivo passage in C57BL/6 mice. Amoebae were recovered from lung but not brain cultures during the first cycle. Brain cultures yielded lineages P2 and P3 during the second and third cycles, respectively, with significantly greater recovery in the third than the second cycle on day 4 after plating. In a separate experiment, P3 infection was associated with greater blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and earlier body-weight loss than E2 infection; body weight differed significantly between infected groups only on day 8. Cldn5 and Ocln expression was lower in P3-infected mice than in controls; Tjp1 showed no significant pairwise differences. RNA sequencing identified 794 differentially expressed genes between parental E2 and P3. Upregulated genes were enriched for carbohydrate metabolism and hydrolase annotations and included transcripts annotated as a putative IgA-specific serine endopeptidase-like protein and cysteine proteinase 5. Phosphorylation-related genes were enriched among downregulated genes. These differences were detected after five axenic subcultures of P3, although their stability and heritability remain unknown. Total gelatinolytic activity was higher in P3 excretory-secretory products than in E2. Phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride reduced activity in both isolates, with no significant difference between isolates after treatment; E-64 produced no significant change in total activity. Serial in vivo passage was associated with brain culture recovery, transcriptional differences, and greater BBB permeability, without establishing causality.

articles.title: Biomarkers of experimental Toxocara canis infection are context-dependent: A systematic review of murine models.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxocara canis infection is a neglected zoonosis associated with multisystemic involvement and persistent larval infection. Murine models are widely used to investigate host-parasite interactions, but methodological heterogeneity limits biomarker comparison and validation.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize experimental murine T. canis infection models and synthesize parasitological, pathological, immunological, molecular, and functional biomarkers and outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Virtual Health Library were searched from inception to September 1, 2026, without publication-date restrictions. Only English-language articles were eligible. Studies were screened using Rayyan and assessed according to a PECOS framework. Risk of bias and methodological quality were evaluated using SYRCLE and an adapted CAMARADES checklist. Findings were synthesized descriptively.

RESULTS: Sixty-seven studies were included. The central nervous system was most investigated (39/67; 58.2%), followed by pulmonary (32/67; 47.8%) and hepatic (24/67; 35.8%) compartments. Larval recovery and tissue PCR characterized parasite localization or persistence, whereas serological, inflammatory, histopathological, molecular, and functional outcomes captured distinct dimensions of infection. Type-2-associated responses, particularly eosinophilia and IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13, were recurrent. Recent studies incorporated transcriptomics, lipidomics, extracellular-vesicle miRNAs, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics. Methodological limitations were particularly evident in randomization, blinding, and sample-size reporting.

CONCLUSIONS: Murine T. canis infection is a dynamic, multisystem process in which biomarker interpretation depends on tissue, timing, and biological context. Evidence supports complementary, purpose-driven outcome assessment rather than a single biomarker or universal protocol. Greater methodological standardization, longitudinal assessment, and multimodal designs may improve reproducibility and biomarker validation.

articles.title: Feasibility and safety of oral propranolol for heart rate control in pre-TAVI cardiac CT in severe aortic stenosis: A prospective study.
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Heart rate (HR) control may improve high-quality cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) image quality in preprocedural planning for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS). Beta-blockers, though useful for HR reduction, pose hemodynamic risks in AS patients. Propranolol, a non-selective beta blocker, may offer a safe and effective solution, but its role in this context remains uncertain. The aim of this paper is to assess the feasibility and safety of oral propranolol for HR control in severe AS patients undergoing pre-TAVI CCTA.

METHODS: This prospective, single-center study involved 113 severe AS patients scheduled for pre-TAVI CCTA. Oral propranolol was administered according to baseline HR and individualized clinical assessment: patients with HR 55-64 bpm were eligible for 5mg, while those with HR >65 bpm were eligible for 10mg. Propranolol was withheld in patients with lower baseline HR or clinical/hemodynamic features favoring avoidance of beta-blockade. The primary outcome was achieving HR <65 bpm at the time of CCTA. Secondary outcomes included HR reduction and adverse events.

RESULTS: Of 113 patients, 73 received propranolol and 40 were withheld propranolol. At admission, patients receiving propranolol had higher HR, whereas those not receiving propranolol more frequently had atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, and previous beta blocker use. Propranolol group showed significant HR reduction from 76.3 ± 11 bpm to a median HR of 66 bpm (p < 0.001). No HR reduction was noted in the non-propranolol group. At CCTA, 43.4% of propranolol patients met the target HR versus 43.3% of the non-propranolol group. No major adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: In selected patients with severe AS undergoing pre-TAVI CCTA, oral propranolol was associated with significant within-group HR reduction and no major adverse events. However, target HR achievement was similar between groups, and this comparison is limited by non-randomized treatment allocation and baseline differences. These findings support the feasibility and preliminary safety of propranolol, while further studies are needed to establish its efficacy and impact on image quality.

articles.title: Medical education and disease awareness in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an underdiagnosed cause of heart failure, with diagnostic challenges often attributed to suboptimal physician awareness. This study aimed to evaluate awareness, knowledge, and clinical practices related to ATTR-CM across various medical specialties in Portugal.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from November 2023 to February 2024 among Portuguese physicians in cardiology, internal medicine, and general practice. A 15-item questionnaire evaluated demographics, familiarity with ATTR-CM, disease exposure, recognition of diagnostic red flags, knowledge of diagnostic algorithms, referral patterns, and management challenges.

RESULTS: Of 1,268 physicians surveyed, 56.8% reported unfamiliarity with ATTR-CM, and 76.0% were unaware of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) diagnostic guidelines. Awareness of diagnostic algorithms was significantly higher among cardiologists (97.8%) and internists (39.1%) compared to general practitioners (13.1%). Clinical suspicion of ATTR-CM was primarily triggered by imaging modalities, especially transthoracic echocardiography, supported by cardiac clinical signs and symptoms and patient history. Regarding diagnosis just 8% of respondents highlighted bone scintigraphy as essential. Referral patterns varied by specialty: cardiologists emphasized patient management and follow-up in a cardiomyopathy consultation, internal medicine bridged suspicion and specialist referral, and general practitioners frequently initiated referrals based on early suspicion and diagnostic confirmation. The principal challenges identified were initial clinical suspicion, selection of appropriate imaging exams, and knowledge of the referral pathways, with specialty-specific barriers influencing management strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: Portuguese physicians exhibit specialty-specific differences in awareness and practices regarding ATTR-CM. Non-cardiologists focus on red flag recognition and structured referral, while cardiologists lead diagnosis and management. Role-adapted educational programs are warranted to optimize early recognition, appropriate referral, and effective multidisciplinary care.

articles.title: Long-term Outcomes after Fontan Single Ventricle Palliation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Regional Registry Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While several Fontan patient registries have been established, a systematic analysis of these collective data does not exist to provide insight into long-term outcomes. This meta-analysis aims to provide an updated assessment of published Fontan patient outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic search identified registry studies reporting long-term outcomes following the Fontan procedure. A reconstructed individual patient data-based meta-analysis assessed survival and failure rates. Subgroup analyses evaluated outcomes across different Fontan techniques.

RESULTS: Six registry studies, including 7,854 Fontan patients, were included. The mean age at Fontan completion was 5.8 years, with a mean follow-up age of 21.4 years. 58.7% of patients were male. An extracardiac conduit (ECC) was used in 62.1% of patients, a lateral tunnel (LT) in 23.1%, and the atriopulmonary (AP) technique in 14.8%. 5.1% of patients underwent early surgical revision. Cumulative survival rates were 93.6% at 10 years, 87.2% at 20 years, and 80.2% at 30 years. Upon comparison, both ECC and LT were associated with significantly improved survival compared to the AP technique (p<0.001). Finally, freedom-from-Fontan-failure rates at 10, 20, and 30 years of follow-up were 76.6%, 74.9%, and 70.2%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: These data demonstrate that Fontan palliation yields better long-term survival than previously reported. ECCs are most common, and both ECC and LT techniques outperform the AP technique. These data provide important context for patient counseling regarding expected long-term outcomes after single-ventricle palliation and underscore the need for lifelong specialized surveillance in this population.

articles.title: Tafamidis: is it truly a game changer for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy?
articles.abstract: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is an increasingly recognized condition caused by the misfolding of transthyretin (TTR) protein, leading to amyloid deposits in various tissues and organs. In 2019, tafamidis was the first FDA-approved disease-modifying therapy to address an unmet need for patients with ATTR-CM, stabilizing TTR proteins and preventing dissociation. Tafamidis has been shown to reduce all-cause mortality and slow decline in functional capacity and quality of life and is generally considered a safe treatment because of its minimal major drug interactions. However, tafamidis has several well-recognized limitations, including high cost, reduced effectiveness in advanced disease stages, limited ability to address established amyloid burden, and limited evidence for advanced polyneuropathy. As new therapies and advancements emerge, further research is needed to compare their relative effectiveness. In this review, we explore the development of tafamidis, pivotal clinical trial results, clinical applications, safety considerations, and future therapeutic directions for ATTR-CM.

articles.title: Efficacy of Standard Meropenem Dosing in Healthcare-Associated Meningitis: Is It Universal?
authors: AtlanRéa Study Group and PKPopLCR Study Group (Members and affiliations of the Study Group in byline listed in Acknowledgements, linked to Pubmed record)
articles.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) infections related to external ventricular drains (EVD) represent a frequent and serious complication of invasive CNS procedures, particularly those due to Gram-negative bacilli (GNB). Meropenem is one of the first-line treatments recommended whereas its limited CSF diffusion, with few studies with proven CNS infections. The multicenter PK/PD study evaluated the impact of EVD-related infections on meropenem distribution in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in 28 neuro-ICU patients with EVD, receiving meropenem via intermittent or continuous infusions (6-8 g/day), by comparing patients with confirmed CNS infection (n = 14) to those with extra-CNS infection (n = 14). Theoretical efficacy of different dosing strategies was assessed by Monte Carlo simulations. Probability of target attainment (PTA) and cumulative fractions of response (CFRs) were derived as the percentage of individuals achieving at steady-state 100% T > MIC for each dosing regimen using meropenem MIC frequency distributions for P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae, E. cloacae, and S. marcescens. A limited penetration of meropenem into CSF was observed, with a CSF/plasma AUC ratio of 16.3 ± 11.4% in CNS infections compared to 6.0 ± 4.5% in extra-CNS infections, highlighting the significant impact of infection. In patients with CNS infection, PTA in CSF was> 90% for MIC up to 0.25 mg/L with 6 g/d and reached 89.7% with 8 g/d for MIC of 1 mg/L. Overall, a daily dose of 6 g appears sufficient to treat CNS infections caused by E. cloacae, K. pneumoniae, and S. marcescens, whereas none of the dosing regimens tested seem adequate for P. aeruginosa, which more frequently exhibits high MICs > 1 mg/L.

articles.title: The association between early core body temperature in ICU and mortality in spontaneous subarachnoid haemorrhage: a binational registry study.
authors: Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Centre for Outcome and Resource Evaluation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fever and hypothermia are important risk factors for mortality in critically ill patients. We examined the association between day-one (D1) core body temperature and in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with spontaneous subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH).

METHODS: We performed a multicentre retrospective cohort study using the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Adult Patient Database. Adults (≥18 years) with SAH admitted to ICU between January 2018 and June 2024 were included (n = 7,567). Primary exposures were core temperature used for the Australian and New Zealand Risk of Death (ANZROD) score (TANZ), and the highest (THI) and lowest (TLO) core temperatures recorded during the first 24 ICU hours. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Associations were modelled using generalised linear models with natural cubic splines and covariate adjustment.

RESULTS: Mean TANZ was 36.0 °C (SD 0.97), mean THI 37.3 °C (SD 0.68), and mean TLO 36.0 °C (SD 0.96). Overall in-hospital mortality was 17% (n = 1,304). TANZ, THI and TLO showed non-linear U-shaped associations with mortality. Lowest observed mortality occurred at TANZ 35.8-38.2 °C, THI 36.8-38.2 °C and TLO 36.1-37.8 °C. Mortality increased below these ranges for TANZ (OR:1.55, 95% CI:1.34-1.79), THI (OR:1.42, 95% CI:1.20-1.69) and TLO (OR:1.38, 95% CI:1.19-1.60), and above the optimal range of THI (OR: 1.47, 95% CI:1.19-1.80).

CONCLUSIONS: In critically ill SAH patients, D1 core temperature had a U-shaped association with in-hospital mortality. Further research should determine whether temperature variation is a modifiable risk factor in this population.

articles.title: Burden of sepsis in obstetric critically ill patients: A qualitative systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major contributor to maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide and represents one of the leading causes of intensive care unit (ICU) admission among obstetric patients. However, the burden and clinical profile of the most severely affected women remain incompletely defined. This systematic review aimed to estimate the epidemiology, characteristics, and outcomes of sepsis in critically ill obstetric patients.

PATIENTS & METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted for studies published between 2013 and 2025, including studies of women requiring ICU admission for sepsis during pregnancy or the post-partum. Following the screening process, 25 of the 5847 screened studies met the inclusion criteria. All were observational. The overall population included 7,434,710 hospitalised obstetric patients, including 3,593 obstetric ICU admissions for sepsis. The incidence of intensive care unit admissions ranged from 21 to 857 every 10,000 hospitalized obstetric patients and reached incidences of 11.3% among hospitalized obstetric patients with sepsis. Sepsis accounted for 5.7% of obstetric ICU admissions.

RESULTS: Half of the patients had one organ dysfunction, while a quarter had three or more, with respiratory and cardiovascular insufficiencies being the most common. The main infection sources were the genital, respiratory, and urinary tracts. Septic shock occurred in 16.6% of the cases. The mean Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score was 6.2 and the Acute Physiologic Assessment and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score was 12.3. ICU and hospital stay were 3 and 8 days. Mortality varied significantly (median 4.6%), with marked disparities between high- and low-income countries.

CONCLUSION: Robust epidemiological monitoring is therefore urgently required.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO under ID 2023 CRD42023446466.

articles.title: Over-expression, purification, and characterisation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT64 from inclusion bodies.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis remains among the top ten deadliest infectious diseases worldwide, primarily due to delayed diagnosis, co-infection with HIV, and multidrug resistance. Targeting early secreted mycobacterial antigens, including MPT64, ESAT6, and CFP10, may be a viable strategy for detecting the onset of tuberculosis. Although recombinant MPT64 has been produced previously, limited information is available regarding its structural integrity and thermodynamic unfolding behaviour following recovery from inclusion bodies. In this study, MPT64 protein was overexpressed, affinity-purified, and characterised using biophysical and biochemical methods. The purified recombinant MPT64 had a purity greater than 95%, yielding 2 mg from 1 L of bacterial culture. Western blot analysis confirmed MPT64 identity, while ELISA demonstrated antibody recognition of refolded MPT64, with markedly reduced binding following heat denaturation, indicating that refolding preserved conformational epitopes. Far-UV circular dichroism (CD) and intrinsic fluorescence spectroscopy spectral profiles confirmed that the purified MPT64 protein retained its folded secondary and tertiary structural integrity.
