To standardize the perioperative management of co-ablation therapy for bone and soft tissue tumors at different anatomical locations, the Expert Committee on Radiological Interventional Therapy, Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO), the Expert Committee on Ablation Therapy, Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO), the Committee of Ablation Therapy in Oncology, Chinese Anti-Cancer Association and the Committee of Tumor Ablation, the Chinese College of Interventionalists organized relevant domestic experts to develop the Expert Consensus on Co-ablation Therapy for the Perioperative Management of Bone and Soft Tissue Tumors, aiming to provide a reference and guidance for clinical practice.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on composite co-ablation for pain caused by bone metastases].
authors: Expert Committee on Radiological Interventional Therapy, Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO)
Expert Committee on Ablation Therapy, Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO)
Committee of Ablation Therapy in Oncology, Chinese Anti-Cancer Association
Committee of Tumor Ablation, the Chinese College of Interventionalists
articles.abstract: Pain caused by bone metastases from malignant tumors is mediated by multiple mechanisms, including direct tumor invasion or nerve compression, release of inflammatory mediators, and peripheral/central sensitization, which severely compromise patients' quality of life and functional status. Composite co-ablation, through alternating cycles of deep cryogenic temperature (-196 ℃) and hyperthermia (80 ℃), offers advantages such as a large ablation volume per probe, lower tissue temperature than conventional cryoablation, a visible ice ball on imaging, and synergistic cryo-thermal effects. This technique achieves rapid pain relief while maximizing preservation of surrounding critical structures. To standardize the clinical application of composite co-ablation for pain caused by bone metastases from malignant tumors, the Radiation Interventional Oncology Committee of the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO), the Tumor Ablation Therapy Committee of CSCO, the Tumor Ablation Therapy Committee of the Chinese Anti-Cancer Association, and the Tumor Ablation Expert Working Group of the Chinese College of Interventionalists jointly organized nationwide experts to formulate this "Expert Consensus on Composite Co-ablation for Pain Caused by Bone Metastases", aiming to better guide clinical practice.

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on the diagnosis and management of older patients with immune thrombocytopenia (2026 edition)].
authors: Platelet Group, Hematology Subcommittee, Chinese Geriatric Society
Hematology Subcommittee, China International Exchange and Promotive Association for Medical and Health Care
articles.abstract: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired autoimmune bleeding disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia. With the accelerating aging of the global population, the incidence of ITP among older adults (≥60 years) is increasing, and this population exhibits distinct epidemiological features, pathogenic mechanisms, and clinical management needs. To standardize the diagnosis and management of ITP in older adults in China, the Platelet Group of the Hematology Subcommittee of the Chinese Geriatric Society and the Hematology Subcommittee of the China International Exchange and Promotive Association for Medical and Health Care jointly established an expert consensus committee on ITP in older adults. This consensus was developed to integrate evidence-based medical data from the literature with clinical practice experience, provide practical recommendations for standardized diagnosis and treatment of geriatric ITP, and promote the conduct of future clinical research specifically targeting this population.

articles.title: Exercise promotes host anti-infection activity through CNDP2 metabolite-mediated inflammasome hyperactivation.
articles.abstract: Exercise can enhance the body's ability to resist infections, but its molecular mechanisms are still unclear. Here, we found that exercise can induce a hyperactivation-like state of the NLRP3 inflammasome during infection, which enhances the body's ability to resist infection by continuously secreting inflammatory cytokines and reducing immune cell pyroptosis. At the molecular level, exercise enhances the binding between CNDP2 and GSDMD, promoting the production of γ-Glu-Cys. γ-Glu-Cys binds to CypD and inhibits the binding between CypD and GSDMD, thereby avoiding further damage to the mitochondrial inner membrane during the occurrence of inflammasomes. Limited mitochondrial DNA leakage allows the NLRP3 inflammasome to a hyperactivate state. Our findings reveal the molecular mechanisms by which exercise enhances the body's ability to resist infections, and provide possible standards for better guiding exercise intensity to improve anti-infection capabilities in the future.

articles.title: Large-scale genome re-annotation uncovers pathogen-specific lncRNA regulators of fungal growth and virulence.
articles.abstract: Invasive fungal infections pose a serious global health threat. Although core cellular processes are broadly conserved across fungi, only a small fraction of known species cause severe human disease, suggesting that pathogenicity may depend in part on pathogen-specific regulators. However, such elements remain poorly understood because they often lack recognizable homologs, limiting accurate annotation and functional characterization. Here, using the invasive mold Aspergillus fumigatus as a model, we combined transcriptome-guided re-annotation with functional screening to identify previously unrecognized long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) required for fungal growth and virulence. Among 423 loci previously annotated as Fumigati section-specific protein-coding genes, 176 were reclassified as non-coding, revealing widespread annotation errors that had obscured potential regulators. We identified two lncRNAs, SSP7 and SSP8, that are required for hyphal growth and virulence in a murine infection model. Mechanistically, SSP7 binds the coding region of pprA mRNA, promotes its association with polysomes and translation, and thereby sustains mitochondrial function, whereas SSP8 contributes to amino acid homeostasis. Together, these findings demonstrate for the first time that pathogen-specific lncRNAs can fine-tune conserved cellular processes to generate distinct fungal growth and virulence traits, and reveal a novel translational regulatory mechanism in fungal pathogenicity.

articles.title: Performance of large language models in the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examinations and Beyond: Scoping review.
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 and DeepSeek have shown potential in medical education and assessment. In China, the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination (CNMLE) has become a critical benchmark for evaluating LLMs' professional knowledge and reasoning ability in non-English contexts. This scoping review aims to synthesize research evaluating LLM performance on the CNMLE and related Chinese medical examinations, identifying performance trends, methodological gaps, and future directions. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed and Web of Science were searched on June 12, 2025, using terms related to LLMs and Chinese medical examinations. Studies were included if they evaluated any LLM on national-level Chinese medical exams and reported performance metrics. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Study quality was assessed using a 12-item checklist covering dataset characteristics, LLM setup, and evaluation methods. Fisher's exact test was used to assess differences in the passing rates of different LLMs. 14 studies were included, covering 51 evaluation records across 8 types of Chinese medical examinations, including CNMLE and specialty exams such as critical care, radiation oncology, and ultrasound medicine. Exam years ranged from 2017 to 2024, with a shift toward using recent exams. A total of 9 LLMs were evaluated, including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, ERNIE, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-72B, Baichuan2-7B, Baichuan2-13B and DISC-MedLLM. GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest scores of 552 (92.00%) and 523 (87.20%) in the 2024 CNMLE, respectively, both surpassing the passing threshold. In an exploratory comparison, GPT-4 achieved a higher pass rate than GPT-3.5 with a statistically significant difference, although inconsistencies in datasets, model transparency, and evaluation criteria persist across the included studies. LLMs show improving performance on Chinese medical exams, especially newer models. Nevertheless, future research should prioritize standardized benchmarks, multimodal capabilities, and transparent evaluation to ensure meaningful clinical relevance and educational value.

articles.title: Anxiety and Depression in Athletes of Different Levels Without Current Injury: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analyses.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Exercise has been demonstrated to positively affect the prevention and treatment of anxiety and depression; however, athletes face an increased risk of mental health issues.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence and incidence of anxiety and depression among athletes and explore potential factors influencing these outcomes.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases were searched between inception and August 18, 2025, for studies in which anxiety and depression in athletes were investigated.

STUDY SELECTION: Studies were included according to the following criteria: (1) athletes of any level including high school or collegiate level, amateur, and elite and (2) prevalence or incidence of moderate to severe anxiety or depressive symptoms or diagnosis of anxiety or depressive disorders.

DATA EXTRACTION: Study characteristics, type of modality, anxiety or depressive symptoms tools with cutoffs for moderate to severe symptoms, and participant characteristics were extracted. Two reviewers assessed risk of bias of the included studies using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Meta-analysis was performed using random-effects models. We calculated incidence and prevalence estimates with 95% CIs for each study, then pooled the data for symptom groups. Subanalyses by level of sport and type of sport were conducted.

DATA SYNTHESIS: We included 64 studies (n = 131 840 athletes) in the systematic review and 64 studies (97 events) in the meta-analysis. The prevalence of diagnosed disorders was 21% for anxiety (95% CI = 0.14, 0.29; 3 studies, 106 403 athletes), 6% for depression (95% CI = 0.04, 0.10; 1 study, 290 athletes), and 14% for combined anxiety and depression (95% CI = 0.12, 0.15; 1 study, 3719 athletes). However, the prevalence of moderate to severe anxiety symptoms was 16% (95% CI = 0.13, 0.21; 33 studies, 12 893 athletes), 18% for moderate to severe depressive symptoms (95% CI = 0.14, 0.22; 46 studies, 19 290 athletes), and 35% for moderate to severe anxiety and depressive symptoms (95% CI = 0.29, 0.43; 11 studies, 4069 athletes). The 12-month incidence for moderate to severe anxiety and depressive symptoms was 40% (95% CI = 0.24, 0.58; 3 studies, 611 athletes).

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence rates for moderate to severe anxiety, depressive, or anxiety and depressive symptoms are relatively different when diagnosed by specialists or assessed using validated screening tools. These findings underscore the importance of early identification and focused attention on athletes' mental health.

articles.title: INVICTUS II: comparison of disc diffusion and broth microdilution methods for susceptibility testing of ceftolozane/tazobactam and five comparator agents against a subset of INVICTUS I Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A subset of clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from the INVICTUS I study was selected to compare antimicrobial susceptibility performance for disc diffusion and broth microdilution of ceftolozane/tazobactam and five comparator antipseudomonal agents.

METHODS: Overall, 159 non-cystic fibrosis isolates were chosen from INVICTUS I that had the smallest zone diameters from disc testing to ceftolozane/tazobactam, including isolates that were close to the breakpoints. The isolates were tested across 14 centres in the UK. Susceptibility results were interpreted using EUCAST 2026 criteria.

RESULTS: Discrepancy analysis showed combined error rates (very major and major errors) highest for ceftolozane/tazobactam, ceftazidime and piperacillin/tazobactam (15.7%, 14.5% and 12.6%, respectively); when adjusted to remove isolates close to the breakpoint for ceftolozane/tazobactam and piperacillin/tazobactam there were still remarkably high error rates (10.6% and 7.2%, respectively). Essential agreement and bias analysis were not performed as MICs were being compared with zone diameters.

DISCUSSION: Our findings highlight substantial challenges in performing and interpreting susceptibility testing for these two important antipseudomonal β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitors, which are commonly employed as either first-line empirical therapy (piperacillin/tazobactam) or for serious and MDR infection (ceftolozane/tazobactam). A review of disc testing for these agents may be warranted, and diagnostic laboratories may wish to review the technical limitations and put in place mitigating measures.

articles.title: Post-Dengue Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Dengue fever is commonly associated with bleeding complications, particularly in patients with thrombocytopenia. However, thrombotic events, such as venous thromboembolism, are rare and under-recognized manifestations, particularly during the recovery phase, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report the case of a 25-year-old previously healthy male who presented with high-grade fever, myalgia, and headache and was diagnosed with dengue fever based on positive NS1 antigen testing. Dengue infection was confirmed by a positive NS1 antigen test performed on Day 3 of illness, consistent with early acute dengue infection. The diagnosis was further supported by the patient's clinical presentation, including high-grade fever, myalgia, and headache in the appropriate epidemiological context of a dengue-endemic region. During the recovery phase of the illness, he developed painful swelling of the right lower limb and progressive dyspnea. Investigations revealed markedly elevated D-dimer levels, right lower limb deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasound, and bilateral pulmonary emboli with right ventricular strain on CT pulmonary angiography images. Although dengue-associated thrombosis has been reported in the setting of thrombocytopenia, as described by Ghatak et al., the present case demonstrates that thrombotic complications may also occur despite preserved platelet counts, highlighting the potential contribution of endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory activation. This case highlights the paradoxical coexistence of thrombosis and bleeding risk in dengue fever. To avoid potentially fatal thromboembolic complications in patients with dengue, early diagnosis, prompt anticoagulation, and a high index of suspicion are crucial.

articles.title: Beyond the Oropharynx: TTMV-HPV DNA Detection in a p16-Positive Hypopharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Plasma TTMV-HPV16 DNA provided complementary molecular evidence in a p16-positive hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, while PET/CT localized the occult left pyriform sinus primary. Serial postoperative TTMV-HPV DNA assays remained undetectable through approximately 19 months of clinical and radiographic surveillance.

articles.title: Endovascular Treatment of Nonsaccular Posterior Circulation Aneurysms: A Comparative Meta-analysis of Flow Diversion versus Stent-Assisted Coiling.
articles.abstract: Background Fusiform and giant aneurysms of the posterior circulation carry a dismal natural history. Flow diversion (FD) and stent-assisted coiling (SAC) are the two principal reconstructive endovascular strategies, yet no meta-analysis of direct comparative studies exists to guide selection between them. Methods A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review of MEDLINE and Embase (2011-2026) identified comparative studies of adult patients with nonsaccular posterior circulation aneurysms reporting outcomes following FD and SAC. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed with the meta package in R (v4.3.3). Two planned sensitivity analyses and leave-one-out analysis assessed robustness. Results Five studies comprising 209 aneurysms (102 FD, 107 SAC) met inclusion criteria. No significant differences were observed between FD and SAC for favorable functional outcome, satisfactory aneurysm occlusion, or ischemic stroke. FD was associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 2.06; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11-3.84; p = 0.03), aneurysm rupture (OR: 2.59; 95% CI: 1.15-5.82; p = 0.03), and in-stent thrombosis (OR: 8.15; 95% CI: 1.43-46.40; p = 0.03). All three findings demonstrated fragility on sensitivity and leave-one-out testing. Conclusion FD and SAC produce comparable functional outcomes and occlusion rates for nonsaccular posterior circulation aneurysms. FD may carry higher mortality, rupture, and in-stent thrombosis, though these signals did not withstand sensitivity analyses and could not be separated from selection bias toward complex aneurysms. These findings support both modalities as viable reconstructive options while underscoring anatomy-driven treatment selection and the need for prospective validation.

articles.title: Spontaneous Pregnancy After Laparoscopic Treatment of Ovarian Endometrioma: A Retrospective Cohort Study Comparing Stripping and Ethanol Sclerotherapy.
articles.abstract: Ovarian endometrioma is associated with infertility, whereas its treatment may compromise ovarian reserve. This retrospective cohort evaluated factors associated with spontaneous pregnancy after laparoscopic treatment of ovarian endometrioma, with particular attention to the Endometriosis Fertility Index (EFI) and reproductive outcomes after cystectomy using the stripping technique vs ethanol sclerotherapy. Forty-eight infertile women with histologically confirmed ovarian endometrioma and revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine stage III-IV endometriosis underwent laparoscopic treatment between 2022 and 2024 in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with follow-up through June 2026; 33 underwent cystectomy, and 15 underwent ethanol sclerotherapy. Overall, 29/48 women (60.4%) had primary infertility, 30/48 (62.5%) had bilateral endometriomas, and 29/48 (60.4%) had stage IV disease. Spontaneous pregnancy occurred in 17/48 women (35.4%), and 11/48 (22.9%) achieved a live birth. Pregnancy occurred in 9/15 women (60.0%) after sclerotherapy vs 8/33 (24.2%) after cystectomy (p = 0.024). Among women with EFI ≥7, 15/26 (57.7%) conceived, compared with 2/22 (9.1%) with EFI <7 (p < 0.001). In the adjusted Cox model, EFI ≥7 (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 7.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.78-35.57; p = 0.007) and ethanol sclerotherapy (aHR 3.11, 95% CI 1.17-8.29; p = 0.023) were associated with a higher rate of spontaneous pregnancy. Both ovarian-reserve markers improved in 15/15 women (100.0%) after sclerotherapy vs 9/33 (27.3%) after cystectomy (p < 0.001). These findings suggest that a favorable EFI identifies women with a higher likelihood of spontaneous pregnancy and that ethanol sclerotherapy may offer reproductive advantages over cystectomy; however, the retrospective design, small sample, and nonrandomized treatment allocation limit causal inference.

articles.title: Ultra-short bowel syndrome after near-total small bowel resection for gangrenous gut due to superior mesenteric artery thrombosis: a case report.
articles.abstract: Ultra-short bowel syndrome (USBS) is a rare and life-threatening condition defined by the retention of ˂30 cm of small intestine following resection. We report the case of a 53-year-old male who presented with gangrenous gut secondary to superior mesenteric artery thrombosis, necessitating near-total small bowel resection. The patient was left with ~15 cm of proximal jejunum and 10 cm of distal ileum, with a jejuno-ileal end-to-end anastomosis. He developed severe postoperative watery diarrhoea and required Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN) via a peripherally inserted central catheter line. With careful multidisciplinary management, the patient achieved intestinal adaptation and was weaned off TPN ~6 weeks postoperatively. This case highlights the challenges of managing USBS in a resource-limited setting and demonstrates that survival with gut adaptation is possible even with very limited residual small bowel length, provided that experienced surgical care and nutritional support are available.

articles.title: Do Physicians' Behaviors Matter for Patients With Chronic Diabetes and Hypertension? A Qualitative Descriptive Study of Patients' Lived Experiences in the Bangladeshi Healthcare Landscape.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: In resource-constrained countries like Bangladesh, healthcare consultation practices are often rushed, and the perceived effects of physicians' behaviors and physician-patient relationship remain overlooked, yet these subtle relational exchanges can profoundly influence outcomes in chronic conditions. The present study therefore aimed at understanding how patients' experiences of physicians' behaviors and physician-patient relationship influenced patients with chronic diabetes and hypertension in the context of Bangladeshi healthcare settings.

METHODS: A qualitative descriptive approach was used, employing in-depth interview in data collection, with 24 adult inpatients admitted to a public tertiary hospital in Dhaka between October and November 2024. Thematic analysis was conducted using NVivo to analyze study data.

RESULTS: Findings revealed that perceived inappropriate behaviors of the physicians affected diabetes and hypertensive patients' emotional state, while inattentive listening contributed to medication non-adherence. However, motivation and support provided by the physicians helped the patients build self-confidence, while physicians' guidance contributed to their perceived positive outcome. Patients' trust and sharing concerns with physicians were found as important relational factors in patients' perception of physician-patient relationship. Besides, systemic factors such as insufficient consultation duration and physicians' excessive patient load influenced the quality of consultation, ultimately affecting patients with chronic diabetes and hypertension.

CONCLUSION: Findings suggest that the quality of healthcare service extends beyond physicians' clinical competencies only; it constitutes physicians' behaviors and physician-patient relationship as therapeutic components in chronic illness care. Enhancing the communication skills of the physicians and relational exchanges between physician and patient may help meaningfully improve the management capacity of patients with chronic diabetes and hypertension.

articles.title: Effects of Cumulative 100 km Gait Training Using Lower-Limb Orthoses in a Patient With Severe Hemiplegia and Limited Independent Ambulation Potential: Case Report.
articles.abstract: A patient with stroke, severe hemiplegia, and limited potential for independent walking was able to achieve a modified level of independent walking after a cumulative 100 km of gait training using lower-limb orthoses. Patients with limited potential for independent walking may benefit from sufficient gait training.

articles.title: Hepatoprotective Effects of Maillard Reaction Products From Perinereis aibuhitensis: Identification and Metabolomic Insights in a Mouse Model of Alcoholic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health burden with limited therapeutic options. The primary aim of this study was to investigate the hepatoprotective effects of Maillard reaction products derived from Perinereis aibuhitensis (P-MRPs) in a mouse model of chronic alcohol-induced liver injury. Male ICR mice were fed a Lieber-DeCarli alcoholic liquid diet for 6 weeks with or without P-MRPs administration. P-MRPs intervention significantly reduced serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) activities, alleviated hepatic histopathological injury, restored antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase), and lowered malondialdehyde and interleukin (IL-6, IL-18, and IL-1β) levels. Mechanistically, P-MRPs treatment upregulated hepatic nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), downregulated NF-κB p65 and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and restored carnitine O-palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A) expression. Liver metabolomic analysis revealed that P-MRPs administration increased N-acyl amino acids and tryptophan-derived metabolites while reversing alcohol-induced accumulation of glycerophospholipids and acylcarnitines. In vitro, P-MRPs reduced ethanol-induced ROS accumulation and attenuated ALT and AST leakage in AML12 hepatocytes. Compositional profiling identified 27 small-molecule compounds with significant changes in P-MRPs abundance, and a high proportion of small-molecule peptides. Collectively, these findings suggest that P-MRPs protect against ALD-related liver injury, potentially through coordinated regulation of antioxidant, inflammatory, and lipid metabolic pathways, and provide a hypothesis-generating framework for future mechanistic investigations.

articles.title: Clinical Characterization and Outcomes of Pneumonic Plague in Madagascar: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: Pneumonic plague is rare compared to bubonic plague; data on clinical presentation and treatment outcomes are scant. We report on 13 prospectively-enrolled suspected pneumonic plague cases (7 laboratory-confirmed, one probable, 5 not-plague) treated with aminoglycoside plus ciprofloxacin for 10 days and discuss findings in the context of the available literature.

articles.title: Shared Medical Appointments (SMAs) in Lifestyle Medicine Practice: An Expert Consensus Statement From the American College of Lifestyle Medicine.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify statements of consensus on the use of shared medical appointments (SMAs) to improve quality of care and patient health outcomes in lifestyle medicine practice especially for prevention, treatment, and management of chronic disease.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel of experts in shared medical appointments (SMAs) followed an a priori protocol for developing consensus statements. Using an iterative, online Delphi process, panel members reported levels of agreement and statements were classified as consensus, near consensus, or no consensus.

RESULTS: The panel identified 106 candidate statements addressing: (1) Definitions and General Concepts, (2) Lifestyle Medicine and Behavior Change, (3) Research and Quality Improvement Outcomes, (4) Delivery Models, (5) Group Cohesiveness, (6) Billing and Documentation, (7) Staffing Models, and (8) Training. After 3 iterations of an online Delphi survey, revisions, and removal of duplicative statements, 56 statements met criteria for consensus. Nine statements met near consensus, and 41 statements did not reach consensus.

CONCLUSION: There is broad consensus among panel members that implementing SMAs highlighting lifestyle medicine has high patient satisfaction, is reimbursable, and can provide high-quality medical care. These specific consensus statements can be used to inform policy and prioritize areas for future research.

articles.title: Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet Pattern and Metabolic Syndrome Prevalence Among U.S. Young Adults: Cross-Sectional Study From the NHANES 2011-2018.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a group of interrelated risk factors associated with elevated risk of cardiovascular disease and Diabetes Mellitus. The United States (U.S.) prevalence of MetS is rising, with concerning trends among young adults necessitating updated prevalence estimates of MetS using the most recent MetS criteria. This study describes MetS prevalence and its association with Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet patterns among U.S. adults aged 18-29 years, using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data.

METHODS: Using cross-sectional data from 2011 to 2018 NHANES, a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults (analytic sample n = 3332 young adults, weighted n = 37,981,063) was included. Multivariable weighted log-binomial models estimated the adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR) for MetS and its five individual components comparing those with high versus low DASH scores, adjusting for socioeconomic and lifestyle factors.

RESULTS: Average participant age was 24 years and 51.8% were women. Over one-third (35.6%) of young adults met MetS criteria. Most participants (87.5%) did not meet DASH nutrient targets intake amounts. High fasting glucose was the most prevalent MetS component (66.4%). In this sample, while high DASH scores were not associated with MetS presence (aPR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.72-1.04), they were associated with lower prevalence of central obesity (waist circumference), a component of MetS (aPR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.64-0.98).

CONCLUSION: Despite low overall adherence to the DASH diet, higher adherence was linked to lower prevalence of MetS central obesity. Findings support targeted nutrition strategies in early adulthood to help reduce long-term cardiometabolic risk.

articles.title: Silent Intraoperative Right Coronary Artery Occlusion at a Prior Stent Site Progressing to Ventricular Fibrillation During Hip Hemiarthroplasty: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Perioperative myocardial infarction may occur without typical ischemic symptoms in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture repair. We describe the case of an 86-year-old woman with hypertension, coronary artery disease, and prior right coronary artery stenting who underwent right hip hemiarthroplasty under spinal anesthesia after clopidogrel had been withheld for one week. Continuous electrocardiographic monitoring showed progressive ST-segment elevation first recognized by the anesthesia nurse, who verified the finding and immediately informed the anesthesiology team. ST-segment elevation preceded a decline in heart rate and blood pressure and was followed by ventricular fibrillation during emergency transfer for coronary angiography. Repeated cardiopulmonary resuscitation and 200-J defibrillation produced transient rhythm recovery, with recurrent ventricular fibrillation until coronary reperfusion. Angiography showed acute right coronary artery occlusion at the previous stent site with thrombus; balloon angioplasty, intracoronary tirofiban, and implantation of a 2.75 × 29 mm drug-eluting stent restored TIMI grade 3 flow, with approximately 30% residual stenosis. Troponin T was >50 ng/mL on postoperative day 1, 4056 ng/mL on day 5, and 900 ng/mL on day 9; no major bleeding, transfusion, or neurological complications were documented. The patient ambulated before discharge on postoperative day 15. This case illustrates a descriptive temporal sequence in which progressive monitor-detected ST-segment changes preceded hemodynamic deterioration and subsequent ventricular fibrillation, followed by nursing verification, escalation, and multidisciplinary rescue; it does not establish that any specific monitoring or escalation strategy altered the outcome. Because this is a single case, the chronology described is observational and does not permit causal inference regarding the outcome.

articles.title: Diagnosis and Management of Infectious Encephalitis in Adults: Guidelines From the European Academy of Neurology and European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Encephalitis is difficult to diagnose and manage, posing a challenge to clinicians. Since the last European guidelines were published in 2010, novel causes have emerged, diagnostic processes have evolved and treatments assessed which need to be reflected in updated guidelines.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to produce recommendations for the diagnosis and management of infectious encephalitis in adults based on current evidence to equip clinicians to improve patient outcomes.

METHODS: These guidelines were developed jointly with the support of two European specialist medical organisations. Clinical questions were prioritised and formulated in PICO format. A systematic literature search was conducted for each question, and the quality of evidence was assessed using standardised tools. Recommendations were developed according to the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE) approach. Where only indirect evidence was available, a good practice statement was made.

RESULTS: Sixteen questions were considered, with two recommendations reached: for initiation of intravenous aciclovir as soon as possible upon suspicion of encephalitis and against replacing pathogen-specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with multiplex CSF PCR panels for diagnosis of adult patients with suspected infectious encephalitis. For adults with proven HSV encephalitis, we were unable to recommend for or against the use of corticosteroids. A further 13 good practice statements regarding when to clinically suspect infectious encephalitis, microbiological investigations, additional investigations, treatment and ongoing care and rehabilitation were agreed.

CONCLUSIONS: Given the clinical severity and public health importance of this condition, the paucity of high-quality evidence is striking. Transnational, large-scale research in infective encephalitis is encouraged.

articles.title: Unstable Reference and Unblinded Comparison Undermine Artificial Intelligence Echocardiography in Pulmonary Hypertension.
Deconstructing Heterogeneity of Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Chronic Lung Disease with Quantitative Chest CT Data.
Glutamine from plasma-like medium fuels nitrogen metabolism and influences proliferation in Leptospira interrogans.
articles.abstract: Leptospirosis, caused by pathogenic Leptospira spp. such as L. interrogans, is a bacterial zoonosis of increasing prevalence with no consistently effective treatments in severe cases. We sought to characterize metabolic mechanisms that support L. interrogans infection, with the ultimate goal of revealing unexplored therapeutic opportunities. We first established and validated a culture medium, which we refer to as supplemented Human Plasma-Like Medium (sHPLM). sHPLM more closely resembles the physiological environment of the human host than standard culture media, such as the EMJH (Ellinghausen-McCullough-Johnson-Harris) medium typically used for Leptospira culture. We also pioneered metabolomics approaches to study sHPLM-cultured Leptospira. Specifically, we developed a liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry (LC/MS) workflow for both medium metabolomics and stable isotope tracing with L. interrogans cultures. The application of these technologies in L. interrogans revealed that the amino acid glutamine is a major nitrogen source among the many available in sHPLM. Subsequent growth studies in three pathogenic Leptospira strains and the nonpathogenic strain L. biflexa Patoc-1 showed robust proliferation when only glutamine-derived nitrogen was available. Further, a small-molecule inhibitor designed to target glutamine utilization, JHU-083, effectively impaired the proliferation of L. interrogans cultures. Adding glutamine to non-physiological EMJH medium also rapidly induced a short-term proliferative boost in L. interrogans and increased biofilm formation. RNA-sequencing after glutamine exposure revealed transcriptional trends for increases in biosynthesis to support these phenotypes. Although ammonium has long been thought to be the sole nitrogen source for Leptospira spp., our results demonstrate that glutamine provides a second source of nitrogen for biosynthesis in multiple strains and may act as a metabolite signal to alter L. interrogans physiology in ways that could influence infection. This work highlights that studying L. interrogans under physiological conditions is key to understanding mechanisms supporting infection and points to nitrogen assimilation as a potential target for therapies.

articles.title: ZBED6 deficiency drives pathological cardiac hypertrophy through MEOX1-ERK1/2-dependent autophagy dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy, a major risk factor for heart failure, is regulated by complex transcriptional networks. We previously identified the transcription factor ZBED6 as a key regulator for skeletal muscle hypertrophy, its role in the cardiac hypertrophy remains unexplored. Here, we report that ZBED6 is a key suppressor of pathological cardiac hypertrophy. ZBED6 is markedly reduced in myocardial tissues from patients with cardiac hypertrophy. ZBED6-deficient pigs exhibited cardiac hypertrophy with diastolic dysfunction. Integrative transcriptomic and ChIP-seq analyses identified MEOX1 as a direct negative target of ZBED6. Loss of ZBED6 upregulates MEOX1 transcription, which subsequently activated ERK1/2 signaling, leading to impaired autophagy-induced hypertrophy. Knockdown of MEOX1 reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and mitigated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy induced by ZBED6 deficiency. Similarly, pharmacological inhibition of ERK1/2 restored autophagy and alleviated hypertrophy in ZBED6-depleted cardiomyocytes. Collectively, these findings define a previously unrecognized ZBED6-MEOX1-ERK1/2 axis that critically regulates cardiac hypertrophy and represents a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Receptor-induced activation of MERS-CoV spike revealed by time-course cryo-EM.
articles.abstract: The Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) initiates infection by engaging its host receptor dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4), which activates the viral spike (S) glycoprotein. However, how receptor binding is structurally coupled to membrane fusion has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of MERS-CoV spike-DPP4 complexes at defined incubation times, capturing a series of conformational states spanning prefusion, receptor-bound, and postfusion conformations. These structures reveal that receptor-binding domain (RBD) opening progressively weakens S1-S2 interactions, while DPP4 binding may induce conformational drift and loosening of the S2 fusion core. These structural changes might destabilize spike trimers, promote S1 dissociation, and prime the fusion machinery. Compared with the SARS-CoV-2 spike, the MERS-CoV spike exhibits greater conformational plasticity, consistent with a lower threshold for receptor-induced fusion. In addition, the postfusion S2 structure suggests that the HR2 upstream linker may function as a conformational switch during six-helix bundle assembly. Together, these findings outline a structural pathway. for receptor-induced activation of the MERS-CoV spike and provide a structural framework for the development of antiviral strategies targeting dynamic fusion intermediates.

articles.title: Screening for patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis via electronic health records: A multicenter machine learning development and validation study.
articles.abstract: Timely detection is crucial to improve outcomes in patients with cardiac amyloidosis (CA) by initiation of guideline-directed disease-modifying treatments. Although confirmatory bone scintigraphy is highly accurate for CA detection, identifying at-risk patients for referral remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, using structured multimodal electronic health record (EHR) data to guide referrals for confirmatory scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. Consecutive all-comer patients (n = 11,616) referred for bone scintigraphy at the Vienna General Hospital (2010-2023) were retrospectively included. Patients referred before August 2020 formed the development cohort. The remaining patients comprised the internal validation cohort. External validation was performed at the University Hospital Essen (n = 1,521). Amylo-Detect was trained using 50 routinely available parameters to predict CA-suggestive uptake (Perugini grade ≥2) and compared with an existing score and clinical routine. High-grade uptake was present in 388 patients (3.0%). Amylo-Detect demonstrated excellent performance in development (AUC 0.93), independent internal validation (AUC 0.91), and external validation cohort (AUC 0.91), outperforming existing scoring systems and clinical routine. Results were consistent across subgroups, even when crucial predictors were missing. Of the 42/388 (10.8%) patients missed in clinical routine, 12/42 (29%) were additionally detected by Amylo-Detect. The model further conveyed significant prognostic value for mortality and heart failure hospitalization. We present Amylo-Detect, a validated EHR-based tool for CA risk prediction, available as a web app, allowing application and further evaluation. By improving timely detection and referral, Amylo-Detect may help address diagnostic delays, pending prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of the ECG-SMART AI score for detecting angiographically significant coronary artery disease in patients undergoing elective coronary angiography.
articles.abstract: The 12-lead ECG is central to the evaluation of patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) but has limited diagnostic accuracy for identifying significant obstructive disease prior to elective coronary angiography. We previously developed an artificial intelligence-enhanced ECG (AI-ECG) model for detecting acute coronary occlusion. Whether this model generalizes to identifying angiographically significant CAD in symptomatic patients undergoing elective evaluation remains unknown. In this prospective cohort study, symptomatic outpatients undergoing elective coronary angiography at a tertiary center received standard 12-lead ECGs before the procedure. ECGs were analyzed offline using a previously validated AI-ECG model originally developed for acute coronary occlusion. Patients were categorized as low or intermediate-to-high risk using predefined thresholds. The primary outcome was angiographically significant CAD (≥70% stenosis in a major epicardial vessel or ≥50% stenosis of the left main coronary artery). Among 363 patients (age 58.9 ± 11 years; 55.1% male), 36.1% had angiographically significant CAD. The AI-ECG classified 56% as low risk and 44% as intermediate-to-high risk. After adjustment for conventional clinical characteristics, intermediate-to-high risk remained independently associated with significant CAD (OR 3.12, 95% CI 1.88-5.20; p < 0.001). Model discrimination was good (AUROC 0.79, 95% CI 0.74-0.84), with 60% precision at 80% recall. In summary, the ECG-SMART AI score demonstrated good diagnostic performance for identifying angiographically significant CAD in symptomatic patients undergoing elective coronary angiography. These findings support the generalizability of a previously developed AI-ECG model beyond acute coronary occlusion and suggest that AI-enhanced ECG analysis may complement existing clinical assessment by providing additional noninvasive information to refine pretest probability during elective evaluation.

articles.title: Advancements in Contrast-enhanced Thoracic MR Angiography.
articles.abstract: There is a clinical need for high-spatial-resolution, electrocardiography (ECG)-gated, respiratory-navigated contrast-enhanced (CE) thoracic MR angiography (MRA; hereafter, NAV CE MRA) robust to physiologic motion artifacts. Compared with first-pass gated techniques, ECG-triggered NAV MRA more effectively suppresses motion and exhibits greater acquisition efficiency and/or artifact mitigation than non-CE MRA. Gradient-echo or balanced steady-state free precession NAV CE MRA has conventionally used diaphragmatic navigators to minimize respiratory motion and parallel imaging for acquisition acceleration. The development of image-based navigators (iNAVs) and variable golden-step Cartesian trajectory with spiral profile order sampling represents a progressive technologic innovation for three-dimensional thoracic CE MRA (hereafter, iNAV CE MRA). iNAV CE MRA can also be combined with time-resolved angiography and abdominopelvic first-pass CE MRA for dynamic information and/or extended anatomic coverage. In this review, we describe techniques for NAV CE MRA motion correction, contrast agent considerations, noncontrast alternatives, use in clinical applications, limitations, and future potential. Keywords: MR Angiography, Congenital, Aorta, Pulmonary Veins, Motion Correction, Aortic Disease, Congenital Heart Disease, Pulmonary Vein Angiography, Variable Density Sampling Supplemental material is available for this article. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license.

articles.title: Gulf regional guidelines for managing diabetic foot ulcers: assessment, treatment and prevention of recurrence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) represent a major and growing complication of diabetes in the Gulf and wider Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, which has the world's highest diabetes prevalence at approximately 17.6% of adults. DFUs carry a high burden of morbidity, mortality and economic cost, and their complex multifactorial aetiology, encompassing peripheral neuropathy, ischaemia, deformity and infection, is compounded by region-specific cultural, climatic and healthcare factors.

AIMS: To develop evidence-based, Gulf-specific clinical guidelines on the assessment, management and prevention of recurrence of DFUs, applicable across varying levels of healthcare infrastructure and sensitive to the cultural context of the Gulf region.

METHOD: An international panel of diabetes and wound care experts from the Gulf region and beyond reviewed current international evidence and guidelines and applied it to Gulf-specific practice contexts. Consensus-based recommendations were formulated across the DFU care pathway through a structured expert panel process.

FINDINGS: The guidelines provide recommendations across five domains: (1) causes and complications, including overlapping aetiological pathways, comorbidities, infection risk, chronicity and psychosocial impact; (2) holistic patient assessment encompassing wound, vascular, neurological, biomechanical, dermatological and footwear evaluation with clear red-flag escalation pathways; (3) management, covering offloading, wound bed preparation, comorbidity optimisation and multidisciplinary collaboration; (4) prevention of recurrence through risk-stratified surveillance, patient education and lifestyle modification; and (5) regional recommendations addressing Gulf-specific clinical, cultural and infrastructural considerations throughout.

CONCLUSION: Effective management of DFUs in the Gulf and MENA region requires a comprehensive, integrated, multidisciplinary approach grounded in international evidence and calibrated to regional context. These guidelines aim to standardise clinical practice, reduce variation in care and improve outcomes for patients across the region.

articles.title: Consensus guidelines on optimal sizing, administration and documentation of cellular, acellular and matrix-like products (CAMPs).
articles.abstract: In January 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) reclassified cellular, acellular and matrixlike products (CAMPs) from 'biologicals' to 'incident-to supplies' under Medicare Part B, introducing a flat-fee reimbursement model. However, there was clinical ambiguity regarding the definition, measurement and documentation of administered and discarded product. This uncertainty has increased audit risk and been associated with reduced confidence among providers in appropriate CAMPs use. In February 2026, a multidisciplinary US panel of wound care and reimbursement specialists convened to establish reco mmendations for CAMPs use consistent with current Medicare policy, addressing three domains: correct clinical use, comprising adequate patient preparation and need for CAMP to conform to both the internal surface area of the wound and an external fixation edge, which combined constitute the therapeutic treatment area (TTA); need for use of drape tracing with planimetry or three-dimensional digital imaging to accurately measure the TTA; and importance of comprehensive documentation of medical necessity and the amount of administered and discarded product, using CMS-aligned terminology. The panel states that traditional length-by-width multiplication is insufficient to measure the TTA.

articles.title: Clinical Performance of a Delphi Consensus and the sFlt-1/PlGF-ratio in Guiding Delivery Decisions in Early-Onset Preeclampsia Before 32 Weeks.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A recent Delphi consensus defined organ-system-based parameters intended to reflect disease severity and delivery urgency in preeclampsia (PE) ≤ 32 weeks. This study evaluates the applicability of these parameters in a real-world cohort.

METHODS: In a retrospective cohort of 1928 women with suspected PE, 148 presented at ≤ 32 weeks, of whom 84 (56.8%) delivered at ≤ 32 weeks. Delivery indications documented in medical records were compared with organ-based Delphi criteria, and Likert scores were calculated. The association between the Delphi Score and the risk of PE-related delivery, as well as Delphi organ-system scores, mean maximal arterial blood pressure and the sFlt-1/PlGF-ratio were examined using regression analysis. ROC analyses and likelihood ratio tests were used to assess the Delphi score, sFlt-1/PlGF-ratio, and the combination of both to predict PE-related delivery.

RESULTS: The Delphi score was associated with an increased risk of PE-related deliveries ≤ 32+0 weeks (OR 1.27 per point, 95% CI 1.12-1.45), p < 0.001) but demonstrated limited predictive accuracy (AUC 0.699 (95% CI 0.612-0.787). Adding the sFlt-1/PlGF-ratio markedly improved model performance (χ 2 from 16.3 to 72.4, p < 0.001; AUC 0.891, 95% CI 0.839-0.943). In the organ subscores, the uteroplacental and fetal Delphi criteria showed the strongest association (44% delivering ≤ 32 weeks vs. 9.4% delivering > 32 weeks). Severe hypertension (≥ 160/100 mmHg), not reflected in the Delphi criteria, led to 60.7% of deliveries.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective real-world cohort, the Delphi score showed limited applicability for guiding delivery decisions in PE ≤ 32 weeks. Incorporating broader hypertension thresholds and biomarkers may enhance decision-making approaches.

articles.title: A Needle Tip Quality-Controlled Training Protocol for Cerebrovascular End-to-Side Bypass: From Bench to Bedside.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Improper techniques in cerebrovascular end-to-side bypass, such as back-wall injury or skiving bites, can lead to stenosis or thrombosis. To address this challenge, we developed a needle tip quality-controlled (TQC) training protocol and evaluated its training value and clinical significance.

METHODS: The TQC protocol mandates continuous visualization of the needle tip within the vessel lumen during each stitch, guided by strict suturing principles that prohibit intraluminal blind suturing. An attending neurosurgeon underwent training using the TQC protocol on a rat femoral vessel model before its clinical application in 26 bypass cases. Cumulative sum analysis was used to assess recipient clamp times during both the animal training and clinical surgeries. Intraoperative and postoperative bypass patency rates were also evaluated.

RESULTS: In the 24 animal models, the mean recipient clamp time was 30.79 ± 6.42 minutes. Cumulative sum analysis revealed that proficiency required 16 models, after which clamp times significantly decreased to 27.37 ± 5.15 minutes (P = .013; mean difference 8.88 minutes, 95% CI, 2.18-15.57). No back-wall injuries or skiving bites were observed, and the delayed patency rate was 95.83%. In the 26 superficial temporal artery to middle cerebral artery bypass cases, the mean recipient clamp time was 26.65 ± 6.16 minutes, with the mastery phase achieved after 6 cases. The intraoperative and 3-month postoperative patency rates were 100% and 96.15%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The TQC protocol effectively prevents technical errors, ensuring high-quality anastomosis. Its high trainability and short learning curve establish it as a practical and valuable training tool for young vascular neurosurgeons.

articles.title: A 2-Year Experience of Robot-Assisted Epilepsy Surgery Using a New Cranial Robotic System With Optical Tracking: Variables Influencing Accuracy and Complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Our institution began using the Globus ExcelsiusGPS cranial robot in 2023 for placement guidance in epilepsy surgeries including depth electrodes for stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG), laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT), NeuroPace responsive neurostimulator, and Medtronic deep brain stimulator. In our first 2 years, we performed 58 epilepsy surgeries for 37 patients using the robot for 466 trajectories. Surgery time, accuracy of trajectory, and hemorrhage rate were analyzed.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of epilepsy surgeries using the Globus ExcelciusGPS cranial robot over our first 2 years of experience. Potential influencing factors analyzed included trajectory length, skull thickness, angle of trajectory with the skull, imaging used for registration, head holder, stabilization of the head, drill used, brain location, type of surgery, the number of each case performed, and the number of trajectories placed. We also analyzed hemorrhage rate and surgery time. Factorial analysis of variance, multiple regression, and Pearson correlation statistics were used.

RESULTS: Accuracy of electrode or laser placement was significantly affected by imaging modality used for robot registration (P = .018), head holder used (P = .014), and the trajectory plan's angle from skull perpendicular (P < .001). The time required for placement per trajectory varied, with SEEG being the fastest and LITT being the slowest (P < .001). There were no symptomatic hemorrhages in this series, with 3 asymptomatic SEEG surgery subarachnoid hemorrhages (9.7% per surgery, 0.7% per electrode) and 2 asymptomatic LITT surgery parenchymal hemorrhages (15% per surgery, 10% per laser). There were no responsive neurostimulator or deep brain stimulator hemorrhages.

CONCLUSION: The accuracy of surgery using the Globus ExcelsiusGPS robot was influenced by factors including the trajectory plan and equipment used. The type of surgery performed influenced the amount of surgical time. These findings may improve the efficiency and accuracy of epilepsy surgery using this cranial robot.

articles.title: Clinical Advantages and Pitfalls of Pulsed Field Ablation: How to Prevent ALH Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Catheter ablation for tachyarrhythmias was first introduced in the early 1980s using direct-current (DC) energy. Following the clinical introduction of radiofrequency (RF) ablation in the late 1980s, thermal ablation technologies became the foundation of catheter ablation because of their superior controllability, efficacy, and safety. In 2014, Wittkampf developed a DC-energy-delivery catheter system preventing electrical arcing, thereby initiating a modern "revival of DC-ablation" based on catheter ablation using electroporation. Subsequent development of high-voltage, short-duration pulse-train delivery led to the emergence of pulsed field ablation (PFA). Exposure of myocytes to high-voltage electric fields induces reversible electroporation through nanoscale pore formation within the lipid bilayer, whereas higher electric-field delivery produces irreversible electroporation, resulting in permanent membrane disruption, apoptosis, and durable lesion formation. PFA is regarded as a predominantly nonthermal and potentially tissue-selective ablation modality. Nevertheless, clinical trials of pulmonary vein isolation for atrial fibrillation have demonstrated that PFA is noninferior to conventional thermal ablation strategies, although clear superiority-other than shorter procedural times-has not yet been established. Importantly, recent studies suggest that electrode-tissue contact remains a critical determinant of durable lesion formation. Accumulating evidence indicates that PFA is associated with new complications not commonly observed with thermal ablation, including acute kidney injury, stroke, coronary vasospasm, myocardial ischemia, ventricular fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. Although the mechanisms remain incompletely understood, hemolysis-related injury induced by high-voltage pulse delivery may represent an important contributing mechanism. Development of PFA systems capable of real-time prediction of irreversible lesion size may be essential for optimizing both procedural efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Differential Associations of Dietary Inflammatory Index and Dietary Antioxidant Indices With Mortality Risk From MASLD/MetALD: Results From a Large Population-Based Study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its subtype, metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD), represent escalating global health challenges. Despite the central role of dietary intervention in current guidelines, evidence remains limited regarding the synergistic impact of anti-inflammatory and antioxidant diets on the survival benefits of steatotic liver disease (SLD) populations, particularly those with moderate alcohol consumption. This study aims to elucidate the associations between dietary inflammatory/antioxidant quality and mortality across SLD subtypes, and provide insights into dietary recommendations for this patient group. Data from 3048 individuals (2146 MASLD, 902 MetALD) who participated in the 2005-2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey were analyzed. Weighted Cox regression analysis was used to estimate the hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for mortality risk assessment. The mediation effects of inflammation-related indicators were explored by mediation analysis. During the follow-up period, a total of 306 deaths were documented. In MASLD patients, higher DII (T3) correlated with increased all-cause mortality (HR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.12-3.47, p = 0.019). Both CDAI and DAQS showed negative associations, with HRs of 0.50 (0.28-0.89) and 0.47 (0.24-0.93) for T3, respectively (both p < 0.05). In MetALD patients, higher DII was associated with increased mortality risk (T2 HR = 4.95, T3 HR = 3.91, both p < 0.05). Joint analysis suggested that higher dietary antioxidant quality was associated with lower mortality risks across SLD subtypes compared with the MASLD group with low dietary antioxidant quality. Mediation analysis suggested that inflammation-related markers (platelets and PHR) may be involved in the associations between dietary indices and mortality in MASLD patients, whereas no statistically significant mediation effects were observed in the MetALD subgroup. Our findings show the key role of dietary quality in reducing mortality among patients with SLD, suggesting that anti-inflammatory and antioxidant-rich diets can improve long-term survival across the SLD spectrum. The findings of this study are expected to provide a new perspective on dietary interventions as a complement to current international guidelines for MASLD/MetALD.

articles.title: Large language models show distinct multidimensional performance profiles and variable reproducibility in consensus-based bone stress injury.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated five publicly available large language model-based systems using a multidimensional, expert-based assessment of consensus-based clinical questions on bone stress injuries.

METHODS: Ten standardised questions derived from a 2025 international Delphi consensus on bone stress injuries were submitted to ChatGPT-5, Perplexity AI, Claude 4, Google Gemini 2.5 and Microsoft Copilot. Responses were independently rated by clinical experts using a multidimensional evaluation framework covering accuracy, comprehensiveness, understanding, reasoning, clarity, potential harm and trust, each rated on a 5-point Likert scale. Median scores were calculated for each question and model, and comparisons were performed using Kruskal-Wallis tests followed by Dunn's post hoc tests with Bonferroni correction. Interrater agreement was assessed using the weighted Gwet's agreement coefficient. Reproducibility was assessed by repeatedly submitting nine questions representing no, partial, and full expert consensus to each model, with response consistency scored from 1 to 3.

RESULTS: Significant differences between models were observed for comprehensiveness, reasoning, clarity and trust (all p < 0.001), with no differences in accuracy or harm. ChatGPT-5 and Claude 4 achieved significantly higher comprehensiveness scores, while ChatGPT-5 and Google Gemini 2.5 had significantly higher reasoning scores than Microsoft Copilot. Claude 4 demonstrated significantly lower clarity than all other models. ChatGPT-5 achieved significantly higher trust scores and showed the highest mean reproducibility score, followed by Perplexity AI and Gemini 2.5; Microsoft Copilot showed the lowest reproducibility. Interrater agreement ranged from fair to almost perfect, with substantial overall agreement.

CONCLUSIONS: Publicly available large language model-based systems demonstrated moderate-to-high performance in addressing expert-derived, consensus-based questions on bone stress injuries, suggesting potential to support the communication of consensus-based knowledge. However, performance varied across evaluation dimensions and reproducibility, indicating that large language models may support, but should not replace, primary consensus documents or expert clinical judgement.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

articles.title: Trends in Premature Mortality Due to Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy Among Working Adults Aged 25-64 Years in the United States, 1999-2024: A CDC Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (WONDER) Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an important alcohol-related cardiovascular condition associated with heart failure and premature mortality. However, long-term national trends in ACM mortality among working-age adults and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic remain incompletely characterized. Methods We conducted a retrospective population-based analysis of United States (US) mortality data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) database. Deaths with ACM (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] code I42.6) as the underlying cause of death were identified for 1999-2024. Adults aged 25-64 years were considered the working-age population. Crude mortality rates (CMRs) and age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 1,000,000 population, with analyses stratified by sex, ethnicity (Hispanic origin), and age subgroup. Results Between 1999 and 2024, there were 13,741 deaths attributed to ACM, including 9,705 (70.63%) among adults aged 25-64 years. The pooled premature CMR was 2.3 per 1,000,000 population (95% CI: 2.2-2.3). Men accounted for 85.24% of premature deaths, with a pooled CMR of 3.9 per 1,000,000 compared with 0.7 per 1,000,000 among women. Adults aged 45-64 years accounted for 78.79% of premature deaths and had a CMR of 3.8 per 1,000,000 compared with 0.9 per 1,000,000 among those aged 25-44 years. Mortality increased during 2020-2021, reaching a peak in 2021, followed by a progressive decline through 2024. In 2024, the premature CMR was 1.9 per 1,000,000. AAMRs largely followed CMR trends. Conclusion ACM accounted for a substantial proportion of premature alcohol-related cardiovascular mortality in working-age adults in the US. Mortality was disproportionately concentrated among men and adults aged 45-64 years, increased during 2020-2021, and subsequently declined. These findings highlight persistent disparities and the need for continued prevention, early recognition, and targeted reduction of alcohol-related cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Hypoglycemic Effect of Astaxanthin Oil-Fish Oil Complex in Mice With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM), a chronic metabolic disorder, is characterized by disrupted glucose homeostasis, and its escalating global prevalence underscores the critical need for safe dietary interventions. This study investigated the hypoglycemic and hepatoprotective potential of a novel formulation combining astaxanthin oil (AO) and fish oil (FO) as an adjuvant nutritional strategy. The efficacy of the AO-FO complex was evaluated using the insulin-resistant HepG2 cell model in vitro and high-fat diet (HFD)-fed insulin-resistant mice in vivo. While individual treatments with AO and FO improved basic insulin sensitivity, their co-administration exhibited enhanced efficacy in promoting cellular glucose consumption. Notably, the combined formulation was associated with changes in key glucose metabolism-related indices, including glucose-6-phosphate, pyruvate kinase, hexokinase, and significantly mitigated oxidative stress markers. In vivo, the AO-FO complex showed greater effects on decreasing fasting blood glucose, improving oral glucose tolerance, and ameliorating systemic dyslipidemia compared to singular oil treatments. Furthermore, histopathological evaluations revealed a marked attenuation of hepatic steatosis and pancreatic islet damage following the combined treatment. Collectively, these findings support the potential combined benefits of astaxanthin and omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids for improving glucose homeostasis, suggesting that the AO-FO complex may be a candidate functional food for DM management.

articles.title: Development of a Survey Instrument Grounded in Resident Voice to Measure Key Drivers of Learning in Simulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Simulation based education (SBE) is frequently driven by competencies necessary to document progress in residency. These competencies, however, are missing crucial factors that matter to residents. Unfortunately, there is no current validated tool that captures learning experiences grounded in factors that residents voice as important. This study was designed to uncover meaningful resident-derived factors within SBE to inform development of a learner-centered tool and provide educators with actionable information to guide simulation curriculum design and improvement.

METHODS: An exploratory sequential mixed methods study was deployed within an accredited emergency medicine (EM) residency at an academic center. Resident focus groups were conducted and themes generated through thematic analysis were collected. A survey tool was developed and underwent a content validation process. Pilot deployment was delivered to EM residency programs across the country. Responses were analyzed for demographics, descriptive statistics, and internal consistency.

RESULTS: Four major themes emerged, each serving as distinct sections of the tool. The Psychological Safety and Learning Effectiveness theme encompasses meaningful resident engagement. The Integration of Experience and Evidence theme connects SBE to evidence-informed practices. The Learner-responsive Simulation Design theme captures learning principles that emphasize metacognitive maturity. The Clinical Reasoning Structure theme provides insights on translation to practice. Quantitative analysis revealed considerable demographic diversity and range analysis with a variable yet expected spread. Cronbach's alpha demonstrated strong consistency for relevant and academically-based constructs and expected modest consistency for nuanced constructs.

CONCLUSIONS: A survey instrument grounded in resident voice was developed and positioned to measure key drivers for residents in SBE. This tool demonstrates early evidence of validity, purposeful internal consistency, and feasibility through pilot testing. Simulation educators may use the instrument to identify strengths and gaps within simulation curricula, evaluate the impact of curricular interventions over time, guide resident-informed program improvements, and facilitate benchmarking across institutions.

articles.title: Efficacy of Vitamin E Administration on Serum Lipid Profile in Adult Patients With Dyslipidemia: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Studies have shown that vitamin E has therapeutic effects on lipid metabolism; however, findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis aims to assess the effectiveness of vitamin E administration on the serum lipid panel in patients with dyslipidemia. A database search through January 2026 was conducted to identify relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Relevant data, including triglycerides (TG), total cholesterol (TC), and low- and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C and HDL-C), were extracted. The overall effect size was estimated using weighted mean differences (WMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) via a random-effects model. The pooled analysis of 22 RCTs (33 intervention arms) demonstrated that vitamin E significantly lowered TG (WMD: -8.14 mg/dL, p = 0.021) and raised HDL-C (WMD: 1.08 mg/dL, p = 0.037) in patients with dyslipidemia, whereas reductions in TC (WMD: -6.48 mg/dL, p = 0.097) and LDL-C (WMD: -9.06 mg/dL, p = 0.063) were not significant overall. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that tocotrienols may exert greater lipid-modifying effects than tocopherols, with potentially larger benefits observed at lower doses, among individuals with more pronounced baseline lipid abnormalities, and during shorter intervention periods. In conclusion, vitamin E supplementation in patients with dyslipidemia shows modest improvements in lipid profiles, mainly lowering TG and increasing HDL-C, with less consistent effects on TC and LDL-C. Tocotrienols may be more effective than tocopherols, suggesting possible isoform-specific effects, but overall clinical impact appears limited and requires further confirmation.

articles.title: Persistent Supraventricular Tachycardia Following Central Venous Catheter Insertion: When Withdrawal of the Mechanical Stimulus Is Not Enough.
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are a recognised complication of central venous catheterisation and are usually attributed to mechanical irritation of the endocardium by the guidewire or catheter tip. These arrhythmias typically resolve following withdrawal of the mechanical stimulus. We report a 42-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and diabetic ketoacidosis who developed an abrupt regular narrow-complex tachycardia at approximately 217 beats/min immediately following advancement of a right internal jugular central venous catheter. The arrhythmia was associated with transient hypotension and dizziness and persisted despite removal of both the guidewire and catheter. This case illustrates that catheter manipulation may trigger a sustained supraventricular tachycardia that persists after removal of the mechanical stimulus, particularly in a patient with structural heart disease and metabolic and electrolyte abnormalities. Persistent tachyarrhythmia following catheter withdrawal should prompt assessment of haemodynamic stability and guideline-directed arrhythmia management rather than an assumption of spontaneous resolution.

articles.title: Totally endoscopic septal myectomy combined with mitral valve replacement for suicide left ventricle following transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) causing acute haemodynamic collapse is a rare but life-threatening complication after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Known as suicide left ventricle (SLV), it results from abrupt afterload reduction leading to hypercontractility and dynamic obstruction. Medical therapy is often insufficient, requiring advanced intervention.

CASE SUMMARY: An 88-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis underwent TAVI. Preprocedural echocardiography showed septal hypertrophy without significant LVOTO. Immediately after valve deployment, she developed LVOTO with systolic anterior motion and severe mitral regurgitation, leading to haemodynamic deterioration. Medical management-including volume loading, discontinuation of inotropes, and beta-blocker-was ineffective. Catheter-based therapies were unsuitable because of severe leaflet calcification. Therefore, totally endoscopic transmitral septal myectomy with mitral valve replacement was performed. Postoperative echocardiography confirmed resolution of LVOTO and mitral regurgitation. She gradually recovered and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative Day 132.

DISCUSSION: TAVI can cause SLV in patients with septal hypertrophy. Although transcatheter therapies are generally preferred in patients at high surgical risk, this case demonstrates that totally endoscopic surgery can be a feasible alternative when catheter-based options are not appropriate. Careful preprocedural risk assessment for SLV and consideration of alternative strategies are essential in patients at increased risk of developing this complication.

articles.title: The dipeptidyl peptidase 1 inhibition landscape in bronchiectasis and its future direction.
articles.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
articles.abstract: Bronchiectasis (BE) is a heterogeneous lung disease characterised by chronic neutrophilic inflammation. A "vicious vortex" develops through the interactions between neutrophilic inflammation, infection and impaired mucociliary clearance, leading to progressive structural lung damage and worsening lung function. As part of this neutrophilic inflammation, neutrophil serine proteases (NSPs) overwhelm their natural inhibitors, with high NSP levels being associated with pulmonary exacerbations in people with BE. NSPs, activated by dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1) during neutrophil maturation in the bone marrow, are released from neutrophils at sites of inflammation. Pharmacological inhibition of DPP1 is a compelling approach to reduce neutrophilic inflammation in BE. Three DPP1 inhibitors have had favourable results in clinical studies for BE, namely brensocatib, florensocatib and verducatib, with recent approval of brensocatib, a first-in-class DPP1 inhibitor, in the US and Europe, providing a promising treatment option for people with BE. Many questions about DPP1 inhibition remain, including long-term efficacy and safety, and efficacy in people with cystic fibrosis, primary COPD and immunodeficiencies, who were generally excluded from prior large studies. Despite the availability of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapy, many people with cystic fibrosis continue to have pulmonary exacerbations. The inclusion of a broad population with a range of aetiologies is key in the development of DPP1 inhibitors to support access to treatment for all those who could benefit. This review explores the current DPP1 inhibition landscape, discussing the clinical studies to date for these three novel DPP1 inhibitors and the evolution of DPP1 studies in BE.

articles.title: Manual compared to automated closed-loop oxygen control strategies in hospitalised adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closed-loop oxygen control (CLOC) systems improve accuracy of oxygen delivery compared with standard manual oxygen adjustment. Determination of their efficacy in delivering oxygen noninvasively to adults, using different delivery methods and across different hospital locations, would enhance clinical practice.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, searching Medline, Embase, Scopus Basic and Advanced, and Cochrane databases. Randomised controlled trials comparing time spent within a target peripheral oxygen saturation (S pO2 ) range between CLOC and manual oxygen control in hospitalised adults (>18 years) were included. Outpatient studies and studies using mechanical ventilation were excluded. The primary outcome was proportion of time spent within a target S pO2 range. Meta-regression was performed for pre-determined study-level covariates, including oxygen delivery mode and locations of care.

RESULTS: The search identified 3777 papers; of these, seven were included, with 635 participants. The mean proportion of time spent within the target S pO2 range was between 81.2 and 94.9% for CLOC and 51.3-84.0% for manual oxygen control. The mean difference was 21.2% (95% CI 18.5-23.8, p<0.0001), favouring CLOC. Evidence of heterogeneity (I2=87.9) was explained by three studies using low-flow oxygen therapy, mean difference 30.9% (95% CI 27.0-34.8, p<0.0001); compared with four studies using high-flow nasal oxygen therapy, mean difference 12.7% (95% CI 9.1-16.4, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: CLOC improves adherence to a target S pO2 range compared to manual oxygen control and is an effective approach for achieving a target S pO2 range when delivering oxygen noninvasively in hospitalised adults.

articles.title: Inflammasomes in respiratory diseases: from disease pathogenesis to drug development and use of multi-omics.
articles.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
articles.abstract: Inflammasomes are pivotal for the initiation and control of host inflammatory responses. This is particularly important in the respiratory system due to its direct exposure to noxious environmental and infectious stimuli, which can cause local inflammation, tissue damage and impaired function. Inflammasomes are activated by a variety of processes that result in a loss of cellular homeostasis, leading to the oligomerisation of specific innate immune sensors. Inflammasome complex formation then results in a form of programmed cell death known as pyroptosis and release of cleaved active pro-inflammatory cytokines, interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18, and the subsequent inflammatory cascade. While acute inflammasome activation can be protective in controlling infection, chronic inflammasome activation is detrimental and can lead to irreversible changes in the lung micro-environment such as chronic inflammation, emphysema, lung fibrosis and impaired gas exchange and lung function.
